articles.title: Ukraine's newest anti-drone laser weapon is already on active combat duty
articles.text:
Ukraine is now using lasers to kill drones — 4Kw Blysk anti-UAV system can shoot flying adversaries up to one kilometer away
Ukraine wants to shoot drones out of the sky without firing a bullet
- Ukraine has deployed Blysk, a domestically developed laser system targeting incoming drones
- The weapon uses a four-kilowatt beam to damage aircraft structures
- Blysk can reportedly engage aerial threats from distances reaching one kilometer
Ukraine has introduced a domestically-developed laser weapon into its air defense network, adding another technology against enemy drones.
Blysk uses a concentrated 4-kilowatt laser beam to damage aircraft by heating and burning their external structures.
Developed by Carmine Sky, the installation can engage aerial threats from distances reaching one kilometer, although its combat effectiveness remains unproven.
Ukraine deploys a 4kW laser weapon against incoming drones
The installation reportedly entered combat service in early November 2026, following development by Ukrainian defense technology company Carmine Sky.
Its introduction comes as Ukraine expands its protection network against Russian unmanned aircraft, including cheap attack drones and faster jet-powered variants.
According to the developers, Blysk identifies approaching aircraft, tracks their movement and directs concentrated laser energy toward vulnerable sections.
The resulting heat damages the aircraft's exterior, potentially disabling its structure and preventing continued flight.
Sign up to the TechRadar Pro newsletter to get all the top news, opinion, features and guidance your business needs to succeed!
The company says small first-person-view drones can be destroyed within fractions of a second after the laser reaches them.
Larger aircraft, including Shahed and Geran drones, require longer exposure because their external structures contain multiple protective materials.
Despite entering service, the installation had not recorded a successful interception when the developers spoke to journalists.
Carmine Sky attributed the initial absence of confirmed engagements partly to persistent cloud cover and fog around Kyiv in November.
Atmospheric conditions present an important limitation because laser energy becomes less effective when moisture and suspended particles interfere with transmission.
This makes visibility and weather conditions important considerations when determining whether the installation can engage approaching aircraft successfully.
The Ukrainian weapon also operates at considerably lower power than Israel's Iron Beam laser defense system.
Iron Beam reportedly delivers 100 kW of laser power and has an advertised engagement distance reaching approximately 10 kilometers.
Ukraine expands laser development as private air defense networks grow
Blysk is not Ukraine's first publicly announced attempt to develop laser weapons for intercepting aerial threats.
In December 2024, Colonel Vadym Sukharevsky announced a Ukrainian project called Tryzub, developed under the country's Unmanned Systems Forces.
During that announcement, Sukharevsky claimed the technology could already engage aircraft.
Despite these public claims, no independently verified aerial interception by Tryzub had been reported, leaving its battlefield effectiveness uncertain.
Carmine Sky insists that its Blysk installation is an independent development rather than another version of the earlier Tryzub project.
The company also says it intends to develop additional laser installations with different capabilities for protecting important infrastructure.
The new weapon joins an expanding network of remotely operated defenses that already includes automated machine-gun installations protecting infrastructure around Kyiv.
Laser weapons could eventually provide another interception option without consuming conventional ammunition during every engagement.
However, Blysk's reported capabilities still require confirmation through successful interceptions, particularly against larger drones under unfavorable atmospheric conditions.
Via BBC (originally in Ukrainian)

articles.title: L’AFP coupe l’accès à sa plateforme après une cyberattaque
articles.text:
L'Agence France-Presse a fermé AFP Forum, la plateforme où ses clients consultent et téléchargent ses dépêches et ses images, après une cyberattaque dans la nuit de mercredi à jeudi. L'agence propose des solutions de repli à ses abonnés et ignore encore qui a mené l'attaque.
Quand vous lisez un article signé « avec AFP », le média a repris une dépêche de l'agence. L'AFP est l'une des trois agences mondiales d'information, avec AP et Reuters. Selon son rapport annuel 2025, ses 1 840 journalistes, répartis dans 210 bureaux, produisent chaque jour en moyenne 2 300 dépêches, 3 000 photos et 300 vidéos, en six langues. Une partie de ce flux passe par AFP Forum, inaccessible depuis l'attaque.
L'AFP a isolé AFP Forum dès la détection de l'intrusion
Les pirates ont frappé à partir de 1 h 30, heure de Paris, selon un message interne de la direction de l'AFP cité par Le Monde. « Dès la détection de l'intrusion, nos équipes ont isolé la plateforme pour la protéger », écrit la direction. Par précaution, l'agence garde le site fermé pour l'instant.
Qui sont les pirates ? L'AFP l'ignore. « Des analyses sont en cours, avec l'appui d'experts extérieurs », affirme l'agence.
Pour rappel, fin septembre 2024, des pirates avaient touché une partie des systèmes qui servent à livrer les contenus de l'AFP à ses clients, lors d'une première cyberattaque.
Les attaques informatiques se sont multipliées ces derniers mois contre les entreprises et les organismes publics en France, souligne Le Monde. Certaines servent à voler des données, d'autres viennent de pays étrangers qui cherchent à déstabiliser le pays. Depuis janvier, la France subit en moyenne trois vols de données par jour, selon le gouvernement, qui a lancé fin avril un plan d'action pour mieux protéger les systèmes de l'État.

articles.title: Une chaîne russe fait parler Dostoïevski à l’écran grâce à l’IA
articles.text:
Fiodor Dostoïevski, mort en 1881, commente l'actualité sur Russia Today. Depuis un mois, la chaîne financée par l'État russe fait intervenir un double du romancier généré par intelligence artificielle, d'abord pour lire ses textes, puis pour attaquer les Russes partis à l'étranger avec des phrases écrites à sa place.
L'idée vient d'un éditorialiste britannique. Dans une chronique publiée par Bloomberg Opinion le 17 octobre, Martin Ivens, rédacteur du Times Literary Supplement, estimait que Dostoïevski, s'il vivait aujourd'hui, soutiendrait sans doute l'invasion de l'Ukraine et passerait sur Russia Today. Margarita Simonyan, la rédactrice en chef de RT, a pris la provocation au mot. Quatre jours plus tard, elle a publié sur sa chaîne Telegram une vidéo de l'écrivain et promis d'en faire un « expert politique permanent » de RT. Dans ce premier extrait, l'avatar lisait un passage authentique du Journal d'un écrivain sur les relations entre la Russie et l'Europe. Le 4 novembre, il a pris la parole depuis un studio de la chaîne avec un texte inédit.
Un Dostoïevski entièrement fabriqué par intelligence artificielle
Le visage du romancier, le décor et les objets autour de lui sont tous générés par IA, selon l'édition russe du Moscow Times. Le rendu est loin d'être parfait. De nombreux internautes russes ont relevé une mimique peu naturelle, avec le haut du visage presque immobile.
Pour le texte, RT a changé de méthode entre les deux vidéos. Après des phrases tirées de l'œuvre de Dostoïevski, la chaîne lui a fait réciter un monologue écrit à sa manière, et personne ne sait encore si ce discours sort de la plume d'un journaliste ou d'un modèle de langage.
La chaîne a de l'expérience dans ce domaine. Dès 2024, Margarita Simonyan affirmait sur la chaîne moscovite TVC qu'une « part importante » des présentateurs de RT étaient des créations de l'IA, visage et voix compris. « Au départ, nous utilisions des modèles occidentaux, mais nous développons activement les nôtres », a-t-elle expliqué cette année au Jakarta Globe. Le nom du modèle qui anime Dostoïevski est inconnu.
En France, Thierry Ardisson avait fait revivre Dalida en 2022 dans Hôtel du temps, sur France 3, avec une tout autre recette. Une comédienne jouait la chanteuse devant la caméra, puis le studio Mac Guff remplaçait son visage par celui de Dalida grâce à l'IA. Chez RT, l'image entière est synthétique, du costume au décor.
Russia Today fait attaquer les exilés russes par son Dostoïevski
Le 4 novembre, jour de la fête de l'Unité nationale en Russie, le double numérique s'en est pris aux Russes qui ont quitté le pays depuis le début de la guerre en Ukraine. « Nous voyons des milliers de Russes fuir leur foyer, abandonnant leurs enfants, leurs anciens », lance l'avatar dans l'extrait diffusé par franceinfo. Plus loin, il accuse les exilés d'avoir le cœur endurci sous l'influence de doctrines étrangères et les traite de traîtres.
Dans ses autres chroniques, d'après franceinfo, le faux Dostoïevski tient des propos conservateurs, souvent hostiles à l'Europe, et soutient la guerre menée par Vladimir Poutine.
Dans l'Union européenne, la diffusion de RT est suspendue depuis le 2 mars 2022, date à laquelle le Conseil de l'UE a coupé en urgence RT France et quatre autres éditions de la chaîne, rappelle un rapport du Sénat. Les autorités françaises ont constaté dès 2022 que RT France contournait l'interdiction en passant par des plateformes installées en dehors de l'Union, telles qu'Odysee et Rumble.
Faire commenter l'actualité à un mort grâce à l'IA est une pratique connue en Russie. En juin 2023, le parti LDPR avait présenté au Forum économique de Saint-Pétersbourg un avatar en 3D de son fondateur Vladimir Jirinovski, mort l'année précédente. Le personnage commentait l'actualité avec sa voix et ses mimiques. Pour l'historienne de la littérature Maria Maïofis, auteure d'une tribune dans l'édition russe du Moscow Times, le Dostoïevski de RT sert surtout aux vivants à faire porter leurs idées par un mort.

articles.title: Denny’s touts renewed support for Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang following reinstatement — says ‘some things you just don’t take off the menu’
articles.text:
Denny’s touts renewed support for Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang following reinstatement — says ‘some things you just don’t take off the menu’
Denny's posted a 200-word statement to its X social media account, ignoring the fact that Huang resigned from Nvidia after admitting he had an affair with a suspected Chinese spy.
Following his recent resignation from the company and his return as CEO earlier this week, Jensen Huang has received a glowing statement of support from Denny's, the chain where he famously began his working life before founding Nvidia. The diner chain Denny's posted a 200-word statement to X in which it sought to maintain its links to the Nvidia founder, saying that there are "some things you just don’t take off the menu." Denny's, famously, is the diner where Huang came up with the idea for Nvidia before founding the then-GPU company, now an AI server outfit.
Notably, the chain also noted that it has restored a plaque commemorating the occasion to "where it belongs," days after it was removed amid growing controversy over Huang and his affair with former Megaspeed employee Alice Huang. Megaspeed is now under criminal investigation over its involvement in bypassing U.S. export controls relating to Nvidia's advanced AI chips. It's also believed that Alice Huang's husband, Kang Wei, may also be a spy with connections to China's Ministry of State Security.
Despite all of that, Denny's has very much hitched its trailer to Huang and his reputation, for better or worse. The diner's statement ends by reminding him that his booth "is always waiting and the coffee's on," although it's unclear whether he'll be able to make time for a visit between his upcoming visit to Congress to discuss the last few weeks' goings-on and joining board meetings with U.S. President Donald Trump. There is good news for Huang, though, even if he's found to have broken the law during his trysts with the suspected spy. Trump says that a pardon is "always an option," meaning Huang could be free to visit all the Denny's diners he wants to in the future.
As for Nvidia, its share price has suffered the same fate as other tech stocks in recent weeks. It rallied after initially nosediving around the time of Huang's resignation, but has since continued its downward trajectory, having fallen almost 2.4 percentage points in the last five days and over 30 points in the last month.

articles.title: North Korea-Linked PolinRider Poisons Over 7,600 GitHub Repositories to Spread Malware
articles.text:
The threat actors behind the PolinRider campaign have been observed planting a Python loader in GitHub repositories, as evidence emerges that the activity may have started as far back as February 2025.
"The loader hides in a small utils package or in conftest.py," SafeDep said in a report published this week. "When Python imports the file, the loader reads the newest transaction that an Ethereum wallet sent to itself. It decodes the input data of that transaction as JavaScript and runs it with Node.js."
The JavaScript code, for its part, reads a second wallet to locate the command-and-control (C2) server and then passes the next stage to a detached interactive Node.js environment by means of a node -i process.
The software supply chain security company said it identified the loader in 375 public repositories that belong to 260 accounts. There is no evidence that the loader has been distributed via PyPI or npm.
PolinRider is the name assigned to a malicious campaign linked to North Korean threat actors. Recent reports indicate that the activity employs various channels to distribute malware, including -
- Fraudulent recruitment campaigns that make use of phishing emails and fake hiring portals like BlockNovas, AccuraSoftHire ("accurasofthire[.]com") and HuntRole ("huntrole[.]org") to trick prospective targets into running malware-laced projects under the pretext of a take-home assessment.
- Publishing malicious packages across open-source ecosystems by hijacking maintainer accounts to plant obfuscated malware through fake font files (fa-solid-400.woff2, fa-solid-500.woff2, or fa-solid-300.llf), Visual Studio Code (VS Code) auto-run tasks, and Git history rewriting.
- Using compromised developer machines to steal their GitHub tokens and force-push malicious commits into open-source repositories they have access to.
At a high level, the PolinRider loader retrieves an encrypted second-stage Node.js payload that scans the infected host for installed developer applications, such as GitHub Desktop, Cursor, VS Code, and Google Antigravity, and tampers with the most frequently used tools to execute attacker-controlled code and deliver infostealer malware.
It's worth noting here that PolinRider is assessed to be a sub-cluster operating in parallel with a long-running campaign codenamed Contagious Interview. While the latter is more of a social-engineering entry point that's used to compromise developer systems, PolinRider abuses the access to modify repositories and turn them into a distribution channel for malware.
"Cybercriminal groups deploy supply chain worms for opportunistic theft. On the other hand, North Korean state-sponsored threat actors use open-source software registries as a primary initial access vector targeting corporate environments," Palo Alto Networks Unit 42 said in a report published last month.
"Threat actors demonstrate how compromising a single maintainer account or registry scope converts open-source dependencies, resulting in widespread affected cloud environments."
Some of the decoy sites have been found to incorporate two other alternate delivery paths -
- Instruct candidates to sideload a Google Chrome extension after enabling "Developer mode" to subscribe to new job alerts.
- Employ ClickFix-style lures to get victims to copy and paste malicious commands into the terminal app depending on the operating system as part of a "standard settings bundle for candidates and interview workflows."
"The [job] application asks for a short verification video," StepSecurity said. "Until the server marks a candidate as having installed a 'driver,' the camera check always fails with a message saying the system does not have a compatible camera environment."
"A separate 'Technical onboarding' page on the site gives a one-line curl command to download the 'driver.' On Windows, the downloaded installer fetches a script from the careers site that installs Node.js if it is missing, downloads a JavaScript payload, runs it in the background and deletes itself. The macOS and Linux versions do the same."
The JavaScript malware is designed to perform the following steps -
- Read the latest transaction associated with an Ethereum wallet ("0xa322E5f3D311D3080e6f0121063e9aDC2490Ef1a").
- Get its destination wallet address ("0x67B38e9b67B38E9b68656c6C6f6970626f742121").
- Extract the C2 server address twice ("103.179.142[.]155") from the first eight bytes ("67B38e9b" and "67B38E9b") of the wallet address, using a technique referred to as NullReceiver, while the last 12 bytes represent the ASCII string "helloipbot!!."
- Use the IP address to fetch two payloads, "0x/cls" and "0x/ls," over port 443.
| The NullReceiver technique | 
The latest findings from SafeDep show that the repositories are injected with a 58-line Python loader that reads the "0x3b1574417524c11a7403c4b232CAcBb320CceBC6" wallet to extract JavaScript code that then reaches out to a second wallet ("0x1eEf0849EDa15d87f64e51C73C8442Cf3c8bCEF3") to obtain the destination wallet associated with the latest transaction ("0x5F87b5545F87b55468656C6C6f6970626f742121"), which is then used to parse the C2 server ("95.135.181[.]84").
A defining aspect of NullReceiver is the marker "68656c6C6f6970626f742121" in the made-up destination wallet address that consistently translates to "helloipbot!!."
"The /0x/cls script runs twice, once with eval in the current process and once in a new process," SafeDep said. "The /0x/ls script runs only in a new process."
The exact nature of these payloads remains unknown. However, prior waves have been observed installing a stealer that harvests environment secrets, browser passwords, cookies, and wallet data. Interestingly, the wallet address "0x1eef0849eda15d87f64e51c73c8442cf3c8bcef3" has been reused by the threat actors across other attack waves -
- Pushing compromised versions of legitimate npm packages such as @adminide-stack/utils, @adminide-stack/health-api-server, @adminide-stack/user-activity-browser, @adminide-stack/utils, @adminide-stack/forms-core, @adminide-stack/yantra-help-browser, server-hemera-mongo, cdeops, @cdmbase/wiki-browser, and @pubngo-stack/help-browser that use the same wallet address to fetch /0x/cls and /0x/ls from "95.135.181[.]151."
- A fake recruitment campaign from HuntRole that convinces victims to complete a coding assessment, which uses a VS Code extension named "huntrole.assessment-tool" from the Visual Studio Marketplace to send system information and fetch and run a malicious JavaScript payload. The script queries the same wallet address to fetch /0x/cls and /0x/ls from "95.135.181[.]84."
- 
    Using a GitHub account named "
    
      Eternity0207
    
    " to open over 200 pull requests targeting open-source projects like AsyncAPI Generator, CircuitVerse, and Open Food Facts, and subsequently force-push a modified commit containing an obfuscated loader that uses the same wallet address to fetch /0x/cls and /0x/ls from "95.135.181[.]84."
    
  - According to the maintainer of AsyncAPI Generator, "Each time, the payload stayed on the branch for 30-40 minutes and was then force-pushed away, so the final diff looked clean." The unauthorized modifications allowed the loader to run when an unsuspecting developer runs "npm run build" (for AsyncAPI), loads the test configuration (for Open Food Facts), or opens the folder in VS Code (for CircuitVerse). The GitHub account has since been suspended.
According to estimates from Apiiro, PolinRider has been detected in at least 7,609 GitHub repos owned by 2,330 accounts, most of them belonging to developers. Some of the victims include Neutralinojs, InstaWP Connect, and fxhash. The loader has been pushed to 2,040 repositories between October 27 and November 6, 2026.
"The worm uses stolen GitHub access to rewrite commits the developer already made, keeping the author, message and date, and adds a loader hidden after hundreds of spaces in a build config," Apiiro researcher Shmulik Cohen said.
"Building the project runs it. In the newest wave, opening the folder in VS Code is enough. The loader reads its server from an Ethereum wallet, so taking a server down changes nothing: one transaction moves every loader to the next."
| PolinRider attack from May 2025 | 
The development comes as OpenSourceMalware said it discovered a PolinRider attack from May 2025, predating the earliest documented victims by eight months. The attack targeted nine packages, using hijacked maintainer account to push poisoned versions within a span of 90 minutes -
- itsa-utils@1.4.2
- itsa-jsext@2.0.3
- itsa-react-docviewer@16.1.2
- itsa-cli@16.5.3
- itsa-react-button@16.0.11
- itsa-react-maskedinput@16.1.2
- itsa-react-checkbox@16.0.5
- itsa-react-focuscontainer@16.0.10
- itsa-react-input@16.1.2
Each of these packages have been found to leverage EtherHiding, a precursor to NullReceiver, to retrieve a JavaScript downloader called JADESNOW, which is then used to deliver InvisibleFerret, a Python-based backdoor used in Contagious Interview campaigns, along with a Socket.IO RAT and a Python-based stealer.
"The 2025 sample carries PolinRider's payload but not its documented spread behavior, which appears in the same maintainer's GitHub repositories in four windows between January and July 2026," security researchers Paul McCarty and Jenn Gile said. "The blockchain records behind it date attacker activity back to February 2025."
"The infection likely persisted on the maintainer's machine from 2025, because the 2026 pushes ran from it. That matches PolinRider's documented propagation script, which rolls back the clock, folds the payload into the tip commit, and force-pushes with the developer's own credentials."

articles.title: WhatsApp deja programar mensajes: qué pasa si mi celular está apagado cuando se envía el texto
articles.text:
WhatsApp comenzó a desplegar mundialmente una función que permite programar el envío de mensajes para una fecha y hora determinadas. La herramienta incorpora una característica que muchos usuarios esperaban: los textos, fotografías y videos podrán llegar a sus destinatarios incluso cuando el celular de quien los envía esté apagado, sin batería o desconectado de internet.
La compañía confirmó el lanzamiento después de probar esta opción en las versiones beta de Android y iOS. La implementación será gradual durante las próximas semanas, por lo que algunos usuarios podrían tener que esperar para encontrarla disponible en sus cuentas.
La nueva herramienta permitirá preparar mensajes con hasta 14 días de anticipación. De esta manera, será posible dejar listo un saludo de cumpleaños para la medianoche, enviar un recordatorio antes de un examen o comunicarse con alguien que vive en otro país sin tener que estar pendiente del reloj.
¿Se envían los mensajes de WhatsApp si el celular está apagado?
Sí. Una de las principales características de esta función es que el envío no dependerá de que el teléfono del remitente permanezca encendido o conectado a internet.
Según informó WhatsApp, una vez programado el mensaje, la plataforma se encargará de entregarlo en el momento seleccionado. Esto significa que el usuario podrá apagar su celular, quedarse sin batería o perder la conexión a internet y el contenido llegará igualmente al chat del destinatario.
El funcionamiento representa una diferencia frente al envío tradicional de mensajes, que requiere que el usuario tenga conexión para transmitir el contenido. Con esta nueva herramienta, la programación queda preparada dentro del servicio para ejecutarse en la fecha y hora establecidas.
Además, el destinatario recibirá el texto, la fotografía o el video como cualquier otro mensaje habitual. No aparecerá una notificación especial que indique que el contenido fue programado con anticipación.
WhatsApp también aseguró que estos envíos conservarán el cifrado de extremo a extremo, el sistema de seguridad que impide que terceros puedan leer el contenido de las conversaciones mientras se transmite.
Cómo programar mensajes en WhatsApp
La función permitirá seleccionar el momento exacto en que se enviará un contenido, tanto en conversaciones individuales como en grupos. Para utilizarla, será necesario seguir un procedimiento sencillo desde el chat correspondiente.
Estos son los pasos para dejar un mensaje programado:
- Abrir WhatsApp e ingresar a la conversación individual o grupal donde se quiere enviar el contenido.
- Escribir el mensaje o seleccionar la fotografía o el video que se desea compartir.
- Mantener presionado el botón de envío, en lugar de tocarlo una sola vez.
- Seleccionar la opción para programar el mensaje.
- Elegir la fecha y la hora en que se realizará el envío.
- Confirmar la programación.
La herramienta permitirá establecer envíos desde 10 minutos hasta 14 días después de haber preparado el contenido. Así, los usuarios podrán organizar comunicaciones con cierta anticipación sin necesidad de volver a abrir la aplicación para enviarlas.
¿Se pueden cancelar los mensajes programados?
Sí. WhatsApp también incorporará un espacio desde el que será posible revisar los mensajes que todavía no fueron enviados.
Esta sección permitirá identificar los contenidos pendientes y eliminarlos si el usuario cambia de opinión. Por ejemplo, si alguien programa un recordatorio para una fecha determinada y después descubre que ya no es necesario, podrá cancelarlo antes de que llegue el momento de entrega.
La posibilidad de administrar estos envíos resulta importante para evitar que se compartan mensajes desactualizados o que ya no tienen sentido cuando llega la hora seleccionada.
La función también admite diferentes formatos de contenido. No estará limitada a textos, sino que permitirá programar fotografías y videos en conversaciones individuales y grupales.

articles.title: Taxe numérique européenne à 3% : Washington monte au créneau et l'Irlande menace de tout bloquer
articles.text:
Pour financer son prochain budget, l’UE envisage de taxer à 3% certains revenus des géants de la tech. En France, Google Ads et des vendeurs sur Amazon ont déjà répercuté un prélèvement comparable.
À l’ouverture du sommet sur le budget européen 2028-2034, ce jeudi 26 novembre, Washington a rejeté le projet de taxe sur les services numériques dans l’Union européenne. Selon une dépêche de l’AFP publiée par Mediapart, le département d’État le juge discriminatoire pour les entreprises américaines et estime que les consommateurs en feraient aussi les frais. Parmi les membres de l’UE, l’Irlande mène l’opposition.
Une recette qui pourrait rapporter jusqu’à 6 milliards d’euros par an
En proposant cette taxe, le président du Conseil européen, António Costa, veut dégager de nouvelles recettes pour l’Union sans trop alourdir les contributions nationales. Danuše Nerudová, corapporteure au Parlement européen sur les ressources propres de l’UE, estime que le prélèvement pourrait rapporter jusqu’à 6 milliards d’euros par an.
Paris soutient le projet. Le Premier ministre irlandais Micheál Martin y voit un frein à la compétitivité européenne. Comme l’adoption de cette nouvelle recette exige l’unanimité des Vingt-Sept, un seul vote contre suffirait à la bloquer. Costa espère un accord sur la directive en 2027.
Ce que la taxe prélèverait sur une vente Amazon
La proposition de texte du 21 novembre retient un taux de 3% du chiffre d’affaires net annuel tiré de la publicité en ligne, de l’intermédiation sur les plateformes et de la monétisation des données des utilisateurs. Seraient concernés les groupes, européens ou étrangers, qui dépassent à la fois 750 millions d’euros de chiffre d’affaires mondial et 50 millions d’euros de recettes numériques dans l’UE sur un an.
Prenons un exemple. Si Amazon touche 15 euros de commission hors TVA sur un casque audio à 100 euros vendu par un commerçant, la plateforme devrait 45 centimes de taxe sur cette commission, même si la vente lui coûte de l’argent.
En France, la facture a déjà bougé
Google Ads ajoute déjà un supplément de 2% aux annonces diffusées en France pour couvrir une partie de ses coûts liés à la taxe nationale sur les services numériques. Une entreprise qui dépense 1 000 euros en publicité paie donc 20 euros hors TVA de plus. Le 1er janvier 2027, Google portera ce supplément à 3%, soit 30 euros hors TVA pour la même campagne.
Dans une étude publiée en mai 2026, Dominika Langenmayr et Rohit Reddy Muddasani ont comparé le prix des mêmes articles vendus directement par Amazon ou par des commerçants qui lui confiaient leurs expéditions. Après l’instauration de la taxe française, les prix de ces vendeurs tiers ont augmenté d’environ 2% par rapport à ceux d’Amazon. Les auteurs estiment le surcoût à 35 centimes hors TVA pour un produit représentatif de l’échantillon français.
En Italie, où Amazon a moins relevé ses frais, les mêmes chercheurs ont mesuré un effet proche de zéro sur les prix. Quoi qu’il en soit, si cette taxe voit le jour, les géants américains pourraient bien en répercuter le surcoût sur les vendeurs européens et les consommateurs. Une addition qui finirait, une fois encore, dans le panier de ces derniers.

articles.title: Google Pixel 10a vs Pixel 9a — here's why I'd choose the older model (if the price is right)
articles.text:
I've used both the Google Pixel 10a and Pixel 9a — if the price is right, I'd choose the older model this Black Friday
The Pixel 10a is newer, but its upgrades are few and far between
With their Pro-rivaling software, impressive main cameras, and affordable price tags, Google's A-series Pixel phones have always offered discerning Android fans great value for money.
If you're in the market for a new Android phone that won’t break the bank, these colorful devices should be top of your list. And historically, I would have simply recommended the latest A series model and sent you on your way.
But in 2026, it's not that simple. The latest A-series Pixel is the Google Pixel 10a, and it’s a very good phone with a refined design, great color choices, a sharp screen, excellent cameras, and decent performance with long software support.
The problem with the Pixel 10a is that the Google Pixel 9a exists, costs less, and is virtually an identical device. Though the 9a is a little harder to find now as stock levels deplete, if you can find one, it’s a better buy than the 10a this Black Friday. I’ll explain why.
I’ve used both the Pixel 9a and Pixel 10a extensively, as I reviewed both devices at their respective launches in 2025 and 2026, and the honest truth is I cannot tell the difference between the two phones in everyday use.
That’s partly because their designs are almost identical. The 10a manages to have absolutely no camera bump at all, with the camera glass sitting flush with the back of the phone. The 9a is also all but bump-less, apart from a very small lip. Otherwise, these are the plainest Pixels going — they both lack the distinctive ‘camera bar’ design of pricier Pixels like the Pixel 10 Pro and Pixel 11 Pro.
The camera on the 10a is not better than that of the 9a. That’s because the hardware specs are 100% the same, with 48MP main, 13MP ultra-wide, and 13MP selfie lenses offered on both phones. Google uses the same photo processing too, so results are indistinguishable and, thankfully, excellent. The Pixel 11 Pro XL I’ve also tested doesn’t take significantly better photos to justify the enormous extra expense.
Sign up for breaking news, reviews, opinion, top tech deals, and more.
The 6.3-inch OLED screen on the 9a and 10a is also identical, as is the not-loads-but-enough 8GB RAM under the hood. Both phones are IP68 water- and dust-resistant too, and both have the same 5,100mAh battery.
There are vanishingly few reasons to spend more on the Pixel 10a — but the real crux here is that both phones have the Google Tensor G4 chipset.
For the Pixel 6a, 7a, 8a, and 9a, Google opted to use the same Tensor chipset as the more expensive Pixel 6, 7, 8, and 9, respectively. This alone made the A series great value, as you were getting the same processor as much more expensive, current-generation Pixel phones.
Indeed, the Pixel 9a has the same Tensor G4 chipset as the Pixel 9 and Pixel 9 Pro, but for some reason, Google decided not to give the Pixel 10a the Tensor G5 from the rest of the Pixel 10 lineup. This doesn’t make the Pixel 10a a bad phone; it just amplifies how good a deal the Pixel 9a is when it's available at a discount.
The Pixel 9a cost $499 / £499 / AU$849 at launch in April 2025, but is often heavily discounted. The Pixel 10a cost the same as the 9a at launch, but Google recently raised its MSRP to $599 / £599 / AU$949.
At full price, it’s worth saving $100 / £100 / AU$100 and getting the 9a. Although the 10a has slightly faster 30W wired charging compared to the 9a’s 23W, this is not, in my opinion, enough to warrant the extra spend.
Then again, as I write this, the Pixel 10a is on sale in the UK at Argos, Currys, John Lewis and Amazon for £349, and on sale at Amazon in the US for $549. These are very good prices, and if they're the same as the 9a's current price in your region, it’s better to opt for the newer phone. But only if the price is right.
The Pixel 10a also has Gorilla Glass 7i on its display, which is supposedly more durable than the Glass 3 on the 9a, and the newer phone also benefits from receiving seven years of software updates from launch in 2026. That'll mean it remains supported until 2033, while the 9a's seven-year update commitment will take it to 2032.
Still, bought in 2026 or 2027, the Pixel 9a will continue to receive updates for five or six years, which is better than many Android phones costing the same price (or more).
The Pixel 10a is a great phone in a vacuum, but the phone market in 2026 is anything but a vacuum. Prices are on the rise, and the newest A-series Pixel is one of the smallest ever year-on-year upgrades over its predecessor.
This makes the Pixel 9a on sale a stellar and genuine bargain — if you buy one, rest easy in the knowledge that you’re not missing out by going for the previous generation. It’s one of the smartest Android moves right now, if I do say so myself.

Henry is a freelance technology journalist with more than a decade of experience in the industry. Formerly Deputy Tech Editor at the Daily Express, he has also held senior positions at Tech Advisor, and has reviewed countless smartphones over the years, obsessing over screens, battery life, and camera smarts. articles.title: Cómo activar en WhatsApp el modo GTA 6 en 3 pasos: rápido y muy fácil
articles.text:
WhatsApp permite modificar la apariencia y experiencia en la aplicación móvil según el estilo visual de Grand Theft Auto VI (GTA 6). Por ejemplo, los usuarios pueden cambiar el fondos de pantalla, interactuar con Meta AI para consultar información del juego, entre otras acciones.
Cabe señalar que el modo GTA 6 en WhatsApp se activa de manera manual y es decisión de cada usuario optar por hacerlo.
Cómo cambiar el fondo de pantalla en WhatsApp
Para cambiar el fondo de pantalla en WhatsApp en el modo GTA 6, el primer paso es descargar una imagen referente al videojuego. Puede ser de Pinterest o directamente de Rockstar Games.
Una vez se haya verificado que la imagen fue guardada en la galería del celular, el siguiente paso es abrir la aplicación de WhatsApp y considerar este proceso:
- Ir a Ajustes.
- Seleccionar Apariencias y luego Estilo predeterminado del chat.
- Escoger Fondo y luego la opción de Fotos.
- Buscar en la galería la foto descargada de GTA.
- Ajustar tamaño y guardar los cambios.
Asimismo, los usuarios pueden cambiar el color de las burbujas de texto que se incorporan en los chats para que combinen mejor con la imagen seleccionada.
Cómo interactuar con Meta AI en el modo GTA 6 en WhatsApp
Para interactuar con Meta AI en el modo GTA 6 en WhatsApp es necesario elegir la opción de este asistente de inteligencia artificial disponible en los chats, tanto en en la app como en la versión web.
Luego iniciar una conversación con Meta AI y realizar consultas referentes al juego. Por ejemplo:
- ¿En qué ciudades transcurre GTA 6?
- ¿Quiénes son los protagonistas de GTA 6?
- ¿Qué se sabe de la historia de GTA 6?
- ¿GTA 6 está disponible para PS5?
- ¿GTA 6 llega a Xbox Series X y Series S?
- ¿GTA 6 tiene una versión para PC?
- ¿Qué vehículos aparecen en GTA 6?
- ¿Hay aviones y helicópteros en GTA 6?
- ¿Qué actividades se pueden realizar fuera de las misiones principales?
- ¿GTA 6 tiene modo multijugador?
- ¿Se puede jugar con dos personajes principales?
- ¿Qué novedades tiene el mapa de GTA 6?
- ¿Hay animales en GTA 6?
- ¿Qué negocios se pueden administrar en GTA 6?
- ¿Qué armas están disponibles en GTA 6?
- ¿GTA 6 incluye misiones secundarias?
- ¿Qué diferencias hay entre GTA 6 y GTA V?
- ¿Cuánto espacio necesita GTA 6 para instalarse?
Cómo seguir el canal de Rockstar Games en WhatsApp
Para seguir el canal de Rockstar Games en WhatsApp y así acceder a novedades y contenido exclusivo de primera mano, basta con ingresar a la plataforma e ir al apartado de Canales.
Allí se debe ingresar “Rockstar Games” y seleccionar la opción señalizada con una verificación.
Rockstar Games comparte información relacionada con la banda sonora del juego, alertas sobre eventos especiales, entre otras actualizaciones.
GTA 6: precios y dónde está disponible
Grand Theft Auto VI está disponible para PlayStation 5 y Xbox Series X|S desde el 19 de noviembre de 2026. Rockstar Games no anunció una versión para PC, PlayStation 4, Xbox One ni Nintendo Switch, por lo que el juego solo se puede adquirir y jugar en las consolas de actual generación de Sony y Microsoft.
El precio de referencia en Estados Unidos para la edición estándar es de USD 79,99, mientras que la Ultimate Edition cuesta USD 99,99.
Esta última incorpora contenido adicional, como vehículos, armas, indumentaria, variantes de armamento y otros elementos distribuidos a lo largo de la historia de Jason y Lucia.
Los valores finales pueden cambiar según el país, la tienda digital, los impuestos aplicados y el tipo de cambio.
La compra digital está disponible en PlayStation Store y Microsoft Store. También puede conseguirse en Rockstar Store y en comercios seleccionados, dependiendo de la región. La versión física incluye un código para descargar el juego: no contiene disco.

articles.title: Most Wanted: The Phishing Kits and Techniques Getting Past Security Controls
articles.text:
Every phishing attack has to get past email security, web filtering, and safe browsing before it reaches an employee. Some kits manage that far more often than others, and those are the kits that security teams need to know about.
At Push Security, we measure this as breakthrough rate: The share of attacks that get past email security, web gateways, and safe browsing to reach the user.
How an attack breaks through
Every browser-based attack starts with a lure, and each control in its path sees only part of the attack:
- Email security: Half of the attacks we see never touch email. The lure arrives through a search ad, a chat message, social media, a calendar invite, or a QR code. The rest come from trusted senders and services, so they pass reputation checks.
- Web gateways: The pages sit on trusted hosting and are assembled in the browser. The domains rotate every few days, so reputation data lags behind them.
- Safe browsing and scanners: Bot checks and cloaking show scanners a harmless page. A new domain isn't on any blocklist yet.
| How a phishing attack gets past email, URL, DNS, web gateway, and scanner controls before it reaches the user in the browser. | 
When the page loads in the user's browser and the user interacts with it, that's a breakthrough. Breakthrough rate counts those attacks, not attempts.
This changes how to read upstream data. A kit with a high breakthrough rate is one that upstream controls are missing. A low count in email or proxy logs doesn't prove that a kit is rare, because the kit may be getting past those controls without a trace.
Our upcoming webinar reveals the five kits with the highest breakthrough rates. Here's an early look at the number one kit.
Save your spot for the webinar
DOMDIFFER: Google's real sign-in page, mirrored from the attacker's browser
From August to October 2026, one kit ranked first by breakthrough rate every month. DOMDIFFER, an AiTM phishing kit that targets corporate Google and Microsoft accounts, broke through 2-4x as often as the next kit each month. DOM mirroring, the mechanism it uses under the hood, also happens to be the newest and fastest-growing way for a kit to relay a sign-in.
We first saw DOMDIFFER in February 2026. DOMDIFFER is our name for the kit (it hasn't yet been linked to a known phishing-as-a-service brand). We believe it grew out of NakedPages, a reverse proxy kit, and the two kits share infrastructure in several places. DOMDIFFER went quiet in the spring, came back over the summer, and has held the top rating since August. Most of its detections in that time came from fake calendar event lures.
| New hostnames per month for three NakedPages variants and DOMDIFFER, from our threat intelligence. | 
One real DOMDIFFER attack starts with a fake Google Voice notification about a new voicemail.
| The lure for one DOMDIFFER attack: A fake Google Voice voicemail notification. | 
The link passes a bot check that turns scanners away. The victim then sees what looks exactly like Google's sign-in page. It isn't a screenshot or a static copy. It's Google's real page, mirrored from the attacker's browser.
| Google's sign-in page, mirrored from the attacker's browser by DOMDIFFER. | 
On the surface, this looks like fairly standard phishing: A notification lure, a bot check gate, then a sign-in page. What makes DOMDIFFER particularly effective lies beneath the surface.
TL;DR: DOM mirroring
AiTM kits relay a sign-in in one of four ways: Reverse proxy, replica page, pixel streaming, and DOM mirroring. In DOM mirroring, the attacker's own browser does the real sign-in. It sends the page's structure (the DOM) to the victim's browser, which rebuilds a working copy. Because a real browser does the sign-in, the kit sends Google genuine browser signals and handles new sign-in steps without needing extra code.
Replica pages are still the most common class, but DOM mirroring is the newest and the fastest growing in 2026. Laurseraph, the main criminal pixel-streaming kit, has switched to DOM mirroring, and kits such as BlueKit and PhantomDOM use it too.
| How common each AiTM class is today, with example kits for each. | 
| What the victim's browser gets in each AiTM class, and what relays the sign-in. Orange lines mark an attacker's browser in the middle. | 
Our research post, From reverse proxies to DOM mirroring, explains the four classes in detail.
Under the hood
DOM mirroring is only part of why DOMDIFFER breaks through security controls. The rest comes from how the kit reaches its victims and stays out of sight of the controls along the way. In the webinar on December 2, Luke will take apart DOMDIFFER and the other four kits in the top five. He'll show how each one works under the hood, and the tricks that get them past controls more often than other kits.
Why controls fall short
Passkeys are worth rolling out, and they stop AiTM phishing where they're enforced. But AiTM is now one payload among several, and attackers are getting creative with how they combine them.
Kits use AiTM interchangeably with payloads that passkeys don't touch. In authorization attacks such as device code phishing, the victim signs in on Microsoft's real page and grants the attacker access. Other kits skip the sign-in page altogether and trick the victim into installing a remote access tool instead.
Kits pick the payload to match the visitor. A Windows visitor might get a remote access tool, a Microsoft account device code phishing, and a Google account AiTM. Some lures now carry two kits at once, so closing one path leaves another open.
Each of these gaps ends the same way: A page loads in the browser, and a user acts on it. In the webinar, Luke will show attackers use these tricks in real attacks.
What the webinar reveals
DOMDIFFER is one of five kits that broke through most often from August to October. On December 2, Luke Jennings will reveal the other four in a live threat briefing. Join the webinar to see:
- The other four kits in the top five, and the techniques behind each one
- How DOMDIFFER works under the hood, and the tricks that get it past controls
- Real attacks from the top kits, from the lure to the stolen session
- How kits now choose the payload to match the visitor's platform
- Which techniques and kits should be on your radar heading into 2027
If you can't make it, register anyway and you'll get a copy of the recording.

articles.title: Lasers, intercepteurs, canon de 20 mm… la France muscle fort sa lutte anti-drones
articles.text:
Le ministère des Armées intègre officiellement la lutte anti-drones au pacte drones aériens de défense. Les start-up comme les grands groupes y sont conviés, avec à la clé une meilleure visibilité sur ce dont les armées ont besoin.
Le ministère des Armées et des Anciens combattants a annoncé ce jeudi 26 novembre l'intégration de la lutte anti-drones (LAD) au pacte drones aériens de défense, une initiative de la Direction générale de l'armement (DGA). La ministre déléguée Alice Rufo a officialisé cette extension la veille, chez le spécialiste franco-italien du semi-conducteur, STMicroelectronics, à Montrouge, devant plus de 150 industriels et représentants du ministère. Des programmes d'armement, des solutions réactives et divers projets innovants sont d'ores et déjà déjà engagés, allant des drones intercepteurs aux armes laser.
Pourquoi le pacte drones aériens s'ouvre à la lutte anti-drones
Alice Rufo le dit, « nous ne pouvons pas penser séparément le développement de nos capacités drones et celui des moyens destinés à les neutraliser. » Jusqu'ici, le pacte se concentrait sur les drones aériens. Il s'ouvre désormais à ceux qui savent les clouer au sol, car le ministère des Armées mise sur les synergies entre les deux domaines. Après tout, mieux vaut bien connaître l'engin que l'on traque.
Concrètement, ce pacte fait office de dialogue entre l'État et les industriels. Les armées disent ce dont elles ont besoin, les entreprises ce qu'elles savent faire, et tous définissent ensemble les technologies clés. La méthode a déjà porté ses fruits. Souvenez-vous, en février, son premier bilan affichait 1 000 drones livrés en moins d'un an par le Français Harmattan AI, pour moins de 1 000 euros pièce, avant une nouvelle commande de 5 000 appareils.
Aux commandes du pacte drones aériens de défense, on trouve la Direction générale de l'armement (DGA), le premier acheteur de l'État. Elle est épaulée par le GICAT, qui fédère plus de 500 entreprises de la défense terrestre et dont le président était à Montrouge. L'état-major, les trois armées et d'autres ministères complètent la table. Tous ont pour but d'offrir à la France un tissu solide d'entreprises capables de concevoir et de produire ces équipements, ce que les militaires appellent la base industrielle et technologique de défense (BITD), au service des armées françaises, comme des alliées.
Alors pourquoi maintenant ? Il y a évidemment l'évidence de la guerre qui frappe aux portes de l'Europe. Comme l'ont montré les conflits récents en Ukraine et au Moyen-Orient, la lutte anti-drones est devenue un enjeu opérationnel majeur pour les trois armées, rappelle le ministère. La menace pèse autant sur les opérations extérieures que sur le territoire national. La rade de Toulon en a fait l'expérience après avoir constaté, entre le 9 et le 13 octobre, que des drones non autorisés avaient survolé de nuit la base navale, un site de la DGA et le 54e régiment d'artillerie d'Hyères. On rappelle que malgré le brouillage, aucun des petits aéronefs ne fut récupéré.
Du laser au canon de 20 mm, l'arsenal anti-drones prend forme
La DGA mène déjà deux programmes d'armement. PARADE est un dispositif de protection anti-drones modulaire, que l'on déploie là où il faut, tandis que MILAD regroupe des moyens mobiles de lutte anti-drones. Elle compte aussi une solution réactive, LADAC, dédiée à la lutte anti-drone depuis les avions de combat. Les forces disposent de leurs propres solutions réactives, du VAB ARLAD à Proteus, un canon de 20 mm monté sur camion. Enfin, l'Agence de l'innovation de défense (AID) porte le projet de drones intercepteurs ELISA et soutient le développement des armes laser.
Le cadre se veut ouvert à tous, « de la start-up au grand groupe », pour embrasser un paysage industriel foisonnant, aux solutions plus ou moins mûres. Le vivier tricolore est de plus en plus séduisant, puisqu'au début du mois de novembre, la start-up française Alta Ares a remporté six des seize lots du contrat-cadre anti-drone de l'OTAN. Les industriels gagneront aussi en visibilité sur les besoins des armées et sur les modes de contractualisation. Les militaires, eux, auront un poste d'observation privilégié sur les dernières capacités technologiques.
Ce nouveau volet prendra la forme d'un forum, un espace d'échange régulier où se retrouveront des experts de la DGA, des militaires et des industriels, pour ajuster au fil du temps les besoins des armées et les technologies à développer. Les solutions y seront testées en continu avec le Centre expert référent lutte anti-drones (CeRLAD), le centre d'expertise qui évalue les équipements anti-drones, et qui a prouvé pendant le conflit au Moyen-Orient qu'il savait le faire vite. Il y a évidemment la question des moyens. En juillet, un rapport sénatorial relevait qu'aucun financement n'était prévu pour la lutte anti-drones dans SAFE, le dispositif d'emprunt européen commun dont la France a obtenu 15,1 milliards d'euros pour sa défense. Pour que « l'épée et le bouclier » puissent vraiment « avancer ensemble », il faudra aussi de quoi forger ce fameux bouclier.

articles.title: The best Black Friday soldering iron deals for hobbyists and makers right now — limited-time sale discounts on digital irons, premium solder, and heat-proof accessories
articles.text:
The best Black Friday soldering iron deals for hobbyists and makers right now — limited-time sale discounts on digital irons, premium solder, and heat-proof accessories
The ultimate kit list for a hobbyist looking for upgrades
Soldering is a skill that every hobbyist should master. It doesn't matter whether you're taking your first steps or you're a seasoned pro, because you're going to need an essential bit of kit: a soldering iron.
Luckily, we've put together a good selection of soldering iron deals that are on sale for Black Friday. This is the perfect chance to grab the bull by the horns and upgrade with an iron that will last you through plenty of hefty projects. We've also got recommendations for solder, as well as kit to keep your workbench safe from fumes and heat.
Check out the full list of suggestions below.
Quick Links
Take your soldering with you with the Fnirsi HS-01
The Fnirsi HS-01 is a great soldering iron for anyone who travels or who needs a soldering iron on the go, as our review makes clear.
It's USB-C with an included power supply, or you can use it with a power bank capable of 65W output. It's good for easy soldering, eliminating the need to search for a DC jack or outlet. The flexibility of both a DC and USB-C jack is nice to have, although with so many USB-C PD power banks on sale now, it's a luxury, not a necessity.
The Fnirsi HS-01 is a great soldering iron and well worth the money for those who solder in workshops or in the field.
Read moreRead less▼
This kit comes with the soldering iron, but there's also a 96W power supply, a high-quality USB-C cable, a stand, and a selection of soldering iron tips for precision soldering, along with larger tips for when you need to lay down the heat.
Controlling the Fnirsi HS-01 is all about the buttons, which let you control the temperature, as well as navigate the built-in OLED screen. Set your temperature, and the HS-01 will get up to the target temperature in seconds. It's also designed to let you switch holding positions if you're right or left-handed.
Hunker down for a long day of soldering with the Yihua 995D+
Every serious soldering hobbyist needs a desktop soldering station with hot air rework to take things to the next level. The Yihua 995D+ hot air rework station delivers just that, and it's a solid soldering station that will get the job done.
A great selection of soldering tips, a large LCD screen, clear controls and a bonus hot air rework wand make the Yihua 995D+ the best option for those who solder for a living.
Read moreRead less▼
The Yihua 995D+ can reach temperatures of 480 °C (896 °F), which gives more than enough heat to solder and reflow even the heaviest solder joint. This soldering station has excellent thermal properties, letting you start soldering speaker wire with ease.
The stand is compatible with right and left-handed users, as it's separated from the main station, so you'll have free access to the soldering iron while reducing the number of cables trailing across your workbench. It has three preset channels to let you switch between jobs quickly, and it feels great to handle, thanks to a non-slip coating and flexible silicone cord to stop any melting accidents. You've also got a good number of tips, from precision tips to heavy tips for large projects.
The hot air gun has a similar cable for protection and is easy to handle. You'll need to select the correct controls before using the central knob to handle temperature and airflow. After that, it's easy to control both.
The Yihua 995D+ is an excellent soldering station for both beginners and pros alike. It gets the job done, looks good, and keeps more cash in your pocket.
Don't need hot air but need a desktop soldering station? The Yihua 939D+ is for you.
If all you need is a reliable and compact desktop soldering station, then the Yihua 939D+ is a good option. This compact soldering station comes with a temperature range of 392°F to 896°F (200°C to 480°C) and ships with a selection of soldering tips to cover many different use cases, from precision to bulky solder joints.
A solid and dependable soldering station that reduces the cost by omitting hot air rework functionality. This is a soldering station that I could personally use all day, everyday!
Read moreRead less▼
It comes with 75W of power, making it suitable for heavier solders like speaker cables. Use the dial to control your settings and the LED display will update accordingly.
Helping hands for successful soldering
Soldering can be a tricky task to complete, and an extra pair of hands is always welcome. Luckily, you don't need a pair of human hands to get the job done, as this helping hands tool can substitute perfectly.
Soldering veterans will know the less-than-glossy metal armature and magnifying glass combos that are available, but this set of helping hands is a little bit different. It comes as a magnetic base, clips, and posts that help to grip your circuit boards as you solder.
With five alligator clips and six posts designed to hold your PCB firmly to the magnetic base, your hands are free to concentrate on soldering up your next project.
Read moreRead less▼
Measuring 11.41 x 7.08 inches (29 x 18 cm), this magnetic helping hands kit is sturdy for holding your PCBs while giving you a choice as to how it holds them. The five flexible alligator clips are used to clamp and hold circuit boards a little nearer to the user. The flexibility of the armatures means that both sides of the PCB can be seen, remaining accessible for soldering either way.
If you need more rigidity, the six posts are used to clamp to the edge of the board you're soldering, which is useful if you're soldering just one side. This is ideal for a maker with plenty of tasks on his sheet.
Keep soldering on, with lead-free and leaded solder.
You'll want lead-free solder if you're planning on soldering. It's the gold standard, it's safer, and it avoids the environmental issues that come with traditional leaded solder.
Lead-free solder is the gold standard these days. Any modern electronics will have components soldered using lead-free solder. It's safer than traditional leaded, and avoids the environmental issues, such as lead leakage during bad disposal. It's the safest option if you're planning on making anything you go on to sell, too.
Lead-free solder is better for the environment, and it means you can build and sell products that are made using it.
This 0.6mm diameter solder has a flux rosin core so it flows neatly around your solder joints.
Read moreRead less▼
That said, there's still a case for leaded solder, especially if you're using it for yourself (and you take precautions).
The solder below is worth considering if you need it. It's a mix of 63% tin to 37% lead, which is a decent mix, and should produce good solder joints.
Lead solder is still great for personal use, and this 0.8mm rosin core 63/38 tin / lead mix will melt great and produce shiny and reliable solder joints.
Read moreRead less▼
Keep your workbench safe from hot soldering irons
Every maker is going to have a workbench that has seen one or two accidents. If you want to avoid any permanent damage, you'll want to pick up one of these sillicone soldering mats.
This silicone repair mat will keep your workbench free from scratches and soldering iron burns. The included magnetic notches and slots will make sure every screw goes back in at the end.
Read moreRead less▼
Silicone soldering mats are an essential buy for a hobbyist. They'll keep the heat from your soldering iron away from the workbench, and often have extra positions to keep screws in one place and to stop magnetics from falling off your bench.
Good for taking apart a laptop, for instance. It'll keep your screws safe, the bench burn-free, and it'll help you from scratching the chassis, too. When you're done, you can just roll it up and put it away.
Stay safe soldering with a fume extractor
Lead-free or not, you're going to see fumes when you're soldering. It isn't a great idea to breathe these in, so a fume extractor can help you to improve the air quality around you as you work.
Keep your lungs healthy by removing the flux fumes and solder smoke from the air. This tiltable solder fume extractor works from up to five inches away and pulls the offensive fumes through an activated carbon filter to keep the air fresh. You get extra filters in the box
Read moreRead less▼
Extractors work, as you'd expect, by using a fan to suck smoke and fumes from the air, directly into an activated carbon filter, with clean air passing through the back of it. This extractor uses a high-speed fan to do it, keeping high suction from up to five inches away: plenty of space for you to solder in comfort.
This extractor comes with four rubber feet, so it won't move around, and the locking tilt mechanism helps you point it to the right places as you work. It also has fenders on both sides of the fan to stop any breezes from moving fumes away from the unit, as it keeps you safe.

articles.title: Japan is packing chipmaking labs into trucks — mobileFab set to travel the country, drumming up interest in hardware careers
articles.text:
Japan is packing chipmaking labs into trucks — mobileFab set to travel the country, drumming up interest in hardware careers
Japan's answer to a 43,000-worker chip talent gap
- Japan's Minimal Fab Promotion Organization debuts mobileFab, a truck-mounted container with three photolithography tools
- The tools are about 30 cm wide, process 12.5 mm wafers without a cleanroom, and add wiring to wafers AIST has already taken to the transistor stage
- No fleet size, route, cost, or funding has been disclosed, and similar mobile fabs are emerging at Purdue and US startup InchFab
Japan has been trying to rebuild its chip industry since 2022, with about ¥10 trillion in public funding now secured, according to the 2026 policy proposal from the Japan Electronics and Information Technology Industries Association (JEITA).
One of the least glamorous yet overbearing obstacles is people: Japan does not have enough engineers who have actually run a fab tool, and an industry group in Tsukuba now thinks part of the answer is to put the tools on the back of a truck.
The Minimal Fab Promotion Organization is due to unveil mobileFab, a shipping container fitted with three ultra-compact chipmaking machines, at SEMICON Japan 2026.
Bringing the fab to students: what actually in the box?
The group's press release pitches it as an inversion of the usual training model: instead of sending students to a semiconductor plant, the plant comes to them. This can be seen as a delayed response to a decade-long engineer shortage, a framing that the organizers are also embracing.
The organization is not a government body, however; It is a general incorporated association of equipment, materials and parts makers and device users, formed in 2017 by merging research programs that began at the state-backed National Institute of Advanced Industrial Science and Technology (AIST) in 2010, according to MONOist.
The container holds a resist coater, a maskless exposure tool, and a developer, the three machines needed for photolithography, the step that prints circuit patterns onto silicon. Each is about 30 cm wide. Each is about 30 cm wide. AIST researchers specified the standard tool footprint as 294 mm wide, 450 mm deep, and 1,440 mm tall, so these probably resemble vending machines rather than desktop gadgets in terms of actual volume.
Minimal Fab wafers are half-inch disks, 12.5 mm across, processed one at a time; A standard 300 mm wafer has roughly 576 times the surface area for context. The tiny format lets the system skip the cleanroom: wafers move between tools in sealed shuttles, and each machine maintains its own local clean environment rather than relying on a building-scale one.
Sign up to the TechRadar Pro newsletter to get all the top news, opinion, features and guidance your business needs to succeed!
The tech itself isn't new, but that is the point: Yokogawa, a core member of the organization and its first certified operator, claims the approach cuts capital investment to about 1/1000 of a conventional fab, and it has built a small integrated circuit of roughly 1,000 transistors on Minimal Fab tools under contract with JAXA.
The container handles lithography only. Under the program the organization describes, AIST's Tokyo Waterfront center first processes wafers through transistor formation, then ships them to schools. There, students use mobileFab to pattern wiring before etching and testing the results on site. The upshot is that a student can design, build, and measure a working circuit without the school owning a front-end line.
The model is borrowed from schools already doing this with fixed installations: The release points to Kumamoto Prefectural Technical Junior College, where students design integrated circuits that AIST takes to the transistor stage before returning them for wiring and electrical testing.
Sasebo National College of Technology in Nagasaki runs four Minimal Fab tools and a year-long, cross-departmental curriculum, and in March 2026it formally opened S-PORT, a semiconductor training center meant to serve as the hub for all 51 of Japan's national technical colleges. AIST's Toru Hayakawa told MONOist in 2024 that educational adoption, including Sasebo, was growing.
The organizers justify the project with a familiar number. Citing JEITA, the release says Japan's nine largest chipmakers alone will need about 43,000 semiconductor workers over the next ten years, a figure JEITA's policy proposal calls a shortfall.
That number has crept upward. In 2022, JEITA put the need at roughly 35,000 engineers across eight companies, when Hideki Wakabayashi, who led its policy task force, told the Financial Times that "the biggest shortage is engineers," as reported by E&T. A year later, it was 40,000 across eight firms, including Kioxia, Renesas, Sony and Toshiba, per EE Times Japan.
Not the only mobile fab play globally
The drivable fab has arrived in several places at once: Purdue University's electrical engineering school unveiled its own Mobile Fab in October 2026, a roughly 100 sq ft truck-based lab with LED lithography and a sputter coater that the school estimates could be reproduced for about $500,000, against roughly $2 million for a comparable cleanroom.
"Lithography can seem very abstract until you see the process happen," said PhD student Yusuf Adebakin. US startup InchFab is building container-sized fabs costing $5 million to $15 million and selling workforce training alongside them, while Carnegie Mellon's Hacker Fab has published an open source DLP stepper that resolves features under 2 microns.
The pressure behind all of them is similar. A SEMI Foundation analysis suggests the US could be short as many as 157,000 semiconductor and microelectronics workers by 2030, and TSMC previously pushed back its first Arizona fab over a lack of skilled installation workers. The cleanroom remains the big barrier to teaching any of this, so much so that one YouTuber converted a backyard shed into one just to make memory cells.
What sets Japan's effort apart is maturity. Minimal Fab has a standardized tool format, a certification scheme, and more than a decade of process work behind it, and AIST spin-off Hundred Semiconductors is already trying to take the same tools into small-volume production. By contrast, most of the alternatives being discussed or explored are still prototypes at best.
One container running single half-inch wafers through a lithography cycle of 15 to 20 minutes is a teaching instrument, not a pipeline, however. The organization has not published a resolution figure for its exposure tool, but comparable DLP systems work at around the micron scale, orders of magnitude away from the 2nm-class process Rapidus is bringing up in Hokkaido. Students will learn process fundamentals, not how a leading-edge line runs.
The harder problem may be motivation rather than access here: Toshiba's Takashi Miyamori told Nikkei in 2022 that "most Japanese studying science subjects are more interested in IT," as relayed by EIS. A truck that lets a technical college student print a circuit pattern and test it the same afternoon is a reasonable bet against that preference, and a cheap one by industry standards.
Whether it shifts career choices at any meaningful scale depends on details the organization has yet to share: how many trucks, how often they visit, and who pays for the whole process.

Rahim Amir is a UAE-based tech writer who enjoys building PCs as much as he enjoys writing about them. He has been professionally writing about PC hardware since 2023, focusing on buyer’s guides, hardware reviews, and sponsored content and features related to tech.
Having built hundreds of gaming PCs and being an avid gamer in his spare time, Rahim tends to have stronger opinions about hardware than most. This is particularly on display when he gets his way with powerful, but minimalistic RGB builds even as Small Form Factor (SFF) PCs come a close second.

articles.title: Anthropic dejará crear e instalar apps para Windows y macOS desde Claude
articles.text:
Anthropic habilitó una función en beta llamada “Install as app” que permite crear, ejecutar y compartir aplicaciones de escritorio para Mac y Windows a partir de los artefactos generados en Claude, sin necesidad de escribir código.
La herramienta convierte una conversación con el asistente en un programa independiente, con ícono propio y ventana separada, que conserva la sesión del usuario sin pedir claves de API adicionales.
Cómo crear e instalar una app de escritorio con Claude
El proceso descrito por la compañía consta de tres pasos. Primero, el usuario describe a Claude qué aplicación quiere construir. Después, la prueba en su formato de artefacto, el modo en que Claude genera y ejecuta fragmentos de código dentro de la propia conversación.
Por último, para transformar ese artefacto en una aplicación instalable basta con hacer clic en la opción Install as app, disponible dentro del menú Compartir.
Según detalla Anthropic, la app resultante no requiere empaquetado ni firma digital, dos procesos técnicos habituales en el desarrollo tradicional de software de escritorio. Tampoco exige un inicio de sesión distinto, porque utiliza la cuenta de Claude del usuario.
Una de las características señaladas por la empresa es la actualización automática: cuando se edita el artefacto original, la aplicación instalada refleja esos cambios sin intervención adicional. Las apps creadas de esta forma también pueden enviar notificaciones al sistema y añadir elementos a la barra de menú en macOS o a la bandeja del sistema en Windows.
Apps de ejemplo creadas con la nueva función
Para mostrar el alcance de la herramienta, Anthropic publicó varias aplicaciones de demostración. Entre ellas figuran Linnet, un editor de imágenes por capas, y Phosphor, un gestor de archivos.
También incluyó Sift, pensado para organizar carpetas, Tern, una terminal que integra a Claude, y Vitals, un monitor de rendimiento del sistema.
La propia página del anuncio aclara que se trata de demostraciones y no de productos oficiales de Anthropic. El material se acompaña además de un video incrustado en YouTube que ilustra el funcionamiento de la función.
Permisos y niveles de acceso al sistema
Anthropic estableció tres niveles de permisos para regular qué puede hacer cada aplicación una vez instalada. El nivel predeterminado limita la app a las mismas capacidades que tendría dentro de un navegador web.
Un segundo nivel, denominado permisos de app, habilita funciones adicionales como ventanas que permanecen siempre encima de otras, atajos de teclado globales o el envío de notificaciones.
El tercer nivel, de acceso completo al equipo, resulta el más sensible: permite que la aplicación ejecute programas y lea, modifique o borre archivos del sistema sin solicitar autorización en cada caso.
La compañía precisa que estos permisos cubren únicamente la versión vigente de la app. Cada vez que se actualiza, incluso si la edición la realiza el propio usuario, Claude vuelve a pedir autorización.
Existe una excepción relevante: si una parte de la aplicación proviene de otro sitio web externo, ese componente puede modificarse sin que se genere una nueva consulta de permisos.
El acceso completo al equipo tiene además una restricción de origen. Solo puede otorgarse a apps creadas por el propio usuario o, en el caso de los planes Team y Enterprise, por otros miembros de la misma organización. Anthropic aclara que no revisa las apps antes de su instalación, por lo que recomienda conceder ese nivel de acceso únicamente a apps de confianza.
Disponibilidad por planes y limitaciones actuales
La función se encuentra en fase beta para todos los planes de Claude, con excepción de las organizaciones preparadas para cumplir con la normativa HIPAA y de los despliegues híbridos.
El comportamiento por defecto varía según el tipo de cuenta. En los planes Team, la función viene activada de entrada, aunque con el acceso completo al equipo desactivado. En Enterprise, en cambio, permanece apagada hasta que un propietario de la organización decide habilitarla.
Para funcionar, la herramienta requiere conexión a internet y sesión iniciada en Claude. Un punto que afecta directamente al uso cotidiano es que las peticiones que la app instalada realiza a Claude se descuentan de los límites de uso del plan contratado.
No todos los artefactos pueden convertirse en aplicaciones instalables. Anthropic excluyó de forma explícita a Claude Docs, Slides y Sheets de esta posibilidad.

Two Californian Nvidia AI chip customers are really Chinese-owned — companies used as workaround for government export controls
articles.text:
Two Californian Nvidia AI chip customers are really Chinese-owned — companies used as workaround for government export controls
One of the two companies is one of Nvidia's "preferred partners," while the other was renamed after its Chinese parent company was blackisted.
While Nvidia is only allowed to sell its most advanced AI chips to whitelisted companies, it appears that two of its Californian customers are actually fronts for Chinese companies. Further, one of the Californian companies was renamed after its Chinese parent company was blacklisted, CBS News reports. The other one, which is on Nvidia's list of "preferred partners," is owned by a Chinese firm whose CEO graduated from a Chinese military university. It's reported that U.S.-based, Chinese-owned companies have been used as a way to work around export controls designed to prevent Nvidia's chips from being sold wholesale to China. Chips are routinely sold to companies in the U.S. before being leased or shipped to other companies in Southeast Asia.
While Nvidia isn't allowed to sell its most capable AI chips to China, it can still do business with the country. It can sell graphics cards for use in personal gaming PCs as well as AI chips that don't use the company's latest, most capable technologies. But that hasn't stopped those chips from turning up in the most unlikely of places. Illegal Nvidia Blackwell Ultra B300 GPUs have been spotted in use inside China Telecom's network, and last year alone, it's believed that around $1 billion worth of Nvidia chips were smuggled into China. Earlier this year, nine people were indicted over the illegal export of Nvidia GPUs, while even older Nvidia hardware has seen huge price increases due to the unavailability of newer hardware.
Megaspeed is one company that is accused of facilitating the breaking of export controls. The company is under criminal investigation currently, and it was recently blacklisted as a result. The company also happens to be a former employer of Alice Huang, the woman whom Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang admitted to having an affair with when he resigned from the company earlier this month. Alice Huang is also believed to be a Chinese Spy, while her husband has even closer connections to a Chinese spy agency.
Back in the U.S., RiCloud AI is an Nvidia customer owned by Yuxing InfoTech Investment Holdings Limited, an outfit with headquarters in Shenzhen, China. Yuxing's CEO and co-owner, Cong Yu, reportedly has a degree in National Defense Mobilization from the People's Liberation Army Command College, a university operated by the Chinese military. Among RiCloud AI's customers is Agencia Comercial Spirits, a small whisky importer that pivoted to AI in 2025. Since then, it has committed to AI data center deals worth up to $598 million.
Airvres is currently listed as an "elite" partner on Nvidia's website, yet it was previously called Inspur, the same name used by its Chinese parent company. The name change came after Inspur-related firms were added to a federal blocklist in March 2023. Airvres reportedly exported at least $5.6 billion of chips to Southeast Asia between April 2024 and February 2026, including Nvidia's top-of-the-line Blackwell silicon. The chips went to two companies in Malaysia, one of which was Alice Huang's Megaspeed.
