articles.title: Drupal Warns of New Highly Critical Site Takeover Vulnerability Under Active Exploitation
articles.text:
Drupal has warned of a new "highly critical" security flaw impacting Drupal core that it said has been exploited in the wild.
The vulnerability, tracked as CVE-2026-136716 (CVSS score: N/A), has been described as a case of improper checking for unusual or exceptional conditions. It also relates to CVE-2026-132165 aka Fail2Install in that it addresses remaining vulnerable installation states that could still be abused to facilitate site takeover even after the fix.
CVE-2026-132165 "recently fixed several vulnerabilities within the Drupal core installer," Drupal maintainers said. "However, certain sites in unusual or incomplete install states remain vulnerable to site takeover following that advisory, including production sites."
"It is not apparent in the user interface if a site is in the affected vulnerable state, and sites that are already compromised may no longer be in the vulnerable state."
Drupal acknowledged that the vulnerability is being exploited in the wild, but emphasized that site owners who have already secured the installer ("install.php") are not impacted.
Specifically, any website that left its installer remotely accessible following the fix for CVE-2026-132165 may have been compromised. Drupal is urging site administrators to take the following actions -
- Check site logs for unauthorized access, including unexpected changes to or by the user 1 account
- Ensure the user 1 email address is set to under their control, and consider resetting user 1's password.
The issue has been remediated in the following versions -
- Drupal 11.4.x - Update to Drupal 11.4.14
- Drupal 11.3.x - Update to Drupal 11.3.23
- Drupal 10.6.x - Update to Drupal 10.6.23
- Drupal 11.0.x to 11.2.x - No fix (End-of-life)
- Drupal 10.5.x and below - No fix (End-of-life)
After updating to the latest supported versions, it's recommended to run "update.php" to fix existing production sites in this state and secure the Drupal installer on all new and existing sites.
According to statistics shared by StepSecurity, there are about 55,800 internet-facing Drupal sites as of November 26, 2026, out of which 31,500 services are running branches that are vulnerable to CVE-2026-132165 and roughly 15,000 are on the end-of-life 8 and 9 branches.

articles.title: Le Black Friday sourit aux gamers : la Nintendo Switch 2 avec batterie remplaçable descend à 429 € chez Amazon
articles.text:
Vous n’avez pas encore craqué pour la Nintendo Switch 2 ? Alors sachez que durant le Black Friday, Amazon propose la console au prix de 429 € au lieu de 499,99 € dans sa version avec batterie remplaçable.
Si vous attendiez une promotion pour passer à la nouvelle version de la console de Nintendo, cette offre du Black Friday peut vous intéresser : Amazon propose la Nintendo Switch 2 à 429 €, avec une remise de 14 % sur son prix conseillé de 499,99 €. La fiche du cybermarchand confirme bien qu’il s’agit de la version européenne qui autorise l’utilisateur à changer lui-même sa batterie. La boîte contient deux Joy-Con 2, une station d’accueil, une alimentation et un câble HDMI.
La Nintendo Switch 2 avec ses Joy-Con 2 et sa station d’accueil est disponible à 429 € chez Amazon pour le Black Friday.
Pourquoi choisir la Nintendo Switch 2 ?
- Pour sa polyvalence : vous pouvez démarrer une partie en mode portable, la continuer sur la TV du salon ou installer la console sur une table.
- Pour son écran plus grand : la dalle LCD tactile de 7,9 pouces affiche une définition Full HD, confortable pour jouer en déplacement.
- Pour sa batterie remplaçable : Nintendo anticipe l’entrée en vigueur des nouvelles règles européennes sur les batteries.
Du jeu portable au grand écran en un seul geste
La Nintendo Switch 2 peut être utilisée en permanence en mode portable, si vous désirez essentiellement jouer lors de vos déplacements. Néanmoins, pour jouer sur un téléviseur, il suffit d’y brancher la station d’accueil de la console. Dans ce mode, elle prend en charge une sortie allant jusqu’à la 4K à 60 images par seconde, ou jusqu’à 120 images par seconde en 1080p et 1440p, selon le jeu et l’écran utilisés.
Son support arrière réglable permet aussi de jouer sur une table avec les manettes détachées, ce qui peut s’avérer utile pour jouer à deux, ou pour utiliser l’un des Joy-Con comme souris dans certains titres. L’espace de stockage intégré monte à 256 Go et il est extensible à l’aide d’une carte microSD Express compatible.
Une évolution de la Switch qui mise encore sur le LCD
Plus performante que la Switch, la Switch 2 peut faire tourner des jeux plus exigeants, tout en restant rétrocompatible avec la plupart des jeux de la première console. Il est néanmoins dommage que Nintendo n’ait pas intégré d’écran OLED à sa nouvelle plateforme : le LCD de 7,9 pouces n’est pas toujours optimal pour les contrastes.
✅ Les points forts
- Trois usages : portable, sur table et sur téléviseur.
- Écran Full HD de 7,9 pouces.
- Station d’accueil et alimentation incluses.
❌ Les limites
- Écran LCD, sans technologie OLED.
- Extension du stockage des jeux nécessitant une carte microSD Express.
Amazon affiche cette Nintendo Switch 2 à 429 € au lieu de 499,99 €, et sa livraison est offerte.
Grâce à son énorme catalogue de jeux et ses Joy-Con précis, la Nintendo Switch 2 donne accès à de multiples expériences vidéoludiques, à la maison comme en déplacement. Le fait qu’il s’agisse du modèle avec batterie remplaçable est un vrai plus.
Si vous possédez déjà une Nintendo Switch, l’achat de la Switch 2 se justifie surtout si vous désirez découvrir son catalogue de titres inédits. Dans le cas contraire, vous pouvez retarder son achat, et encore plus si vous possédez une Switch OLED.

articles.title: RAM Altman might have come for your memory, but at least he can’t get his hands on OLED monitors this Black Friday
articles.text:
The only thing not affected by AI this Black Friday? Gaming monitors! Here's how to bag yourself a bargain
Have you thought about another screen?
Ok, I think we can all agree at the minute that, unless you hold a butt load of stock in one of the Magnificent 7 and enjoy the rigmarole of dubious day trading, or you've got quite the hefty pension fund sat in NASDAQ, the whole AI situation is kinda garbage, putting it lightly. Particularly if you're big into PC gaming, and are looking for a good deal this Black Friday (don't worry we're covering all the best deals right here).
The sad news is that right now, a big chunk of our hobby is insanely overpriced.
• Browse all today's best Black Friday deals
I've written extensively about how bad the situation is compared to 2025 on TechRadar already. How SSDs are basically double the cost, RAM is now 5x the amount it was two years ago, and DDR4 is suddenly back on the menu boys at nearly 3x what it was four years prior, (not to mention the hilarious $6,600 RTX 5090s).
That said, there is an albeit modest silver lining, and that comes in the form of peripherals. Particularly monitors.
Now, I know what many of you may be thinking. What's the point? I get it. It's a cruddy year for hardware, why even bother looking for PC deals, right? Well, after 11 years of doing this, gaming monitors, as far as I'm concerned, represent one of the biggest and most overlooked upgrades that you can make to your setup, and right now in 90% of cases, they're cheaper than they ever have been. Make sure you check out our roundup of the best Black Friday 2026 monitor deals — you could save yourself a fair bit of cash!
Why gaming monitors represent one of the best purchases you can make
To get somewhat philosophical. As far as I'm concerned, we can categorize PC hardware into three distinct roles. The first, performance drivers, are your GPUs, RAM, SSDs, CPUs... you know, those things that generate the frames and determine your overall experience.
The second are the enablers: your interconnects, motherboards, cases, PSUs, cooling (admittedly the latter does sort of straddle the first group a bit as well).
And the last one is your experientials, basically what you use to engage with whatever it is you're doing.
It's that last group that's often overlooked in terms of real potential, and particularly how much joy and satisfaction an upgrade here can give you. Keyboards obviously grant that tactile feel and feedback every time you hit a key switch. The mouse then determines how smooth your engagement is, while headphones and speakers drive such an emotive auditory stimulus it's hard to measure.
Yet more importantly than all of those combined is the humble monitor. It's that that has the biggest impact on your PC gaming experience. Because, to use a PC in this capacity, you're going to be staring at a screen, and you're going to be doing that for 100% of the duration that you're using it. You might not type, your APM might be low, your mouse movement paused, you could be sat on the desktop doing nothing, but by god your eyes are going to be fixed on that panel.
It's why a lot of journalists get obsessive over high refresh rates and beautifully color-accurate QD OLED panels for desktop work. Because the reality is it makes every OS you can imagine feel so much smoother and more enjoyable to use, even outside of gaming.
And, typically, it does that without necessarily needing a massively OP graphics card (although obviously the latter does help). Nothing gives you a more premium feel than being sat in Excel on one of the best 34-inch Ultrawide OLED panels, that's for sure.
OLED panels are now the cheapest they've ever been, and it gets even better
So why is now the best time to buy? Simply put, AI data centers don't need an abundance of monitors to operate, unlike the shipping containers full of DRAM, GPUs, and NAND, and that's a good thing for us, because production rates and development of this tech are continuing to improve rapidly, driving down prices.
We've seen some of the lowest price tags ever for OLED panels this year, across the myriad of Prime Days that Amazon has thrown our way seemingly every other month, with a whole host of 27-inch OLED 240 Hz monitors sitting around the $200-300 mark.
Why? Well, the brilliant thing here (aside from low demand from AI), is that there's not just one manufacturer producing the panels. Both Samsung Display and LG Display produce QD-OLED and WOLED gaming monitor panels, respectively. On top of that, we're actually getting two additional panel manufacturers joining the party as well, with TCL CSOT and BOE dipping their toes into the water too, either already producing them, or converting manufacturing lines over.
On top of that, production is increasing rapidly with the big two as well. And as we're seeing new, more exotic tech hit the market, in terms of 720 Hz refresh rates, RGB stripe QD-OLED, and Tandem OLED, these all drive down the prices of those older models, which are still exemplary to look at and use, particularly when gaming.
Combine that with a slew of secondary parties taking those panels and competing against each other for sales (Asus, MSI, AOC, ViewSonic and so on) and all of a sudden us consumers are finally on the receiving end of some good genuine capitalism for once.
It's not all sunshine and cheap monitors
There is one slight caveat to all that, however, and it does once again revolve around DRAM componentry.
Unfortunately, we are seeing some impact from memory chip demand hit monitors as well (as they do use memory in the construction). KTC, AOC, and Dell have all seen price adjustments this year to name a few, attributed to, you guessed it, data center demand. So there's a chance the pricing might not fall as fast as we'd like. But it is falling.
What should you be looking for?
A lot of this is going to depend on your use case. Namely, what graphics card you have, what games you play, what you do day-to-day. If you're an RTS or MMORPG nerd like me, I highly recommend a 34-inch ultrawide, at 3440x1440.
It's just enough pixel density to keep you sated but not enough to murder your GPU. 100 Hz plus is a must, ideally a WOLED panel, but grab what you can afford (it also makes any productivity work a dream, unless you're editing 4K footage). Something like Alienware's legendary AW3425DW is a good fit.
Do you play FPS games, or competitive multiplayer titles? I'd highly recommend any of the myriad of 240 Hz 27-inchers. Acer's Predator X27U W1 is at an insanely low $270 already, meaning that may shift even further on the run up to the big day.
If you either already own an RTX 5090 or have just splurged solid second hand car money on one, 32-inch 4K QD-OLED is the way to go. Samsung's Odyssey G81SF is up there with the best of them, albeit at a four-figure price tag to match (although I have seen it float around the $700 mark at times).
Honestly though, I can't stress enough the advantage of a 34-inch ultrawide for productivity work. If you spot one at a low price, with solid reviews, that's the first thing I'd be looking to sink my teeth into.
Below, you'll find the best Black Friday gaming monitor offers that our crack team of deal hunters have found so far:

Watch movies and TV shows, play games, or dive into productivity tasks like video editing with the AOC Q27G41ZE 1440p monitor. The 260Hz refresh rate, ensures unparalleled smoothness, no matter what activities you throw at this monitor.
The Samsung Odyssey is a great all-round gaming package. Its 1440p resolution renders your games in great detail, and its 178-degree viewing angles make it easier for friends to get in on the action.
The Gigabyte GO27Q24G W-OLED is a no-brainer purchase this Black Friday, with a 15% discount making it one of the cheapest OLEDs on Amazon. For only $297.49, you get to enjoy the premium OLED experience that produces the best black levels and up to 1,300 nits of peak brightness.

Despite that affordable price, it's rocking some astonishing gaming features you can enjoy in your downtime — including a lightning-fast 0.5ms response time and absurdly smooth 240Hz refresh rate.

articles.title: Stickers con sonido en WhatsApp sí tienen restricciones: qué no puedo hacer en Sound Stickers
articles.text:
WhatsApp sumó los stickers con sonido, pero la función no permite usar cualquier audio sin límites. La aplicación de mensajería habilita de forma gradual esta herramienta, conocida como Sound Stickers, que convierte imágenes estáticas y animadas en piezas capaces de reproducir voz, frases o efectos al tocarlas en el chat.
Aunque los mensajes viajan bajo cifrado de extremo a extremo y Meta no bloquea canciones comerciales de forma automática en conversaciones privadas, sí existen restricciones técnicas y de contenido que conviene conocer antes de crear un sticker sonoro.
Qué audios no se pueden usar en los stickers de WhatsApp
La primera limitación es la duración. El sistema rechaza los archivos completos que excedan el máximo permitido: diez segundos de audio para los stickers creados a partir de una imagen fija, y cinco segundos para los elaborados desde un video.
La música descargada dentro de aplicaciones de streaming tampoco funciona. No es posible importar canciones obtenidas directamente desde Spotify, Apple Music o YouTube Music, porque ese contenido está encriptado mediante sistemas de gestión de derechos digitales (DRM) y no aparece como un archivo local estándar en la carpeta de audio del teléfono.
A esto se suman los formatos incompatibles. Los archivos que no respondan a estándares soportados por el dispositivo (como MP3, AAC, M4A, WAV u OGG) quedan afuera, al igual que aquellos guardados únicamente en la nube sin una descarga previa al celular.
Existen además restricciones ligadas al contenido y a los derechos de autor. Si se crean o distribuyen paquetes públicos de stickers en tiendas o enlaces masivos con música o voces protegidas sin autorización, la plataforma puede eliminarlos tras recibir denuncias.
Y aunque los chats sean privados, si otro usuario reporta un sticker cuyo audio incluye acoso, discurso de odio, spam masivo o contenido ilegal, la cuenta puede quedar suspendida.
Qué tener en cuenta antes de agregar audio a un sticker
Más allá de lo que no se puede incorporar, hay opciones que sí están habilitadas sin inconvenientes. Las notas de voz grabadas en el momento desde el propio editor son válidas, al igual que el sonido original de videos grabados o descargados en el celular, siempre recortado al límite de cinco segundos.
También se pueden usar archivos locales guardados en el teléfono (efectos de sonido, memes o audios en formato MP3 o M4A) y la biblioteca de sonidos predeterminados que incluye el editor de WhatsApp, una alternativa pensada para quienes no cuentan con audio propio a mano.
Otro punto a considerar es la reproducción. Para evitar que las conversaciones se saturen de ruidos inesperados, el sonido está desactivado de manera predeterminada. Los stickers con audio se identifican por un pequeño ícono de altavoz silenciado sobre la imagen, y recién se escuchan cuando el destinatario los toca de forma deliberada. En el caso de las animaciones, el sonido puede repetirse hasta tres veces junto con el movimiento de la imagen.
La recepción de estos stickers no depende de tener la función de creación habilitada: cualquier usuario puede escucharlos, guardarlos entre sus favoritos y reenviarlos, aunque todavía no le aparezca el botón para generarlos.
Cómo poner audio a un sticker paso a paso
El procedimiento se realiza íntegramente desde el editor integrado de la aplicación, sin necesidad de recurrir a programas externos como Sticker.ly o StikSound, utilizados hasta ahora para lograr este efecto.
Los pasos son los siguientes: abrir una conversación individual o grupal y tocar el ícono de emojis junto al campo de texto. Luego, seleccionar la pestaña de stickers y presionar la opción “Crear sticker”.
A continuación, elegir una fotografía o un video corto desde la galería del celular como base de la imagen. El paso siguiente consiste en presionar el ícono de ondas sonoras que aparece en la barra superior del editor. Si ese botón no se muestra, significa que la función todavía no fue habilitada para esa cuenta, ya que su activación es por etapas.
Una vez dentro de esa opción, hay que elegir la fuente del audio: grabar la voz en el momento, seleccionar un archivo guardado en el teléfono, conservar el sonido original si se partió de un video, o recurrir a un efecto de la biblioteca integrada.
El último paso es recortar el fragmento deseado, escuchar la vista previa y presionar el botón de enviar.
La herramienta se distribuye por el momento entre los participantes del programa de pruebas, en la versión beta para Android y iPhone, por lo que algunos usuarios deberán esperar para poder acceder a la función.

articles.title: Hackers Exploit 10 Vulnerabilities Across Mitel, Juniper, Vates, and Danfoss Products
articles.text:
The U.S. Cybersecurity and Infrastructure Security Agency (CISA) on Wednesday added 10 security flaws to its Known Exploited Vulnerabilities (KEV) catalog, including five vulnerabilities impacting Mitel MiCollab that were disclosed last week.
The Mitel MiCollab vulnerabilities are listed below -
- CVE-2026-133275 (CVSS score: 5.3) - An arbitrary file upload vulnerability in the Audio, Web and Video Conferencing (AWV) Component of MiCollab that could allow an attacker to upload arbitrary files to the target system.
- CVE-2026-133303 (CVSS score: 9.0) - An XML injection vulnerability in the Audio, Web and Video Conferencing (AWV) component of MiCollab that could allow an attacker to execute arbitrary commands within the context of the system.
- CVE-2026-133311 (CVSS score: 5.9) - An unauthorized access vulnerability in the Audio, Web, and Video Conferencing (AWV) Component of MiCollab that could allow an attacker to obtain sensitive information.
- CVE-2026-133323 (CVSS score: 10.0) - A command injection vulnerability in the Audio, Web, and Video Conferencing (AWV) Component of MiCollab that could allow an attacker to execute arbitrary commands within the context of the system.
- CVE-2026-133324 (CVSS score: 5.3) - An authentication bypass vulnerability in the Audio, Web, and Video Conferencing (AWV) Component of MiCollab that could allow an attacker to bypass authentication controls and perform unauthorized actions within the context of the application.
The issues affect MiCollab versions 10.3 and earlier. "Mitel provided a patch available for release 10.3 (10.3.0.18) that addresses these vulnerabilities," the company said in an advisory published November 16, 2026. "Upgrade to this release and apply the provided patch, or upgrade to a later release."
Customers who are unable to apply the updates are recommended to mitigate the risk by restricting external access to the AWV component. As of writing, there are currently no details on how the vulnerabilities are being exploited in the wild.
Customers who are unable to apply the updates are recommended to mitigate the risk by restricting external access to the AWV component. The addition comes against the backdrop of a report from Accenture's Apex Labs, which revealed that an unknown threat actor may have been weaponizing the flaws as zero-days as part of what's suspected to be an artificial intelligence (AI)-assisted data theft campaign.
Evidence indicates the deployment of a web shell against one victim organization a day before Mitel released patches, only for the intrusion to progress rapidly and allowing the threat actor to harvest credentials and steal sensitive business data from a line-of-business database server within hours.
"At that victim, we found the threat actor ran its first command 12 minutes after its first request, then reached root on the MiCollab server within 30 minutes and used the directory credentials that MiCollab stores for its LDAP connector to authenticate to a domain controller within 32 minutes," Accenture said.
The activity is assessed to be part of a broader campaign targeting MiCollab instances, with a second organization's MiCollab server observed holding a persistent HTTPS channel to the threat actor infrastructure since November 9, 2026. It has not been established how this server was compromised as it had been found running an older MiCollab version affected by previously disclosed flaws (i.e., MTLVULN-1694).
The indicators of compromise associated with the intrusions are listed below -
- 204.76.203[.]204 (Command-and-control server)
- 204.76.203[.]216
- 204.76-203-204.sslip[.]io
- 204.76.203[.]204/bkup/ (Data exfiltration path)
- 204.76.203[.]204/bkdl/ (Tool download path)
"MiCollab presents an attractive target because it is commonly internet-facing and connected to critical enterprise services, including Active Directory," Accenture said. "Its history of exploitation further underscores this risk."
Also added to the KEV catalog are the following vulnerabilities -
- CVE-2026-133469 (CVSS score: 9.8) - An improper validation of specified type of input vulnerability in Vates Xen Orchestra that could allow an unauthenticated attacker to bypass authentication and perform actions with administrative privileges via a specially crafted authentication token containing an empty JSON object.
- CVE-2026-103406 (CVSS score: 9.8) - An operating system command injection vulnerability in Hewlett Packard Enterprise (HPE) Juniper Session Smart Conductor and Session Smart Router that could allow a remote attacker to execute arbitrary commands as root via a specially crafted salt minion ID.
The addition of CVE-2026-133469 follows an advisory from Vates VMS that the vulnerability, also tracked as VSA-2026-062, has been exploited by a threat actor from the following IP address and TOR domain -
- 91.211.251[.]112:8001
- ustar3rqxgnskzgnwkgpofgtvxevm6cx3lxdbwt4mndtveqyaohid[.]onion:3333
"At least one instance of malicious exploitation of CVE-2026-103406 has been reported to the Juniper SIRT," Juniper Networks said in an advisory. "Customers are encouraged to upgrade to a fixed release as soon as possible and in the meantime take steps to mitigate this vulnerability."
The remaining three security flaws relate to Danfoss AK-SM 800A Series refrigeration controllers that could lead to authentication bypass and arbitrary command execution -
- CVE-2023-25914 (CVSS score: 8.8) - A path traversal vulnerability that could allow an attacker to access and read underlying server system files via the XML interface.
- CVE-2023-25915 (CVSS score: 9.9) - An improper input validation vulnerability that could allow a remote attacker to run arbitrary commands on the affected system.
- CVE-2025-41450 (CVSS score: 8.5) - An improper authentication vulnerability that could allow an attacker to generate a web report exposing sensitive information, including internal IP addresses, usernames, and store names.
Although Danfoss makes no mention of the flaws being exploited, it's likely that they were put to use as part of high-impact attacks targeting supermarket chains across Europe in recent weeks. France has attributed the October 2026 attacks on its retail sites to Shahid Kaveh (aka Cyber Aveng3rs and Cyber Isnaad Front), an Iranian cyber unit affiliated with the Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps (IRGC).
In light of active exploitation, Federal Civilian Executive Branch (FCEB) agencies are being advised to apply the necessary fixes for all the flaws, except CVE-2026-133311 and CVE-2025-41450, by November 28, 2026. The remaining two vulnerabilities must be addressed by December 9, 2026.
CISA Warns of New Unpatched Danfoss AK-SM 8xxA Series Flaw
The development comes as CISA has warned of an unpatched critical flaw in Danfoss AK-SM 8xxA Series (CVE-2026-129713, CVSS score: 9.8 / 9.3) controllers that could be exploited to execute arbitrary code with webserver privileges.
"A stack-based buffer overflow in an unauthenticated CGI handler of the Danfoss AK-SM 8xxA Series controller allows remote attackers to send specially crafted HTTP/S POST requests, leading to memory corruption, webserver restart and hypothetically potential arbitrary code execution with webserver privileges," CISA said. "Authentication is not required to exploit this vulnerability."
Danfoss, which has issued an alert of its own, said the security flaw impacts versions 5.4.0 and earlier. A fix for the vulnerability is expected to be addressed in an upcoming software version (5.5.x). It also said it will remove the option that allows customers to disable "Strict mode" in the product.
Until the fixes are available, system administrators are advised to take the following actions -
- Make sure remote access to the units is possible only through a secure VPN or in general over a protected network
- Configure the units to Strict mode, which ensures higher security levels on the product
- Recommend using strong passwords
CISA is also recommending that organizations minimize network exposure of such devices, place control system networks and remote devices behind firewalls, and isolate them from business networks.
"When remote access is required, use more secure methods, such as Virtual Private Networks (VPNs), recognizing VPNs may have vulnerabilities and should be updated to the most current version available," CISA added. "Also recognize VPN is only as secure as the connected devices."

articles.title: Credit rating agency puts Nvidia on notice for possible downgrade — S&P Global Ratings says ‘board members may have compromised their independence’
articles.text:
Credit rating agency puts Nvidia on notice for possible downgrade — S&P Global Ratings says ‘board members may have compromised their independence’
The market is getting nervous with all the shenanigans involving Nvidia and Jensen Huang.
S&P Global Ratings, one of the world’s largest rating agencies, announced that it’s putting Nvidia’s credit rating on watch as the company faces a possible downgrade. The agency says that the issues surrounding Jensen Huang regarding export control violations, as well as his resignation and subsequent reinstatement 11 days later, reveal the weakness of Nvidia’s management team and board oversight.
“We believe the long tenure of certain board members may have compromised their independence,” the rating agency said in its press release. It also added, “Issues related to Nvidia’s China exposure also raise questions regarding geopolitical risk management and internal controls. While Nvidia management has delivered significant returns for its stakeholders over decades, weak executive oversight and lack of succession planning have brought questions around the ‘key man’ risk to the forefront. The departure, then reinstatement of the CEO, does not sufficiently answer our questions regarding board oversight of executive code of conduct.”
Nvidia CEO and founder Jensen Huang resigned from the job on November 12, after multiple allegations of affairs, especially with Megaspeed CEO Alice Huang, who’s also accused of enabling the smuggling of $7.5 billion worth of AI GPUs into China. Even though Huang left the company he founded in disgrace, he was reinstated to the position by the Nvidia board on November 23. This was a major surprise, especially as it had previously refused to bring him back due to the ongoing national security investigation into Jensen.
However, it seems that Nvidia’s board of directors has folded to the pressure, especially after President Donald Trump himself said that he talked to them directly, with the board saying that it “received input from senior levels of the United States” that “Mr. Huang’s reinstatement poses no national security risk.” Despite those assurances, the Nvidia chief still faces multiple investigations, including an internal inquiry at Nvidia, a private meeting with the House of Representatives’ Select Committee on China, and a public testimony in front of the Senate Banking Committee, among others.
Even though the AI chipmaker’s risk profile remains unchanged, S&P Global Ratings’ warning is a sign that the market is uneasy about the situation regarding stricter export controls and the allegations of chip diversion. The ratings agency said that the downgrade could happen in the next 90 days after it concludes its due diligence, although it expects any potential drop to “be limited to one notch, unless investigations or disclosures lead us to believe Nvidia’s reputation or future business prospects have been harmed.”

La JBL Flip Essential 3 SE est un modèle qui répond à ce besoin, et même à d’autres grâce à sa protection contre l’eau et la poussière. Néanmoins, pour une grande fête, sa puissance risque de montrer ses limites très rapidement. articles.title: Black Friday Australia laptop deals for 2026: score up to 52% off Lenovo, Apple, Dell, HP and more
articles.text:
Black Friday Australia laptop deals for 2026: score up to 52% off Lenovo, Apple, Dell, HP and more
I'm tracking the best Australian discounts and you can save a bundle on a new notebook for home, work or gaming
Black Friday is here! The sale fell on 27 November this year, and runs through to Cyber Monday on November 30, and Australian retailers are offering excellent discounts on a huge range of laptops.
You can get a Lenovo machine with 16GB of RAM for under AU$900, and there are also deals on lightweight 2-in-1s through to high-end gaming laptops.
Apple deals are also better than usual, with some great prices on refurbished MacBook Neos, or new models from Amazon.
As TechRadar Australia's resident laptop expert, I'm here to help. I've been keeping tabs on price changes across the entire year, so I can confidently tell you what's an actual good buy and filter out all the bad deals. I've been hunting Black Friday deals since the start of the month, as many device-makers started their sales early, and will be here till at least December 3.
If you’re still deciding what to buy, our guides to the best laptops in Australia and the best gaming laptops explain what to look for. It’s also worth checking our HP coupon codes and Lenovo coupon codes if you’re buying direct.
Top retailers for Black Friday laptop deals
- Lenovo: great deals on a wide range of everyday and gaming laptops
- Amazon: sparse but solid laptop deals
- JB Hi-Fi: big discounts on Apple laptops
- HP: take an extra 5% off with code FUTURE5
- Mwave: deals on major PC brands
- The Good Guys: great for MacBooks and Microsoft deals
- Apple: much loved laptops but few discounts when buying direct
After something else entirely? Check out our full coverage of Black Friday deals and get your Christmas shopping done before the rush.
Everyday laptop deals
The Aspire Lite is a budget Windows laptop with a 14-inch, 1920 x 1200 anti-glare screen and a weight of just 1.3kg. The Ryzen 3 and 8GB of RAM are fine for browsing and streaming, and the 256GB SSD is reasonable for the price.
The IdeaPad Slim 3x gives you a roomy 15.3-inch, 1920 x 1200 IPS display and 16GB of RAM at an affordable price. Its eight-core Snapdragon X is well suited to everyday multitasking, though it’s worth checking that any specialist apps or peripherals you rely on support Windows on Arm.
The Dell 15 is well equipped for the money, with a 10-core Intel Core i5-1334U and 16GB of RAM to handle everyday tasks and multitasking. Its 15.6-inch display pairs a 1920 x 1080 resolution with a 120Hz refresh rate for a smooth experience.
The OmniBook 5’s 14-inch, 1920 x 1200 OLED display covers the full DCI-P3 colour gamut, so it’s a good pick for editing photos as well as watching movies. At 1.33kg it’s easy to carry, and the Intel Core 5 320 and 16GB of RAM are well suited to everyday use.
MacBook deals
This Apple Certified Refurbished MacBook Neo is an affordable way into macOS and comes with a one-year Apple warranty. The A18 Pro and 8GB of memory suit everyday use, and the 13-inch, 2408 x 1506 display is sharp for a laptop in this price range. Buying refurbished gives a decent discount compared to buying it new for AU$1,049 from Apple.
The MacBook Neo hasn't seen much in the way of discounts yet (in fact, it has had a price rise), so this meagre 5% off is the best we have seen. Still, it's something at least, and it's well worth checking out our MacBook Neo review for the full scoop.
This Apple Certified Refurbished Neo has a 512GB SSD for keeping photos and apps on the laptop, plus Touch ID for signing in and approving purchases. The A18 Pro and 8GB of memory make it a good everyday Mac, and Apple includes a one-year warranty. Buying refurbished gives a decent discount compared to buying it new for AU$1,249 from Apple.
The MacBook Neo hasn't seen much in the way of discounts yet (in fact, it has had a price rise), so this meagre 4% off is not far off the best we have seen for the 512GB model with Touch ID. Still, it's something at least, and it's well worth checking out our MacBook Neo review for a deeper dive.
This is the cheapest option going if you want the M5 Air and with the 512GB SSD. Want to know more? Check out our MacBook Air M5 review.
Apple has raised prices, and we have seen very few discounts so far, making this minor drop worth considering. This is the upgraded Air with the 1TB SSD and M5 CPU with a 10-core GPU (rather than the base spec 8-core) that costs AU$2549 from Apple. Want to know more? Check out our MacBook Air M5 review.
Also consider the 15-inch Air with 1TB SSD for AU$2,597 — now 12% off compared to buying from Apple.
The 16GB MacBook Pro currently has a small discount from Amazon compared to buying it for AU$3,199 from Apple. Read our Apple MacBook Pro M5 review for the full scoop.
Thin and light laptop deals
The Yoga Slim 7 weighs just 1.16kg, yet its 14-inch, 1920 x 1200 OLED display gives movies deep blacks and rich colours. The Core Ultra 5 226V and 16GB of RAM make it a capable everyday laptop for travel.
This Snapdragon-powered laptop has an impressive spec for the price, with an X Elite X1E78100 CPU, 32GB of RAM and a 1TB SSD. It also has a very nice 2944 x 1840 OLED touchscreen display that outputs 100% of the sRGB gamut. We have seen this machine slightly cheaper, but it's still a good deal if its Windows on Arm compatibility suits the apps you use.
2-in-1 laptop deals
The 14-inch OLED touchscreen folds back for tablet use, and the included pen is handy for handwritten notes or sketches. At 1.38kg it’s light enough to carry to class, and the Core Ultra 5 226V and 16GB of RAM give it the performance to be a capable everyday laptop.
This large-screen 2-in-1 from HP uses the Intel Series 2 Core Ultra 7 258V CPU, giving it a good mix of performance and battery life. The 16-inch laptop also has a 2880 x 1800 OLED touchscreen, 32GB of RAM, 1TB of storage, Wi-Fi 7, Thunderbolt 4 and a facial recognition webcam. We have seen it for slightly less, but this is still a pretty good price if you want a big premium 2-in-1.
Gaming laptop deals
This Victus 15 with an RTX 3050 is refurbished by HP, and is currently one of the cheapest gaming laptops going. And yes, it's a last-gen GPU, plus only an RTX 3050, but it's still a fairly capable option for entry-level gaming for the price.
The Victus is an entry-level gaming laptop with an RTX 4050 that’s well matched to its 15.6-inch, 1920 x 1080 display. The 144Hz refresh rate suits competitive games. Use BFDEAL at checkout to get the full discount.
The Cyborg 15 is an affordable option for 1080p gaming, with an RTX 5060 and a 15.6-inch, 144Hz display that suits fast-paced multiplayer games. The 16GB of RAM is a decent starting point, though be aware the GPU is limited to 55W so the 5060 will give slower frame rates than models with higher graphics power levels.
The Lenovo LOQ Essential 15 is an affordable way to get RTX 5060 graphics, with a 15.6-inch, 1920 x 1080 display that refreshes at 144Hz for smooth play in fast-paced games. The main trade-off is the GPU’s 65W power limit, so expect lower frame rates in demanding games than you’d get from a higher-powered RTX 5060 laptop.
The Legion 5i gives its RTX 5060 up to 115W, a good match for playing demanding games at the 15.3-inch screen’s native 1920 x 1200 resolution. The 1TB SSD is a welcome inclusion at this price, especially if you keep several big games installed.
The Gaming A16 is a relatively affordable way to get an RTX 5070 and a 16-inch IPS screen in the same laptop. The 165Hz refresh rate suits competitive games, while the 1TB SSD gives you room for a mix of multiplayer favourites and larger single-player titles.
The Legion 5a’s 15.3-inch, 2560 x 1600 OLED display combines deep blacks with a 165Hz refresh rate, so it suits both atmospheric single-player games and fast shooters. The 32GB of RAM also gives you headroom for demanding tasks beyond gaming, such as video editing.
Intel’s 24-core i9-14900HX and 32GB of RAM make this Legion a good fit for heavier workloads beyond gaming, including video editing and 3D rendering. Its RTX 5070 drives a 15.1-inch, 2560 x 1600 OLED display with a 165Hz refresh rate.
The Raider pairs a 140W RTX 5070 Ti with 12GB of video memory with a 16-inch, 2560 x 1600 display that runs at 240Hz. That’s an appealing combination for high-detail gaming, though the 512GB SSD is small for a machine in this class.
The Pro model of one of our favourite Lenovo laptops has a reasonable discount on the RTX 5070 Ti variant. The pre-discount web price is beyond steep, but at this sale price it's decent enough value for a premium gaming machine with an OLED, 2560 x 1600, 165Hz display.
The Legion Pro 7i pairs a 175W RTX 5080 with a 16-inch, 2560 x 1600 OLED display, giving demanding games plenty of graphics power and the deep blacks that make dark scenes stand out. The 240Hz refresh rate also makes good use of the higher frame rates you can reach in competitive games.
The Infinity Y16 pairs a 175W RTX 5090 with a 16-inch, 2560 x 1600 display, making it a good pick for playing demanding games at high settings. The screen’s 300Hz refresh rate is particularly useful for competitive shooters, where the GPU can push much higher frame rates.
For those who want mighty gaming power, the Legion Pro 7i with an Intel Ultra 9 275HX processor and RTX 5090 GPU is one of the better options going, despite the painfully high cost compared to last year. There are very few comparable machines at this price, making it an excellent deal if you are willing to spend big. Read our review to learn more.
Black Friday has begun!
Good morning and happy Black Friday! The coffee’s strong, the deals are good and I’ve got 3 screens of price histories open.
You’ll find all my best laptop picks here throughout the Black Friday weekend, through to Cyber Monday on November 30.
For everything else on sale, head over to TechRadar’s full Australian Black Friday coverage.

articles.title: “Vendemos la capacidad de procesamiento porque no podemos competir”: Elon Musk sobre alquilar sus centros de datos para IA
articles.text:
Elon Musk reconoció en privado que alquilar la infraestructura de cómputo de SpaceX a sus propios competidores en inteligencia artificial resulta más rentable que destinar esos recursos al desarrollo interno de la compañía. Así lo señaló un informe de The New York Times, que tuvo acceso a comunicaciones internas de la empresa.
El dilema surge en momentos en que Anthropic y Google pagan sumas considerables cada mes para acceder a los recursos de procesamiento que SpaceX desarrolló originalmente para sus propias ambiciones en materia de inteligencia artificial.
Conversación interna de Musk y su equipo
En agosto de 2026, Musk cambió el nombre de un grupo de conversación de un equipo de ingeniería para manifestar su malestar por la posición competitiva de SpaceX en el desarrollo de inteligencia artificial. El nuevo nombre decía “Sell compute because we can’t compete” (“Vendemos la capacidad de procesamiento porque no podemos competir”), según las comunicaciones internas revisadas por el diario.
El empresario también advirtió a los empleados sobre el uso indebido de las unidades de procesamiento gráfico (GPU), el componente que proporciona la capacidad computacional necesaria para entrenar y operar modelos de inteligencia artificial sofisticados.
“A cualquiera que desperdicie GPU en estupideces mientras no logramos competir se le pedirá que se vaya de inmediato, ya que esto constituye una traición a su equipo”, afirmó Musk, según las comunicaciones citadas por el medio.
A partir de ese momento, Musk comenzó a exigir explicaciones semanales a ingenieros seleccionados sobre sus actividades y el consumo de estos recursos computacionales especializados.
El negocio de alquiler de cómputo supera a xAI en ingresos
Estas tensiones internas coinciden con el crecimiento acelerado de la operación de arrendamiento de infraestructura de SpaceX, que ya genera más de la mitad de los ingresos de la compañía. La división, rebautizada como SpaceXSI, obtiene miles de millones de dólares mensuales al proveer capacidad de procesamiento a organizaciones que desarrollan productos de inteligencia artificial competidores.
Anthropic se convirtió en su principal cliente, con un acuerdo valuado en aproximadamente 3.100 millones de dólares mensuales, mientras que el convenio con Google alcanza los 800 millones de dólares. Ambos contratos podrían mantenerse vigentes hasta 2029, aunque cualquiera de los dos clientes puede rescindirlos con un preaviso de 90 días, según las condiciones pactadas.
La relación comercial resulta particular: las mismas empresas que compiten contra las ambiciones de Musk en inteligencia artificial dependen en gran medida de su infraestructura. El negocio de inteligencia artificial de Musk, xAI, ingresó al mercado tras el lanzamiento de ChatGPT en 2022 y posteriormente invirtió miles de millones de dólares en instalaciones de cómputo para desafiar a los competidores ya establecidos.
Centros de datos de Colossus operan por debajo de su capacidad
Uno de los principales logros de esa estrategia fue la construcción de la planta Colossus (un clúster de supercomputadoras y centros de datos), en Memphis, Tennessee, en 2024. Musk anunció en su momento que la compañía había instalado más de un millón de procesadores especializados para sostener herramientas de inteligencia artificial de alta demanda.
Sin embargo, documentos internos indicaron que xAI utilizó menos de la mitad de la capacidad disponible de Colossus durante el último año. Esta subutilización explicaría por qué el arrendamiento de capacidad sobrante se volvió una opción financieramente atractiva mientras el desarrollo interno seguía enfrentando dificultades frente a rivales ya consolidados en el sector.
La compañía redirigió recursos de ciertos proyectos, entre ellos Grok Imagine, tras el despido de unos 60 empleados que trabajaban en generación de imágenes y video.
Musk anticipa una expansión del vínculo con Anthropic
Pese a la competencia directa entre ambas compañías en el terreno de la inteligencia artificial, Musk indicó que la relación de Anthropic con SpaceX podría ampliarse en lugar de reducirse. “Me han dicho que el resultado de mayor probabilidad es que querrían un incremento de 10 gigavatios de capacidad de cómputo de SpaceX”, señaló el empresario.
El director ejecutivo de Anthropic, Dario Amodei, también se refirió en términos favorables al acuerdo vigente entre ambas compañías, al destacar la calidad de los recursos de cómputo de SpaceX y la relación de trabajo establecida entre las dos firmas.

articles.title: iPhone 20 Pro : une version céramique en édition limitée au programme
articles.text:
Apple pourrait bien apporter du nouveau avec l'iPhone 20 Pro. Car certaines appareils de ce modèle pourraient avoir une finition en céramique !
Le lancement de la dernière Apple Watch 12 à la rentrée dernière a été l'occasion pour Apple de réintégrer un matériau que l'on n'avait plus vu depuis longtemps pour ces montres : la céramique. Et ça pourrait ne pas être seulement réservé à ces dernières, puisque l'iPhone 20 Pro, qui sera le smartphone anniversaire des 20 ans du téléphone mythique d'Apple, y aurait aussi droit (dans certaines limites).
Des composants en céramique actuellement produits dans le cadre de l'iPhone 20 Pro
Il devrait y avoir clairement un côté nouveauté avec l'iPhone 20 Pro. La semaine dernière, nous vous informions ainsi que le titane devrait faire son retour pour cette édition. Et ce ne sera pas le seul nouveau matériau dans la partie, selon l'information du leaker chinois Fixed Focus Digital.
En effet, ce dernier a indiqué dans un message posté sur Weibo qu'il avait pu avoir accès à des composants en céramique, actuellement produits pour Apple. Des composants en céramique destinés au prochaine iPhone 20 Pro, qui devrait être lancé l'an prochain.
Une édition limitée réservée à une certaine clientèle ?
Mais Apple ne compterait pas mettre de la céramique partout. Fixed Focus Digital explique que les capacités de production réservées à ces composants sont assez minimes, ce qui indiquerait que peu de composants devraient ainsi être produits. Il ne précise par contre pas s'il s'agit d'un petit élément, du dos complet ou bien si une grande partie du boîtier adopterait la céramique.
On semble dans tous les cas s'orienter vers une production très réduite d'éventuels iPhone 20 Pro en céramique. Alors, Apple prépare-t-il une version édition limitée de cet iPhone 20 Pro, qui est extrêmement important, vu qu'il doit permettre de fêter l'anniversaire du téléphone ? On espère que les prochains mois nous en apprendront plus grâce à d'éventuelles fuites.
Source : Macrumors

articles.title: Actualización de Windows impide iniciar sesión en redes de empresas, confirma Microsoft
articles.text:
Microsoft confirmó que las actualizaciones de seguridad de Windows publicadas desde el 10 de noviembre pueden impedir el inicio de sesión en algunas redes corporativas. El problema afecta a servidores proxy, sistemas de acceso único y herramientas de empaquetado de aplicaciones de terceros que usan el protocolo de autenticación NTLM.
La empresa lo reconoció como problema conocido en un documento de soporte (KB5135557), publicado el 10 de noviembre y actualizado el 20 de noviembre de 2026. Allí describe una solución provisional y un calendario: en mayo de 2027, los servidores Windows empezarán a exigir por defecto una protección que hoy solo se ofrece de forma opcional. Las actualizaciones alcanzan a Windows 11, Windows 10 Enterprise LTSC 2021 y a Windows Server 2016, 2019, 2022 y 2025.
NTLM es un método de autenticación con el que un equipo demuestra su identidad ante otro dentro de una red, por ejemplo al conectarse a un servidor interno.
Qué cambió con la actualización
Las actualizaciones corrigen la vulnerabilidad CVE-2026-118737 y representan la primera de dos fases de mejoras en la firma de mensajes NTLM. El objetivo, según Microsoft, es que cada sesión autenticada establezca una clave criptográfica y firme los mensajes, lo que reduce la exposición a los llamados ataques de retransmisión.
Antes del cambio, las aplicaciones que no pedían expresamente esa protección recibían un sustituto: un marcador de 16 bytes en cero que, según el documento, no ofrece ninguna protección criptográfica. Ahora los equipos con Windows ofrecen la firma real en todas las conexiones, salvo las anónimas y las de cuentas de invitado, que quedan exentas.
En esta primera fase, los servidores aceptan tanto clientes que firman como clientes que no lo hacen. Microsoft precisa que todas las versiones de Windows Server compatibles con la actualización pueden firmar, y que los eventos de auditoría permiten identificar qué equipos no lo hacen.
Por qué fallan algunos inicios de sesión
Según Microsoft, el fallo aparece cuando un dispositivo intermediario implementa mal el protocolo. El ejemplo que da el documento: un proxy que avisa de que enviará datos sobre el servidor, pero entrega ese campo vacío o incompleto.
Cuando la autenticación usa firma, Windows exige que el mensaje de desafío incluya el nombre del equipo y el del dominio, dos datos que la especificación de NTLM define como obligatorios. Si falta alguno, el sistema rechaza el intento con un error de inicio de sesión.
Para detectar un dispositivo afectado, Microsoft recomienda capturar el tráfico de red y buscar un mensaje de desafío con la lista de información del servidor vacía. También sugiere revisar el evento 4021 del registro de NTLM: un valor “Not Found” en el campo de información de destino puede indicar un equipo afectado. Para el usuario final, el síntoma probable es que un proxy o un sistema de acceso único vuelva a pedir la contraseña sin dejar entrar.
Solución provisional y plazo de mayo de 2027
Microsoft creó dos valores nuevos en el registro de Windows. El primero, ClientAllowUnsignedNtlm, vale 0 por defecto, lo que hace que el cliente ofrezca la firma. Si se cambia a 1, el cliente deja de ofrecerla, algo que la empresa indica que debe usarse solo como medida temporal de compatibilidad.
El segundo, ServerRequireNtlmSign, vale 0 por defecto y permite que el servidor acepte clientes sin firma. Con valor 1, rechaza a los que no firman. Microsoft recomienda activarlo cuando la auditoría, a través del evento 4023, confirme que ya no quedan conexiones sin firma, y aclara que no exige reiniciar el equipo.
La segunda fase llegará en mayo de 2027, cuando los servidores Windows pasarán a exigir la firma por defecto, con lo que los clientes que no la ofrezcan serán rechazados. El documento no precisa el día exacto de ese mes.

articles.title: Electronics manufacturers set up memory 'war rooms' to find, lock in DRAM supplies amid worst shortage in history — employees scour eBay, contact hundreds of brokers, and snap up even small batches of just 5 to 12 units
articles.text:
Electronics manufacturers set up memory 'war rooms' to find, lock in DRAM supplies amid worst shortage in history — employees scour eBay, contact hundreds of brokers, and snap up even small batches of just 5 to 12 units
Even Elon Musk can't seem to get special treatment.
The memory shortage has gotten so bad that many companies, especially smaller ones, have started establishing “procurement war rooms,” where employees are desperately trying to find memory chip supplies on sites like eBay and trying to figure out how they could make manufacturers offer them even just a small amount of DRAM. This massive shortage has pushed up costs for electronic manufacturers, with some companies forced to increase prices to make up the difference while others cut the specifications of their products while introducing a smaller price bump.
The Wall Street Journal reports that Taiwanese memory module and storage maker Apacer had to take out loans just to have money on hand in case it finds a supply of memory chips. “If chips show up, we take it,” Apacer President Gibson Chen told the publication. “This is crazy, but there is no other way.” Even one of the world’s richest people, Elon Musk, was reportedly having trouble finding memory chips. A portfolio manager claimed that Musk offered Samsung an LTA and even a financial guarantee for new Samsung chip factories, but the company’s executive chairman, Lee Jae-yong, allegedly answered that everyone else was offering those things already. OpenAI CEO Sam Altman also recently went to South Korea to meet with Samsung leadership just to secure more RAM for data centers.
Even though PC builders and enthusiasts were the hardest hit by the 500% climb in memory prices, many other electronics manufacturers are also now feeling the squeeze. Big companies like Amazon, Apple, and Microsoft could use their scale and resources to pay more and secure massive amounts of memory chip supplies under long-term agreements (LTAs). However, smaller firms would usually have to rely on brokers and whatever’s available to find what they need. Some have reportedly contacted hundreds of brokers and go through online listings, where they would snap up even small batches of just five or 12 units just to have some supply. Others proceed to the gray market, although they must be careful as some unscrupulous sellers mix in batches of used memory chips with brand new orders to inflate their deliveries.
The scramble for AI compute has caused a massive memory chip shortage, especially as the big three memory chip manufacturers — Micron, Samsung, and SK hynix — have focused their production on more lucrative HBM. Both memory chip manufacturers and RAM kit makers are warning of continued shortages, too, with SK hynix saying 2027 will be the “worst year” for memory shortages, while TeamGroup’s CEO said that it could reach a point where “even money can’t buy goods.” Although the big three manufacturers are building new factories, they’re not expected to go online and start pushing out memory chips until 2028.
It’s difficult for a new player to enter the memory chip market. Aside from the enormous costs involved in setting up a factory and supply chain to build memory chips, any potential entrant must also license a ton of patents and develop its own technologies before it can start making competitive chips. Even if it was able to get its hands on the knowledge required to design memory chips, it still needs the manufacturing expertise needed to produce them at scale. CXMT is the only new player that has successfully produced mainstream consumer DDR5 RAM, but it’s facing multiple allegations that it stole the technology needed to achieve that from Samsung. Even then, the DDR5 memory chips that the Chinese company produced don’t have the same performance as its competitors and track market prices, meaning it’s not the affordable alternative that many tech enthusiasts imagined it to be.
The memory chip market is known for its boom-and-bust cycle, which is why manufacturers were initially reluctant to increase their capacity. But even if they started building factories at the first sign of a shortage, it would still take several years before these new facilities could start pumping out chips to ease the situation. Nevertheless, the three companies are currently facing a price-fixing lawsuit alleging that they coordinated their shift to HBM to cut DDR3 and DDR4 production, with the judge handling the case saying that it’s plausible they colluded as the market experienced the price surge.

articles.title: 'Standoffish behavior, deliberate delays, heavy involvement from lawyers, and a constant theme: prioritizing corporate interests over those of their customers': HaveIBeenPwned's Troy Hunt reveals exactly what companies say when told they've been hacked
articles.text:
'Standoffish behavior, deliberate delays, heavy involvement from lawyers, and a constant theme: prioritizing corporate interests over those of their customers': HaveIBeenPwned's Troy Hunt reveals exactly what companies say when told they've been hacked
"Hack off, Troy"
- HaveIBeenPwned’s Troy Hunt has published a summary about why data breach disclosure is hard
- Hunt fed 8.5 years’ worth of email exchanges into Anthropic’s Claude, and used the AI to compose the summary
- Claude also identified seven patterns in the company responses, none of which were initially customer focused
Claude AI has been used to assess a tranche of disclosure communication emails between Troy Hunt and various hacked businesses over an 8.5 year period – and concluded that those organizations need to do better.
Publishing the results on his website HaveIBeenPwned, Hunt explained that using Claude was the “best way to highlight the behaviors” that he has seen repeated over the best part of a decade.
Using Claude to evaluate the exchanges has certainly done that, with the AI offering suggestions as to how businesses affected by data breaches could make communication and disclosure easier.
No way in
Claude’s analysis of Hunt’s emails covers a large amount of repetition, attempts to control narratives, and contact from legal teams.
Sadly, the customers affected by the data breaches are barely considered by the hacked businesses.
Several patterns are identified by Claude, such as an inability to find a way in to contact someone, a denial, and an open-ended investigation that apparently goes nowhere. It also spotted the lawyer-lead response, requests to review wording, and the bizarre response of “disclosure as harm” – essentially, suggesting Hunt sharing the breach is worse than the breach itself (ignoring the fact that the data is being traded on the dark web).
Organizations interested in the results should, says the AI, publish contact details for their security teams, along with a series of steps that are basically asking organizations to be responsible.
Sign up to the TechRadar Pro newsletter to get all the top news, opinion, features and guidance your business needs to succeed!
Disclosure experiences
Covering so much correspondence for the report, Claude concludes that the organizations need incentives to agree to disclosure and inform their customers. It notes “every day without a public statement is a day without bad headlines…” while for those affected “every one of those days is a day they're exposed without knowing it.”
Referring to the deep dive into his emails by Claude, Hunt remarked: “Hundreds of emails back and forth with companies that had had data breaches, and some very common patterns. I knew the emails contained standoffish behavior, deliberate delays, heavy involvement from lawyers, and a constant theme: prioritizing corporate interests over those of their customers.”
While the results didn’t necessarily surprise him, revisiting so many disclosure warning events did have an effect. “I didn't know just how stark it would be to read such a candid analysis of my own emails, nor how frustrating it would be to relive many of those disclosure experiences.”
Troy Hunt performs one of the greatest services online, and everyone should be extremely grateful for HaveIBeenPwned.

articles.title: Black Friday : 17 PC portables à prix CASSÉS chez Amazon, du Dell 15 au MacBook Air M5
articles.text:

À la veille du Black Friday, nous ouvrons avec les deux PC portables testés par notre rédaction, le MacBook Air M5 et le Dell XPS 13, puis le Dell 15 que nos lecteurs ont le plus acheté ce mois-ci, avant les quatorze autres, du moins cher au plus cher, que nous n'avons pas testés.
La sélection va de l'ordinateur de cours à 449 € au PC gamer en RTX 5070, avec des remises de 12 % à 47 % sur les prix de référence affichés par Amazon au relevé du 26 novembre. Les plus fortes économies en euros, 470 €, reviennent au Dell 15 Core i5 16 Go et au Dell 15 Core i7, et la plus forte en pourcentage, 47 %, aux deux Dell 15 Core i5.

MacBook Air M5 : l'ultraportable d'Apple noté 8/10, à 1 199 € pour le Black Friday

- Silence total : aucun ventilateur, et des performances solides au quotidien selon notre test.
- Stockage rapide : des vitesses de lecture et d'écriture doublées en un an, d'après nos mesures.

Dell XPS 13 : 450 € de moins sur l'ultraportable de 1 kg noté 7/10, à 1 349 €
Notre test du Dell XPS 13 (2026) lui donne 7/10 pour son châssis en aluminium usiné, son écran tactile mat de 13,4 pouces et ses 8 à 10 heures d'autonomie. Nous l'avions en main en Core 5 320 avec 16 Go ; cette version, annoncée par Amazon en Core Ultra 7 355 avec 1 To de SSD, n'est pas celle que nous avons testée.

- Très compact : 1 kg et 12,7 mm d'épaisseur sur notre modèle de test.

- À savoir : seulement deux ports USB-C, pas de prise casque, et le chargeur est vendu à part.

- À savoir : il coûte 80 € de plus que la version 8 Go de cette sélection, pour le double de mémoire.
Dell 15 Core i5 8 Go : la même base à 449 €, avec 2 ans d'intervention à domicile

- Connectique généreuse : deux USB-C, deux USB-A, HDMI 2.1 et une webcam 1080p.
- À savoir : la définition est HD+ et non Full HD, et le chargeur n'est pas fourni.

- À savoir : la puce ARM oblige à vérifier la compatibilité de vos logiciels, et le SSD s'arrête à 256 Go.
Lenovo IdeaPad Slim 3 Ryzen 5 : 512 Go de SSD pour moins de 450 €, à 449,99 €
Ce 15,6 pouces Full HD mat associe un AMD Ryzen 5, 8 Go de LPDDR5 et un SSD de 512 Go, avec un clavier AZERTY. C'est une base simple pour les cours et la bureautique. Nous ne l'avons pas testé.
✅ Points forts
- Stockage confortable : 512 Go de SSD à ce prix.
- Dalle mate : moins de reflets près d'une fenêtre.
- À savoir : l'écran est une dalle TN de 250 nits, et le chargeur n'est pas fourni.
Lenovo IdeaPad Slim 3 14 pouces : un clavier rétroéclairé pour moins de 500 €, à 479,99 €

articles.title: Cómo activar en iOS 27 la función del iPhone para frenar estafas
articles.text:
Apple incorporó en iOS 27 una herramienta contra las estafas por suplantación de identidad: Impersonation Risk Detection, que puede traducirse como detección de riesgo de suplantación. Según la documentación de soporte que la empresa publicó, el usuario debe activarla a mano desde Ajustes.
La función apunta a las estafas en las que un delincuente se hace pasar por un banco, una oficina del Estado o una persona de confianza para presionar a la víctima a pagar o a cambiar los datos de su cuenta. Apple explica que la verificación en dos pasos no siempre frena estos casos, porque es la propia víctima quien realiza la acción.
El sistema analiza datos del dispositivo y de la cuenta de Apple para detectar señales de una estafa en curso. Luego entrega a la aplicación solo un nivel de riesgo, sin los datos que lo originaron. Los niveles son tres: desconocido (no se detectó actividad sospechosa, lo que no equivale a una confirmación de seguridad), medio y alto.
Los pasos para activarla
El procedimiento figura en la página oficial de Apple. Los nombres son los que aparecen en el iPhone en inglés; en otros idiomas el menú puede mostrar una traducción.
Primero, abrir la aplicación Ajustes (Settings) del iPhone o del iPad. Segundo, tocar “Privacy & Security” (Privacidad y seguridad) y bajar hasta “Impersonation Risk Detection”. Tercero, activar el interruptor “Share with App Developers” (compartir con desarrolladores de aplicaciones). Apple aclara que puede pedir iniciar sesión en la App Store con la cuenta de Apple.
Fox News señaló que el ajuste viene apagado, de modo que actualizar a iOS 27 no basta. Apple añade que los cambios en este ajuste pueden tardar hasta 24 horas en aplicarse. La propia página de ayuda incluye una advertencia: si alguien le pide al usuario que apague esta función, puede tratarse de una estafa.
Qué ve cada aplicación y qué datos usa Apple
La detección solo opera en aplicaciones que la hayan incorporado, y es cada app la que decide qué hacer con el nivel de riesgo: pedir una verificación de identidad, agregar una demora o mostrar una advertencia. Apple precisa que no controla esa decisión. La compañía todavía no publicó una lista de aplicaciones compatibles, según 9to5Mac.
Las acciones que pueden disparar la consulta son, por ejemplo, un pago o el cambio de la contraseña de una cuenta. Dentro del mismo menú, la sección “Recent Activity” (actividad reciente) muestra qué aplicaciones pidieron una evaluación, y “Reasons for Access” (motivos de acceso) detalla qué acción la motivó.
Para quitar el permiso a una sola aplicación, basta con tocarla en esa lista y apagar su interruptor. Este cambio también puede demorar hasta 24 horas.
Sobre la privacidad, Apple afirma que el análisis se hace en el propio dispositivo y que la empresa nunca recibe los datos usados para calcular el riesgo. Según la documentación, se consideran patrones de interacción, tiempos, contexto y datos básicos de sensores. La empresa asegura que no analiza el contenido de Fotos, Mensajes ni Correo.
Apple sí conoce el tipo de acción que el usuario intentó en la aplicación cuando esta solicita la evaluación.
Una revisión antes de las compras de fin de año
Tom’s Guide recomienda activar esta función antes del Black Friday, con el argumento de que los mensajes falsos de envíos y las alertas bancarias falsificadas se mezclan con las confirmaciones reales de compra.
El alcance tiene un límite: la protección depende de que el banco o la tienda usen la herramienta. Un usuario puede activarla y, aun así, no recibir ningún aviso si sus aplicaciones no la incorporaron.
La página de soporte de Apple indica que la función está disponible desde iOS 27 y iPadOS 27.

articles.title: Nvidia stops AI GPU shipments to Southeast Asia amid purported China cloud access ban, report claims — data centers in Singapore, other countries, in trouble as Commerce Department requires cloud providers to obtain export license
articles.text:
Nvidia stops AI GPU shipments to Southeast Asia amid purported China cloud access ban, report claims — data centers in Singapore, other countries, in trouble as Commerce Department requires cloud providers to obtain export license
Dell, Supermicro, and other server manufacturers have been told to suspend shipments to Singapore, Thailand, Malaysia, and Indonesia.
AI data centers in Singapore, Thailand, Malaysia, and Indonesia are facing trouble as Nvidia has reportedly ordered its manufacturing partners to stop shipping AI servers to the region. According to the Financial Times, Dell, Supermicro, and other firms that make AI servers using Nvidia AI GPUs have told their customers from the four countries that the AI chip maker has forbidden them to ship their orders. The move comes as the U.S. closed the loophole that let Chinese AI companies rent compute from data centers outside China equipped with advanced AI chips sourced from American semiconductor manufacturers like Nvidia.
The U.S. has banned the export of advanced AI chips to China since 2022 in an effort to limit its advancement. Even though President Trump eventually allowed Nvidia to export H100 AI GPUs to China in December 2025, companies that wanted to buy them needed to secure an import license from the Commerce Department. Aside from that, the White House is also collecting a 25% fee for every chip, making it more expensive for a data center in China to buy them. Because of this, many Chinese AI labs are instead renting compute from data centers located abroad. They mostly do this in Southeast Asia, which is just around a four-to-six-hour flight from major cities like Hong Kong, Shenzhen, and Shanghai, although some firms are looking in further areas like Europe.
It remains unclear if Nvidia’s order is permanent or temporary, but the new export rules give cloud providers 90 days to apply for an export license and prove that their customers do not include restricted entities. However, one cloud provider executive told the Financial Times that there are no clear instructions on how to go about this. “There’s this new rule but no guidance on execution,” they said. “No one knows how to apply for this license while the 90-day clock is ticking. It’s causing sheer chaos in the region.”
This sudden halt of orders is causing trouble for many data centers in Southeast Asia. Sources say that Aolani, a Singapore-based cloud company with a deal to provide compute to ByteDance, is losing financing for the project as bankers have stopped issuing credit to the tune of $500 million as Nvidia GPU shipments to the region remain in jeopardy. The Chinese social media giant could also potentially drop out of the arrangement, as it won’t be able to access the powerful Nvidia chips that many AI labs still prefer for training their models.

Samsung's rugged T9 hits speeds of up to 2,000MB/s over a 20Gbps USB connection, and it just got a $140 Black Friday price cut

Save 29% on the 2TB Samsung T9 external SSD, offering up to 2,000MB/s transfer speeds over USB 3.2 Gen 2x2, 3-meter drop protection, and both USB-C and USB-A cables included.
Why we recommend it
This rugged, credit card-sized portable SSD ranked number one in our guide to the best portable SSDs as a great all-round performer that pushes the limits of USB 3.2 Gen 2x2 standard, especially in its 2TB capacity.
The USB 3.2 Gen 2x2 connection allows for the editing of high-bitrate 4K or 8K footage directly off the drive without throttling, and the 256-bit hardware encryption keeps work files secure if it ever goes missing.
Price Context & Historical Value
At a time of unpredictable memory prices, the 2TB Samsung T9 has sat around the $490 mark in the run up to Black Friday. The $140 price cut brings the T9 far below the typical pricing.

you need fast and portable storage that can handle heavy creative workflows without stuttering in a sturdy case.
❌ Skip the Samsung T9 2TB if...
your device doesn't have a USB 3.2 Gen 2x2 as your read and write speeds will be capped at the 10Gbps (around 1,000MB/s) limit.
