articles.title: Inside the indium phosphide squeeze and the optical boom — InP remains tightly constrained as the demand from AI puts the entire supply chain under pressure
articles.text:
Inside the indium phosphide squeeze and the optical boom — InP remains tightly constrained as the demand from AI puts the entire supply chain under pressure
As the focus goes in on Optical, InP comes under the spotlight.
Indium phosphide (InP) is a compound material used in specialized chip-making. Unlike silicon, which is the fundamental building block for mainstream logic and memory chips, InP — made from indium and phosphorus — is mainly used to manufacture highly specialized photonic and high-frequency electronic chips, largely due to its outstanding optical properties. Its immensely expensive and complex manufacturing process also makes it impractical for the large volumes and die sizes needed for logic and memory chips. With the industry predicting a shortfall of this crucial material right as the shift to optical interconnects in data centers begins, we explore the current state of the supply chain.
InP chips have powered high-speed lasers, modulators, photodetectors, and various other optical components used across the telecommunications industry and defense for decades. While the InP supply chain was relatively small and highly specialized, it was generally stable and sufficient to meet global demands.
Then came the AI boom. As AI clusters hit the physical limits of moving enormous amounts of data over copper, the industry began the switch to optical interconnects. First came ever-faster optical transceivers. Now the industry is transitioning to silicon photonics, near-packaged optics, and co-packaged optics, bringing optical links progressively closer to the processors themselves. InP is central to much of this transition, building the critical active optical components needed to turn electrical data into light and back again.
Individual AI data centers are already being built around hundreds of thousands of accelerators, with upcoming gigawatt-scale buildouts expected to house millions. Connecting those processors translates into demand for millions upon millions of indispensable optical components, all relying on the same relatively tiny InP supply chain.
Japan's Sumitomo Electric and U.S.-headquartered AXT together account for almost 80% of global InP substrate manufacturing, with JX Advanced Metals adding roughly another 10%. AXT, however, manufactures most of its InP substrates in China, where exports now require government licenses, further exacerbating the situation. It gets worse: China accounts for around 70% of global refined indium output, which is recovered as a byproduct of processing zinc. Export controls mean that restrictions apply to both the material itself and the finished wafer.
The resulting squeeze is already sending ripples across the industry, with several companies predicting shortfalls. Michael Hurlston, CEO of optical-component manufacturer Lumentum, said in July that the company's InP fabs were shipping more than 30% below customer demand, despite rapid capacity expansion. Coherent also described InP capacity as the “primary constraint” on its transceiver business.
A simple solution would be to expand the supply chain. However, growing large, low-defect InP crystals is difficult, while qualifying new suppliers requires time that doesn't align with the industry's demand. Furthermore, expanding substrate and laser-fabrication capacity can take years. Meanwhile, to secure optical components capacity for its accelerators, Nvidia has invested $2 billion each in Lumentum and Coherent, attaching multibillion-dollar purchase commitments and future capacity rights to both deals. Both companies, along with several others in the supply chain, are frantically pursuing solutions.
What is indium phosphide?
Indium phosphide belongs to the III-V family of compound semiconductors, named after the periodic-table groups of their constituent elements; in InP’s case, indium and phosphorus. Its better-known relatives include gallium arsenide and gallium nitride.
Indium phosphide’s distinguishing property, which separates it from silicon, is its direct bandgap, measured at about 1.34 eV at room temperature. In a direct-bandgap material, electrons dropping across the gap release their energy efficiently as photons, making the material particularly useful for lasers and other active optical devices.
Silicon, on the other hand, has an indirect bandgap, meaning that the same transition requires an additional interaction with a crystal lattice and mostly sheds its energy as heat instead. Therefore, while the material can — in silicon photonics — guide, split, and modulate light using structures fabricated with mature CMOS processes, it does not produce the light beam. As a result, Modern silicon-photonics systems commonly rely on a III-V laser source, most commonly based on the InP material system, to provide the light that the silicon circuitry manipulates.
The fiber-optic wavelength window’s alignment with InP's properties is another reason for the material's ubiquity. Modern telecom and data-center links commonly operate around 1,310 nm and 1,550 nm, where optical fiber exhibits favorable transmission characteristics. Pure InP itself does not emit at those exact wavelengths. However, InGaAsP and InAlGaAs alloys, which are grown on lattice-matched InP substrates, can have their bandgaps engineered for those bands. InGaAs layers on InP are also highly effective photodetectors at telecom wavelengths.
These characteristics and functionalities make the InP platform critical to many active functions in optical communications, including distributed-feedback (DFB) lasers, electro-absorption modulated lasers (EMLs), continuous-wave (CW) lasers, semiconductor optical amplifiers, photodetectors, and complete photonic integrated circuits. Silicon photonics and InP consequently complement each other. Silicon provides scalable optical circuitry, while InP provides efficient light generation and several high-performance active optical devices.
Beyond photonics, InP is also commonly used in high-frequency electronic chips. Electrons move through the material far faster than through silicon, giving it strong high-frequency performance that makes it suitable for millimeter-wave and terahertz electronics, radar receivers, and high-speed data converters. This market is much smaller than photonics, but it has few substitutes at the top of the frequency range.
Indium phosphide’s roles across telecommunications and AI data centers
InP lasers and transceivers have been converting electrical signals into light for long-haul fiber networks, metro links, submarine cables, and eventually shorter-reach data-center connections for decades. Despite 5G rollouts driving demand higher, the indium phosphide supply chain remained a stable, moderately sized business with predictable growth. The AI boom has now driven demand up by several orders of magnitude.
Modern AI clusters can contain hundreds of thousands of interconnected accelerators that continuously exchange data. Copper remains a cheap, effective connector over short distances, but electrical losses, signal integrity, and power requirements progressively worsen as bandwidth and distance increase. This has led to the rapid adoption of optical interconnects.
In this setup, a modulator encodes electrical data from the switch or accelerator onto light from a laser. Fiber cables then carry it across the link to a photodetector that converts the received photons back into an electrical signal. In pluggable transceivers, many of these functions are integrated into a compact module plugged into the front of a network switch, with InP-based components executing several steps in the process.
Lumentum's 200G EML, for example, monolithically combines a wavelength-locked DFB laser and an electro-absorption modulator on its InP platform, and is designed for 200-Gbps-per-lane links used in 1.6T transceivers. Coherent is producing InP EMLs, high-power CW lasers, and high-speed photodiodes for the same generation of hardware. As aggregate link speeds move from 400G and 800G to 1.6T and beyond, the number and performance of these InP-based optical components become increasingly important.
At the same time, the industry is bringing optics right to the board with co-packaged optics (CPO) to further shorten the distance data travels. Conventional pluggable optics leave around 15 to 30 centimeters (5.90 to 11.81 inches) of high-speed copper trace between the switch ASIC and the optical module. CPO brings the optical engine onto the accelerator package as a photonic integrated circuit (PIC) chip, shrinking that electrical path and reducing power consumption. Nvidia's Quantum-X and Spectrum-X photonics switches are among the first major AI platforms built around that approach.
While they integrate several optical functions onto the boards, PIC chips do not generate the laser. CPO and silicon-photonics designs still mostly use external InP CW lasers to supply light to the silicon photonic circuits, further consolidating the demand for indium phosphide in AI data centers and the industry as a whole.
The state of the supply chain
As a result of the enormous, rapidly expanding market for the material, indium phosphide’s supply chain is constrained at several points, starting with the raw material itself. Unlike many metals which are mined from dedicated deposits, indium is typically recovered as a trace byproduct of processing zinc sulfide ore. Manufacturers then combine high-purity indium and phosphorus and grow them into a single-crystal InP ingot, or boule, which they process into substrate wafers with tightly controlled properties. Next, manufacturers grow extremely thin epitaxial layers of InP-related compounds over it, commonly using metal-organic chemical vapor deposition. The epiwafer then goes through several chip-making processes and module assembly to become optical chips and devices.
Indium production's dependence on Zinc processing creates bottlenecks in InP's supply chain, right at the beginning of the stream. The USGS put global primary refined indium production at roughly 1,100 tonnes in 2025, with China accounting for 760 tonnes. For context, the BBC estimates that 30,000 tonnes of electronic-grade silicon used exclusively to make microchips are mined yearly. The United States imports all of the InP it consumes, producing nothing. Meanwhile, indium substrate manufacturers Japan's Sumitomo and JX Metals source more than 90% of their high-purity indium feedstock from China, meaning even non-Chinese substrate makers begin their process with Chinese material.
Further downstream, at the substrate manufacturing level, Sumitomo Electric holds roughly 40% of the global InP substrate market, U.S.-based AXT around 35%, and JX Advanced Metals about 10%. Together, the three control more than 90% of capacity. Although AXT is headquartered in California, most of its InP substrate production runs through its Beijing Tongmei subsidiary, which puts it directly under China's export licensing regime. Other fringe substrate manufacturers include Freiberger Compound Materials in Germany and a growing set of Chinese entrants, including Yunnan Germanium.
The supply chain is also highly concentrated at the device and component level, with Coherent and Lumentum dominating Western laser and component production. IQE supplies epitaxial wafers, and Japanese firms, including Mitsubishi Electric, supply laser components. Chinese module makers such as Innolight and Eoptolink assemble a large share of the world's finished 800G modules, pairing Western lasers with Broadcom and Marvell DSPs. We recently explored how this entanglement complicates any attempt to decouple the two ecosystems, even as the FCC is considering a ban on Chinese optical hardware. Coherent primarily sources substrates from AXT, while Lumentum relies heavily on Sumitomo and JX.
On the technical side, wafer-size limitations in InP semiconductors add another constraint. While silicon logic and memory moved to 300-mm wafers in the early 2000s, the InP industry is only now transitioning from 3-inch to 6-inch (150-mm) production; primarily because the material is brittle, expensive, and grown in small boules, factors that limit wafer size. Doubling the wafer diameter gives four times the area. Coherent's six-inch line, for example, yields more than four times as many devices as its three-inch line at a lower cost per die. On the other hand, moving a fab to six-inch requires new crystal-growth recipes, new handling equipment, new process qualification, and extensive customer requalification.
The supply chain was already struggling under these constraints when, in February 2025, Beijing placed InP, trimethylindium, triethylindium, and the technology used to produce them under export controls, requiring licenses for overseas shipments. AXT called the export controls its most significant current challenge, noting that even with sufficient capacity and strong demand, its ability to ship outside China depends on Chinese licensing decisions.
The shortfall and the race to expand
The widening gap between demand and InP industry output points to a fast-approaching shortfall. Coherent first warned of an InP shortage on its May earnings call. At the close of its fiscal year in August, CEO Jim Anderson described indium phosphide availability as the company's primary constraint, confirming that transceiver assembly and test capacity were available.
Lumentum CEO Hurlston said in July that telecom customers historically ordered lasers in the hundreds, while Nvidia and the hyperscalers were asking for hundreds of millions. Despite operating multiple InP fabs, Lumentum was shipping more than 30% below customer requirements. Earlier in the year, Hurlston said the company's capacity was sold out through 2027 and probably into 2028, even with the expanded output. In both cases, capacity was mostly bought out via Nvidia’s $4 billion investment.
To ease the multifaceted bottleneck, the industry is pursuing several solutions simultaneously, primarily expansions. Coherent is expanding its Sherman, Texas campus, reportedly described as the first and largest high-volume 6-inch InP semiconductor manufacturing facility. Washington signed a letter of intent in June for up to $50 million in CHIPS Act funding for the expansion. Coherent is now on track to double internal InP output in 2026, one quarter ahead of its original plan, and more than double it again by the end of 2027, while also adding 6-inch production in Sweden and Zurich.
Lumentum, meanwhile, is converting a 240,000-square-foot former Qorvo gallium-arsenide facility in North Carolina, which it bought for about $18 million, into another InP fab. The relevance of these expansions largely depends on the downstream InP substrate supply. Lumentum signed an agreement in July to reserve AXT InP substrate capacity through 2031, with an initial $43.5 million deposit and another $43.5 million payment contemplated for 2028. Coherent signed its own three-year 6-inch supply agreement with AXT a month earlier and prepaid $22.3 million against committed capacity.
The substrate suppliers are also expanding in kind. AXT is channeling fresh funds into Beijing Tongmei to double capacity by the end of 2026 and double it again in 2027. Similarly, JX Advanced Metals plans to invest roughly ¥120 billion ($746 million) through FY2030 to lift capacity seven to ten times above FY2025 levels, its largest-ever commitment in semiconductor materials.
Indium production — the uppermost stage of the stream — is far less active, with the biggest hurdle being the reliance on Zinc production. Global zinc mine production hasn't grown materially since 2011, sitting at or below 13 million tonnes a year, according to analysts. Wood Mackenzie expects just 0.1% growth in 2026. On the other hand, not everyone expects the crunch to last. LightCounting estimated in April that optical component demand exceeded supply by about 30% but projected that shortages would largely clear by the end of 2026 as new capacity comes online.
There are also viable, albeit slow, technical workarounds to ease the crunch. Heterogeneous integration bonds InP onto silicon to combine the strengths of both, while quantum dot lasers offer better temperature stability for uncooled operation. Furthermore, researchers continue to push InP quantum dot structures grown directly on silicon substrates. While these do not remove indium from the equation, they change how much each device needs and how it attaches, reducing consumption. Photonics is widely viewed as one of AI's major bottlenecks. However, the indium phosphide supply chain is itself tightening that bottleneck.
Etiido Uko is a news contributor for Tom's Hardware covering the latest updates in big tech and the PC industry. He is a mechanical engineer and senior technical writer with over nine years of experience in documentation and reporting. He is deeply passionate about all things engineering and technology, and is an expert in gadgets, manufacturing, robotics, automotive, and aerospace.

articles.title: Samsung QS90H : 13 haut-parleurs pour une immersion sans caisson
articles.text:
Vous ressentez comme une envie de donner une nouvelle dimension au son de votre téléviseur, sans transformer votre salon en installation home cinéma ? Bonne nouvelle, Samsung profite du Black Friday pour proposer sa nouvelle barre de son QS90H à 599 € seulement au lieu de 849 €.
Afin de pallier la relative faiblesse audio de nos Smart TV modernes, une barre de son permet de retrouver davantage d’ampleur dans les films, les séries ou les jeux vidéo, sans avoir pour cela à multiplier les enceintes dans la pièce et dénaturer le salon.
Avec sa QS90H, Samsung entend pousser le concept un peu plus loin. Cette barre de son tout-en-un rassemble pas moins de 13 haut-parleurs dans un seul et même boîtier, et promet une expérience sonore immersive en 7.1.2. Et à l’occasion du Black Friday, elle profite d’une remise de 250 €, faisant dégringoler son prix de 849 à 599 €. L’offre est annoncée du 26 novembre 2026 au 5 janvier 2027.
Samsung QS90H : 13 haut-parleurs pour retrouver une véritable immersion sonore
La QS90H adopte une configuration de type 7.1.2, avec des haut-parleurs orientés vers l’avant, les côtés, mais aussi les coins et le plafond. Cette disposition permet de diffuser le son dans plusieurs directions, afin de mieux envelopper les spectateurs. Au total, Samsung intègre 13 haut-parleurs donc, dont quatre woofers chargés de restituer les basses.
L’intérêt de cette conception tout-en-un ? Inutile d’installer un quelconque caisson de basses séparé pour profiter d’un rendu plus ample, puisque malgré son absence, la QS90H parvient à descendre jusqu’à 35 Hz dans les basses fréquences. La barre concentre l’ensemble des composants dans un seul appareil, ce qui permet de conserver une installation très sobre, très discrète, directement sous le téléviseur.
La compatibilité Dolby Atmos vient compléter cette configuration, et les bandes-son compatibles peuvent ainsi profiter d’une spatialisation en trois dimensions, avec des effets qui semblent provenir de différentes directions, y compris du dessus.
Avec les téléviseurs Samsung compatibles uniquement, la barre prend même en charge le Dolby Atmos sans fil via Wi-Fi, pour profiter des contenus compatibles sans avoir à la relier au téléviseur avec un câble HDMI.
Une barre de son qui adapte automatiquement son installation
C’est l’une des particularités les plus intéressantes de cette nouvelle QS90H : son étonnant design convertible. Grâce à un capteur gyroscopique intégré, la barre détecte automatiquement sa position et adapte le fonctionnement de ses haut-parleurs.
En d’autres termes, que vous choisissiez de la poser sur un meuble TV ou de la fixer au mur, elle reconnaît son agencement et se charge alors d’ajuster automatiquement la diffusion sonore. Une fonctionnalité particulièrement bienvenue, l’emplacement d’une barre de son ayant une influence directe sur le rendu audio ressenti.
Samsung ajoute également plusieurs technologies destinées à améliorer l’écoute au quotidien. SpaceFit Sound Pro ajuste notamment le son en fonction de la pièce, tandis que l’amplificateur vocal AVA Pro aide à conserver des dialogues audibles, même lorsque l’environnement est bruyant.
De quoi profiter plus confortablement d’un film ou d’une série, sans avoir à jongler constamment avec le volume.
Wi-Fi, Bluetooth, AirPlay, Chromecast… Une barre de son bien connectée
La Samsung QS90H ne se limite pas à la seule restitution sonore du téléviseur. Elle peut également servir à diffuser de la musique directement depuis un smartphone ou une tablette, pour animer une soirée par exemple. Pour cela, Samsung prévoit une connectivité Wi-Fi et Bluetooth, ainsi que la prise en charge de Chromecast, Apple AirPlay et Spotify Connect.
Côté branchements, la barre dispose d’une entrée HDMI 2.1 et d’une sortie HDMI eARC (4K 60 Hz), pour récupérer le son du téléviseur et profiter des formats audio compatibles. Si besoin, le kit d’enceintes arrière sans fil SWA-9500S permet de créer facilement un authentique son surround à la maison, et il est également possible d’associer à la QS90H des enceintes Music Studio 5 ou Music Studio 7.
Enfin, les possesseurs d’un téléviseur Samsung compatible pourront profiter de Q-Symphony, une technologie qui permet de faire fonctionner simultanément les haut-parleurs du téléviseur et ceux de la barre de son, avec pour objectif d’enrichir encore un peu plus la scène sonore.
8/10 dans le test de Clubic : une barre de son qui n'a pas besoin de caisson
Clubic a eu l'occasion de passer la QS90H sur le banc d'essai, et elle en ressort avec la note de 8/10. Dans son test, Guillaume Fourcadier décrit « une barre de son immersive, qui n'a pas besoin de caisson », dotée d'« une extension vraiment impressionnante dans les graves » et d'un rendu « percutant mais pas fatigant », qui « fait mouche sur les films spectaculaires ».
Black Friday : la Samsung QS90H passe à 599 € au lieu de 849 €
Avec sa configuration 7.1.2, ses 13 haut-parleurs intégrés et son installation convertible, la Samsung QS90H (et ses 6,7 kg sur la balance) s’adresse à tous ceux qui souhaitent améliorer le rendu audio de leur téléviseur, de manière très simple et sans multiplier les équipements dans le salon.
A l’occasion du Black Friday 2026, Samsung fait passer son prix de 849 à 599 €, soit 250 € de remise.
L’occasion de s’équiper enfin de cette barre de son premium qui nous tente depuis si longtemps, une barre de son compatible Dolby Atmos et suffisamment polyvalente pour accompagner aussi bien les soirées cinéma que les sessions de jeu ou l’écoute musicale.

articles.title: Plataforma de pagos Cleverbridge admitió el robo de números de tarjeta y códigos de seguridad
articles.text:
Cleverbridge, una empresa que procesa pagos y suscripciones para compañías de software, informó que atacantes accedieron a su plataforma y copiaron datos de tarjetas de compras. Según una notificación enviada a los afectados, entre los datos comprometidos figuran el número de tarjeta, la fecha de vencimiento y el código de seguridad CVV o CVC.
La compañía detectó actividad no autorizada el 4 de noviembre de 2026. Ese día desconectó temporalmente los sistemas afectados y los restableció, según el aviso público que emitió sobre el incidente. La investigación posterior confirmó que un tercero había copiado información almacenada en la plataforma.
Cleverbridge empezó a notificar a los afectados el 20 de noviembre, 16 días después de la detección. La empresa explicó que actuó con rapidez y que avisó sin demoras indebidas una vez que identificó a las personas cuyos datos pudieron quedar comprometidos.
BleepingComputer, el sitio especializado en seguridad informática que dio a conocer el caso el 22 de noviembre, tuvo acceso a una de esas notificaciones. El texto indica que no se copiaron otros datos personales, como el nombre, los datos de contacto o los de facturación.
Sin información sobre la cantidad de afectados
El aviso público de Cleverbridge habla de una cantidad limitada de datos personales y de una pequeña cantidad de datos de tarjetas. Sobre el código de seguridad, precisa que en una minoría de los casos la información incluyó el CVV. La notificación a la que tuvo acceso BleepingComputer lo menciona sin esa salvedad.
La empresa no informó cuántas personas resultaron afectadas, cómo entraron los atacantes ni cuánto tiempo estuvieron dentro de sus sistemas. Tampoco dijo si los datos de las tarjetas estaban cifrados ni por qué el código de seguridad estaba disponible en la plataforma. El medio especializado le hizo esas preguntas y no recibió respuesta.
Cleverbridge descartó que se trate de un ataque de ransomware, es decir, de un programa que bloquea los sistemas para exigir un rescate: aseguró que ninguno de sus sistemas fue cifrado. La firma indicó que informó del caso a las autoridades de protección de datos, a la policía, a las redes de tarjetas y a sus socios de pago.
La compañía ofrece a los afectados un servicio gratuito de monitoreo de crédito o identidad, donde esté disponible. La gestión de los avisos está a cargo de TransUnion/Cyberscout, un proveedor externo. Cleverbridge aclara que esas comunicaciones son legítimas.
Empresas involucradas
Cleverbridge vende como intermediario en nombre de otras empresas, por lo que muchos compradores no saben que su pago pasó por allí. BleepingComputer indica que la firma lista entre sus clientes a Red Hat, SUSE, Tenable, Veeam, Jamf, Sony y Parallels.
Ni la compañía ni el sitio especializado precisan qué clientes tuvieron compradores afectados. Cleverbridge explica en su sección de preguntas frecuentes que tiene los datos de una persona porque se usaron en una compra a uno de los negocios que atiende.
Para quienes recibieron la notificación, la empresa recomienda revisar con atención los resúmenes de la tarjeta y avisar de inmediato al banco emisor ante cualquier movimiento desconocido. El banco puede decidir reemplazar la tarjeta, y conviene seguir sus indicaciones.
La firma también pide desconfiar de correos, llamadas o mensajes inesperados sobre el incidente, y aclara que nunca solicita datos de tarjeta, contraseñas ni códigos de seguridad por correo electrónico, teléfono o mensaje de texto. La investigación sigue en curso, según su aviso público, y no se ha anunciado una fecha para una nueva actualización.

articles.title: Melhor ar-condicionado 9.000 BTUs em 2026: qual modelo comprar?
articles.text:
Melhor ar-condicionado 9.000 BTUs em 2026: qual modelo comprar?
Guia de compras reúne os melhores ar-condicionados inverter de 9.000 BTUs em eficiência energética, conectividade, durabilidade e preço
Escolher o melhor ar-condicionado de 9.000 BTUs em 2026 exige olhar além da capacidade térmica para quartos e escritórios compactos. Com os novos parâmetros de eficiência energética (IDRS) do Inmetro, as diferenças entre modelos envolvem consumo anual, ruído, conectividade e resistência da unidade externa.
Nesta seleção, reunimos dez opções de ar-condicionado inverter de 9.000 BTUs disponíveis no Brasil, comparando preços encontrados, recursos inteligentes e pontos de atenção. Seja para economizar na conta de luz, evitar vento direto ou gastar o mínimo possível na compra, há um modelo adequado para cada perfil de uso.
Conteúdo gerado por IA ✨
Esse conteúdo foi gerado com auxílio de inteligência artificial e revisado pelo time de especialistas do Tecnoblog.
O Midea AI Ecomaster entrega equilíbrio entre economia na conta de luz, automações inteligentes e proteção contra corrosão sem disparar no preço. Para quem busca conforto contínuo sem precisar ajustar o controle o tempo todo, o aparelho adapta o funcionamento ao ambiente e à rotina da casa.
Na parte técnica, o modelo reúne inteligência artificial (AI Ecomaster e controle de umidade), fluido refrigerante R-32, IDRS de 7,6, consumo anual estimado de 286,8 kWh e conectividade via aplicativo com suporte a assistentes de voz. Ele também traz o pacote Prime Guard com Gold Fin, proteção anticorrosão na placa eletrônica e autolimpeza reversa da condensadora, além de filtragem Air Magic com tripla filtragem e íons negativos.
Como ponto de atenção, a unidade condensadora é um pouco mais larga que a média da categoria, o que pede conferência prévia do espaço externo. Ainda assim, é uma das escolhas mais completas da faixa intermediária para quem quer eficiência sazonal elevada e recursos conectados.
O Daikin EcoSwing Smart Gold é voltado a quem prioriza eficiência energética máxima, silêncio e durabilidade acima do custo inicial. Na prática, ele se destaca em quartos ou escritórios usados por muitas horas seguidas, onde o baixo consumo anual e a operação discreta fazem diferença no dia a dia.
Esses benefícios são sustentados pelo compressor EcoSwing Inverter, gás R-32, serpentina de cobre, classificação energética A no Inmetro com 263 kWh/ano de consumo normalizado e ruído interno que vai de 25 dB(A) a 38 dB(A). O modelo também conta com ciclo quente e frio e Wi-Fi integrado com suporte ao aplicativo Daikin Smart AC e comandos de voz via Google Assistente e Alexa.
O principal entrave é o preço de aquisição bem superior ao da média do segmento. Para quem pretende usar o equipamento intensamente por anos e busca confiabilidade mecânica e eficiência de topo, o investimento tende a se justificar.
O Samsung WindFree AI Pro (a partir de R$ 2.184,05 na Amazon) é indicado para quem se incomoda com o jato de ar frio direto no corpo, especialmente durante o sono ou o trabalho. Em vez de manter o fluxo intenso após atingir a temperatura desejada, ele dispersa o ar suavemente por milhares de microfuros.
A proposta combina o modo WindFree com recursos de inteligência artificial e integração completa ao ecossistema SmartThings, permitindo automações, rotinas e monitoramento pelo celular. É uma opção atualizada para quem já utiliza dispositivos conectados da marca e busca maior conforto térmico sem sensação de corrente de ar forte.
Por outro lado, o valor fica acima dos modelos de entrada, e quem gosta de sentir rajadas rápidas de vento direto pode notar uma adaptação gradual ao fluxo difuso. É uma escolha certeira para quem valoriza suavidade no clima e conectividade avançada.
O LG Dual Inverter Compact +AI atende bem a quem busca estabilidade de temperatura e resposta rápida de resfriamento. Ele funciona bem em ambientes de uso frequente nos quais manter a faixa térmica sem oscilações bruscas é prioridade.
Por trás dessa experiência está o compressor Dual Inverter, projetado para operar com maior estabilidade térmica e controle de consumo, aliado aos recursos de inteligência artifical. O formato compacto da linha também ajuda na composição visual de espaços menores.
Um ponto de atenção é a integração limitada com o app LG ThinQ. Como o aparelho não tem Wi-Fi, não é possível controlar o ar-condicionado pelo aplicativo ou usar comandos de voz. Ele serve apenas para funções de suporte e pós-venda.
O Gree G-Side Auto Inverter é uma alternativa para quem busca construção robusta, boa distribuição de ar e confiabilidade de uma fabricante especializada em climatização. O modelo entrega resfriamento ágil e operação silenciosa para o uso cotidiano.
Entre as especificações, o aparelho utiliza fluido R-32, serpentina de cobre com proteção Goldenfin na condensadora e Bluefin na evaporadora, IDRS de 7,01 Wh/Wh, consumo de 311 kWh/ano e 7 velocidades de ventilação. Ele também traz Wi-Fi integrado com compatibilidade para o app Gree+, Google Assistente e Alexa, além de proteção contra oscilações de tensão.
A principal limitação está no ecossistema smart, menos popular no Brasil que os de LG ou Samsung. Para quem prioriza durabilidade construtiva e desempenho térmico sólido, continua sendo uma opção equilibrada.
O Electrolux Color Adapt Inverter foi pensado para quem quer esconder ou harmonizar o ar-condicionado com a decoração do ambiente, sem abrir mão da tecnologia inverter. Ele funciona bem em salas, quartos planejados ou estúdios onde o apelo estético pesa tanto quanto a climatização.
Seu grande diferencial é o painel personalizável para pintura, que permite adaptar o visual da unidade interna à cor da parede, somado a uma unidade externa compacta e fluxo de ar indireto. A linha também oferece controle automático de temperatura e acabamento anticorrosão.
Em contrapartida, o foco estético e a proposta de personalização elevam o preço em comparação a modelos básicos de 9.000 BTUs. Vale a pena quando a integração visual com o cômodo é um critério decisivo.
O Elgin Eco Inverter III é indicado para quem quer gastar menos sem abrir mão de gás atual, conectividade Wi-Fi e versatilidade de ciclo. É uma escolha prática para quartos ou escritórios em regiões que alternam dias quentes e períodos mais frios.
O modelo traz fluido refrigerante R-32, conectividade Wi-Fi via aplicativo AC Elgin Smart com suporte a Alexa e Google Assistente, controle remoto iluminado e opções de ciclo frio ou quente/frio na linha. Essa combinação entrega recursos úteis na faixa econômica sem exigir salto de orçamento.
Por outro lado, o aplicativo é mais simples e o refinamento acústico e aerodinâmico fica abaixo dos modelos mais caros da lista. Ainda assim, oferece um pacote competitivo para quem busca custo-benefício com conectividade.
O Hisense Eco Plus II Inverter aparece como uma das portas de entrada mais baratas entre os splits inverter atuais. Ele atende bem a quem busca economia na compra e operação inverter eficiente para ambientes compactos.
Na ficha técnica, o aparelho opera com gás refrigerante R-32 e tecnologia inverter voltada à redução do consumo em relação aos modelos convencionais, mantendo um conjunto direto para o uso diário. É uma alternativa interessante para reduzir o desembolso inicial sem ficar preso a refrigerantes antigos.
Como ponto de atenção, a rede de assistência técnica e o ecossistema conectado têm menor capilaridade no Brasil em comparação a marcas tradicionais. Se a disponibilidade local de serviços pesa na sua decisão, vale verificar o atendimento na sua cidade antes da compra.
O TCL BreezeIn Inverter é voltado a quem precisa climatizar quartos ou escritórios pequenos com orçamento contido e funções inverter essenciais. Ele entrega estabilidade térmica básica para rotinas simples sem cobrar por recursos avançados.
A linha reúne os fundamentos da operação inverter em um conjunto acessível, pensado para manter o ambiente agradável com consumo controlado em comparação a aparelhos convencionais. Para espaços compactos e de uso direto, cumpre o papel sem complicações.
Em troca do preço mais baixo, traz menos recursos inteligentes e acabamentos mais simples frente aos modelos intermediários. É uma opção funcional para quem quer um inverter econômico no dia a dia.
O Philco Split Hi Wall Inverter é uma alternativa econômica para quem busca funções diretas do dia a dia, filtragem básica e preço competitivo no varejo. Serve bem a quartos ou salas pequenas com uso regular e sem exigência de automações complexas.
O modelo conta com tecnologia inverter, gás R-32, classificação energética A, serpentina de cobre, modos de operação essenciais (como resfriar, desumidificar, ventilar e dormir) e filtro lavável antibacteriano e antifungos. Também traz resfriamento rápido e garantia estendida de 10 anos no compressor conforme condições do fabricante.
Como contrapartida, tem menor destaque em eficiência sazonal e menos recursos avançados de automação em relação aos primeiros colocados do guia. Ainda assim, é uma opção acessível e direta para climatizar ambientes compactos.
Escolher o melhor ar-condicionado 9.000 BTUs em 2026 exige observar o tamanho do ambiente e a combinação entre tecnologia Inverter, boa eficiência energética e baixo ruído. Além disso, analise os seguintes critérios:
- Tecnologia Inverter: mantém o compressor em rotação contínua para estabilizar a temperatura e reduzir o consumo elétrico em comparação aos modelos convencionais on/off.
- Eficiência energética e IDRS: priorize aparelhos com classificação Classe A e maior Índice de Desempenho de Resfriamento Sazonal, indicador que avalia o rendimento ao longo do ano.
- Gás refrigerante e serpentina: o fluido R-32 alia eficiência térmica a menor impacto ambiental, enquanto a serpentina de cobre com proteção anticorrosiva ajuda na durabilidade, especialmente perto do litoral.
- Ruído e fluxo de ar: em quartos, níveis de ruído próximos de 35 dB a 40 dB na unidade interna e a difusão suave do ar evitam desconforto durante o sono.
- Ciclo, voltagem e conectividade: defina entre Só Frio ou Quente e Frio, confirme a tensão elétrica do ponto de instalação (comum em 220V nessa faixa) e avalie o uso de Wi-Fi, aplicativo ou comandos de voz.
Um aparelho de 9.000 BTUs costuma atender bem ambientes compactos de cerca de 12 m² a 15 m², como quartos, home offices ou salas pequenas com pouca incidência solar direta e número reduzido de pessoas e aparelhos eletrônicos. Incidência intensa de sol, grandes janelas de vidro ou equipamentos que geram calor podem exigir potência superior para evitar que o compressor trabalhe no limite.
O modelo inverter ajusta continuamente a velocidade do compressor para manter a temperatura estável sem picos constantes de liga e desliga, o que reduz o consumo de energia elétrica, diminui oscilações térmicas e tende a tornar o funcionamento mais silencioso ao longo do uso. Já o modelo convencional opera em ciclos intermitentes de partida e parada, geralmente com custo inicial menor, mas maior gasto energético em períodos prolongados.
O fluido refrigerante R-32 consolidou-se como padrão em grande parte das linhas atuais no Brasil por oferecer boa eficiência térmica e menor potencial de aquecimento global (GWP) em comparação ao antigo R-410A. Ao escolher um split inverter, vale verificar a compatibilidade do gás com as ferramentas e procedimentos da equipe de instalação.
Na prática, o impacto na conta de luz depende mais do tempo de uso diário, da temperatura programada e do isolamento térmico do cômodo do que apenas da capacidade nominal de 9.000 BTUs. Em comparação aos splits convencionais de velocidade fixa, os modelos inverter costumam apresentar consumo anual menor em regimes prolongados, especialmente quando comparamos o consumo anual em kWh/ano e o índice IDRS na etiqueta do Inmetro.
Além do preço do equipamento, o orçamento deve prever tubulação, suporte, disjuntor/rede elétrica adequada e mão de obra especializada, já que uma instalação mal executada compromete o desempenho, aumenta o consumo e pode invalidar a garantia do fabricante. Também é importante conferir a voltagem do aparelho (127V ou 220V) e o espaço físico disponível para a unidade condensadora.

articles.title: IA : Microsoft alerte sur une vague de pannes à venir dans la tech
articles.text:
L'explosion de la puissance de l'IA oblige les systèmes à une mise à jour très rapide. Ce qui, selon le président de Microsoft, va entraîner nécessairement un certain nombre de problèmes.
La puissance de l'intelligence artificielle se fait aujourd'hui surtout sentir dans le secteur de la cybersécurité, avec la capacité exceptionnelle de l'IA à détecter les vulnérabilités dans les systèmes. Il est donc nécessaire de rapidement patcher des systèmes quelques fois assez vieux, et pour Brad Smith, le président de Microsoft, il faudra s'attendre à ce que ça accroisse temporairement le risque de panne !
L'IA va découvrir de très nombreuses vulnérabilités dans les systèmes ces prochains mois
Brad Smith, le président de Microsoft, s'est ces derniers jours exprimé dans un entretien avec CBS News sur la question de la cybersécurité aujourd'hui. Il a ainsi expliqué que l'arrivée de l'IA obligeait à une transformation, sans précédent dans sa vitesse, des systèmes informatiques.
« Partout dans le monde, les acteurs disposant des moyens technologiques nécessaires utilisent ces [IA] pour identifier les failles et les corriger à un rythme sans précédent, afin de devancer les cybercriminels et de les empêcher de s'en servir pour pirater les systèmes » a-t-il expliqué. Mais en voulant prendre de vitesse les cybercriminels, on peut se créer de nouveaux problèmes.
La pression mise sur les systèmes par les correctifs accroît les possibilités de panne
Brad Smith note en effet que ce rythme d'enfer sera appliqué sur des infrastructures qui peuvent être assez souvent anciennes, et que la vitesse à laquelle les correctifs doivent être appliqués empêche de tester dans les meilleurs conditions les modifications apportées au code. Résultat, « on augmente alors le risque que quelque chose tourne mal ». Brad Smith appelle ce phénomène, les « effets d'entraînement liés à l'IA » (« AI ripple effects »).
Reste que, de toute manière, les divisions IT à travers le monde n'ont pas d'autre choix que de rapidement se mettre à jour, malgré les risques évoqués. Microsoft avait en effet déjà expliqué, dans une publication officielle portant sur la cybersécurité en date du 19 novembre, le fait que les cybercrminels découvraient de plus en plus de failles logicielles avant même que les différentes organisations n'aient le temps d'apporter de correctif. Raison pour laquelle sûrement on observe toutes ces grandes cyberattaques actuellement.
Source : Wccftech

articles.title: Más del 80% de las personas admiten querer alejarse de sus dispositivos, según un estudio
articles.text:
Los investigadores de la Universidad de Bath y la Universidad Goethe de Fráncfort desarrollaron y validaron la primera escala científica para medir la actitud de las personas hacia la desintoxicación digital (la reducción deliberada del uso de dispositivos tecnológicos), y hallaron que más del 80% de los participantes se mostraron favorables a la idea de desconectarse temporalmente de las pantallas.
La investigación, publicada en la revista académica Psychology & Marketing, liderada por el equipo de ambas universidades europeas, parte de una realidad cada vez más extendida: correos electrónicos laborales, mensajería instantánea, redes sociales, notificaciones automáticas y recomendaciones generadas por inteligencia artificial compiten de forma creciente por la atención de los usuarios.
Frente a ese escenario, la desintoxicación digital término que designa la reducción voluntaria y temporal del tiempo frente a pantallas ganó relevancia como práctica de autocuidado. El equipo construyó una herramienta de medición denominada escala de Actitud hacia la Desintoxicación Digital (ADD), compuesta por siete ítems que evalúan qué tan positivamente percibe una persona la posibilidad de reducir su consumo virtual de manera transitoria.
Más del 80% de los participantes quiso desconectarse, aunque no se midió si lo hicieron
Para validar la escala, los investigadores realizaron siete estudios con grupos de colaboradores de distintos perfiles: adultos residentes en Estados Unidos reclutados mediante plataformas de investigación en línea, estudiantes universitarios de Europa Central, miembros de comunidades de Reddit orientadas tanto a actividades digitales como presenciales, y especialistas en comportamiento del consumidor de universidades europeas.
De acuerdo con el artículo divulgado en Phys.org, los resultados mostraron que más del 80% de los participantes expresó una predisposición favorable hacia la desintoxicación digital, lo que sugiere un deseo generalizado de reducir el tiempo de exposición a dispositivos. Sin embargo, el estudio aclaró que no evaluó si esa disposición se tradujo finalmente en un cambio de conducta.
Además, la investigación identificó que las actitudes medidas por la escala ADD se asociaban con rasgos como la atención plena (la capacidad de estar presente en el momento sin distracciones) y el autocontrol; ambas características mostraron una relación con la predisposición a desconectarse.
La herramienta predice el tiempo que los usuarios dedican a ver videos en línea
Uno de los hallazgos más concretos del estudio fue que las puntuaciones obtenidas en la medición podían ayudar a anticipar cuánto tiempo dedicaban los sujetos a ver vídeos en línea posteriormente. Esto convierte a la herramienta en un posible predictor del comportamiento tecnológico futuro.
Jan Landwehr, profesor de la Universidad Goethe de Fráncfort, explicó el origen del proyecto: “Muchas personas se sienten abrumadas por el flujo constante de información digital y experimentan la necesidad de desconectarse. Desarrollamos una escala de medición científicamente validada para cuantificar esta vaga actitud positiva hacia la reducción de las actividades digitales”. El profesor añadió que “la gran mayoría de nuestros participantes tiene una necesidad latente de desintoxicarse de las actividades digitales”.
Según los investigadores, medir estas posturas ofrece un nuevo enfoque para analizar la relación de los individuos con la tecnología, en particular para comprender qué motiva a algunas a querer desconectarse, por qué hay quienes son más receptivas a esa idea que otras y si esa disposición puede transformarse en hábitos concretos.
La herramienta podría usarse para estudiar cuándo y por qué se busca la desconexión
El profesor Torsten Bornemann, también de la Universidad Goethe de Fráncfort, amplió las posibles aplicaciones: “Esta escala podría utilizarse para explorar cuándo y por qué las personas desean reducir su consumo digital y si un cambio de actitud hacia la desconexión podría, en última instancia, ayudar a las personas a tener un mayor control sobre su relación con la tecnología”.
Los autores señalan que la herramienta representa un avance metodológico en el campo del comportamiento del consumidor virtual, ya que hasta ahora no existía una escala validada diseñada específicamente para cuantificar esta predisposición.
La diferencia respecto a instrumentos anteriores radica en que la ADD no mide el tiempo real de uso de pantallas ni el grado de dependencia tecnológica, sino la predisposición psicológica hacia la reducción voluntaria de ese uso.

articles.title: Amazon's Black Friday sale is live for Australia and I'm hunting the top deals — these are my picks for the 70+ best discounts
articles.text:

There are some all-time low prices on coffee machines, air fryers, vacuums, headphones and more

The biggest sale of the year will continue through to Cyber Monday on November 30, giving you 14 days of deals mayhem.

• Shop all Amazon Black Friday deals

Editor's picks: today's top deals
This USB-C charger is extremely compact, which makes it an ideal choice to leave in a bag as a backup option. It can fast charge most phones and with 20V output, even top up a laptop if needed.
We may not have tested these buds ourselves here at TechRadar, but it’s hard to ignore the 100K customer reviews on Amazon. While often discounted to this price, if you’re after dependable Bluetooth buds on a budget, these are a great option.
Apple’s second-gen AirTag is a handy buy if you want one tracker for keys, a wallet or luggage rather than committing to the four-pack. In our AirTag 2 review, we found the familiar setup and tracking experience felt better than before, helped by improved Find My range and a louder chime.
The MacBook Neo hasn't seen much in the way of discounts yet (in fact, it has had a price rise), so this meagre drop is the best we have seen. Still, it's something at least, and it's well worth checking out our MacBook Neo review for the full scoop.
Boasting a 12,000dpi 'Hero' sensor, as well as 6 programmable buttons, a 250-hour battery and onboard memory for your settings, the Logitech G305 Lightspeed Wireless Gaming Mouse is ideal for competitive play. Want to know more? Check out our review, but not that only the blue and lilac colourways get the best discount.
While they don't include ANC, these affordable Sony headphones are still a solid buy, plus this is the best price we have seen on Amazon so far. In our Sony WH-CH530 review we said that "they supply great sound for the price, with beautiful warm bass, clean mids, and expressive treble."
This little pod machine is very popular among TechRadar's Aussie team. We've had past and present staff say how much they love it, and they'd even buy it at full price. With a very compact footprint and plenty of Vertuo pods to choose from, you'll get delicious coffee at just the press of a button.
If you're after a compact model that can feed one or two people, this Philips option is great for under a hundred dollary-doos. It's been hovering around the AU$95 mark for a while, so it's quite the best deal, but it's still a discount that's hard to pass up on an air fryer with a staggering 13 preset cooking options.
This discount matches the Blink Video Doorbell System’s last all-time low price during the last Prime Day sale in July. It’s worth noting, though, that many of the features are locked behind the AU$4.95/m Blink Basic or AU$15/m Blink Plus subscription plans, so those costs should be considered if you want video storage, person detection and more.
Already quite affordable, this Blink video doorbell can rival anything from the more expensive Ring line, while also offering a long battery life and IP65 weatherproofing. Also included is the Sync Module that you'll need to make everything work, but you will need to take into account that it requires a Blink Subscription Plan if you want all its functions at your fingertips.
If you're after a really good electric toothbrush that won't cost an arm and a leg (or some teeth), then this is it. It's an entry-level oscillating brush, which means it rotates at fast speeds and may not be ideal for people with sensitive or bleeding gums as that movement can be harsh, but it sure does remove a heck of a lot of plaque and keeps your teeth healthy.
If you don't enjoy flossing the traditional way, use the power of water instead. Removing plaque using three different water pressure settings, this handy flosser will clean out those hard-to-reach gaps that your toothbrush can't. Plus, it's cordless, meaning you can take it on your travels too. Admittedly these were a lot cheaper in July (just over AU$48), but it was bestseller then, so it would be remiss of me to not include it here again.
The Lavazza Jolie machines are excellent and affordable alternatives to Nespresso. This Evo model just has a single button for extracting coffee (compared to the Jolie Plus that has programmable buttons), making it oh so simple to use.
This food processor's biggest drawcard is its small footprint (30cm tall and 16cm wide), making it great for those with smaller kitchens, but it also has a powerful 650W motor to help blitz foods to slice, grate, chop and knead in seconds. This is the lowest price we've seen for the MultiPro Go, and you can read the full review here.
We might be in the middle of winter, but there's no denying some parts of Australia need a good fan year round. This Vornado model creates tornado-like air flow that circulates around the room. Note that this is the smallest model in the range, ideal for bedrooms.
While often discounted to around this same price, we haven't seen the Nebula Mars 3 go lower, and it's a great deal. It serves up great brightness levels for a portable model, although you'll benefit most from watching at night.
Amazon devices
Amazon's current midrange 7-inch Kindle has dropped to cost less than its newer 6-inch sibling in this Black Friday deal, making it the best choice if you want to pick up one of Amazon's e-readers on the cheap. That said, with more storage than the standard model, a brighter screen and wireless charging, the Paperwhite Signature Edition is arguably better value than the base model above if you think you'll make full use of the storage and its wireless charging capabilities. It's currently down to AU$257, or 36% off.
The Kindle Colorsoft is one of the best ereaders with a colour display, even offering a feature to make the hues more vivid. While I wouldn't recommend at full price, this discount makes it a little easier on the pocket for the 32GB version that also has wireless charging.
Kindles are known for their reading capabilities, but with the Kindle Scribe, you get that and a whole lot more. With a wide range of writing features, you can take notes, create sketches and brainstorm like a pro. I love its 10.2-inch glare-free screen with an ambient light sensor, and it's battery life is excellent too. It's now the previous-gen model, but arguably better value than the 2025 3rd-gen release.
Amazon's Echo Dot it's a great smart speaker with decent sound and Alexa built-in. It also has motion detection and can measure temperature, which is handy if you have a connected thermostat. It is a little long in the tooth now, having released in 2022, but it's a bargain at this price.
The Echo Dot Max features almost 3x the bass of the Echo Dot (5th gen), and its sound can automatically adapt to your space, making it the perfect addition to any smart home or party setup. We gave it a nice 4 stars in our review, namely for its great smart home capabilities and stellar sound. Now at its lowest-ever price.
Launched in October, the latest Echo home display devices have gotten a much-needed glow-up Echo Show 8 and the Echo Show 11. Aside from the updated in-cell touch and negative liquid crystal screens, both devices include new front-facing stereo speakers and a custom woofer for room-filling spatial audio. The key difference between the two? The Echo Show 8 has a smaller 8.7-inch display.
With all the same great features as the new Echo Show 8 above, if you're after a larger home display screen to connect to your Ring devices, check recipes while cooking or control your smart devices using Alexa, then the 11-inch Echo Show could be the move for you. Also discounted by 35%.
Headphones & Audio
We gave these earbuds a very impressive 4.5-stars in our Sony WF-C510 review, and slapped them with the 'TechRadar Recommends' award. We were so impressed, we'd actually pick these over the Apple AirPods 4. While we didn't love the 11 hours of charge provided by the case, the earbuds themselves will last 11 hours before needing to return to the case – making them equally excellent sounding, feeling and long-lasting.
These affordable earbuds with ANC are brimming with features, including a range of ANC modes, EQ presets and other audio adjustments. They sound good (but you'll want to tweak it from the default) and they'll last up to 7.5 hours with ANC on before they need a recharge. Check out our Earfun Air Pro 4 review for more info and take advantage of this offer.
The JBL Grip plugs the gap between the smaller Clip and formidable Flip. It's a compact speaker that delivers a big sound, offers impressive protection against dust and water and has some nifty LED lighting on its rear.
If you're looking for a great set of noise-cancelling over-ears but don't want to pay a lot of cash, this deal on the excellent WH-CH730N headphones is worth a look. As we said in our WH-CH730N review, they offer great value-for-money option with an excellent set of features, solid sound quality, and a nifty, foldable design,
The Beats Pill is a sturdy, classy portable speaker that you can use anywhere from the living room to the poolside, thanks to its IP67 waterproof and dustproof rating. It also has a substantial 24-hour battery life, so you can listen for a long time without worrying about recharging. This matches the last all-time low from February 2026.
Offering “incredible sound” according to our review, the Bose Ultra Open Earbuds have all the power and quality you’d expect from a Bose-branded item while providing the benefits of an open-ear form factor. The Immersive sound is excellent, and they give up to 7 hours of music. While they have been slightly cheaper, this is the not far off the best price we have seen since lately.
We gave these stunning earbuds 4.5 stars in our review as they have class-leading audio handling and impeccable sound quality that rivals the best wireless earbuds. With balanced sound, effective ANC and a great battery life, these Sennheiser buds will make any audiophile smile.
Dropping to the the lowest price we've seen, this is a fine chance to snap up Apple's flagship earbuds. The ANC is best-in-class, and the sound and fit have been improved over the Pro 2. Check out our review for the full story.
The original QC Ultra was already an excellent set of ANC cans, and now these Gen2 Bose QC Ultras reassert the brand's true mastery of sound and noise cancellation. Check out our review for the full scoop.
Now down to AU$797 in all colours, there's never been a better time to secure Apple's ridiculously good noise cancelling over ears. While the design hasn't changed much, the internals have been upgraded to deliver even better ANC performance, Lossless audio over USB-C and a wealth of useful features made possible by the new H2 chip.
There's much to be said still of wired headphones, as they offer a more reliable and stronger connection to your source devices. You will likely need a 3.5mm-to-USB or -Lightning adapter (or one of the best headphone DACs) to get them connected to your phone, but do so and you’ll be rewarded with a gorgeous, high-fidelity sound. And, being Sennheiser, they’re impeccably built and are super comfortable to wear for longer sessions.
The JBL Charge 5 can bring the party, and quite loudly I might add. I use this Bluetooth speaker at home myself and love it, with up to 20 hours of playback. It's also dust and waterproof (IP67 rating), so you can take anywhere, plus it will double as a phone charger in a pinch if you need some extra juice on your handset.
We haven’t reviewed this Bose soundbar, but if it’s anything like the brand’s other models, we’re confident it will do a mighty fine job of boosting the sound from your TV, ideal when watching movies. If you want to add even more low-end grunt, it works with the company’s Bass Modules (sold separately). A Dialogue mode helps to boost vocals, and if you fancy a dance around your bedroom or living room, Bluetooth is onboard for you to stream your favourite tunes.
Coffee machines
This do-it-all machine from Ninja really can make pretty much any coffee you could want, whether it be hot or iced. It will select the right grind size, has user profiles to store settings, and even two bean hoppers so you can swap out for different beans.
Also available in stainless steel for the same AU$948 price.
The best entry-level bean-to-cup coffee maker has received a good discount for Black Friday, although not quite as good as the AU$359 we saw during Prime Day. It's simple to use, taking care of the grinding, tamping and pouring for you. The porta filter will even automatically slide into position for you. Do note there's no milk frothing here, but a matching milk frother is available.
This compact manual coffee machine can pour up to two espresso shots at once and features a steam wand for cafe-quality milk foaming. There's no built-in grinder, but you either use ground coffee beans or invest in a separate grinder using the cash you save with this deal.
If you've already got a decent coffee maker but one without a grinder, just add this Breville machine to get fresh ground coffee. It has over 60 settings for precise control over your beans, meaning you should be able to extract the most delicious shot from the grind catering to your taste.
A welcome saving on Breville's answer to the SodaStream. Not only can you use the InFizz Fusion to carbonate water, but you can fizz any liquid you can think of — other than hot beverages of course. This nifty machine is sure to be a hit during at-home cocktail nights.
The Breville Bambino Plus is incredibly simple to use, and can take care of most of the coffee making process for you. Grind some beans into the porta filter, insert it into the group head and use the one-touch controls to brew. It also has a hands-free milk texturing system for expertly frothed milk, while ThermoJet technology means the machine is ready to use in seconds. There's very little you need to do to simply enjoy the results — now AU$20 more than what it cost at the start of the sale.
With a nice saving, it's hard to dismiss this Breville coffee machine deal. The Barista Express has a built-in grinder, tamper, and bean hopper, so there's no need to buy a separate grinder or hand tamp. Available in a few colourways under the same listing, only the Charcoal model gets the full discount.
If you’re after a coffee that makes itself, then it’s hard to go past the Breville Creatista Plus. A great compact pod machine that uses the Original Nespresso pods, and one that can also do milk frothing without requiring a whole other appliance.
We've only reviewed the more expensive Touch model, but if you take your coffee seriously – and want a barista-level cup of joe easily, this is the deal for you. Offering automatic grinding, dosing, tamping and milk texturing, this machine lets you go from beans to latte in seconds.
Vacuum cleaners
The Shark PowerDetect UV Reveal uses light to pick up hidden stains on your floors, has a heated mop pad and anti-tangle brush roller, and is equipped with LiDAR navigation. Now discounted for Amazon's Black Friday sale, this new Shark robovac is hard to pass up. Also available in Café Noir Mocha for AU$1,070.
This affordable Dreame stick vac can handle regular everyday cleaning tasks — it may not be the most powerful tool in the shed, but it sure will keep it clean. Even handy for the boat, the car or your home for not a lot of cash.
Now down by a huge AU$660, Dyson's Detect Submarine houses a powerful suction and a superb runtime of up to 60 minutes. It can handle all floor types, including wet and dry messes.
We haven't tested this cordless vacuum ourselves but user reviews are glowing and I think that says something. For quick and daily vacuuming. This one always proves popular during major sales, and I reckon it will be once more, as this is a new all-time low price in Australia.
In our Ecovacs Deebot X8 Pro Omni review, in which it scored an impressive 4.5-star score, we called it a "chatty all-in-one robot vacuum that cleans better than most others". Its biggest drawback is its regular price, but this deal takes care of that — letting you enjoy its strong suction, efficient edge cleaning, effective mopping and smart navigation.
A huge discount on what is a relatively new flagship model from Ecovacs. We haven't tested this version out yet, but if it works as well as the previous X8 Pro Omni did, then I think this is a good premium robovac to consider without the hefty price tag.
Kitchen Appliances
The Nutribullet is great value if you need a powerful blender for your liquid breakfast needs. In fact, it will even come in handy if you want to use it as a regular blender to make sauces, dips and small batches of soup. This model has a 900W motor and comes with a single 700ml cup.
The Ninja Slushi lets you skip the ice and still enjoy perfectly smooth icy drinks with very little effort. Whether you're craving a frappe, smoothie, or even a cheeky spiked slushi, its multiple drink modes have you covered. Even better, the current deal price is near to the lowest we have seen on Amazon. Check out our Ninja Slushi review for the full rundown.
This compact air fryer packs 1700W of power into a portable design, with two borosilicate glass containers that serve as both frying baskets and serving dishes. The borosilicate glass can withstand extreme temperatures, making it easy to take your favourite foods from frozen to crispy, and it's safer to use than any non-stick basket. The Crispi also comes with two removable crisping grates and two snap-on container lids for easy storage.
It's got a cult-like following and two members of our own staff are massive fans. If you love your chilled desserts — ice creams, gelatos, smoothies — but want to control your calorie intake, you really should consider getting the Ninja Creami. This Deluxe edition gets you three containers, which is great value at this price.
Not a big discount and even I balk at recommending a toaster that costs more then AU$50, but I have the Black Truffle model of this 2-slice toaster and trust me when I say it's one of the best toasters I've used. Sure, it's overkill for the average person but if you can get the perfect toast every morning (or arvo or evening), I think it's worth considering.
This Shark fan has twisting ends that allow it to shoot air out in any direction. The blades can be positioned horizontally or vertically too, and while the ends need manual intervention, all other controls can be adjusted via a remote control.
PC & Gaming
This lovely little vertical mouse has dropped as low as AU$67, but I think this is still an excellent price to pay for the pointer I use every day myself. It's perfect for small mitts and encourages better posture, helping ease wrist, shoulder, and shoulder blade discomfort. And, for once, all three colour variants are around the same price.
A 100Hz-refresh-rate monitor for just AU$100? Sign me up! This display from Lenovo may be a bit small at under 24 inches with a 1080p resolution, but it uses IPS technology for sharp image quality. This is price is the lowest we've seen this monitor go on Amazon.
This handheld gaming PC has been cheaper before, dropping to the AU$899 mark but, then again, nothing really comes cheap these days. Importantly, though, this is a great performer, with a vivid 8-inch display and 144Hz refresh rate for smooth gameplay. It's also rather nice looking and comfortable in the hand.
Phones, tablets & wearables
The Ray-Ban Meta Gen 2 Wayfarer Smart Glasses are a great choice for anyone who likes wearing sunglasses but wants the perks of an AI-powered wearable. Just like wireless earbuds, you can listen to music and talk on the phone, but you can also take POV photos and videos in 3K.
A small but welcome discount on the Google Pixel Watch 5. This competent wearable delivers accurate GPS, all the essential health and fitness tracking features you need, and an attractive design. If you're upgrading from a Pixel Watch 3 or 4, you won't notice a huge leap, but for everyone else, it's easily the best Android smartwatch right now.
Samsung's answer to the AirTag, the SmartTag 2 works with select Samsung phones to help you find mislaid items. It has a built-in hole for easier attachments, up to 700 days of battery life and it's water-resistant.
The Vivoactive 5 contains a lot of the premium Garmin features found in its more expensive offerings, while also priced closer to conventional smartwatches. These features include on-board GPS, on-device storage for offline music via Spotify, and fitness metrics like Body Battery and VO2 Max.
We called this the best smart ring for battery life (rated up to 12 days + a further 150 days with the charging case) while also being a more affordable option than Oura and Samsung at full price. The Gen 2 added a sleep apnoea tracker to make up for the price hike over its predecessor. Again, be sure to source the sizing kit first as not all smart rings are made the same.
Beauty & grooming
If you didn't know what a 'sonic' brush is, it's quieter and gentler than an oscillating electric toothbrush (like Oral-B). The DiamondClean 9000 has 4 cleaning modes, and one of them gets you 3 intensities. This value pack gets you a his-and-hers version, plus the glass is actually the charger.
Offering one of the most fuss-free shaves, the Philips OneBlade 360 is a nigh-on essential tool for any man's grooming routine. The cutting blade itself can move in any direction, ensuring constant, comfortable contact with your face to remove your beard entirely, while an included guard comb allows you to trim your facial fuzz to a desired length.
The Lawn Mower 5.0 Ultra is a solid choice if you want one device for general trimming and getting a closer shave. It includes interchangeable SkinSafe trimmer and foil heads, a built-in LED light and a waterproof design for wet or dry use, while USB-C charging and the included travel case make it easier to take on the road.
We're huge fans of the Shark CryoGlow here at TechRadar. The brand's advanced face mask combines LED facial care with a clever InstaChill cooling system to help reduce under-eye puffiness. During testing, we found this unique model to be very comfortable and capable of surprisingly good results. While a little pricey, the CyroGlow could be worth it if you're already spending a lot of cash on your skincare routine.
Gaming
Enter the wizarding world of Harry Potter, in Lego form on the Switch 2, with this collection of two games, covering Lego Harry Potter: Years 1-4 and Years 5-7.
It's fair to say Wolverine received a mixed reaction from gamers when it launched. If you were initially hesitant to play as the clawed mutant, then perhaps this 45% discount at Amazon could be enough to persuade you.
"It isn’t cheap, but the audio quality is near perfect". That was us reviewing the Inzone H9 II, and while it's still a premium price, this is a big discount on a superb gaming headset.
This deal offers you a decent saving on Meta's best 'affordable' headset, and a close second to its best ever headset according to our resident VR headset tester. In fact, he thinks it's the second-best headset anyone can buy from any brand, and it's only a more tempting offer thanks to this limited-time deal, which includes a free copy of GOLF+ to get you started.
Are you a Prime member yet?
If there's one thing you need to do to take full advantage of any major Amazon sale is to become a Prime member. While I think many Aussies already are, some of you might still be wondering what it means to be a Prime member, what you're actually paying for and if shelling out a monthly or annual sum is actually worth it.
In short, if you're a regular Amazon shopper, I think it's worth signing up for it. Your AU$12.99 monthly fee gets you free and expedited shipping on thousands of eligible products without needing to fulfil a minimum spend.
That fee also gets you free access to Prime Video (which does have some excellent shows and movies), along with Prime Reading and Prime Gaming. Just the first one more than makes up for the investment you're making in my opinion.
While there are generally no Prime-exclusive deals right now, there are the occasional coupons or lightning deals that won't explicitly say it's for Prime members, but will only appear if you're signed in with a paid account. You can find out more about the subscription service in my dedicated guide to what is Amazon Prime in Australia.
It's also worth noting that if you've never tried this service before, signing up now will get you a 30-day free trial that more than covers the sale. If you don't want to pay at all, you can cancel as soon as the sale finishes. Keep in mind that if you use the same email later to sign up again, you will not get that free trial later even if you didn't use all 30 days.
If you're interested in getting your delivery from Amazon expedited this sale season, you can hit one of the buttons below to sign up.
It's officially Black Friday!
We're now on day 11 of Amazon's sale, and I'll be spending the day hunting down the biggest discounts and checking which deals offer the best value for money. Keep this page handy and check back regularly, as I'll be adding the best new bargains as they drop.
