Aviso de ética: ao clicar em um link de afiliado, o preço não muda para você e recebemos uma comissão.

articles.title: Cuántos edificios se pueden visitar en GTA 6: un jugador hizo el experimento y su resultado fue sorprendente
articles.text:
Grand Theft Auto 6 permite visitar 1.563 de los 5.588 edificios identificados en Leonida, según un experimento de un jugador. El cálculo sitúa la accesibilidad en 28%, pero los inmuebles abiertos reúnen 51% de la superficie construida. El resultado indica que Rockstar concentró buena parte de la exploración interior en instalaciones grandes, comercios y áreas urbanas con actividades para jugadores.
La proporción parece limitada frente al total, aunque adquiere otra dimensión cuando se consideran aeropuertos, centros comerciales, tiendas, viviendas y edificios públicos con interiores utilizables durante misiones, persecuciones, compras o recorridos libres por Leonida.
El método empleado
El creador de contenido Neutral_State no recorrió a pie cada calle, casa y local del mapa. El usuario detectó una diferencia de color en las construcciones que aparecen en el mapa oficial de Rockstar Games y en la interfaz del juego. Los edificios azules más claros permanecen cerrados; los de tono oscuro señalan interiores accesibles para Jason y Lucía durante la partida y sus actividades secundarias.
La relación entre tamaño y acceso explica por qué la superficie visitable supera la mitad del área construida. Entre los edificios de menos de 200 metros cuadrados, el 24% está abierto. En las estructuras superiores a 5.000 metros cuadrados, la proporción asciende al 68%. Las tiendas rondan siete de cada 10 accesibles; iglesias y hospitales, menos de dos por categoría.
El aeropuerto VCIA encabeza la lista de interiores accesibles con 131.000 metros cuadrados, una extensión equivalente a unos 18 campos de fútbol. El segundo puesto corresponde al centro comercial Waning Sands, que reúne 31.600 metros cuadrados. Estos espacios ayudan a entender por qué pocos inmuebles abiertos pueden concentrar gran parte del terreno construido disponible para explorar en el juego base.
Grandes interiores
La presencia de comercios y grandes complejos amplía las posibilidades de exploración más allá de las calles. Las tiendas pueden servir para adquirir ropa, conseguir suministros, activar actividades o iniciar encuentros con personajes. Los espacios de mayor tamaño también ofrecen escenarios para misiones, persecuciones, enfrentamientos y rutas de escape, elementos centrales en la experiencia de mundo abierto que propone Rockstar.
El análisis revela que la accesibilidad no se distribuye de forma automática por el mapa. Los edificios de gran tamaño reciben una mayor atención, mientras que las construcciones pequeñas suelen cumplir una función visual. Esta diferencia permite que zonas específicas del estado tengan más servicios, actividades y detalles, sin necesidad de que cada inmueble del escenario tenga una puerta abierta.
Barrios con acceso
La distribución tampoco es uniforme entre regiones. Tequesta lidera el análisis con 80% de su superficie construida accesible. Downtown alcanza 62% y Ocean Beach llega a 61%. La presencia de comercios, oficinas, viviendas y lugares de ocio eleva las posibilidades de exploración en estos sectores urbanos de Vice City y de sus alrededores inmediatos dentro de Leonida para los jugadores.
En cambio, Ambrosia registra 17% de superficie accesible; Breakwater Quarry, 18%; y Mile Zero, 26%. La central eléctrica de Tortoise Head es el caso más cerrado: ninguno de sus 60 edificios permite el ingreso. Estas diferencias muestran que las zonas industriales, rurales o periféricas priorizan carreteras, paisajes, canteras y actividades exteriores antes que una red extensa de interiores disponibles al jugador.
Un estado diverso
La diversidad de Leonida va más allá de una Vice City modernizada. El mapa incorpora playas, barrios residenciales, zonas financieras, puertos, autopistas costeras, cayos y humedales inspirados en los Everglades. Grassrivers propone canales, manglares y fauna; Port Gellhorn añade moteles, carreteras secundarias y una atmósfera menos turística que los distritos centrales de la ciudad principal del estado ficticio de Rockstar.
El diseño del mundo también incorpora clima, habitantes y redes sociales ficticias. Tormentas tropicales, lluvia intensa y vientos fuertes alteran la visibilidad, el mar y la conducción sobre asfalto mojado o barro. Los ciudadanos reaccionan a incidentes, mientras las publicaciones dentro del teléfono de los protagonistas registran peleas, accidentes y persecuciones ocurridas cerca de Jason y Lucía durante sus desplazamientos.
GTA 6 concentra su exploración interior en comercios, viviendas, instalaciones públicas y grandes complejos que pueden albergar misiones, actividades y situaciones imprevistas. Esa elección permite combinar una ciudad extensa con espacios que aportan contexto a la historia de Jason y Lucía, sin convertir cada edificio en un escenario vacío.

articles.title: GTA 6 : une fuite détaille les écarts graphiques entre PS5, PS5 Pro et Xbox
articles.text:
Une fuite des réglages graphiques de GTA 6 détaille plein de petits détails techniques sur les versions du jeu comme les ombres en ray tracing de la PS5 Pro. Sur Xbox Series S, les compromis iraient même jusqu’à réduire le trafic et le nombre de piétons dans Vice City.
Les différences entre les versions console de GTA 6 se verraient jusque dans les embouteillages de Vice City. Rockstar vise 30 images par seconde sur les quatre machines, et un relevé de réglages que le dataminer Tex2 dit avoir tiré des fichiers du jeu donne un aperçu des compromis faits pour tenir cette cadence.
Partagé le 25 novembre sur X par Tex2, le document a depuis disparu du réseau social. Heureusement, certains sites comme MP1st, ont pu reproduire les tableaux des réglages graphiques de GTA 6, console par console.
La PS5 Pro gagne des ombres en ray tracing
Dans ces tableaux, la PS5 standard et la Xbox Series X partagent les mêmes réglages graphiques. Les textures et la tessellation, qui subdivise les surfaces pour affiner leur géométrie, y sont réglées sur « élevé ». L’illumination globale, le calcul des rebonds de la lumière entre les surfaces, reste sur « moyen ». Rockstar avait déjà précisé que les deux consoles calculent leur image en 1440p avant de la reconstruire en 4K avec le même algorithme maison d’anticrénelage temporel, ou TAA.
La PS5 Pro conserve les textures en qualité élevée et part elle aussi du 1440p. Elle s’appuie sur le PSSR 2 de Sony pour reconstruire l’image en 4K. Rockstar avait déjà confirmé qu’elle serait la seule à calculer des ombres en ray tracing.
D’après le relevé, l’illumination globale passerait sur « élevé ». Le lancer de rayons servirait à calculer l’ombre d’un arbre au soleil aussi bien que celle d’un passant sous un lampadaire. Les réglages correspondants, pour les ombres directionnelles et les ombres liées aux sources de lumière locales, seraient tous deux sur « élevé ». Leurs équivalents calculés par rastérisation passeraient sur « faible ».
La Xbox Series S réduit aussi la circulation
Sur Series S, Rockstar part d’une image en 720p que le FSR 4 d’AMD reconstruit en 1080p. Les développeurs disent avoir tenu à conserver l’illumination globale en ray tracing malgré la mémoire plus limitée de la console. D’après les tableaux, la qualité des textures et celle de la simulation de l’eau et des vagues reculeraient à « moyen ». La tessellation, elle, tomberait sur « faible ».
L’écart se verrait aussi dans la rue. Sur Series S, la densité des piétons et celle du trafic seraient toutes deux réglées sur « moyen », contre « élevé » sur les trois autres consoles. Le même écart apparaît dans les réglages de la physique et dans plusieurs paramètres de l’IA. Comme quoi, même à Vice City, le diable se cache dans les détails.
La rastérisation calcule l’image en projetant des triangles sur l’écran, puis en appliquant des astuces (shadow maps, filtrage, biais) pour simuler les ombres à moindre coût. Le ray tracing, lui, lance des rayons dans la scène pour déterminer si un point est éclairé ou occulté, ce qui produit des ombres généralement plus cohérentes (contacts plus crédibles, pénombres mieux gérées). En pratique, le ray tracing est nettement plus gourmand en calcul et en bande passante mémoire, d’où des choix ciblés (activer certaines ombres RT et baisser d’autres réglages). Beaucoup de jeux combinent les deux : RT pour quelques effets « premium », rastérisation pour le reste afin de tenir une cadence stable.
L’upscaling reconstruit une image de sortie (1080p/4K) à partir d’un rendu interne plus bas (720p/1440p) pour réduire la charge GPU tout en gardant une image détaillée. Le TAA (Temporal Anti-Aliasing) exploite plusieurs images successives et les vecteurs de mouvement pour lisser les bords et stabiliser le rendu, mais il peut introduire du flou ou des artefacts sur les fins détails. PSSR 2 (Sony) et FSR 4 (AMD) sont des techniques de reconstruction qui utilisent elles aussi des informations temporelles et spatiales, avec des approches et une qualité variables selon le contenu affiché. Le principe reste le même : économiser du calcul en rendu natif, puis « remonter » la définition pour viser une sortie 4K ou 1080p plus propre.
La densité de trafic et de piétons ne dépend pas seulement du GPU : elle sollicite aussi le CPU (IA, comportement, navigation), la mémoire (assets, animations) et le streaming (chargement des modèles/variantes). Réduire le nombre d’entités à l’écran baisse mécaniquement le coût de simulation, les collisions, et la quantité de données à charger en continu, ce qui aide à stabiliser les temps de frame. À 30 FPS, l’objectif est surtout d’éviter les chutes et les saccades, pas uniquement d’atteindre un chiffre moyen. Sur une machine plus contrainte, ces réglages « monde » (foule, circulation, physique) peuvent peser autant, voire plus, que la résolution ou les textures.

articles.title: Startup news and updates: daily roundup (November 26, 2026)
articles.text:
Startup news and updates: daily roundup (November 26, 2026)
YourStory presents the daily news roundup from the Indian startup ecosystem and beyond. Here's the roundup for Thursday, November 26, 2026.
Uber India gets a new head as investors continue to invest in Indian startups, YourStory brings you today’s headlines with the latest developments across sectors.
Featured stories
Uber appoints former Zomato CEO Rakesh Ranjan as President for India, South Asia
Uber has appointed former Zomato food delivery CEO Rakesh Ranjan as President for India and South Asia, effective January 4, 2027.
Ranjan joined Zomato in 2017 and spent eight years at the company. During his tenure, he led its food ordering and delivery business as CEO, having previously held leadership roles across Zomato Gold and sales.
HC to hear on Friday Tata Trusts’ pleas against Chandrasekaran’s reappointment
The Sir Dorabji Tata Trust (SDTT) and the R.D. Tata Trust (RDTT) on Thursday filed suits in the Bombay High Court against Tata Sons and six of its directors, challenging the reappointment of N Chandrasekaran as executive chairman for a third five-year term. The court will hear the matter on Friday. The SDTT has sought Rs 50 crore, while the RDTT has sought Rs 15 crore in damages, with 18 per cent annual interest.
Funding news
Finnable raises Rs 405 Cr in Series C to expand multi-product lending
Fintech company Finnable has raised Rs 405 crore in a Series C round from Bharat Value Fund, part of the Pantomath Group, Pratithi Investments and NKSquared. Existing backers Z47, TVS Capital and Claypond Capital continue in the company.
Green Aero raises $14M as India pushes for indigenous jet propulsion
Green Aero, an aerospace and defence startup has raised $14 million in a Series A round led by Crane Ventures. The other participants were 3one4 Capital, Antler Elevate, and pi Ventures.
Other news
CredAble acquires 70% stake in AI regulatory intelligence platform Reql
CredAble, a working capital and banking technology platform, has acquired a 70% stake in Reql, an AI-native regulatory intelligence platform, expanding its presence in the regulatory technology (RegTech) segment. Reql helps banks, financial institutions and corporates automate regulatory research, policy gap analysis and compliance management. Its platform monitors official regulatory sources in real time and captures new circulars, enabling organisations to assess their impact and track compliance actions.
The company aims to reduce the time required to close compliance actions from as much as 60 days to less than four hours. CredAble plans to leverage its network of over 100 banking partners and 175 corporate clients to expand Reql's adoption. It expects the platform to contribute 25% of consolidated revenue over the next 24 to 36 months.
Panasonic, IvyCap launch IGNITION Challenge 2.0 for Indian startups
Panasonic Life Solutions India has launched the second edition of its IGNITION Challenge in partnership with IvyCap Ventures to accelerate the adoption of hyperspectral camera technology in India. The initiative will connect Panasonic's advanced imaging technology with Indian startups and innovators to develop applications across healthcare, agriculture, industrial quality, energy and food manufacturing. The programme will combine hyperspectral imaging, artificial intelligence and domain-specific expertise to address industry challenges.
IvyCap Ventures will lead startup sourcing and ecosystem engagement, while Panasonic's India Innovation Centre will oversee programme design and evaluation. The initiative aims to shortlist six to eight startups for technical evaluation. It will culminate in a Demo Day in March 2027, with three to four potential co-development partners expected to be selected.
Biz2X partners with SIDBI to strengthen digital lending operations
Biz2X, a digital lending platform and subsidiary of Biz2Credit, has partnered with the Small Industries Development Bank of India (SIDBI) to streamline lending operations and improve credit delivery to MSMEs. Under the partnership, Biz2X will provide its lending customer relationship management platform to consolidate leads generated through multiple channels, including WhatsApp, direct selling agents, OEM partners and marketing campaigns.
The platform offers AI-powered BizBot for pipeline insights, management dashboards to monitor conversions and productivity, and mobile applications to support field teams. The initiative comes amid growing demand for formal MSME credit. According to the July 2026 MSME Pulse report, outstanding commercial credit balances reached ₹65.8 lakh crore in March 2026, registering 14% annual growth. However, only 41% of registered MSMEs have accessed formal credit.
Australian retailer Officeworks opens GCC in Bengaluru
Australian omnichannel retailer Officeworks has inaugurated its Global Capability Centre (GCC) at Manyata Tech Park in Bengaluru as part of its multi-year business transformation strategy. The centre, operating as Officeworks Bengaluru, will work alongside the company's Melbourne support office to strengthen capabilities in data, digital technology, artificial intelligence and retail operations.
The Bengaluru team will support functions including merchandising, customer operations, finance, analytics, AI, digital engineering and core retail platforms such as SAP and Salesforce. It will also contribute to developing omnichannel customer experiences and improving operational efficiency.
94% of Indian brands fail basic AI website readiness test: Publive-IAMAI study
A study by AI visibility infrastructure company Publive and the Internet and Mobile Association of India (IAMAI) has found that 94% of India's leading brands fail the basic test of website readability by artificial intelligence systems. The study, titled Can AI Read India Inc.?, examined 951 mid-market and enterprise brands across sectors including automotive, financial services, consumer durables, hotels and B2B SaaS. Only one brand achieved strong AI readiness.
The findings show that AI bots receive 84% code and just 16% actual content from the median brand website. Additionally, 48 brands provide no readable content to AI crawlers. The study highlights the need for businesses to improve website structures and introduce structured data so AI platforms can accurately understand and represent their brands.
Dhan launches free AI-powered charting platform TradingCharts
Raise Financial Services, the parent company of stockbroking platform Dhan, has launched TradingCharts, an AI-powered charting platform designed for Indian traders and investors. Developed entirely in-house, the platform offers more than 20 chart types, 200 indicators, eight chart layouts and multiple timeframes. It also includes advanced tools such as Order Flow, Volume Profile, Depth of Market and Bar Replay. TradingCharts provides real-time market data across enabled NSE, BSE and MCX segments when connected to a brokerage platform. Dhan’s Fuzz AI assistant allows users to create indicators and trading strategies through natural-language prompts. The platform also features an Indicator Marketplace where creators can monetise their tools.
Chariot launches indigenous AI foundation models under IndiaAI Mission
Chariot Artificial Intelligence has launched its Chariot-1 foundation models under the IndiaAI Mission, marking a development in India's efforts to build indigenous AI capabilities. The models include an 11-billion-parameter large language model and a text-to-speech system supporting English and 10 Indian languages. Both were pretrained from scratch in India. The company has introduced three research innovations: IndicShift, which improves processing across Indian scripts; Nested Training, which enables multiple model sizes to be trained simultaneously; and Mixture of Vocabularies, which improves training efficiency.
Chariot-1 is available in three model sizes to support deployment across data centres, laptops, smartphones and edge devices. Its speech model has recorded over 97% verbalisation accuracy in the reported benchmark tests. The launch was inaugurated by MeitY Secretary S. Krishnan.
Wadhwani Foundation invites applications for employment and livelihood grants
Wadhwani Foundation has invited Expressions of Interest from organisations across India for grants aimed at expanding job creation, employment and livelihood opportunities. Through Wadhwani Grants, the foundation plans to provide multi-year funding over three to five years, with support linked to independently verified outcomes such as job placements, jobs created and improvements in household incomes.
The initiative targets organisations working in three areas: job fulfilment through skilling and placement, job creation through entrepreneurship and MSME growth, and livelihood upliftment for self-employed individuals and households. The grants will complement existing funding without equity dilution or repayment obligations. Selected organisations will also receive free access to the foundation's AI-powered GenieAI platform and its wider technology ecosystem. The foundation aims to help proven organisations multiply their impact by two to three times.
ACKO brings insurance innovations to life through entertainment-led Purple Carpet
Digital insurance company ACKO has hosted The Purple Carpet, an entertainment-led brand experience to showcase its latest innovations across motor, health and travel insurance. Designed around a film-premiere format rather than a conventional product launch, the event brought together MS Dhoni, Javed Akhtar, Farah Khan and more than 60 creators and comedians.
One of the key attractions was 'Where's the Saboot?', a courtroom-style game show featuring ACKO Drivecam footage and performances by comedians and creators. The event also included stand-up comedy sets highlighting ACKO Drivecam-linked car insurance, ACKO Air Pass and ACKO Clinic. A conversation between Dhoni and Javed Akhtar explored clarity of purpose and intention in the context of insurance. ACKO said the initiative reflects its strategy of using entertainment and storytelling to make insurance more relevant to consumers.
Axis Communications expands BIS-certified camera portfolio in India
Axis Communications has expanded its portfolio of BIS-ER-01 certified network cameras in India, securing certification for nine additional models. This takes its total certified portfolio in the country to 20 models. The latest certifications cover multiple product families as the company strengthens its compliance with India's regulatory and cybersecurity requirements. Its M-Series camera model AXIS M4216-LV is already available in India, while additional models across the P14 and P32 series are progressing through the certification process.
SpotDraft appoints Sajana Shankaran as VP of Human Resources
AI-native contract lifecycle management platform SpotDraft has appointed Sajana Shankaran as Vice President of Human Resources as it prepares for its next phase of global expansion. Shankaran will lead the company's people strategy across the Americas, Europe, the Middle East, Africa and India, focusing on organisational development, talent capabilities and building scalable structures. She brings more than 20 years of experience in strategic HR leadership and joins SpotDraft from Branch, where she served as Director, HR Business Partner and Head of People Partner for APAC.
Atovio launches wearable air purifier for children
Indian wearable technology startup Atovio has launched Atovio Nino, a wearable air purifier designed for children aged four and above. Priced at Rs 3,499, Nino uses ion technology without a filter or fan to address airborne particles, including PM2.5 and PM10. It offers three operating modes and provides up to 72 hours of battery life on a full charge. The company said laboratory tests at IIT Kanpur recorded a 90% reduction in airborne particle concentration within 25 minutes in a sealed chamber.

articles.title: Black Friday Darty : PC, tablettes et imprimantes avec 10% de remise immédiate dès 400 € d'achat
articles.text:
Black Friday Darty : PC, tablettes et imprimantes avec 10% de remise immédiate dès 400 € d'achat
Le Black Friday bat son plein chez Darty, et l'enseigne frappe fort avec une offre exclusive : 10% de remise immédiate dès 400 € d'achat sur une sélection de PC portables (hors gaming), PC de bureau, tablettes, imprimantes et encreurs. Cumulez cette réduction avec les prix déjà cassés du Black Friday pour faire le plein de high-tech à moindre coût.
Comment profiter des 10% de remise dès 400 € ?
La mécanique est d'une simplicité redoutable. Vous ajoutez à votre panier un ou plusieurs produits éligibles parmi les PC portables, PC de bureau, tablettes, imprimantes ou encreurs. Dès que le total atteint 400 €, la remise de 10% s'applique automatiquement.
L'astuce ? Grouper ses achats. Un PC à 649 € vous fait déjà dépasser le seuil, mais si vous cherchez une tablette à 399 €, l'ajout d'une imprimante ou d'un petit consommable vous permet de basculer dans la zone de réduction et de rentabiliser votre panier.
Les PC et tablettes : le cœur de l'offre
C'est sur l'informatique que la remise de 10% prend tout son sens. Les paniers moyens y sont élevés, et les réductions Black Friday déjà appliquées permettent de maximiser l'économie finale.
PC portable Asus Vivobook S17
Affiché à 649,99 € au lieu de 999,99 €, ce PC portable au grand écran de 17 pouces est déjà à -35% pour le Black Friday. Avec son processeur Intel Core 5, ses 16 Go de RAM et son SSD de 512 Go, il est parfait pour le télétravail ou les études. La remise de 10% vient faire tomber la facture encore plus bas.
PC tout-en-un Lenovo A100
Idéal pour un salon ou un bureau, ce tout-en-un gris nuage s'affiche à 549,99 € au lieu de 699,99 € (-21%). Son écran FHD de 23,8 pouces, son processeur Intel N100 et ses 16 Go de RAM en font une machine élégante et compacte. Un achat qui vous fait immédiatement basculer dans la tranche des 400 € éligibles aux 10% de remise.
Tablette Samsung Galaxy Tab S10+
C'est l'une des plus grosses remises de cette sélection. La tablette tactile Samsung passe à 699,99 € au lieu de 1 219,99 €, soit 520 € d'économie immédiate (-43%) ! Avec son écran immersif sans reflet, ses 12 Go de RAM et son stockage de 256 Go, elle surpasse largement la plupart des ordinateurs portables. Grâce au seuil des 400 €, elle est pleinement éligible aux 10% de réduction supplémentaires.
Écrans et imprimantes : pour compléter son panier
Pour atteindre le palier des 400 € tout en se faisant plaisir, les périphériques et l'impression sont d'excellents choix.
Écran PC Gaming Asus ROG XG27AQWMG-R
La pièce maîtresse des setups gaming. Cet écran OLED de 26,5 pouces avec un taux de rafraîchissement de 280 Hz passe à 469,99 € au lieu de 549,99 € (-14%). À noter que les PC gaming étant exclus de l'offre, cet écran constitue une excellente alternative pour intégrer le panier de 400 € et déclencher la remise de 10%.
Imprimante multifonction HP Envy 6130
Pratique et connectée, elle imprime, scanne et copie sans fil. Affichée à 59,99 € au lieu de 95,99 € (-38%), elle est le complément parfait pour valider le seuil des 400 € (par exemple, en l'ajoutant à un PC). Cerise sur le gâteau : elle est éligible à Instant Ink et permet de bénéficier de 3 mois d'abonnement offerts.
Le Black Friday Darty ne s'arrête pas là
Si l'informatique et l'impression sont au cœur de cette opération, le catalogue Darty regorge d'autres pépites à prix réduits pour cette fin de semaine. Du gros électroménager aux téléviseurs, en passant par le petit électroménager, l'audio ou la cuisine, des milliers de références profitent des remises Black Friday. L'occasion de renouveler un appareil fatigué ou de préparer ses cadeaux de fin d'année sans exploser son budget.
Que vous cherchiez à équiper votre salon, à automatiser votre quotidien ou à faire plaisir, les promotions en cours couvrent l'ensemble des univers de la maison. Pensez à vérifier les conditions de chaque offre (remises immédiates, cagnottes ou reprises) pour cumuler les avantages au mieux.

articles.title: Vous partez au Japon à Noël ? Voici le prix de l’eSIM Holafly
articles.text:
Voyage au Japon à Noël : combien coûte l’eSIM Holafly avec données illimitées pendant 7 jours ?
Pour un séjour au Japon pendant les vacances de Noël, Holafly propose une eSIM avec données illimitées pendant 7 jours à 25,50 €. Une solution pratique pour rester connecté sans frais d’itinérance.
Une semaine de données illimitées pour visiter le Japon
Un voyage au Japon prévu pour les vacances de Noël ? L’eSIM Holafly avec données illimitées revient à 25,50 € pour 7 jours. De quoi utiliser Google Maps, consulter les horaires des trains, partager des photos ou garder le contact avec ses proches sans dépendre du Wi-Fi des hôtels et des restaurants. Le forfait fonctionne sur les réseaux 4G et 5G disponibles dans le pays et évite les frais d’itinérance liés à l’utilisation d’un forfait mobile français à l’étranger.
Avec cette formule, pas besoin de surveiller constamment sa consommation de données. L’eSIM donne accès à Internet en illimité pendant la période sélectionnée. Elle peut ainsi servir à consulter un itinéraire dans le métro de Tokyo, réserver une activité, traduire un menu ou retrouver facilement une adresse à Kyoto.
Le partage de connexion est également prévu. Pour une formule de 7 jours, le volume indiqué pour cette fonction atteint 7 Go. Cela permet de connecter ponctuellement un ordinateur ou un autre appareil, même si les données utilisées en partage ne sont donc pas illimitées.
Autre élément intéressant : Holafly inclut son service Always On. Celui-ci fournit 1 Go de données de secours par mois, même après le voyage, à condition de conserver l’eSIM. Une petite réserve qui peut dépanner lors d’un prochain déplacement.
Une installation avant le départ et une activation à l’arrivée
L’eSIM s’achète directement en ligne, puis s’installe sur un smartphone compatible. L’opération peut être effectuée avant le départ ou pendant le voyage, à partir du guide transmis par e-mail ou disponible dans l’application Holafly. Le forfait s’active une fois arrivé au Japon, lorsque l’eSIM est allumée.
Avant de commander, mieux vaut toutefois vérifier que le téléphone prend bien en charge cette technologie et qu’il n’est pas verrouillé par un opérateur. La carte eSIM permet par ailleurs de conserver sa carte SIM habituelle pour continuer à utiliser son numéro, notamment sur WhatsApp.
Holafly annonce aussi une assistance disponible 24 h/24 et 7 j/7, en français, par chat, e-mail ou WhatsApp. En cas de changement de programme, une demande de remboursement peut être effectuée dans un délai allant jusqu’à six mois, sous réserve des conditions prévues par le service.
Au final, les 25,50 € demandés pour sept jours représentent un budget à prévoir avant les vacances de Noël. Cette formule conviendra surtout aux voyageurs qui souhaitent disposer d’une connexion mobile dès leur arrivée au Japon, sans avoir à chercher une carte SIM locale sur place.

articles.title: Tous les fabricants de smartphones revoient leurs ambitions à la baisse pour 2027, sauf un
articles.text:
Autant dire que la crise mondiale de la mémoire frappe durement les constructeurs de smartphones. Les principaux modèles touchés sont ceux d’entrée de gamme et de moyen de gamme, les fabricants n’étant plus capables d’absorber l’explosion des prix des composants sur ces appareils. Ceux haut de gamme étaient en revanche plus épargnés, en raison de leur prix plus élevé. Du moins, jusqu’à maintenant. La crise semble désormais toucher quasiment tous les acteurs du secteur et toutes les gammes. C’est simple, quasiment tous les constructeurs de smartphones auraient revus leurs objectifs de livraison à la baisse pour 2027.
Des objectifs de livraison revus à la baisse pour 2027
Selon les informations exclusives du média chinois Jiemian News, quasiment tous les fabricants de smartphones auraient revu à la baisse leurs objectifs de livraison pour 2027. Apple et Samsung font partie des constructeurs les moins touchés par la crise de la RAM. Pourtant, Apple aurait prévu de produire environ 220 millions d’unités en 2027, soit une baisse de 5,6 % par rapport à l’année précédente. De son côté, Samsung aurait prévu de produire 210 millions d’unités en 2027, soit une diminution de 9,5 % par rapport à l’année précédente.
D’autres constructeurs prévoiraient de réduire encore plus drastiquement leurs livraisons, à l’image de Xiaomi (- 25 %), Oppo (- 14 %), Huawei (- 16 %) ou encore Vivo (- 29 %). Seul un fabricant n’aurait pas prévu une réduction de ses livraisons pour 2027, à savoir Honor. Le constructeur chinois prévoirait de mettre sur le marché 50 millions d’unités en 2027, soit autant qu’en 2026. Ceci s’explique par ses bons résultats financiers ces derniers mois.
Les fabricants de smartphones n’ont pas fini de souffrir
Même en revoyant leurs objectifs de livraison à la baisse pour 2027, les fabricants de smartphones parviendront-ils à faire face à la crise ? Pour l’instant, rien n’est moins sûr. Les principaux acteurs du marché pourraient continuer à augmenter les prix de leurs appareils, tout en effectuant des compromis, avec par exemple des caractéristiques techniques revues à la baisse. Ces limitations ne se limiteraient d’ailleurs pas aux fiches techniques des smartphones, étant donné que même les applications sont dorénavant bridées afin de limiter la consommation de mémoire.
Par ailleurs, une baisse des prix de la mémoire ne serait pas attendue avant 2030. Les fabricants de smartphones vont probablement devoir faire face à cette crise durant encore plusieurs années. Une crise qui déborde d’ailleurs sur les PC et l’industrie automobile. Un conseil : si vous avez besoin d’un nouveau téléphone, n’attendez pas trop longtemps.

articles.title: Hisense presenta el 32S6S, un televisor portátil con Hi-QLED y hasta 10 horas de batería para moverlo o llevarlo fuera de casa
articles.text:
Los televisores han pasado históricamente por un mismo guión: se anclan a la pared o a un mueble del salón y ahí se quedan. Hisense busca romper esa dinámica en España con el lanzamiento del 32S6S, un televisor portátil de su familia lifestyle que integra batería propia y tecnología Hi-QLED para funcionar sin depender en todo momento de una toma de corriente.
El planteamiento parte de una idea sencilla: acercar la pantalla a donde estés (en otra habitación, en la terraza o en el jardín) y permitir incluso sacarla de casa en una escapada o llevarla a una segunda residencia. En Amazon, está disponible por 1.399 euros.
Hisense Roam View 32S6S - Hi-QLED Smart TV Táctil 32 pulgadas 4K
Hasta 10 horas sin enchufe y panel Hi-QLED
El principal argumento del Hisense 32S6S frente a un televisor tradicional es su batería integrada, con una autonomía que promete hasta 10 horas. Esa cifra abre la puerta a ver una película, seguir un partido, jugar o abrir plataformas de streaming sin tener que buscar un enchufe o tirar de alargadores en zonas exteriores.
En el apartado visual recurre a la tecnología Hi-QLED, enfocada a ofrecer mayor precisión cromática y un nivel de brillo superior para mantener una imagen legible tanto en interiores como en espacios más iluminados. Se trata de una tele de 32 pulgadas montado sobre un soporte con base y orientación adaptable, un enfoque habitual en este tipo de pantallas rodantes o multiposición pensadas para acompañar el uso cotidiano más allá del sofá.
Qué aporta este formato y qué conviene tener en cuenta
Más allá del reclamo de movilidad, llevar el televisor de un espacio a otro plantea matices prácticos que vale la pena sopesar antes de verlo como un sustituto directo de una tele fija. La autonomía máxima de hasta 10 horas depende, eso sí, del brillo y del tipo de uso y un equipo portátil de este tipo suele brillar más como segunda pantalla versátil o de apoyo que como televisor principal para un salón grande.

articles.title: Stromversorgung von KI-Rechenzentren: „Dass die Gaskraftwerke viel länger genutzt werden, ist ein echtes Risiko“
articles.text:
Über 100 Gaskraftwerke geplant: Warum US-Rechenzentren auf diese Strategie setzen
Wer ein großes Rechenzentrum aufzuziehen will, muss geduldig sein: Der Knackpunkt ist vor allem, der Anschluss ans Stromnetz. Auf diese Genehmigung müssen Entwickler der Großanlagen in den Vereinigten Staaten eine lange Wartezeit einplanen. Bis zur Inbetriebnahme kann da, ähnlich wie in Europa, bis zu ein Jahrzehnt vergehen. Einige Entwickler von KI-Rechenzentren sind nicht bereit, solange zu warten. Sie setzen stattdessen auf eigene netzunabhängige Gaskraftwerke (also Energieerzeuger hinter dem Stromzähler), um am noch immer anhaltenden KI-Boom teilzuhaben.
Dieses Vorgehen hat Konsequenzen für die Anwohner:innen und die Umwelt. Der Campus von SpacexAI in Memphis setzt etwa bereits seit 2024 Dutzende Erdgasturbinen ein, einige davon sogar ohne Genehmigung. Zum Zeitpunkt der Einrichtung war diese Anlage eine Seltenheit und wurde noch von den Aufsichtsbehörden genau unter die Lupe genommen. Und sie ist auch jetzt noch Gegenstand laufender Rechtsstreitigkeiten. Abgeschreckt hat das die Entwickler von Rechenzentren nicht: im Gegenteil.

articles.title: Kioxia and Nvidia demo 144 SSDs that expand GPU memory past 1 petabyte in a GB200 NVL72 rack
articles.text:
In a nutshell: The computational capabilities of AI accelerators and GPUs are now limited by how much high-bandwidth memory the processors can access at any given time. According to Kioxia, enterprise SSDs can serve as a viable alternative to HBM when they are embedded directly in the server rack system.
Kioxia is working with Nvidia to significantly expand memory capacity in AI data centers by exploiting its spacious, enterprise-grade SSDs. The Japanese memory manufacturer, credited with inventing flash memory back when it was part of Toshiba, recently unveiled a new proof-of-concept solution. The company linked terabytes upon terabytes of SSD storage to "effectively" expand GPU memory capacity to 1 petabyte and beyond.
The new test employed 144 Kioxia 7.68 TB NVMe SSDs belonging to the XD8 Series line, which were installed in an Nvidia GB200 NVL72 system. The rack included 18 server nodes, with each node supporting eight E1.S SSDs. All in all, the configuration supported around 60 terabytes of flash-based memory per node, which was available directly to the GB200 GPUs thanks to Nvidia's SCADA software stack.
Kioxia's XD8 Series includes six different PCIe 5.0 SSDs ranging between 1.9 TB and 7.68 TB. The drives support the Open Compute Project initiative, and employ Kioxia's all-proprietary hardware and software architecture. According to Kioxia data, the new experimental setup was able to provide around 1.1 petabytes of "raw" SSD capacity. The system supports 512-byte data access, potentially going up to 2 trillion 512-byte vectors.
The new system would be useful for storing, managing, and processing large-scale vector databases, including the massive datasets used in graph neural networks. To put it simply, this novel approach would make increasingly massive AI models readily available to GPUs and other hardware accelerators, going beyond the limits of traditional on-board HBM solutions both in terms of costs and supply chain availability.
Like other hardware makers caught up in chip manufacturing these days, Kioxia is now mostly focused on serving the needs of data center customers and other AI hyperscalers. Earlier this year, the managing director of Kioxia's memory division said the era of cheap 1 TB consumer SSDs is over.
Kioxia and Nvidia described the XD8-based system as a PoC still going through testing, but the Japanese manufacturer is already working on some brand-new storage units to expand memory capacity beyond costly HBM chips. The recently introduced GP1 Series is designed to exploit the PCIe 6.0 standard to further optimize direct GPU access, while Kioxia and Nvidia keep evaluating novel solutions based on SCADA and the Storage-Next architecture.

articles.title: Como saber quantos aparelhos estão conectados ao seu Wi-Fi (e como bloqueá-los)
La versión no oficial de GTA 6 para PC avanza: prepara mods y su propio lanzador
articles.text:
La versión no oficial de Grand Theft Auto VI (GTA 6) para PC continúa desarrollándose pese a los intentos de Take-Two Interactive y Rockstar Games por frenar su distribución. El proyecto, que busca adaptar al ordenador una copia del videojuego filtrada para Xbox Series, ya tendría sus primeros mods y prepara un lanzador propio para facilitar su ejecución a otros usuarios.
El avance se produce después de que las compañías detrás de la franquicia consiguieran cerrar más de 3.000 repositorios vinculados con esta iniciativa. Las plataformas afectadas contenían archivos y herramientas utilizados para trabajar en una versión del juego compatible con computadoras.
Sin embargo, el cierre no habría detenido el desarrollo. Según la información difundida por comunidades de jugadores, algunos de los proyectos trasladaron sus repositorios a espacios privados para continuar trabajando sin exponer públicamente sus avances.
La aparición de las primeras modificaciones y el anuncio de un lanzador representan nuevos pasos para esta adaptación no autorizada. También podrían facilitar que personas sin conocimientos técnicos avanzados intenten ejecutar el videojuego en una computadora, aunque todavía no se trata de una versión oficial ni de un lanzamiento compatible con todos los equipos.
GTA VI ya tendría sus primeros mods para PC
Uno de los aspectos que más llama la atención de este proyecto es que sus desarrolladores no solo buscan conseguir que GTA VI funcione fuera de las consolas para las que fue diseñado, sino que también trabajan en herramientas para modificar su contenido.
Los primeros mods publicados serían modificaciones creadas por la comunidad para alterar determinados elementos del videojuego. Este tipo de archivos suele utilizarse en los juegos de PC para cambiar personajes, vehículos, escenarios, gráficos o características de la experiencia.
La existencia de estas modificaciones indica que el proyecto comienza a desarrollar un entorno similar al que tienen otros videojuegos de ordenador, donde los usuarios pueden incorporar contenido creado por terceros.
Además, los responsables de esta adaptación anunciaron que trabajan en un lanzador propio. Se trata de un programa que permitiría iniciar el juego sin tener que realizar manualmente todos los procedimientos técnicos necesarios para ejecutarlo.
Esta herramienta estaría pensada especialmente para quienes no cuentan con conocimientos sobre compilación, archivos del sistema o configuraciones avanzadas. No obstante, todavía no se han detallado sus características ni una fecha concreta para su publicación.
También habrían conseguido ejecutar GTA VI en una PS5 modificada
Los avances de la comunidad no se limitan a las computadoras. Un usuario de Reddit publicó información sobre la supuesta ejecución de GTA VI en una PlayStation 5 con un firmware modificado.
Según lo compartido en esa comunidad, el videojuego habría funcionado en una consola que utilizaba la versión 13.40 del firmware, anterior a la exigida oficialmente para ejecutar el título. Otros participantes de la discusión señalaron que también sería posible hacerlo con la versión 13.60.
El firmware es el software interno que controla el funcionamiento de una consola. Cuando se modifica, algunos usuarios pueden acceder a funciones que normalmente están restringidas, aunque estos procedimientos también pueden implicar riesgos para el dispositivo y limitar el acceso a determinados servicios.
Por ahora, estas pruebas deben interpretarse con cautela, ya que proceden de publicaciones de usuarios y no de confirmaciones oficiales de Sony o Rockstar Games.
Rockstar busca frenar las versiones no autorizadas
El desarrollo de estas adaptaciones ocurre en medio de los esfuerzos legales de Take-Two Interactive para proteger la propiedad intelectual de la franquicia.
La compañía solicitó retirar miles de repositorios relacionados con el proyecto después de que se detectara que algunos usuarios estaban utilizando una versión filtrada para Xbox Series como base para conseguir una adaptación a PC.
Aunque el cierre de más de 3.000 repositorios representó un golpe para los responsables de estas iniciativas, el traslado de algunos proyectos a espacios privados habría permitido que continuaran trabajando.
La situación también refleja el interés de los jugadores por una versión para ordenador. Aunque GTA VI fue desarrollado inicialmente para consolas, una parte de la comunidad espera que Rockstar amplíe su disponibilidad a PC.
Mientras tanto, las adaptaciones no oficiales avanzan sin garantías de estabilidad, compatibilidad o seguridad. Descargar archivos de repositorios desconocidos también puede exponer los equipos a programas maliciosos.
Por ello, los usuarios deberán tener en cuenta que estos proyectos no cuentan con el respaldo de Rockstar Games y que su funcionamiento puede cambiar a medida que las compañías continúen tomando medidas contra su distribución.

articles.title: Kioxia Announces GP2 Super High IOPS SSD Series
articles.text:
Thursday, November 26th 2026
Kioxia Announces GP2 Super High IOPS SSD Series
Kioxia Corporation, a world leader in memory solutions, today announced the KIOXIA GP2 Series Super High IOPS SSD, the second product in its KIOXIA GP Series of SSDs optimized for direct GPU access. Building on the technology and architecture of the KIOXIA GP1 Series SSD announced in August 2026, the KIOXIA GP2 Series delivers over 18 million random read IOPS at a 512-byte block size, nearly double the performance of its predecessor. It is also expected to deliver sequential read throughput of up to 28 GB/s, enough to saturate a PCIe 6.0 x4 link.
Super High IOPS SSDs can expand the effective capacity of a GPU system's High Bandwidth Memory (HBM) by providing an additional flash-based memory tier directly accessible by the GPU, supporting industry efforts to improve AI system capability and efficiency. This approach enables AI systems to access larger datasets, including those used in large graph neural networks, at a significantly lower cost than adding more HBM or DRAM at the same capacity, while improving GPU utilization.KIOXIA GP2 Series SSDs leverage the company's XL-FLASH generation 3 low-latency, high-performance flash memory, which is uniquely positioned to deliver higher endurance and approximately 2.5 times the IOPS of typical TLC-based SSDs, to support fine-grained data access needed for memory extension usage, and consume significantly less power per I/O. Next generations of the KIOXIA GP Series will target up to 100 million random read IOPS.
KIOXIA GP2 Series Super High IOPS SSD
Key features of the KIOXIA GP2 Series include:
- Designed to PCIe 6.0 and NVMe 2.3 specifications
- Features KIOXIA XL-FLASH generation 3 low-latency flash memory
- Random read performance of more than 18 million IOPS at 512-byte block size
- Form factors under consideration include E1.S 9.5 mm and E3.S
- Direct Liquid cooling support
- Sequential read throughput performance of up to 28 GB/s
- Up to 50 DWPD endurance
As AI workloads continue to grow in scale and complexity, Kioxia remains committed to advancing flash memory technology to help address the evolving performance and capacity demands of AI and high-performance computing architectures.
Evaluation samples of the KIOXIA GP2 Series SSDs will be available to select customers by the end of 2027.

articles.title: A month with the iPhone Duo has changed how I use my phone
articles.text:
For years, the definition of a premium smartphone depended on its cameras, processors, and how light it felt when you stowed it in your pocket. The iPhone Duo challenges that concept by asking consumers to pay more for a fundamentally different smartphone experience, even if it means sacrificing what they’ve long thought of as high-end features.
In a little under a month of using the Duo, I’ve found that the trade-offs I was initially concerned about matter far less to me than I had expected. What’s been more interesting is how the Duo’s foldable form factor has changed my everyday habits, including how I interact with apps, which apps I use, and how I organize and personalize the phone itself.
I also easily forgot a number of my initial concerns about switching to the Duo. The apps, for the most part, are now optimized for the Duo; I’ve reacquainted myself with Touch ID; and I don’t miss the Pro Max camera on most days.
That’s not to say the Duo doesn’t have its shortcomings. I still miss that telephoto lens sometimes, and I’m still longing for Face ID — though not as much since Apple shipped a face unlock feature in the latest update. But after a month of using the Duo, I’ve found these compromises have had less of an impact on my day-to-day experience compared with the benefits that the new form factor brings.
Multitasking feels more natural
I was surprised by how much I’ve grown to appreciate the Duo’s multitasking capabilities. Initially, I didn’t think I’d regularly use it to view two apps side by side, given the still fairly limited screen space even while the phone is unfolded, especially compared with an iPad. But I’ve found myself snapping apps to both halves of the screen more often than I had imagined.
For starters, Apple has made this side-by-side mode incredibly intuitive and easy to use — you simply drag the app over to the left or right side of the screen and drop it into the target box that appears.
I have regularly taken advantage of this feature to do all sorts of things.
I really enjoy keeping X open as I read through the news, which allows me to switch back and forth between the article I’m reading and real-time reactions to it. Sometimes I’ll keep email or Slack open on the side while I’m working on something else so I don’t miss an important message or notification.
And much like the overstimulated members of Gen Z (which I am not), I sometimes like scrolling social media while engaging with some other media off to the side.
Case in point: I passively watched Netflix’s “Love is Blind” reunion while reading the gossipy tweets and Reddit posts about the main characters on the other side of the screen. This sort of TV watching behavior used to be called second-screen viewing, but now it’s morphing into something new. Everything is happening on one screen, so should we call it “Duo screen viewing,” perhaps? It makes me long for even more interactive TV experiences where commentary and content are combined.
It really is like having two phones
I’ve noticed another shift in my behavior since adopting the Duo as my main device. When I’m out and about, the Duo feels more like an (arguably heavier) iPhone mini. For those who still miss smaller iPhones, the Duo is the next best thing. Despite its weight, the phone feels small. You can cover it with one hand; you can type with a thumb; you can reach the top and bottom easily; and you can even fit it into your front and back pockets. The Pro Max now feels unbelievably strange in my hand — how was I ever comfortable wrangling this giant rectangle?
The Duo’s small screen works well when you’re on the go, especially for short interactions like responding to a quick text or pulling up directions to a destination. It’s not as great for mindless scrolling, which I appreciate, as it forces me to engage with the real world instead of killing every moment of boredom or unease by opening up apps.
But when you’re home or somewhere with time to kill, you can unfold the screen and enjoy your apps super-sized. It’s the best of both worlds.
I find that I instinctively unfold the phone when I’m preparing to watch videos, because the larger screen is best for that. It’s also unfolded if I’m shopping, as it’s more convenient for looking at products, zooming in to examine the details, or complete checkout forms.
Generally, I also unfold the Duo when I’m actively using apps. This setup has also allowed me to rethink my Home Screen layout: With the Duo closed, I prefer to see just widgets on the small screen with key information like weather, time, battery life, and so on. Meanwhile, the only app icons on the Home Screen are those in the dock.
The Duo apps are ready now
In the weeks since its launch, most of the apps that weren’t yet optimized for the Duo have been upgraded to support its foldable form factor. In mid-November, Apple said there were over 200,000 Duo-ready apps, and in my experience, that certainly feels true. A majority of my so-called “daily drivers” — with the glaring exception of key Google apps like Gmail and Drive — have dropped the black band on the side of the screen that was frustrating early testers of the phone.
Most apps now take advantage of the available space, whether that’s on the Duo’s small front screen or the wider, unfolded one.
I’ve also found it interesting to see the different interpretations developers have had for how to best optimize their app for Duo.
Some have used the form factor as a way to bring in some sort of novelty: there’s a note-taking app that opens and closes like a notebook, with pages you can write on with the Apple Pencil; a retro Walkman-like music player; a tiny typewriter; a gaming handheld; a game where you close the phone to make grilled cheese.
As much as I love the whimsy of this group of apps, I appreciate how my everyday apps feel better to use on the unfolded screen. Spotify, at last, feels less cluttered when it has more screen real estate. A number of note-taking, list-making, and calendar apps also feel somehow more usable when spread out.
The Netflix app is actually fantastic with its support for multiple viewing modes, which include playing video on the closed outer display, the “laptop” orientation with its big player controls, and the “tent” mode.
Other developers have similarly reimagined how their app would work if it had originally been designed for the Duo’s small and larger screens.
One good example of this is Sofa, a handy utility for organizing the books, movies, TV shows, podcasts, albums, and games you want to check out. When the Duo is closed, its navigation is tucked off to the right side in a vertical bar, while the main screen focuses on the items you’ve saved. But when the Duo is unfolded, the number of items displayed on the screen also expands into a two-column layout, with more of your items featured on the screen and your lists on the left side. It doesn’t feel like two different apps, but like you’ve opened up the app itself and given it more space to spread out.
In terms of your daily social media scroll, apps like TikTok and Instagram have been updated to be perfectly usable on the Duo, whether the phone is open or closed. When closed, TikTok now stretches the video to cover the screen, instead of showing the ugly black bar. Scrolling short-form videos on the Duo, while unfolded like a slightly smaller iPad mini, has become my preferred way to watch.
I’m reading more books
Here’s another surprise: I’ve spent less time with my Kindle, and am instead reading books on my Duo. Unfolded, the Duo is a decent enough replacement for an e-book reader, albeit it can be a bit more stimulating as it’s not an e-ink device. However, the matte inner screen isn’t quite as bright and distracting as your typical glossy OLED display. There’s less glare and softer reflections, but there’s also something about the display that just feels calmer than a smartphone, allowing you to more fully engage with a book’s text.
Unfolded and held vertically, reading on the Duo feels a lot like reading on the standard Kindle, at least in terms of hand-feel. And putting your phone into the “Do Not Disturb” focus mode can help you not be distracted by incoming notifications and messages while you read.
You can also unfold the device while keeping it in landscape orientation, with the screens bent slightly inward like a real book. For even more fun, you can turn on Kindle’s page-turn animation, which makes it seem as if you’re turning the page in a physical book. And I love how you can “performatively read” using an app like Book2Life or Actually Read — they display the book’s cover on the Duo’s outer screen as you read the text on the inner screen.
E-book readers will likely find they can carry one less device when they’re out and about, because the Duo can stand in for whatever Kindle or other reader you typically keep in your purse or bag. You can save the Kindle for other times, whether that’s at home, on long travel days, or when you don’t want to worry about sand getting into your $2,000 phone.
I don’t need a PopSocket
On the big-screened iPhone 17 Pro Max I used to carry, I tended to keep a PopSocket of some sort on the back because the phone was both heavy and large, which made it hard to hold for longer periods of time. The Duo is similarly heavy, but its shape makes it far easier to hold in one hand without the extra help.
Folded, you can do the usual one-handed hold where the bottom edge of the phone rests on your pinky, your other three fingers cradle the back, and your thumb is free to navigate the screen.
Unfolded, the Duo’s like using a small Kindle or iPad mini, where two hands are required. You also don’t need a PopSocket for balancing the phone on the side, because it can be propped up like a tent or opened like a tiny laptop. Or, if you prefer, Apple and others offer Duo cases with a built-in stand. (Apple’s case comes in navy and taupe, though, so if you’re not boring, you’ll probably want to shop from third-party vendors).
If you think you still might need a PopSocket at times, or you just aren’t ready to give it up, the brand now makes a slimmer version: its Low-Pro Grip. There are other competitors, like the OhSnap grips, which aren’t a bad alternative either.
It’s inspiring personalization
There’s something about the Duo that seems to have kicked off a new iPhone personalization trend, at least judging by what I’ve been seeing on social media.
Unlike a regular iPhone, where every phone case is simply a shell that offers a degree of protection based on the materials used, the Duo case lineup provides far more variety.
You can buy cases with and without built-in screen protectors, and some use adhesive to better stick to the outer screen, while others don’t. Some cases let you customize the band around the outer screen with a different color than the case that protects the rest of the phone.
Then you have cases that cover the hinge, while others leave it exposed. There are cases that offer holes where you can attach straps, wristlets, and charms. Some of those have attachment points at the bottom and others on the side.
Essentially, there are a lot of options for customizing how you want to carry the Duo and how you want to express your own style.
I’m also now starting to see whimsical cases that come with attached pens. (Thank goodness — most of the pen cases so far have been kind of plain!)
I also believe there’s something about the Duo that particularly appeals to women. Maybe because it’s small, or maybe it’s because you can attach a strap to its side and carry it like a little purse. Or maybe because, like a purse, you can deck it out with chains and charms — a choice that’s grown increasingly popular as young people have embraced whimsical, retro tech as a way to express their individuality and sense of fashion.
The Duo easily lends itself to this trend, perhaps even more than a regular iPhone. It becomes an accessory you want on display, not one buried in a bag.
Before switching to the Duo, I spent a lot of time thinking about what I’d be giving up by moving away from the Pro Max.
I’m surprised to find that, a month later, I only think about what I’d have to give up if I switched back to a traditional iPhone. It’s not just the extra space of the unfolded screen I’d miss — it’s all the little habits I’ve developed around having different screen sizes for different purposes.
The Duo makes me pause and think about how I want to use an app. That small moment of deliberation, before I even open the phone, has helped me break some of my more mindless smartphone habits, particularly around social media.
That’s not a benefit I could have anticipated if I’d judged the device by its specifications alone.

articles.title: Are there hidden gems in Dollarama’s tech section? [Part 3]
articles.text:
All the way back in 2022, I took it upon myself to find out whether the tech section at Dollarama carries hidden gems — you know, to alleviate some of the financial burden that comes with being a tech enthusiast.
Armed with a few dollars and VERY low expectations, I bought a bunch of products from the Canadian value retailer, including Bluetooth speakers, headphones, wireless chargers, gaming mice, and more. Although some of the purchases turned out to be complete duds, I actually managed to find some decent products that punched well above their weight class.
That one-off experiment turned into a two-part series, and now, four years later, I’m back with a third edition.
First things first, Dollarama’s tech section has definitely gotten more interesting in the last four years, even though it’s still dominated by the Tech1 brand.
My new haul includes not only a wireless mouse and a MagSafe-compatible accessory, but also wireless earbuds and even a gadget designed to give other drivers the middle finger — literally.
Here’s what I found at my local Dollarama:
Audio on a budget
Acellories GemstonePro wireless earbuds ($5.03)
We’re starting strong with this one. After selling wired audio products for years now, Dollarama now carries wireless earbuds, and they’re surprisingly good considering they cost just about the same as two large double-doubles from Timmies.
The first thing I noticed when I was picking up the earbuds was their packaging. For something that costs $5, Accellories has spent a lot of resources ensuring a somewhat positive first impression. The other big thing is that they’re available in two colorways: White and Black.
I picked up the Black ones and was surprised to see extra silicone tips and a charging cable included in the box.
It makes you wonder what the company’s margin is if it includes all that in a $5 package. Also makes you wonder whether all the bigger brands are charging us a premium for things that don’t cost all that much. Of course, there’s a lot more that goes into the price of wireless earbuds than what all is included in the package, and the GemstonePro shines in that department too.
The earbuds don’t boast the most premium build out there, but they don’t feel flimsy either. The buds and the case feature a Nothing-like translucent design, with an RGB LED battery indicator on the latter. The buds themselves feature a mic and capacitive touch buttons on each stem to play/pause music, which I REALLY wasn’t expecting on a $5 device.
The case charges via USB-C, and I’ve found that the buds are good for roughly 1.5 hours of playback on a full charge. Acellories claims 20 hours of playback with the case, though that claim is definitely incorrect. I was able to get roughly 5 hours of playback. Just one full charge of the buds knocked the case’s battery indicator from 100% down to 52%.
Lastly, and most importantly, the buds don’t sound tinny, as we’ve come to expect from cheap earbuds. In fact, they’re surprisingly decent for something that costs $5, as long as you’re not expecting audiophile-grade sound here. Normally, I’d say that earbuds this cheap are best reserved for listening to podcasts and audiobooks, but the GemstonePro are good enough for music too.
They’re also a great option for kids who just can’t be trusted with expensive options just yet.
Tech1 wired gaming headset ($4.78)
Remember when I said the GemstonePro doesn’t feel flimsy? Well, these are the opposite. One wrong move, and I feel like I could snap these with ease. That, however, is the only real complaint I have with the headset.
Audio-wise, they sound decent enough, with loud and clear audio. Bass is practically non-existent, but I was still able to make out which direction enemy footsteps were coming from in games like Valorant. That, in itself, justifies the $5 price tag.
The microphone works great too, so your teammates shouldn’t have any trouble understanding your comms.
Similar to the GemstonePro, I’d recommend picking these up for a kid who’s just getting into gaming. Considering the build quality, they won’t last long, but they’ll get the job done.
Tech1 USB-C to 3.5mm audio adapter ($4.50)
Nothing much to see here. If you own 3.5mm wired headphones or earbuds and would like to use them with your modern USB-C phone, this $4.50 adapter works as intended.
Note that Tech1 hasn’t mentioned any audio specs on the packaging, so we don’t know the adapter’s bit depth. What I was able to confirm, however, is that the adapter works seamlessly with both Android and iOS phones and supports mic use too.
Phone accessories without the premium
Tech1 USB-C charging cable ($4.53)
Again, this isn’t a particularly exciting find, but a functional one nonetheless. Tech1’s USB-C to USB-C charging cable is 3ft long. More impressively, it’s braided and doesn’t feel cheap.
The packaging advertises 5V/2.1Amps, making these cables more suited to slow overnight charging, instead of quick refills during the day.
XO Poppy MagSafe-compatible case and wallet ($5)
This one actually comes as a case plus MagSafe wallet combo, though for this experiment, I was only interested in the latter.
The case fits the iPhone 12 Pro Max and the iPhone 13 Pro Max. I couldn’t find a combo for other phones, so if you happen to own either of those models, great for you. If not, getting a MagSafe-compatible wallet for $5 is still a pretty sweet deal on its own.
The wallet can hold 3 cards comfortably. You can squeeze in a fourth, but that’s also where things start getting a little tight. More importantly, the wallet’s magnets are surprisingly strong. I gave my phone a vigorous shake with the wallet attached, and it did not detach.
Tech1 touchscreen stylus and ballpoint pen ($3)
The Tech1 stylus is the first real bust of the haul. It’s a pathetic excuse of a stylus that’s basically a ballpoint pen with a soft silicone tip slapped onto the other end. There’s no tech here — the silicone tip’s job is to mimic your finger, and it doesn’t do a great job at that.
It works just fine for regular tapping and scrolling, but that’s about it. It doesn’t track properly enough to be used for sketching or for handwritten notes. In my use, I found it easier to just use my finger for tasks that required even a little accuracy.
For $3, I can see the stylus being useful for people with limited hand mobility, but for all others, I’d recommend saving your money.
Nathan Vista handheld phone carrier ($4)
This goes for over $45 on most online stores, so it being available for just $4 at Dollarama is already a big win.
Runners need to carry their phone not just for navigation, tracking, and music, but also for communication in emergency scenarios, and this phone carrier makes that easier without hurting the wallet.
The strap feels gentle on the skin and is stretchy, allowing you to wrap it around your wrist, arm, and even bicep. The phone itself sits inside a transparent compartment that registers touch, which means you can continue using your phone through the carrier while running. The case is one-size-fits-all, and I was able to squeeze an iPhone 17 Pro Max in with ease, so most slab phones should fit just fine.
For just $4, this is an absolute steal for runners.
Budget desk setup
Tech1 wireless optical mouse ($4.78) and N Squared multicoloured desk pad ($4.50)
After the wireless GemstonePro earbuds, the Tech1 wireless mouse might just be the biggest standout of the haul.
Looks-wise, the mouse isn’t all that special. It has an ordinary look to it, but don’t let that fool you. The mouse sports a small footprint, and it’s extremely light too. It runs on a single AA battery, which does add to the mouse’s overall weight, but nothing substantial.
It communicates over a 2.4Ghz connection with a USB-A dongle that you plug into your device of choice. When not in use, the dongle can conveniently sit inside the mouse body, making the $4.78 gadget a solid addition to your portable setup.
The N Squared multicoloured desk pad, on the other hand, seems to have confused itself with a mousepad. A traditional mousepad only needs to accommodate your mouse, while a desk pad is supposed to cover a big portion of your desk, if not all of it.
At 14×14 inches, the $4.50 N Squared multicoloured desk pad is so small that it can’t really be called a desk pad. I don’t see the point of getting this, unless you’re looking to cover your bedside table with it.
And even if you do try to use it as a mousepad, the leather-like finish will ensure that there’s just enough friction that your mouse can’t glide across as intended. This was another miss for me.
Wonderfully unnecessary
Tech1 electronic hand gesture for cars ($5)
That subhead is exactly how I felt when I first saw the hand-gesture light at Dollarama. It’s literally a hand with Orange LEDs across it that alternate to display three different hand gestures: rock on/devil horns, an open palm, and the middle finger.
The sign is meant to go on the rear glass of your car, attached with the included sticky Velcro pads. The sign itself takes three AA batteries, while its remote takes one AAA cell.
Although not exactly my thing — I’d rather focus on the road than flipping other drivers off — the device works surprisingly well. The LEDs themselves are bright, and I was easily able to make out the gestures through my car’s tinted rear windshield — even during the day.
And if you’re like me and don’t want to gesture to other drivers on the road, no one’s stopping you from using it in your room instead. Think of it like that reversible octopus mood plushie, but with a remote control.
HomeDeco colour-changing moon light ($5)
I’m leaving this haul’s biggest dud for the end. I’m actually a big night light guy. I’m not scared of the dark, but I like having a faint light glowing somewhere in the room if and when I need to get up in the middle of the night.
The light requires three AA batteries, and even after popping in a fresh set, the light just didn’t turn on.
I found others online with working units, so I likely got a defective one. This happened with a few products in earlier editions, so I’m not all that surprised. That’s $5 lost on a moon that never shines.

articles.title: Agnikul’s rocket ambitions gather pace, but commercial revenue yet to take off
articles.text:
Agnikul’s rocket ambitions gather pace, but commercial revenue yet to take off
The spacetech company is investing heavily in its launch ambitions and attracting fresh funding, but, with no operating revenue yet, commercialisation remains its biggest test.
Agnikul Cosmos is continuing to build the technology and infrastructure for a private launch business. But its FY26 audited accounts show that the financial returns from its efforts are yet to materialise.
The Chennai-based spactech company reported no revenue from operations for the fourth consecutive financial year, even as its spending and investment commitments increased.
For the year ended March 31, 2026, Agnikul reported a net loss of Rs 60.22 crore, against Rs 54.79 crore in FY25. Total income fell 22.5% to Rs 6.04 crore. Crucially, almost all of this came from interest on fixed deposits, which contributed Rs 5.83 crore.
Total expenses rose 25.2% to Rs 66.27 crore. Employee benefits accounted for Rs 29.37 crore, while other expenses came to Rs 29.15 crore. Cash used in operating activities increased to Rs 58.50 crore from Rs 36.73 crore. The figures show the cost of maintaining a technical workforce and developing a complex hardware business before commercial operations begin.
The balance sheet points to continued investment. Capital work-in-progress increased to Rs 82.63 crore from Rs 51.30 crore, while property, plant and equipment rose to Rs 34.29 crore from Rs 16.13 crore.
The group also disclosed Rs 121.84 crore of outstanding commitments for capital expenditure, against Rs 17.82 crore a year earlier. Cash and bank balances stood at Rs 105.22 crore, although only Rs 13.76 crore was classified as cash and cash equivalents.
Agnikul has, however, made progress on the technology front. Its Agnibaan SOrTeD mission, launched on May 30, 2024, was a sub-orbital technology demonstration that tested its indigenous systems, including a single-piece 3D-printed engine. The flight, from the company’s privately developed launchpad at Sriharikota, was an important milestone.
There are also signs of a shift towards commercial applications. In February, Agnikul announced a multi-mission, multi-year agreement with Bengaluru-based NeevCloud to launch and host an orbital AI data-centre module using Agnibaan’s extendable upper stage.
Co-founder and CEO Srinath Ravichandran noted that the agreement would extend over three to four years. Its financial value was not disclosed. The initial plan was to prototype the concept in 2026, with deployment targeted for mid-2027.
Ravichandran has also outlined ambitions to achieve profitability within two years and scale up to 50 launches annually by 2030, subject to market demand and available capacity. The company is exploring a business model that combines launch fees with recurring income from hosting customer equipment on orbital platforms.
Agnikul’s next launch is expected in the first half of 2027, with the company indicating that it will demonstrate reusable launch-vehicle and upper-stage technologies.
Meanwhile, on September 25, 2026, the Technology Development Board, under the Department of Science and Technology, announced Rs 200 crore in financial support under the Research, Development and Innovation Fund for developing a fully reusable Agnibaan launch vehicle. The support, structured through optionally convertible debentures, aims to advance the technology from Technology Readiness Level 4 and above towards Level 8.
Agnikul has demonstrated that it can build and fly an indigenous rocket technology demonstrator, while beginning to establish commercial relationships. The challenge now is to turn these advances into repeatable missions, paying customers, and sustainable revenue.
Edited by Swetha Kannan

articles.title: ChatGPT et Codex vont partager les limites d'utilisation, qu'est-ce que ça va changer ?
articles.text:
Vous utilisez ChatGPT, Codex et Work ? Les limites d'utilisation vont bientôt être fusionnées. Si vous voulez discuter avec ChatGPT, il va falloir faire attention à votre consommation de tokens. OpenAI se veut toutefois rassurant.
OpenAI va modifier la gestion des quotas pour ses abonnements payants Plus, Pro et Business. Dès décembre, les outils ChatGPT, Work et Codex partageront une limite d'usage unique. En plus de ça, OpenAI va lâcher le décompte par message, au profit d'une mesure basée sur la consommation de tokens.
Une fusion de Chat et Work
OpenAI a annoncé vouloir fusionner Chat et Work. Sur X, Thibault Sottiaux, d'OpenAI, a annoncé le déploiement progressif de cette expérience combinée auprès d'un petit groupe d'utilisateurs ayant souscrit à l'abonnement Pro, avant de généraliser la fusion.
Certains utilisateurs pourraient d'ailleurs voir ces changements s'appliquer avant le mois de décembre, le temps pour l'entreprise de recueillir des retours.
Codex et Work partageaient déjà leurs limites
Jusqu'ici, les outils Work et Codex, conçus pour des tâches allant de la création de présentations au développement d'applications, partageaient déjà un plafond commun. Les conversations classiques sur ChatGPT avaient toutefois leur propre quota. Il était donc possible d'épuiser son quota Codex en développant une application, tout en conservant la possibilité d'utiliser les modèles « Thinking » de ChatGPT pour échanger des idées ou résoudre des problèmes complexes.
Mais à partir de décembre, le quota devient global. Passer des heures à programmer sur Codex réduira ainsi la capacité à utiliser ChatGPT pour des tâches exigeantes, comme la recherche approfondie.
Dans le même sens, un usage intensif de ChatGPT grignotera des tokens d'utilisation pour Codex ou Work.
- Assistant IA extrêmement polyvalent
- Fonctionnalités gratuites nombreuses
- Automatisation de tâches complexes
La fonction de discussion instantanée « Instant chat » fera toutefois exception. Elle ne sera pas décomptée de ce quota partagé. Les utilisateurs pourront ainsi avoir des discussions courantes avec ChatGPT, sans puiser dans leur crédit destiné aux requêtes complexes.
Un changement de la méthode de calcul
Pour cette mutualisation, OpenAI change sa méthode de calcul. La consommation ne sera plus évaluée au nombre de messages, mais au nombre de tokens consommés. Les modèles avancés et les requêtes lourdes pèseront donc davantage sur le forfait. Par d'exemple, poser une question simple à un modèle « Thinking » consommera moins de ressources que de lui soumettre un long document à analyser.
Si OpenAI n'a pas précisé le volume exact de ces nouveaux plafonds, l'entreprise estime que la majorité des utilisateurs payants atteindront leurs limites moins fréquemment qu'aujourd'hui. Les utilisateurs auront également la possibilité de suivre l'état de leur consommation dans la section Réglages > Utilisation.
Si vous épuisez votre quota, alors, racheter des crédits supplémentaires est toujours possible. Sinon, il faudra passer à une formule d'abonnement supérieure, ou attendre la réinitialisation de la limite.
Source : Android Authority

articles.title: L’intelligence artificielle, nouveau moteur de l’obsolescence programmée ?
articles.text:
L’intelligence artificielle, nouveau moteur de l’obsolescence programmée ?
Le développement tous azimuts de l’intelligence artificielle est-il compatible avec le nécessaire allongement de la durée de vie de nos produits ? Pour l’Ademe, la question se pose sérieusement.
On le sait désormais très bien, les centres de données nécessaires au développement de l’intelligence artificielle ont un impact concret et direct sur le changement climatique. Mais qu’en est-il des impacts indirects ?Dans un rapport publié en juillet 2026, l’agence de l’environnement et de la maîtrise de l’énergie (Ademe) pose la question s’intéresse entre autres aux "effets rebonds et les transferts d’impact" que peut présenter cette technologie.
Y est notamment posée la question du rôle de l’intelligence artificielle dans le raccourcissement du cycle de renouvellement des produits. En d’autres termes, la manière dont l’IA peut représenter un nouveau moteur de l’obsolescence programmée.
Obsolescence et usure prématurée
L’arrivée de nouveaux ordinateurs taillés pour Copilot ou pour l’exploitation de modèle d’IA locale pourrait ainsi "accélérer le renouvellement d’équipements fonctionnels afin d’accéder à des équipements IA-compatibles", note l’Ademe, tout en reconnaissant qu’"à ce stade, il semblerait que ce soit surtout une opportunité marketing, jouant sur l’obsolescence culturelle".
Mais l’impact carbone de ces effets de bord pourrait dépasser la seule obsolescence culturelle. "Afin de faire fonctionner des IA localement sur les smartphones […] il faut des puces spécialisées, de la mémoire vive en quantité importante… ce qui augmente inévitablement l’empreinte environnementale de leur fabrication", explique l’agence. Et si les outils d’IA continuent de se glisser dans tous les recoins de nos logiciels, c’est des pans entiers de notre flotte actuelle d’appareils électroniques qui pourraient être victime d’une certaine forme d’obsolescence logicielle.
Enfin, l’agence note aussi qu’"avec l’arrivée d’agents IA autonomes, le nombre de bots (utilisateurs artificiels) pourrait croitre significativement et exercer une pression sur les réseaux de télécommunication" qu’il faudrait renforcer ou renouveler pour leur permettre de tenir le choc. On pourrait sans doute en dire autant des GPU qui sont soumis à un usage intensif lors des phases d’entraînement des modèles, ce qui use prématurément les composants.
L'effet de l'IA sur la durabilité
Pour l’association Halte à obsolescence Programmée (HOP), "les exigences de durabilité, de réparabilité et de réemploi appliquées aux appareils du quotidien ont vocation à s’étendre aux infrastructures qui font tourner l’IA et le cloud sur ces derniers."
Dans ses 40 mesures stratégiques pour 2027, HOP appelle à s’intéresser à ces effets de bord encore ignorés. Elle appelle de ses vœux la conception d’un rapport qui prendrait en compte "les effets de l’IA sur la durée de vie matérielle des produits, sur la contribution réelle que pourrait avoir l’IA sur l’entretien et la réparation des produits et sur les risques d’obsolescence et de renouvellement accéléré".
