articles.title: Microsoft ruft Code Red aus: Nach IT-Ausfall sollen Fehler schneller behoben werden
articles.text:
Alarm nach globalem IT-Ausfall: Microsoft ruft intern Code Red aus
Mitte November 2026 sorgte eine massive IT-Panne dafür, dass Nutzer:innen und Firmen weltweit rund 24 Stunden lang nicht auf Microsoft-Dienste wie Outlook, Teams oder Copilot zugreifen konnten. Laut Microsoft-365-Manager Jason Henderson handelte es sich zudem um den folgenschwersten Ausfall der Cloud-E-Mail-Lösung Exchange Online.
Ursache für Mega-Microsoft-Panne
Noch nie seien so viele Kund:innen so lange ohne E-Mail-Zugang gewesen, schrieb Henderson in einem internen Memo, das Reuters vorliegt. Die Ursache für den Ausfall sieht Microsoft in einem Programmfehler, der seit Juli 2026 unentdeckt im System geschlummert haben soll. Aber warum hat es so lange gedauert, die Dienste wieder zum Laufen zu bringen?
Internen Dokumenten nach hätten sich die Microsoft-Ingenieur:innen durch eine Art „Nebel des Krieges“ kämpfen müssen, wie Vice President Amanda Silver klagte. Die für die Behebung der Schäden eingesetzten Mitarbeiter:innen hätten in elf verschiedenen Team-Chats mehr als 11.000 Nachrichten ausgetauscht, wie es bei Reuters heißt.
Mitarbeiter verlieren den Überblick
Dabei sei es schwergefallen, den Überblick zu behalten. Die Diagnosedaten seien über verschiedene interne Systeme verstreut gewesen. Dadurch soll über einen längeren Zeitraum ein gemeinsamer Überblick über mögliche Ursachen gefehlt haben. Auch schon getroffene Entscheidungen sollen nicht bei allen angekommen sein.
Mithilfe des jetzt ausgerufenen Code Red will Microsoft die technischen Abläufe und die interne Reaktion auf größere Störungen optimieren. Ziel ist es, künftige weitere weltweite Störungen innerhalb von einer Stunde zu beheben.
KI-Agenten sollen Daten schneller auswerten
Dabei sollen unter anderem KI-Agenten zum Einsatz kommen. Diese sollen technische Daten schneller auswerten und Fehlerquellen erkennen. In täglichen oder wöchentlichen Besprechungen sollen entsprechende Fortschritte kontrolliert werden, wie heute.at berichtet.
Weiterhin will Microsoft auch die Geschwindigkeit bei der Verteilung von Softwareupdates erhöhen. In anderen Fällen habe ein entsprechender Patch schon einmal fünf bis sechs Tage bis zum weltweiten Rollout gebraucht, wie es intern heißt. Künftig sollen besonders dringende Sicherheitsprobleme ebenfalls innerhalb einer Stunde adressiert sein.
„Mitarbeiter verlieren den Überblick“ ach nur die Männlichen?

articles.title: New LCD technology promises three times the brightness and twice the lifespan of OLED
articles.text:
First look: A television's backlight usually starts as white light that a color filter then splits into red, green, and blue. Seoul Semiconductor wants to drop that step by placing individual red, green, and blue chips behind a standard LCD panel, spaced only tens of micrometers apart. The company says the approach, called WICOP Pixel, covers 100% of the DCI-P3 color gamut used in digital cinema, reaches peak brightness of up to 3,000 nits, and has now entered mass production.
The design comes from Seoul Viosys, a Seoul Semiconductor subsidiary. Its WICOP technology removes the conventional package, the housing that normally surrounds an LED die. The chip structure is robust enough to be handled like an ordinary electronic component. The technique was first applied to blue opto-semiconductors and has since been extended to green, red, and ultraviolet wavelengths.
WICOP Pixel combines several of those wavelengths in a single pixel unit. Each color is controlled independently and mixed precisely. The company says this reproduces tens of thousands of natural colors efficiently and vividly.
The performance claims are aimed squarely at OLED, which has long been the reference for premium picture quality. Seoul Semiconductor says peak brightness of up to 3,000 nits is more than three times what OLED delivers, and that the design lasts more than twice as long. Brightness matters most in rooms with a lot of ambient light, and the company points to living rooms and public spaces as the settings where the gap shows. It says the result is sharp images even in bright indoor and outdoor environments.
DCI-P3 is a color gamut developed for digital cinema. Hitting 100% means a display can reproduce the entire range. The company says that coverage gives richer, more vivid color than OLED. The release also lists BT.2020, the ITU's standard for ultra-high-definition video, among its reference standards, though it gives no coverage figure for it.
None of these numbers come from independent testing. They are the manufacturer's own specifications, and real-world results will depend on how TV makers tune panels, local dimming, and image processing around the new light source.
Because the light source sits behind an ordinary LCD, the design keeps TV makers on familiar panel supply chains. Seoul Semiconductor argues this raises product value and profitability for manufacturers and reduces their dependence on expensive LCD panels. It also frames the technology as a draw for home-theater sets.
The company is also researching the removal of the color filter, which accounts for about 20% of LCD panel material costs. That follows from the design itself: if the backlight already produces pure red, green, and blue, a filter that carves colors out of white light becomes less necessary. The company describes this as research, not a shipping feature.
Seoul Semiconductor says it has begun expanding supply to global TV manufacturers. Its display-related revenue in the third quarter rose nearly 20% year over year. Rather than commit to significant new capital spending, it plans to convert existing white-backlight capacity to WICOP Pixel production.
A patent licensing program is also part of the plan. The company expects royalties to boost revenue and profit while keeping customer supply stable. It says it will channel that income into research and development in biotechnology, 3D printing, AR, and AI data communications.
Market research firm Omdia says the shift to RGB backlights is accelerating. It expects global RGB TV shipments, led by large-screen premium models, to reach about 7 million units by 2030, representing more than 10% of global TV market revenue. The white-backlight market is about $3 billion today. Seoul Semiconductor says the market is expected to more than double as it shifts to RGB with the adoption of advanced packaging technology.
Industry watchers will want to see which TV brands adopt the chips, how the sets compare with OLED in independent tests, and whether color-filter removal makes it from the lab into commercial products. The licensing strategy also warrants attention, since it positions the company as both a component supplier and a patent holder in a segment that Omdia expects to grow quickly.

articles.title: A fully 3D-printed quadcopter drone is bidding for a speed world record challenge — but does it have what it takes?
articles.text:
A fully 3D-printed quadcopter drone is bidding for a speed world record challenge — but does it have what it takes?
The world’s fastest drone record is up for grabs again, and the biggest obstacle may be paperwork, not speed
- Three teams are attempting the fastest battery-powered RC quadcopter record in Cape Town today, using drones built on Bambu Lab H3C and H2C printers
- The official record is 657.59 km/h, set by the Bells in December 2025, though Biggs's uncertified runs have already averaged 685 km/h
- Only the airframes are printed, and Bambu Lab has not said whether Guinness witnesses will attend or what build rules apply
Three teams of makers from three countries are aiming for the Guinness World Records title for the fastest battery-powered remote-controlled quadcopter, flying drones built on Bambu Lab's new H3C and H2C 3D printers as part of the company's Let's Make It Fund program.
The number to beat is 657.59 km/h (408.60 mph), set on December 11, 2025, by Cape Town father-and-son duo Luke and Mike Bell, who are also among today's challengers.
They will be joined by Australian aerospace engineer Ben Biggs and John Xu, an MIT mechanical engineering student living in Boston.
A number on the board, three teams, and one very fast target
Guinness's rules for this category are narrower than their "fastest drone" moniker suggests: the aircraft must have four separate fixed rotors providing lift and thrust; tiltrotors fall under a different category, and commercially available models are excluded, so every contender must be a prototype or a heavily modified one-off.
Speed is not a single flat-out pass either: the drone flies back and forth along a measured course, and the runs in opposite directions are averaged to cancel out the wind.
The record has moved quickly too: According to Guinness, the Bells first set it at 480 km/h in 2024 and pushed it to 580 km/h in June 2025. Biggs then took it with his Blackbird at around 626 km/h (389 mph) in late 2025, before the Bells snatched it back with the Peregreen V4. The official figure has therefore climbed roughly 37% in under two years.
The Bells arrive as both holders and hosts. Luke Bell, an engineer and YouTuber, built the V4 with his father, and printed its airframe on Bambu Lab's H2D as one multi-material piece in PETG, PA6-CF, and TPU, then sanded and polished it. Bell said the printer's larger build volume and dual-nozzle system made it possible to print the body as one continuous piece.
Sign up to the TechRadar Pro newsletter to get all the top news, opinion, features and guidance your business needs to succeed!
The pair have since worked with the H2C as well: in July, Luke used one alongside an H2D to build the multirotor that set a Guinness endurance record of 4 hours, 21 minutes and 39 seconds on a single charge.
Biggs is the man with the fastest numbers and the thinnest paperwork. Flying with Aidan Kelly under the Drone Pro Hub banner, he has made a habit of answering every Bell record. "So, we couldn't have that!" he said in one video after losing the crown, as New Atlas reported. In early 2026, his Blackbird hit 690 km/h on a downwind pass and averaged about 661 km/h. In May, the pair posted a 685 km/h (426 mph) two-way average with a 730 km/h (453 mph) peak. Both runs beat the official figure, and neither sadly counted because no professional observer was present.
Xu is the wild card. Bambu Lab's announcement says little beyond his studies and location, and there don't seem to be any published speed runs under his name, making his drone, team, and target speed an interesting dark horse for now.
On the teams' own telemetry, the record has already fallen twice this year. Biggs's May average sits about 27 km/h, or roughly 4%, above the Bells' certified figure. The obstacle has been logistics rather than physics, and DroneXL argues that the real gap is getting certified observers and timing equipment to a remote paddock on a calm day.
A scheduled, sponsored event in one location could close that gap, which may be the most useful thing Bambu Lab brings to the table. The company, however, does not state whether a Guinness-accredited witness will be on hand.
Cape Town's weather and Bambu Labs both have a say here
Weather will also play a large part here: Late spring and early summer are prime southeaster season in Cape Town, with November through February the city's windiest months. The setting might suit the Bells here, as they set the current record on a farm near Melkbosstrand, north of Cape Town, in December, and Luke Bell told the Cape Argus that the V4 needed about 30 test flights over five months of tuning.
The contest is not happening in a vacuum, however: Bambu Labs' H3C went on sale on November 3, just 23 days before the attempt, priced at $2,499 for the AMS Combo. It is Bambu Lab's first third-generation desktop printer, with nine independent tools that swap in about six seconds and heat to 350°C. TechRadar's H3C review awarded it an Editor's Choice badge while cautioning that its mixed-nozzle printing still feels like "a technology in development."
The older H2C uses Bambu Lab's Vortek system to swap between six interchangeable hotends, and TechRadar's H2C review flagged premium pricing and more moving parts than its siblings.
The driving force behind this is the Let's Make It Fund, launched in December 2025 with grants of up to $300,000 and two to five projects selected each quarter. Bambu Lab frames it as an investment in makers, "not as a PR stunt," and asks only that recipients document their journey. All3DP reported that payments arrive in stages as agreed milestones are met to Bambu Lab's satisfaction.
Drones are close to home for the company, too: CEO Ye Tao previously ran DJI's consumer drone department before co-founding Bambu Lab with fellow DJI engineers. Win or lose, today puts a three-week-old printer in front of exactly the audience that cares about high-performance printed parts, which is a large part of the point.
If conditions cooperate, the most likely outcome is a new certified figure above 657.59 km/h. Whose name goes next to it is harder to call; Biggs has the raw numbers, Xu is an unknown quantity, and the Bells' local knowledge and certification track record make them hard to bet against.

articles.title: Qué es la criptografía poscuántica y por qué el cifrado actual tendrá fecha de retiro en 2035
articles.text:
El Instituto Nacional de Estándares y Tecnología de Estados Unidos (NIST) publicó en agosto de 2024 los primeros tres estándares de criptografía poscuántica, algoritmos diseñados para resistir ataques de computadoras cuánticas. En octubre de 2026 fijó un calendario: dejará de aprobar el cifrado vulnerable a esas máquinas después de 2035.
La criptografía poscuántica es el conjunto de métodos de cifrado que ni una computadora común ni una cuántica podrían descifrar con rapidez. No requiere dispositivos cuánticos: funciona en los dispositivos actuales y se basa en problemas matemáticos distintos de los que protegen hoy internet.
El cifrado actual sostiene los mensajes privados, el correo, las compras en línea y los registros médicos. Según el NIST, se apoya en cálculos que las computadoras convencionales no pueden resolver, pero que una máquina cuántica suficientemente potente podría recorrer a gran velocidad hasta vulnerar esa protección.
El NIST no precisa cuándo existirá una máquina así. En 2024 citó la previsión de algunos expertos, que la sitúan en el plazo de una década, y por esa razón pidió comenzar la migración sin esperar.
Tres estándares de seguridad listos desde 2024
Los tres estándares se denominan FIPS 203, FIPS 204 y FIPS 205, y fueron el resultado de un proceso de ocho años. El NIST explicó que partió de 82 algoritmos propuestos por grupos de 25 países y que la comunidad criptográfica global los evaluó hasta reducir la lista.
El primero, FIPS 203, es el estándar principal para el cifrado general: sirve para que dos partes acuerden una clave secreta por una red pública. Se basa en el algoritmo CRYSTALS-Kyber, rebautizado ML-KEM, tiene claves pequeñas y funciona con rapidez.
Los otros dos protegen las firmas digitales, que confirman la identidad de quien envía un archivo o una actualización de software y que nadie lo alteró. FIPS 204 usa el algoritmo CRYSTALS-Dilithium, ahora llamado ML-DSA, y FIPS 205 se basa en SPHINCS+.
El director del proyecto, el matemático Dustin Moody, dijo en 2024: “No hay necesidad de esperar a futuros estándares”. Pidió a los administradores de sistemas que empezaran a integrar los tres algoritmos de inmediato, porque la integración completa llevará tiempo.
En marzo de 2025, el NIST eligió un algoritmo de respaldo llamado HQC, que usa otro enfoque matemático. Moody aclaró que no reemplaza a ML-KEM, que seguirá como opción recomendada, y que las organizaciones deben continuar la migración a los estándares de 2024.
El calendario de retiro: 2030 y 2035
El informe NIST IR 8547, en su versión final de octubre de 2026, establece que los algoritmos de clave pública vulnerables a la computación cuántica quedarán en desuso después de 2030 y se prohibirán, dentro de los estándares y guías del NIST, después de 2035. RSA y las curvas elípticas pertenecen a esa familia.
Ese margen de cinco años está pensado para sistemas de menor riesgo o con limitaciones heredadas. El propio informe aclara que no cambia los plazos anteriores que rigen para los sistemas federales más sensibles, fijados por la orden ejecutiva 14412 y el memorando M-26-15 de la Oficina de Administración y Presupuesto.
Europa propone una ley y un fondo de 50.000 millones de euros
El 25 de noviembre de 2026, la Comisión Europea propuso la Ley Cuántica. Busca convertir la investigación europea en capacidad industrial, reforzar las cadenas de suministro y preparar a la región ante los riesgos de ciberseguridad ligados a la computación cuántica.
La propuesta incluye un Fondo Europeo de Capital para la Soberanía Tecnológica, con un objetivo de hasta 50.000 millones de euros para invertir en tecnología cuántica y en otras áreas, como la inteligencia artificial.
La cifra tiene una salvedad. Según Finance News International, que cita las preguntas y respuestas de la Comisión, la propuesta no asigna un presupuesto fijo: el dinero dependerá de decisiones presupuestarias posteriores. La Comisión aspira a que el fondo funcione cuando empiece el próximo presupuesto europeo de largo plazo, en 2028.

articles.title: AI uncovers hidden bladder cancer warning signs years before diagnosis
articles.text:
AI uncovers hidden bladder cancer warning signs years before diagnosis
- Date:
  November 21, 2026
- Source:
  University of Plymouth
- Summary:
  Scientists have developed an AI tool that can uncover hidden warning signs of bladder cancer up to five years before diagnosis, identifying 85% of cases in a major study involving nearly 70,000 patients. By revealing subtle patterns that conventional screening misses, the technology could help doctors detect cancer earlier and spare patients unnecessary invasive procedures.
- Share:
Bladder cancer kills approximately 220,000 people worldwide each year, yet recognizing the disease early can be difficult. Its symptoms can resemble those of far less serious conditions, including kidney stones, allowing warning signs to go unnoticed.
Researchers at the University of Plymouth have now developed an artificial intelligence system that could help doctors identify people at risk of bladder cancer years before they receive a diagnosis. In some patients, the technology detected subtle warning signals dating back as far as five years.
The new approach uses AI to examine electronic health records, searching for combinations of symptoms, medical conditions, risk factors, and healthcare activity that might otherwise be overlooked. By recognizing these patterns, researchers hope to make bladder cancer screening more accurate and help doctors find the disease when treatment is most likely to succeed.
AI Finds Hidden Bladder Cancer Clues in Medical Records
Under current medical referral guidelines, one of the main warning signs of bladder cancer is visible blood in the urine (hematuria). However, blood in the urine can also result from noncancerous problems, including kidney stones and prostate conditions. This overlap makes it difficult to determine which patients need further investigation and contributes to missed cases.
Confirming bladder cancer currently requires a procedure called cystoscopy (where a long, thin tube with a small camera inside is moved up the urethra and into the bladder). Although effective, the examination is invasive, highlighting the need for better ways to identify patients who are most likely to have the disease.
To explore a possible solution, a team led by Professor Shang-Ming Zhou at the University of Plymouth's Centre for Health Technology studied electronic medical records from nearly 70,000 patients. The records covered a 25-year period, from 1995 through 2020.
The researchers created an AI model called PRECISE-AGZ and used it to investigate 48,261 possible health indicators (from smoking and exercise habits to medication use). From this enormous collection of information, the system narrowed the list to 38 features that were especially useful for predicting bladder cancer risk.
AI Identifies 85% of Bladder Cancer Cases
The results suggest that AI could substantially improve the way patients are assessed for bladder cancer.
The model correctly identified 85% of patients who had bladder cancer and accurately classified 91% of those who did not have the disease. It also performed better at detecting bladder cancer than existing NHS referral guidelines.
Importantly, the system demonstrated effective detection as early as 12 months before a patient's official diagnosis. Some of the warning signals it recognized could be traced back up to five years, suggesting that valuable clues may exist in medical records long before cancer is discovered.
The AI confirmed the importance of established risk factors, including smoking and blood in the urine. However, it also uncovered unexpected associations that conventional screening approaches would be unlikely to detect.
For example, patients diagnosed with Parkinson's disease or dementia appeared to have a lower risk of bladder cancer. Meanwhile, long-term use of tamoxifen (a breast cancer medication) was associated with a higher risk.
These findings do not establish that Parkinson's disease or dementia protects against bladder cancer, or that tamoxifen causes it. Instead, they raise questions about possible shared biological mechanisms that researchers believe deserve closer examination.
Another surprising finding involved blood in the urine. Although this symptom is often considered a major warning sign, its significance appears to depend partly on a patient's other medical conditions. Among men with benign prostate enlargement, for instance, blood in the urine was associated with a lower bladder cancer risk.
Understanding these relationships more fully could eventually help doctors distinguish patients who need urgent investigation from those who may not require invasive testing.
A New Approach to Early Cancer Screening
Beyond identifying warning signs, the AI system could also divide patients into three groups according to their estimated likelihood of having bladder cancer: low-risk (below 7% probability), uncertain (grey zone: 7-55%), and high-risk (above 55%).
This approach could help healthcare providers decide which patients need immediate attention and which may benefit from additional monitoring.
For example, patients in the uncertain category might be monitored before undergoing procedures such as cystoscopy. If further research confirms the system's reliability, this could reduce unnecessary examinations while allowing doctors to concentrate resources on people at greatest risk.
PhD student Xu Wang, who led the data analysis, said: "Bladder cancer ranks as the ninth most common cancer worldwide, with 614,000 new cases diagnosed in 2022."
"Despite its prevalence, no routine screening program exists for the general population, and - following symptoms - detection relies heavily on invasive cystoscopy procedures. Our system goes far beyond traditional symptoms, and it's great to have uncovered the results that we have. The research shows that the combination of multiple factors - from medication histories to seemingly unrelated conditions - can reveal patterns invisible to conventional screening methods."
Could AI Help Doctors Catch Bladder Cancer Earlier?
The potential benefits extend beyond improving diagnostic accuracy. Detecting bladder cancer earlier could mean more treatment options, better survival outcomes, and fewer patients undergoing invasive procedures unnecessarily.
Dr. Helen Winter, Clinical Director for the Somerset, Wiltshire, Avon and Gloucestershire (SWAG) Cancer Alliance, emphasized the importance of developing better screening methods.
"Bladder cancer has a major unmet need in early detection and the prospect of a screening tool is hugely exciting for patients and their families.
"It could identify those most at risk more accurately, reduce harm from invasive procedures, and catch cancer earlier, when survival outcomes and quality of life can be dramatically improved."
Professor Shang-Ming Zhou believes the findings point toward a more individualized approach to cancer screening, in which AI helps doctors interpret a patient's broader medical history rather than relying primarily on individual symptoms.
"This work represents a paradigm shift towards precision screening for bladder cancer.
"By harnessing the power of interpretable machine learning and comprehensive health records, we're moving closer to detecting this disease at its earliest, most treatable stages."
More Research Needed Before Clinical Use
Despite the promising results, the researchers caution that the technology is not yet ready for widespread clinical use.
All the patient information used in the study came from the SAIL database in Wales. Before the model can be introduced into other healthcare settings, researchers will need to determine whether it performs equally well with different patient populations and medical record systems.
Professor Zhou explained why broader testing is essential.
"It's important to emphasize that further validation across different healthcare systems is essential before anything is rolled out more widely - for example, all of the data analyzed came from the SAIL database in Wales, so we'd want to investigate other datasets too.
"But it's a very exciting early study. Additional studies would also be needed to confirm the causal relationships suggested by the model's predictions."
The findings offer an encouraging glimpse of how artificial intelligence might improve cancer screening by uncovering patterns hidden within years of routine medical information. With further validation, such tools could help doctors recognize bladder cancer sooner, prioritize patients who need testing, and potentially improve outcomes.
The study, "Early Detection of Bladder Cancer Using Advanced Feature Engineering and Swarm Intelligence Optimization on EHRs," was published in IEEE Transactions on Biomedical Engineering.
The research also involved collaborators from North Bristol NHS Trust and University Hospitals Bristol NHS Foundation Trust.

articles.title: Your Google Meet calls are about to get a little clearer
articles.text:
If you spend a lot of time on Google Meet, you might soon notice that everyone’s video looks a little better. Why? Google is finally upgrading users to higher-res video.
According to an update on the Google Workspace blog, the search giant revealed that it would expand 1080p video sending to Meet on the web for all users. Previously, Full HD video was limited to select paying users, and 1080p receiving was already available to all.
Now, everyone with a computer sporting a 1080p camera and sufficient compute and bandwidth will automatically have 1080p video sending. However, Workspace administrators can set different video quality defaults, so some people might not see the higher resolution depending on their workspace settings. Video settings can be adjusted by heading to Settings > Video.
Google also noted that Meet automatically scales resolution according to the size of the video tiles. In other words, when more people are in the meeting and the video tiles are smaller, it will reduce the resolution accordingly so it doesn’t burn unnecessary CPU or bandwidth.
It’s also worth noting that 1080p video is limited to those using Chromium-based browsers like Google’s own Chrome, Microsoft Edge, Brave, Vivaldi, or others. Non-Chromium browsers like Safari or Firefox won’t have 1080p video.
The search giant didn’t clarify in the blog post if there would be changes to Meet on mobile devices. Currently, smartphones can receive 1080p video, but can only transmit 720p video. Hopefully, with this change on the web, the Meet apps on Android and iOS will be next.
Google started rolling out the change on Nov. 11, but noted it could take as long as 15 days for the change to show up for users.
Source: Google Via: Android Police

articles.title: Kenya drops FlexPay criminal case in $240,000 Naivas dispute
articles.text:
Kenyan prosecutors have dropped criminal charges against four executives of fintech firm FlexPay over theft of KES 31.2 million ($240,000) claimed by supermarket chain Naivas, directing the police to close the investigation and advising the retailer to pursue the money through the civil courts.
The Office of the Director of Public Prosecutions (ODPP), in a letter dated November 6 seen by TechCabal, reversed its earlier decision to charge the four after a review of evidence submitted by the Directorate of Criminal Investigations (DCI) found the dispute civil in nature.
The decision brings to an end months of criminal investigations that saw two FlexPay executives arrested in September following the collapse of a five-year partnership between the fintech and Kenya’s largest supermarket chain, through which the two companies had processed more than KES 3 billion ($23.1 million) in customer transactions, according to court documents.
“The Director of Public Prosecutions, upon further independent and thorough review of the evidence contained in the inquiry file, has established that the dispute is civil in nature,” the ODPP said in the letter addressed to the Nairobi Regional Criminal Investigation Officer.
“Consequently, the Director of Public Prosecutions directs that the complainant, Naivas Limited, be advised to seek civil redress and the investigation file be closed with no further police action.”
Police as debt collectors
The letter followed separate representations made by lawyers from Ayieko Kangethe & Co Advocates and Guandaru Thuita & Company Advocates on September 2 and September 9, respectively, challenging the decision to institute criminal proceedings.
FlexPay directors Dennis Karanu Mwangi and Richard Machomba, chief growth officer and former director Martin Kariuki Maina, and shareholder Johnson Gituma Mwangi had faced possible prosecution for stealing by an agent after Naivas lodged a police complaint.
The four, alongside Flexitech Group Limited, the company that operates FlexPay, filed a case at the High Court in September, accusing the supermarket chain of using the police to recover a disputed commercial debt.
Four days after the DPP directed the closure of the investigation, High Court judge Roseline Aburili issued orders barring the police and prosecutors from arresting, detaining or charging the four over the dispute pending the determination of their constitutional petition.
“The prosecution must be seen to be in the public interest and not intended to aid a complainant to recover a civil debt,” Justice Aburili said in her November 10 ruling.
“Public interest is not merely served by securing convictions at all costs; it is primarily anchored on the integrity of the administration of justice. The public must have confidence that the criminal process is even-handed.”
The prosecutors’ decision is a setback for Naivas, which had maintained that FlexPay collected money on its behalf and failed to remit it, amounting to theft rather than a breach of a commercial agreement.
Competing claims
According to court documents seen by TechCabal, Naivas and FlexPay entered into a seven-year agreement on February 10, 2021, that allowed customers of the supermarket chain to pay for goods in instalments through the fintech’s digital platform.
The agreement, subsequently amended in February 2022 and December 2023, was to run until February 2028.
In an affidavit filed on October 7, Naivas told the court that FlexPay retained a 5% commission on customer payments and was required to remit the remaining 95% to the retailer by the next business day.
Naivas said the arrangement worked for five years until early 2026, when FlexPay allegedly stopped remitting the money collected from shoppers.
The retailer claimed that the fintech had written letters acknowledging the outstanding amounts and requesting more time to pay. It subsequently reported the matter to the police.
FlexPay disputed the nature of the arrangement, maintaining that it was a corporate customer of Naivas and not an agent of the supermarket chain.
The fintech told the court that Naivas had opened a corporate credit account in its name, through which it bought goods on credit and periodically settled the outstanding balances, establishing a creditor-debtor relationship between the two companies.
FlexPay also claimed that Naivas owed it at least KES 24 million ($185,000) in unreimbursed customer loyalty points and that it had incurred losses exceeding KES 300 million ($2.3 million) through alleged price manipulation by employees of the supermarket chain.
The fintech further claimed that KES 3.07 million ($23,600) it paid Naivas during the dispute had not been credited to its account. Neither the DPP’s decision nor the High Court ruling determined the validity of the financial claims either company made.
The DPP’s decision to close the inquiry file, three months after its initial correspondence with investigators on August 11, now leaves Naivas the option of pursuing its claim through civil proceedings against its former technology partner.

articles.title: Científicos recuperan bajo la Antártida un archivo geológico de entre 17 y 19 millones de años tras dos intentos fallidos y atravesar 523 metros de hielo
articles.text:
Bajo el hielo de la Antártida occidental se encuentran sedimentos que son los que nos indican cómo era esta zona antes de que quedara bajo el hielo. Para ello han tenido que trabajar en un campamento que queda a unos 700 km de las bases antárticas más cercanas. En Crary Ice Rise han conseguido sacar un núcleo de 228 m de longitud de barro y roca. Hasta ahora habían fallado en dos intentos.
Tras perforar 523 metros de hielo, han conseguido recuperar materiales de millones de años de antigüedad. Han analizado los microfósiles de los sedimentos y los más antiguos se remontan hasta hace entre 17 y 19 millones de años. Se trata de los últimos 20 m de la perforación sedimentaria. La mayor parte del núcleo está entre los 7 y los 10 millones de años.
Esto forma parte del proyecto internacional SWAIS2C, que trata de conocer la sensibilidad de la capa de hielo de la Antártida occidental ante un calentamiento de 2 grados Celsius. Los responsables del proyecto pretenden conocer qué pasó en esta zona en épocas cálidas del pasado para poder mejorar las predicciones de su respuesta al calentamiento global.
Primero el hielo, después los sedimentos
Para ello, primero han tenido que crear un agujero en el hielo mediante una técnica de perforación con agua caliente. Una vez hecho el agujero, han podido colocar las tuberías para extraer los materiales del subsuelo. En el comunicado de la expedición destacan que han trabajado en rotación durante las 24 horas del día.
Extraído un segmento, lo describen en el campo y toman fotografías. A medida que van perforando, ven las diferencias entre los diferentes estratos. Por un lado, hay materiales que corresponden a depósitos bajo el hielo sobre el terreno y, por otro, se pueden ver otros sedimentos que muestran que eran otras condiciones marinas.
De esta manera se ha obtenido el núcleo sedimentario más largo que se ha recuperado bajo una capa de hielo. Según la Escuela Politécnica Federal de Zúrich (ETH), esto es muy útil porque muestra una sucesión de ambientes que van desde los depósitos bajo el hielo hasta los de un océano abierto o plataforma flotante. De esta manera se puede estudiar la evolución de este mismo lugar.
Qué cuentan los fósiles sobre su edad y entorno
En un primer momento, la expedición estimaba que podía llegar hasta los 23 millones de años. Sin embargo, se han ido corrigiendo estos valores. Esto es gracias a los ensambles de especies de diatomeas. Estas son algas microscópicas que dejan restos que permiten datar los sedimentos.
También se pueden encontrar restos de conchas o de organismos que requieren de luz. De esta manera podemos saber que se dieron momentos de océano abierto en una zona que está ahora bajo cientos de metros de hielo.
Hasta ahora, las predicciones sobre la respuesta del hielo ante el calentamiento se basaban fundamentalmente en datos satelitales y registros geológicos de zonas cercanas (por ejemplo, bajo plataformas flotantes) o bien en el propio mar de Ross y océano Austral. Con este nuevo núcleo tenemos una secuencia directamente en el margen de la capa de hielo.
Reconstruir el retroceso para mejorar las previsiones
Las observaciones satelitales (que es lo que recoge el proyecto) muestran que esta zona de la Antártida occidental viene perdiendo masa a un ritmo que se ha acelerado en las últimas décadas. Si se derritiera totalmente, produciría un aumento medio global del nivel del mar de entre 4 y 5 metros.
Para estudiar los cambios en nuestro planeta, los investigadores emplean modelos. Para ello deben disponer de datos que les permitan validar sus predicciones. Mediante estos sedimentos van a poder comparar qué es lo que los modelos indican que haría el hielo frente a lo que realmente ocurrió en aquellos episodios en los que la temperatura media global superó en más de 2 °C los niveles preindustriales.
Por otro lado, deben seguir afinando las edades de las diferentes capas. También deben reconstruir las temperaturas oceánicas en los períodos de aguas abiertas. Esto les va a permitir saber qué procesos fueron los que desencadenaron el retroceso de la capa de hielo.

articles.title: Cloudflare now lets websites add search for AI agents with a single toggle. Site owners foot the query bill.
articles.text:
Cloudflare now lets websites add search for AI agents with a single toggle. Site owners foot the query bill.
Cloudflare has announced a new feature that makes it easier for AI agents to find and retrieve relevant information from websites, helping site owners make their content directly searchable by agents at the flick of a switch.
However, doing so could come at a cost to website owners, who are responsible for the associated search infrastructure charges.
Search for Agents, as it’s called, builds on other initiatives from Cloudflare designed to make the web more accessible to AI systems. Last month, the company officially launched AI Search, a managed service that enables developers to index their own data and integrate search functionality into applications and agents. And this serves as the underlying search infrastructure for Search for Agents.
Back in February, Cloudflare also launched Markdown for Agents, which automatically converts HTML pages into a lightweight, text-based format that AI agents can consume more efficiently — part of a broader evolution of the web to accommodate both human and machine visitors.
Search for Agents takes this further by giving websites their own agent-discoverable search API, allowing agents to query a site’s content directly without having to navigate individual pages to find the information they need.
The agent retrieval problem
Back in September, developer documentation platform Mintlify highlighted a problem with llms.txt, a file that serves AI agents with a map of a website’s content. Larger documentation sites were hitting Mintlify’s 100,000-character limit for these files, resulting in some pages being omitted. The company addressed this by introducing a hierarchy of smaller index files, allowing agents to discover all available pages without having to load the entire index.
The issue was particularly pertinent for Mintlify, which reported in April that AI coding agents accounted for 45.3% of requests across documentation sites powered by its platform, almost on a par with traditional browser traffic.
Cloudflare, for its part, also reported last year that AI crawling triggered by users’ queries had increased more than twentyfold through 2025.
Even with improvements such as those introduced by Mintlify, agents still have to navigate a website’s content index to find the information they need. Search for Agents seeks to bypass that process by allowing agents to query the website directly.
In a blog post published on Wednesday, the company detailed how website operators can enable the feature, currently in beta, via the Quick Actions section of their domain’s Cloudflare dashboard or programmatically through an API.
Once activated, Cloudflare provisions a dedicated AI Search instance and begins crawling and indexing the website’s content. Website operators can subsequently manage that instance from their AI Search dashboard, adjusting settings such as caching and enabling reranking to improve the relevance of search results.
Cloudflare also inserts instructions into the metadata of each page, telling visiting agents where the search API resides and how to use it. For websites that have enabled Markdown for Agents, these instructions are also included in the Markdown document’s YAML front matter.
Agents can then send keywords or natural-language questions to the website’s /.well-known/search endpoint, receiving relevant excerpts from the site’s content in Markdown. The agent can use this to formulate its own response to the user’s question.
Who pays for agent search?
Search for Agents is available across all Cloudflare plans, including its free tier. However, with AI Search billing set to begin on December 1, there are cost considerations for website owners looking to make their content more accessible to AI agents.
Each account receives a monthly allowance of 5 million ingestion tokens, 10 GB-months of storage, and 1,000 queries each for semantic and full-text search. Beyond those allowances, Cloudflare charges $0.75 per million ingestion tokens, $2 per GB-month of storage, $0.75 per 1,000 semantic, vector or hybrid queries, and $0.10 per 1,000 full-text queries.
Moreover, there are limits on how much content Cloudflare can crawl to populate the search index. Customers on the Workers Free plan are limited to 500 pages per day, while paying customers face no daily crawl limit. Both are subject to a 100,000-page limit per discovery crawl.
This raises an interesting question in the context of Cloudflare’s broader efforts to help website owners monetize AI traffic. Last July, the company introduced pay-per-crawl, enabling website owners to charge AI companies for fetching individual pages. The company expanded on that initiative this July with a push toward pay-per-use, whereby publishers would be compensated when their content appears in AI-generated answers. It’s part of a broader effort, as The New Stack reported at the time, to build the economic layer of the AI web.
Then in September, Cloudflare launched its Monetization Gateway in closed beta, enabling domain owners to charge AI agents for accessing websites, APIs, MCP tools and datasets using the x402 payment protocol.
Against that backdrop, the economics of Search for Agents are particularly striking. Having spent much of the past 18 months developing ways for website owners to generate revenue from AI traffic, Cloudflare is now asking those same website owners to shoulder the cost of making their content more readily accessible to AI agents.
“Our data shows that agents have now surpassed humans using the Internet and are an important audience for any website owner.”
So what incentive do website owners have to absorb these costs? According to Celso Martinho, VP of engineering at Cloudflare, it comes down to the growing importance of AI agents as an audience in their own right.
“Our data shows that agents have now surpassed humans using the Internet and are an important audience for any website owner,” Martinho tells The New Stack.
For context, Cloudflare reported back in June that bots, which include AI agents, accounted for 57% of HTML page requests across its network. Martinho also points to existing tools such as Cloudflare’s AI Crawl Control and the x402 payment protocol, which website operators can use to manage and monetize access to their content.
Moreover, plans are afoot to extend Cloudflare’s Monetization Gateway to cover the new search endpoints, which would enable website owners to charge agents directly for search queries.
“We are working on adding first-class support for Search for Agents and other agentic content APIs to Monetization Gateway,” Martinho says, though no timeline was provided.
For now, those search costs fall to website owners.
A common language for agent search?
While companies can, of course, build and expose their own search APIs, Search for Agents essentially gives Cloudflare customers an off-the-shelf solution. According to Martinho, existing agents with web browsing capabilities should be able to discover and use these endpoints without developers having to build dedicated integrations.
Cloudflare has tested the approach extensively across its own blog and developer documentation sites, Martinho says, “demonstrating that using a search API is more efficient for agents than crawling individual pages to find answers.”
“Using a search API is more efficient for agents than crawling individual pages to find answers.”
There have been broader efforts across the industry to standardize how AI agents interact with the world around them. Last December, the Linux Foundation announced the formation of the Agentic AI Foundation (AAIF), of which Cloudflare is a founding member, bringing projects such as the Model Context Protocol (MCP), AGENTS.md and Goose under a common umbrella.
For now, though, Cloudflare is pursuing its own approach to search endpoint discovery.
“Agents do a pretty good job at adjusting to different instructions and web protocols,” Martinho says, adding that Cloudflare’s research into agent behavior through initiatives such as Radar’s AI Insights and its Agent Readiness project informed its choice of technologies for Search for Agents.
Cloudflare’s approach draws on established web conventions such as well-known URIs and HTTP GET, alongside the newer HTTP QUERY method, an Internet Engineering Task Force (IETF) proposed standard co-authored by Cloudflare engineer James Snell.
However, Martinho acknowledges the merits of a broader industry effort in this area.
“Interoperability absolutely matters,” Martinho says. “A common approach to discovering search endpoints across providers would also make sense.”

articles.title: SA’s Community Wolf raises seed funding round led by Terra Industries
articles.text:
South African public safety tech startup Community Wolf has opened its seed round with a strategic investment from Terra Industries, which takes the strategic lead.
Founded in 2024 by Nick Mills and Michael Houghton, Community Wolf started with a WhatsApp number that lets anyone report crime and suspicious activity for free, anonymously and in their first language.
Its AI models structure the images, video and pin drops users submit, then alert people nearby and local responders. The startup – recently a winner at the South African Startup Awards – has since added emergency assistance, family safety, community communication and operational software for security operators. It has more than 700,000 users and has recorded over 180,000 incidents.
Terra Industries, also founded in 2024, builds autonomous security systems to protect critical infrastructure such as mines, power plants and pipelines across Africa and the Global South. Its air, land and maritime systems run on ArtemisOS, its software platform for large-scale security operations. Disrupt Africa reported in August the company had raised an additional US$18 million in strategic funding to close its own seed round at US$52 million.
The investment in CommunityWolf, the amount of which is undisclosed, marks Terra’s entry into public safety, with Terra CEO Nathan Nwachuku joining Community Wolf’s board. Community Wolf will use the funding to expand into communities around critical and urban infrastructure, while the two companies will also look at linking Community Wolf’s products to Terra’s software, so verified incidents reach Terra’s command centres alongside drone and sensor data.
“The people living around critical assets like mines are the first to feel an attack, and they are often the first to see it coming,” said Nwachuku. “We believe communal security will also be pivotal in how we protect lives and secure infrastructure.”
“Community Wolf gives residents a way to report and security operators an integrated platform to manage their communication and response,” said Mills. “Alongside Terra’s autonomous ground and aerial systems, we can keep millions more people safe across the continent.”

articles.title: Votre Chromecast avec Google TV s’offre une seconde jeunesse grâce à cette mise à jour
articles.text:
On pensait le Chromecast avec Google TV relégué aux oubliettes par le nouveau Google TV Streamer, mais Google ne semble pas encore avoir coupé le cordon. Onze mois après le dernier patch, le géant de Mountain View vient de déployer un nouveau firmware pour sa clé TV lancée il y a six ans déjà. Cette mise à jour vient prolonger la durée de l’appareil, toujours très populaire chez les amateurs de streaming.
Un correctif ciblé pour le streaming et la sécurité
La mise à jour déploie le patch de sécurité Android d’août 2026, remplaçant la version d’octobre 2025 installée l’an dernier. Google ne se contente pas de boucher les failles puisque la page officielle mentionne des améliorations sur la connectivité Wi-Fi, la stabilité du flux vidéo et le rendu de l’affichage. De nombreux bugs sont également balayés au passage, venant ainsi rendre la navigation plus fluide.
D’abord repéré sur le Chromecast avec Google TV (4K), le Chromecast avec Google TV (HD) reçoit aussi une mise à jour (voir ci-dessus). Si vous ne voulez pas attendre la notification de mise à jour, vous pouvez la lancer manuellement en vous rendant dans les paramètres du système, puis dans « À propos > Mise à jour du système ».
Le Chromecast avec Google TV toujours debout
Pour les plus bidouilleurs, ce correctif pourrait corriger la faille sabrina-unlock-v2 qui est utilisée par la communauté pour déverrouiller le bootloader et installer des systèmes alternatifs comme LineageOS. Cette vulnérabilité serait donc bloquée, même si Google n’a pas confirmé l’information officiellement. Les utilisateurs de ROMs personnalisées devront donc vérifier à deux fois avant de valider l’installation.
À lire : Le Chromecast avec Google TV gagne une des meilleures fonctionnalités de son successeur
Commercialisé en 2020 puis retiré du catalogue il y a deux ans, le Chromecast avec Google TV continue donc son chemin. Face à la hausse globale du prix des lecteurs multimédias, pouvoir conserver ce petit dongle reste donc une bonne affaire. Même si Google pousse désormais son nouveau TV Streamer, on ne refusera pas des mises à jour pour les anciens modèles.

articles.title: Friedrich Merz, canciller de Alemania, sobre el futuro de la guerra en Europa: "Rusia quiere algo más que Ucrania"
articles.text:
Durante décadas, Alemania pudo permitirse mantener un gasto militar relativamente reducido mientras destinaba buena parte de sus recursos a sostener su Estado del bienestar. Esa época, qué duda cabe, parece haber llegado a su fin. El Gobierno alemán se dispone a asumir un endeudamiento extraordinario y su canciller acaba de explicar ante el Parlamento, sin medias tintas, por qué considera que no tiene otra alternativa.
La factura de Ucrania. El debate sobre los Presupuestos de 2027 dejó este miércoles una de las advertencias más contundentes de Friedrich Merz desde que llegó a la Cancillería. Ante las críticas por los 11.600 millones de euros que Alemania prevé destinar a Ucrania el próximo año, el mandatario respondió con una pregunta: “¿Estamos gastando demasiado dinero en apoyar a Ucrania?”.
Su respuesta resume el planteamiento estratégico de Berlín: “Rusia sabe exactamente lo que quiere, y Rusia quiere más que Ucrania”. Para Merz, sostener militarmente a Kiev es también una forma de proteger a los propios alemanes.
Mucho más que Ucrania. El canciller enumeró los escenarios en los que, a su juicio, Moscú está intensificando su actividad hostil: el Báltico, Polonia, el mar Negro, el espacio exterior y la propia Alemania. Berlín ha responsabilizado a Rusia de varios incidentes, entre ellos un presunto intento de ataque con drones contra el aeropuerto de Leipzig/Halle en septiembre.
También ha expresado su preocupación por informes de inteligencia occidentales sobre un posible despliegue ruso de un arma nuclear en el espacio. Moscú niega las acusaciones de sabotaje y asegura que no busca una confrontación militar con la OTAN.
Un problema de 200.000 millones. La traducción económica de las advertencias de Merz es clave. Alemania prevé destinar 139.400 millones de euros a Defensa en 2027, frente a los 108.200 millones de este año, un incremento cercano al 30%. En 2030, el gasto militar anual superará los 200.000 millones, equivalentes al 3,7% del PIB.
Merz aspira a convertir la Bundeswehr en el mayor ejército convencional de Europa, al tiempo que participa en conversaciones con Francia sobre la posible extensión de su paraguas nuclear ante la incertidumbre sobre el compromiso estadounidense con el continente.
Los alemanes empiezan a hacer cuentas. El problema para Merz es que la sociedad alemana parece compartir su diagnóstico sobre Rusia, pero cada vez menos su receta. Según una encuesta de Forsa difundida por la Fundación Körber, más de ocho de cada diez alemanes consideran que Moscú representa una amenaza, pero únicamente el 46% respalda la ayuda militar a Ucrania, frente al 60% del año anterior.
Con unos Presupuestos que contemplan un nuevo endeudamiento superior a los 210.000 millones de euros y un creciente debate sobre los recortes sociales, el propio canciller ha admitido una realidad incómoda: “Ya no tenemos dinero para todo”.
Ucrania también tiene algo que ofrecer. Otro de los argumentos esgrimidos por Merz resulta especialmente significativo. Alemania se ha convertido en el mayor proveedor europeo de ayuda militar a Ucrania desde la invasión rusa de febrero de 2022, pero el intercambio de conocimientos empieza a funcionar en ambas direcciones.
“Estamos aprendiendo de Ucrania, tecnológicamente para aplicaciones civiles, pero también, por supuesto, en tecnología de defensa”, explicó el canciller. Tras casi cinco años de guerra, la experiencia acumulada por los ucranianos y el desarrollo de su industria militar representan un activo para unas fuerzas armadas europeas que están acelerando su modernización.
Mientras tanto, en Polonia. Las declaraciones de Merz coincidieron con un endurecimiento de las medidas defensivas polacas. La Fiscalía de Lublin confirmó que tres objetos que habían penetrado en el espacio aéreo del país eran misiles de crucero rusos. Varsovia prepara ahora una zona de exclusión aérea de varias decenas de kilómetros dentro de su territorio, paralela a la frontera oriental, para facilitar la identificación e interceptación de objetos hostiles.
Según Bloomberg, Polonia también habría planteado estudiar la posibilidad de interceptar proyectiles rusos sobre territorio ucraniano antes de que alcancen las fronteras de la OTAN, una medida que requeriría el consentimiento de los aliados.
El precio de la seguridad. Desde posiciones ideológicas opuestas, tanto Alternativa para Alemania (AfD) como La Izquierda (Die Linke) reclaman el fin de la ayuda militar a Kiev. Berlín, entretanto, busca garantizar financiación plurianual para Ucrania dentro del próximo presupuesto comunitario de 2028-2034. La estrategia de Merz pasa por convencer a los contribuyentes de que el dinero destinado a Ucrania no debe interpretarse únicamente como el coste de una guerra ajena, sino como una inversión en la seguridad alemana.
En otras palabras, el canciller está intentando trasladar el debate desde cuánto cuesta ayudar a Ucrania hasta cuánto podría costarle a Alemania dejar de hacerlo.

articles.title: Dough, design, drool: food entrepreneurship insights from Bakery Business 2026
articles.text:
Dough, design, drool: food entrepreneurship insights from Bakery Business 2026
In this photo essay from Jio World Convention Centre in Mumbai, we showcase food industry highlights from the exhibition halls along with insights for innovators.
Launched in 2014, PhotoSparks is a weekly feature from YourStory, with photographs that celebrate the spirit of creativity and innovation. In the earlier 1,040 posts, we featured an art festival, cartoon gallery. world music festival, telecom expo, millets fair, climate change expo, wildlife conference, startup festival, Diwali rangoli, and jazz festival.
Looking to begin your entrepreneurial journey in the food space? A good event for product insights, industry trends, and professional networking would be the 19th annual edition of the Bakery Business trade show, being held this week at the Jio World Convention Centre, BKC, Mumbai.
Organised by Hospitality First, it is held alongside the 14th annual HoReCa Business exhibition for the hospitality, restaurants and catering industry. With around 200 exhibitors, it reportedly attracted 15,000 business visitors.
As seen in this photo essay, it features not just cutting-edge technology and ingredients, but also demonstrations and competitions. For example, The India Pizza Championship brought together talented pizzaiolos (artisan pizza chefs) from across the country to showcase their skills on a national platform.
Such events point to a number of trends in this space for food entrepreneurs: the rise of cloud kitchens, the combination of bakeries with indulgent dining experiences, the growth of institutional investment, and the proliferation of bakery and restaurant chains that involve central kitchens and heavy automation.
In this photo essay, we showcase some of the exhibitors at Bakery Business 2026, such as Mahe to the World, Tandoor King, Mavee's, Mala's, Stagioni, Celebre, Ecolane, Morde, Pro Dough, Bakersville, and others.
Tandoor King International is a Mumbai-based manufacturer and supplier of commercial tandoors and baking equipment. Its product range includes stainless-steel tandoors, mild-steel tandoors, clay tandoors, gas-operated tandoors, and charcoal tandoors.
Mahe is a new premium bakery brand launched by Bikaji Foods International in partnership with master baker TK Khaleel. It aims to bring European baking traditions and artisanal craftsmanship to the Indian market, via offerings such as semi-finished bakery bases that foodservice operators can customise.
Morde Foods is a leading manufacturer of chocolate and cocoa-based products, with a strong presence in the B2B segment. It supplies compound chocolates, chocolate fillings, spreads, toppings, decorations, and inclusions to chocolatiers and restaurants.
Bakersville India is a prominent supplier and manufacturer of bakery ingredients, food decoration products, baking tools, and food packaging solutions. It has developed a substantial distribution network across India, and operates retail outlets under the Food Décor Shop name.
Mala’s, based in Panchgani near Mahabaleshwar, is famous for its strawberry and fruit jams, crushes, syrups, sauces, and fresh fruit treats. It is a major fruit-product manufacturer with pan-India distribution and exports to over 20 countries.
Meeting such exhibitors and large players helps aspiring food entrepreneurs explore opportunities to launch new offerings, improve product quality, and differentiate their menu. They can evaluate how technology can improve consistency, reduce wastage, save labour, and increase production capacity.
Such technologies include commercial ovens, mixers, processing machinery, refrigeration, and automation solutions. They can help improve operating economics for standalone and chain systems.
The food ecosystem is enriched by a wide range of business models. Entrepreneurs can explore opportunities via bakery cafés, central kitchens, QSRs, and cloud kitchens. Such models help understand how new businesses can diversify beyond traditional retail sales.
Meeting ingredient manufacturers, equipment suppliers, distributors, and fellow entrepreneurs helps forge new relationships. Live demonstrations, professional competitions and knowledge activities can spur innovation in product categories.
In sum, such industry exhibitions help entrepreneurs benchmark prices, calculate the unit economics, discover new products, and explore the use of automation. They enable identification of growth opportunities and ideas for product lines.
The overall opportunity at such a trade show is not simply to buy better equipment or ingredients. It is to rethink how to launch, improve and scale a food business in a fast-changing world with ever-increasing customer expectations.
Now what have you done today to pause in your busy schedule and harness your creative side for a better world?
(All photographs taken by Madanmohan Rao on location at Bakery Business 2026.)

articles.title: Google Messages va enfin régler le problème des conversations de groupe en désordre
articles.text:
Bonne nouvelle pour les utilisateurs de Google Messages : des fils de discussions devraient bientôt être disponibles au sein de la messagerie.
Alors que GrapheneOS développe sa propre messagerie RCS, L’équipe en charge du développement de Google Messages travaille depuis un certain temps sur une refonte des messages vocaux de la plateforme. Des jeux et des appels vidéo pourraient aussi être déployés prochainement au sein des échanges. Une autre fonctionnalité devrait permettre de mettre un peu d’ordre dans les discussions de groupe un peu trop chaotiques. On vous explique.
Google Messages va bientôt se doter de fils de discussions dans les conversations de groupe
Pour l’instant, dans Google Messages, il est possible de faire des renvois à un message en affichant un texte au-dessus d’une réponse. Mais quand on fait partie d’un groupe où tout le monde parle en même temps de sujets différents, cette fonction est loin d’être suffisante. Heureusement, Google s’est enfin penché sur ce problème dans la version messages.android_20261120_01_RC00.phone.openbeta_dynamic de l’application.
L’équipe est en effet en train de développer des réponses organisées en fils de discussions. Le code de la version bêta montre qu’il devrait bientôt être possible de relier plusieurs réponses à un seul et même message. Le fil disposera notamment de son propre champ de saisie. Un bouton « X » a notamment été prévu pour revenir en arrière et retrouver la discussion principale.
Et comme une bonne nouvelle n’arrive jamais seule, l’option ne se limitera pas au texte : les images et les emojis sont aussi pris en charge.
Une fonctionnalité qui ressemble beaucoup à celle d’iMessage
Cette nouveauté devrait permettre de ne pas surcharger le fil principal. Bien sûr, quand on jette un œil aux captures d’écran réalisées par l’équipe d’Android Authority, la nouveauté fait tout de suite penser à ce qui est déjà disponible sur iPhone, dans l’application iMessage. Sachant que les fils de discussion sont aussi disponibles sur WhatsApp, Slack ou encore Discord, Google arrive encore une fois après la bataille. On ne va toutefois pas se plaindre que la firme ait enfin pris le temps de rattraper son retard.
- L'application est gratuite à télécharger.
- On peut écrire des messages dans des groupes.
- Elle s'intègre parfaitement dans l'écosystème logiciel de Google.
Pour l’instant, Google n’a rien confirmé officiellement. On ne sait donc pas quand le géant de Mountain View a prévu de déployer cette nouvelle fonctionnalité. Rien ne garantit non plus que la fonction soit un jour disponible globalement. En attendant d'en savoir plus, il faudra donc, comme toujours, attendre et espérer que l’option ne soit pas abandonnée.

articles.title: 118 grammes, trois usages, zéro fioriture : le trépied UGREEN LP962 MagSafe vaut enfin son prix
articles.text:
Le UGREEN LP962 appartient à la gamme d’accessoires mobiles de la marque chinoise, qui s’est taillé une solide réputation sur les câbles, chargeurs et supports. Ce modèle cible les utilisateurs d’iPhone MagSafe (iPhone 12 et ultérieurs) qui cherchent un accessoire polyvalent sans encombrement : plié, il mesure environ 11,5 cm et pèse 118 grammes, soit moins qu’un paquet de cartes. La structure en alliage d’aluminium le distingue des étriers plastique du même segment, avec une finition et une durabilité sensiblement supérieures. L’offre Amazon en cours permet de profiter du LP962 pour 17,47 euros.
Les atouts du UGREEN Trépied Magnétique MagSafe LP962
- Châssis en alliage d’aluminium, léger à 118 g et très compact plié
- Compatible MagSafe : 20 aimants N52 pour un accrochage ferme de l’iPhone
- Triple usage : trépied de table, poignée stabilisatrice, support de bureau
Le UGREEN LP962 est affiché à 22,99 euros en temps normal sur Amazon. Pour ce Black Friday, il est disponible à 17,47 euros, soit environ 24 % de réduction sur un accessoire déjà positionné entrée de gamme.
Un format poche qui ne lésine pas sur la construction
Plié, le LP962 tient dans la paume ou dans une poche de veste. Les trois branches se déplient en quelques secondes pour former un trépied stable sur n’importe quelle surface plane. La tête pivote sur 206 degrés, ce qui couvre aussi bien le portrait que le paysage, et le socle est lestée pour absorber les vibrations légères lors d’un appel vidéo.
La construction en alliage d’aluminium n’est pas un argument purement esthétique. Par rapport aux modèles plastique du même prix, la résistance aux chocs et aux déformations est nettement meilleure, un accessoire qu’on glisse et retire de poche vingt fois par jour, ça s’use vite. Le seul bémol : la hauteur maximale, environ 15 cm dépliée, ne convient pas à un tournage debout. C’est un support de table, pas un pied de reportage.
MagSafe et visserie 1/4 de pouce : deux systèmes d’accroche
L’accrochage MagSafe repose sur 20 aimants N52 pour une force d’attraction d’environ 1 600 grammes. En pratique, l’iPhone 16 s’aimante en une fraction de seconde et ne bouge pas, même en mode paysage avec un peu de vibration. Pour les téléphones sans MagSafe natif, UGREEN inclut un anneau magnétique adhésif à coller sur le dos de l’appareil. Le LP962 n’assure pas la charge sans fil : il faut retirer l’iPhone pour le brancher, ce qui reste un compromis acceptable à ce prix. Le pas de vis 1/4 de pouce intégré permet aussi de fixer le LP962 sur un trépied photographique classique ou un rail de caméra, ce qui lui ouvre un usage légèrement plus avancé que la simple utilisation de bureau.

articles.title: Amazon Autos : acheter sa voiture sur Amazon arrive en Europe, mais la vente se conclura toujours en concession
articles.text:
Au Royaume-Uni comme en France, on cherche encore une voiture neuve sur les sites d’annonces ou en faisant le tour des concessions. Aux États-Unis, Amazon a ouvert une autre voie en décembre 2024 avec Amazon Autos, un rayon de son site qui affiche les stocks des concessionnaires partenaires. Le service y est passé de 48 villes au lancement à plus de 150, avec 35 marques en neuf et en occasion. Amazon a annoncé le mercredi 25 novembre 2026 que le service débarquera sur le site britannique début 2027. C’est le premier pays hors des États-Unis, et donc la première fois qu’on pourra chercher sa voiture sur Amazon en Europe.
Hyundai, qui était déjà le premier partenaire aux États-Unis, ouvre le bal avec des modèles électriques, hybrides et essence, comme la nouvelle compacte Ioniq 3 ou le crossover Ioniq 5. Le groupe Vertu Motors, qui compte environ 200 sites au Royaume-Uni, y ajoutera ses voitures d’occasion. C’est le quatrième groupe de distribution indépendant d’Europe en chiffre d’affaires, d’après le classement du cabinet ICDP repris par Automotive News Europe.
Sur le site, on pourra filtrer les modèles, voir le prix affiché, faire estimer la reprise de sa voiture actuelle, comparer les financements et réserver un véhicule. Amazon promet d’autres marques et d’autres concessionnaires dans les prochains mois.
La vente se signe toujours en concession
Cependant, tout ne se passera pas non plus comme on achète un autre produit chez Amazon. Le géant américain ne vendra pas les voitures lui-même. L’achat se conclut toujours chez le concessionnaire et c’est lui qui fixe ses prix. Hyundai précise que ses distributeurs assureront aussi la remise du véhicule, l’entretien et le service après-vente.
Matt Nuffort, directeur d’Amazon Autos International, veut un achat de voiture « aussi simple et transparent que n’importe quel achat sur Amazon ». Dans les faits, Amazon Autos reste une vitrine avec un bouton de réservation, et la paperasse se fait toujours en concession.
Les concessionnaires américains avaient pourtant eu peur. En novembre 2023, quand Amazon et Hyundai ont annoncé leur partenariat au salon automobile de Los Angeles, les actions des groupes de distribution ont d’abord baissé, parce que les investisseurs y voyaient une menace pour les showrooms. Dans une interview à Bloomberg, Matt Nuffort minimise le risque et parle d’« un canal supplémentaire pour toucher les clients plus efficacement ».
Ce mercredi, à la Bourse de Londres, les investisseurs ont plutôt vu une menace pour les sites d’annonces. L’action d’Autotrader, la plateforme britannique d’annonces automobiles, a perdu jusqu’à 3 %. Celle de Vertu a gagné jusqu’à 4,5 %, le jour où le groupe annonçait aussi le rachat de quatre concessions.
Un marché grignoté par les marques chinoises
Amazon arrive sur un marché bousculé. Le Royaume-Uni n’applique pas aux voitures chinoises les droits de douane punitifs en vigueur aux États-Unis et dans l’Union Européenne. Les marques chinoises y ont pris 17,5 % des immatriculations de voitures neuves sur les neuf premiers mois de 2026, et 23,3 % au seul mois de septembre, contre 12,4 % un an plus tôt, d’après les chiffres de la SMMT, l’association des constructeurs britanniques. Vertu profite justement de cette vague en vendant des BYD et des Chery.
Hyundai, de son côté, compte sur Amazon pour trouver de nouveaux acheteurs. Selon José Muñoz, PDG de Hyundai Motor, 78 % des ventes réalisées par ses concessions américaines après un passage par Amazon viennent de clients nouveaux pour la marque.
Pas encore de date précise, et rien pour la France
Amazon n’a pas encore donné de date précise de lancement ni la liste complète des marques. Aucun horizon de lancement n’a été annoncé non plus pour d’autres pays d’Europe comme la France ou l’Allemagne.
