articles.title: Hoher Arbeitsspeicherverbrauch: Microsoft zieht bei drei Windows-Apps den Stecker
articles.text:
Hoher Arbeitsspeicherverbrauch: Microsoft zieht bei drei Windows-Apps den Stecker
Im Jahr 2025 hat Microsoft die sogenannten „Microsoft 365-Begleit-Apps“ (Microsoft 365 companions) angekündigt, zu denen auch die drei Anwendungen „People“ (Personen), „Files“ (Dateien) und „Calendar“ (Kalender) gehörten. Die Idee dahinter war, dass diese kleinen Apps in der Taskleiste die Produktivität der Nutzer:innen steigern würden. Doch dieser Plan ist nicht aufgegangen.
Microsoft spricht von „hohem Speicherverbrauch“
Da diese drei Apps laut Microsoft „für einen hohen Speicherverbrauch und zahlreiche Probleme“ gesorgt hätten, sind sie aus Windows 11 entfernt worden. Microsoft hat den Stecker gezogen. Der US-Konzern hatte die drei auf Copilot ausgerichteten Apps schrittweise für Nutzer:innen mit einem Microsoft 365-Abonnement eingeführt. Doch sie brachten nicht die erwünschten Ergebnisse.
Während einer Fragerunde zwischen Microsoft und Kund:innen erklärte ein Microsoft-Mitarbeiter, der auf die drei Apps angesprochen wurde, laut windowslatest.com: „Sie waren die Ursache für einen hohen Arbeitsspeicherverbrauch und diverse Probleme. Obwohl sie also einen gewissen Funktionsumfang boten, war der Preis dafür sehr hoch.“
Die „Calendar“-App brachte den Outlook-Kalender direkt in die Taskleiste
Über die „People“-App konnte man Informationen zu Personen abrufen, ähnlich wie bei der Kontaktverwaltung in Outlook. Die „File Search“-App ermöglichte das Durchsuchen von Dateien. Auch diese App verfügte über eine Copilot-Integration: Wer eine Microsoft 365 Copilot-Lizenz besaß, konnte die jeweilige Datei zur Analyse an die KI übermitteln. Und die „Calendar“-App brachte den Outlook-Kalender direkt in die Taskleiste der Nutzer:innen.
Bei der Ankündigung im Oktober 2025 lautete Microsofts Botschaft noch: „So wie ein Formel-1-Team dafür sorgt, dass das Auto stets Höchstleistung erbringt, sind diese Begleit-Apps immer zur Stelle. Sie arbeiten im Hintergrund und stellen sicher, dass Sie effizient und organisiert bleiben und die Kontrolle behalten – damit Sie sich darauf konzentrieren können, Ihren Tag erfolgreich zu meistern, anstatt nach Dokumenten oder Besprechungen zu suchen.“
Ab dem 16. Dezember werden die drei Apps nicht mehr funktionieren
Doch rund ein Jahr später sind die drei Apps schon wieder Geschichte. Nutzer:innen, bei denen die drei Mini-Apps bereits installiert sind, müssen sie entfernen – ab dem 16. Dezember 2026 werden sie ohnehin nicht mehr funktionieren.
„Diese Begleit-Apps boten eine zusätzliche Möglichkeit, Kalenderinformationen, Kontakte und Dateien zu finden. Ihr Entfernen hat keinerlei Auswirkungen auf bestehende Funktionen oder Daten in Microsoft 365. Die entsprechenden Informationen lassen sich weiterhin über die gewohnten Microsoft 365- und Windows-Funktionen abrufen“, heißt es in einem aktualisierten Support-Dokument von Microsoft.

articles.title: AI-powered bionic eye breakthrough could help the blind see again
articles.text:
AI-powered bionic eye breakthrough could help the blind see again
Using AI to make bionic vision smarter and more precise, scientists are bringing the possibility of restoring sight to people with blindness one step closer to reality.
- Date:
  November 12, 2026
- Source:
  University of California - Santa Barbara
- Summary:
  Scientists have developed an AI-powered approach that makes experimental bionic vision technology more precise, helping predict the flashes and shapes of light perceived by a blind man with a brain implant. By learning how an individual's brain responds to electrical stimulation, the technology could bring researchers closer to restoring some degree of sight to people with blindness.
- Share:
Artificial intelligence could help overcome one of the biggest challenges in restoring vision to people who are blind: getting a brain implant to produce reliable visual experiences. Researchers from three institutions, including UC Santa Barbara, have demonstrated that AI can improve how precisely an experimental visual prosthesis stimulates the brain and predicts what a person perceives.
The team used a deep learning system to develop electrical stimulation patterns for electrodes temporarily implanted in the visual cortex, the region at the back of the brain responsible for processing visual information. By analyzing the brain's responses, the technology gave researchers greater control over neural activity and helped them better anticipate the visual sensations produced by the implant.
Published online in the journal Neuron, the proof-of-concept study represents progress toward more advanced visual prostheses, sometimes described as bionic eyes. These devices could eventually become more effective by learning how each person's brain responds to stimulation rather than relying on predetermined settings.
"Building a model in the abstract is one thing," said Michael Beyeler, an associate professor of computer science and psychological and brain sciences at UC Santa Barbara. "Seeing it shape an experiment with a person is something else entirely. That ability to go from theory to something that may one day help people is what drives much of the work in our lab."
How Bionic Vision Could Bypass Damaged Eyes
For decades, scientists have worked to develop technologies capable of restoring some vision to people who are blind, although the results have generally been limited. Some experimental devices stimulate the retina, the layer of tissue at the back of the eye that detects light. Others attempt to activate parts of the visual system farther along the pathway that carries visual information to the brain.
Visual cortical prostheses work differently. Instead of depending on the eyes or optic nerves, they deliver electrical signals directly to the visual cortex. This approach could offer a potential solution for people whose visual pathways have been damaged but whose visual cortex can still respond to stimulation. Possible candidates include individuals who lost their sight because of strokes, neurodegenerative diseases, or traumatic brain injuries.
The ability to regain even limited vision could be especially meaningful for people who remember what it was like to see.
Beyeler highlighted those "who have been able to see for part of their life, but then, because of an inherited eye disease or an accident, have lost their vision," adding, "For those people, the desire may be very strong to get some vision back."
The new findings build on earlier computational research supported by Beyeler's 2022 National Institutes of Health (NIH) Director's New Innovator Award. The five-year, $2 million grant has supported his efforts to make artificial vision systems more accurate, predictable, and effective.
Scientists Test AI With a Brain Implant in a Blind Man
An important opportunity to test the technology came in 2024, when researchers from Beyeler's Bionic Vision Lab traveled to Spain. Their goal was to determine whether their computer models could improve the performance of a brain implant already being used in an experimental study.
At Hospital IMED Elche, the team worked with a 27-year-old man who had become blind following a traumatic brain injury. He had received an implant containing 96 electrodes arranged in an array within his visual cortex. The device was intended to remain in place for six months before being removed.
When researchers activated the electrodes using electrical current, the participant experienced visual sensations known as phosphenes. These can appear as spots, flashes, or shapes of light, sometimes resembling stars or fireworks.
Producing these sensations is possible, but making them consistent and predictable is much more difficult. The same electrical stimulation does not always trigger an identical response, and activating particular electrodes does not guarantee that the person will perceive a specific visual pattern.
To address this problem, the researchers trained a deep neural network, a type of AI designed to recognize complex patterns, to predict how the visual cortex would respond to different electrical stimulation settings. The model also considered the brain's resting activity immediately before stimulation, giving it information about the participant's current neural state.
Using these predictions, the researchers identified combinations of electrical signals that were most likely to produce particular patterns of brain activity.
AI Makes Bionic Vision More Precise
When the scientists tested the stimulation patterns selected by AI, the results were encouraging. The new approach generated the intended patterns of neural activity more accurately than the comparison methods while requiring less electrical current.
Another important discovery emerged when the team examined the relationship between brain activity and the participant's visual experiences. The patterns recorded directly from his brain were better predictors of what he perceived than the stimulation settings themselves.
This distinction matters because activating the brain is not the same as knowing what a person will see. Even when researchers can produce a desired neural response, they still need to understand how the brain transforms that activity into a conscious visual experience.
"Engineers naturally want to treat phosphenes like pixels: stimulate more electrodes, and you should get a more complete image," Beyeler said. "But the brain does not work that way. Electrodes interact, neural responses fluctuate, and what we put into the brain is not necessarily what the person perceives. The challenge is to learn more about that transformation."
The findings suggest that future visual prostheses may need to do more than simply deliver electrical signals. They may also need to monitor how the brain reacts and use that feedback to continually improve stimulation.
Teaching Brain Implants to Adapt to Each Person
A key advantage of the implant used in the experiment was its ability to perform two tasks. It could stimulate the visual cortex with electrical current while simultaneously recording the resulting neural activity.
This allowed researchers to train their AI model using the brain's actual responses rather than relying exclusively on information about which electrodes were activated and how much current they delivered.
The participant also provided feedback about what he experienced. He reported whether he saw a phosphene and, during certain experiments, described its appearance, including its shape, size, brightness, and color.
Comparing these reports with the recorded brain activity revealed that neural responses contained more useful information about the perceived visual sensations than the electrical stimulation parameters alone.
The AI system also used measurements of resting brain activity to account for changes in the participant's neural state before each stimulation. This could be particularly valuable because the brain's response to electrical signals can vary over time, including from one day to the next.
By adapting stimulation to these changing conditions, future prostheses might provide more consistent visual experiences without requiring users to adjust to a rigid set of signals.
"A useful visual prosthesis cannot rely on a fixed recipe," Beyeler said. "It has to learn how an individual brain responds and adapt the stimulation accordingly. Ultimately, the device should adapt to the person, not the other way around."
A Collaborative Step Toward Restoring Sight
The research brought together scientists from UC Santa Barbara, ETH Zurich, and Miguel Hernández University (MHU). Beyeler described the effort as "a true collaboration."
The project was led by co-first authors Pehuén Moure of ETH Zurich, Jacob Granley of UC Santa Barbara, and Fabrizio Grani of MHU. The supervising researchers were Beyeler, Shih-Chii Liu of ETH Zurich, and Eduardo Fernández of MHU. Their work forms part of a larger feasibility trial taking place in Spain.
Although the technology remains experimental and the participant's visual experiences were limited to flashes and shapes of light, the results demonstrate how AI could improve communication between artificial vision devices and the brain.
Rather than treating every brain as if it responds the same way, future bionic vision systems could learn from each individual and adjust their signals accordingly. That personalized approach may prove essential to developing implants that can eventually restore useful vision to people who have lost their sight.

articles.title: Según los psicólogos, las personas que crecieron en los años 60 y 70 desarrollaron fortalezas mentales que la Generación Z está perdiendo
articles.text:
Tenían que esperar unos días para recibir una carta, para que revelaran el carrete de fotos para poder ver las vacaciones, los programas de televisión eran en horario fijo… Una hipótesis sobre quienes crecieron en los años 60 y 70 es que, al crecer con menos inmediatez, aprendieron a ser más pacientes. Además, tendrían menos problemas con la frustración que los de la generación Z.
Para ver si estas esperas han dejado una huella a largo plazo, tenemos que realizar comparaciones entre generaciones. Existe un estudio sobre personalidad y edad. Se analizaron datos de cuestionarios de gente de 16 años en adelante. Los datos corresponden a Reino Unido y Alemania.
Se encontraron diferencias en varios aspectos de personalidad en función de la edad, aunque realmente con esos datos es imposible separar qué parte de esto se debe a la edad y qué parte a la generación. Además, no se sabe qué parte se debe a los hábitos de infancia.
Existe otro estudio sobre resiliencia en Bulgaria. En él se comparan los de la generación X (entre 46 y 60 años) con los de Z (entre 18 y 30). En una escala relacionada con la capacidad de afrontar situaciones difíciles, los primeros obtienen mayores puntuaciones. En otra escala relacionada con la adaptación al cambio y la recuperación tras dificultades o enfermedades, son los segundos los que obtienen mayores puntuaciones.
Qué sabemos de la atención y la paciencia
Hace años, si algo fallaba en el aparato, no podías ir a YouTube a buscar un tutorial sobre cómo desmontarlo. Pero se podía intentar arreglarlo uno mismo. Si la primera idea no funcionaba, se podía mirar el manual o pedir ayuda. En cualquier caso, muestra cómo ha cambiado la búsqueda de las soluciones a un problema.
También hay diferencias en cómo se afronta un conflicto. En los estudios de Gross y John se encontró que el hecho de que habitualmente se ocultara la expresión de las emociones estaba asociado a un menor bienestar y a más problemas en las relaciones, algo que la gente de las generaciones que vieron en directo a The Beatles lleva mejor.
Se atribuye también a quienes crecieron en los años 60 y 70 una mayor satisfacción con lo que tienen. Hoy es fácil hacer comparaciones gracias a las redes sociales. Basta con abrir la app y saber a dónde viajan (o qué compran) los demás. Para ver si esto lleva a mayor ansiedad en una generación que en otra, hacen falta datos que tengan en cuenta la edad y las circunstancias.

articles.title: Steam suma 58 juegos gratis que antes eran de pago: cómo descargarlos sin esperar al Black Friday
articles.text:
Steam incorporó 58 juegos que antes tenían precio y ahora pueden descargarse gratis, sin depender de las ofertas del Black Friday ni de una promoción limitada a unos días. La selección incluye títulos de terror, rol, estrategia, simulación, cartas, carreras y multijugador, además de tres programas que también pasaron a ser gratuitos.
El cambio permite ampliar la biblioteca digital sin esperar descuentos de temporada. A diferencia de las promociones temporales, estos productos modificaron su modelo de distribución: el juego base dejó de tener precio. Por tanto, no hay una cuenta atrás para reclamarlos, aunque conviene comprobar el importe antes de añadir cada título a la cuenta.
Los juegos gratuitos permanecen vinculados a la biblioteca
Los 58 títulos pueden incorporarse a una cuenta de Steam y descargarse en otro momento. La plataforma permite asociar los juegos al perfil del usuario, de modo que no es necesario instalarlos de inmediato ni disponer de espacio libre en el disco duro al momento de obtenerlos.
El catálogo suma propuestas de distintos tamaños y géneros. Algunos proyectos son experiencias breves o se encuentran en acceso anticipado, mientras otros incorporan partidas cooperativas, juego competitivo o compatibilidad con realidad virtual.
También hay casos con contenido adicional de pago. Que un juego base sea gratuito no significa que todos sus objetos, expansiones o funciones lo sean. Algunos títulos conservan compras opcionales, paquetes descargables o elementos cosméticos dentro de la propia ficha de Steam.
La condición esencial es comprobar que el precio del juego principal aparezca como cero antes de confirmar la incorporación a la biblioteca. Si la página muestra un importe, puede tratarse de una edición distinta, un complemento o una oferta que todavía no se actualizó en una región concreta.
El terror concentra buena parte de la nueva selección
Los juegos de terror tienen una presencia destacada entre los títulos que dejaron de ser de pago. An Agonized Mind propone supervivencia y disparos desde una perspectiva cenital, en un escenario marcado por experimentos humanos. GeneBreak sigue a un periodista que investiga un hospital bajo cuarentena.
La lista también incluye Evil Timefall, un juego de disparos con estética de horror medieval; Lil Doll House, centrado en una muñeca que debe superar trampas; y Little Red, que retoma el imaginario de Caperucita Roja para enfrentar oleadas de criaturas.
En Replace the Lamp: The Last Shift, una tarea cotidiana como cambiar bombillas deriva en una situación de terror psicológico. RealEscape, por su parte, plantea puzles dentro de un hospital abandonado.
Estas propuestas reflejan una tendencia habitual en el catálogo independiente: equipos pequeños recurren al terror porque permite construir atmósferas y mecánicas directas sin necesitar mundos abiertos o presupuestos elevados. La gratuidad puede servirles para alcanzar a más jugadores y aumentar la visibilidad de sus próximos proyectos.
Rol, estrategia y cartas amplían las opciones
Quienes busquen combates y progresión de personajes encontrarán opciones como Canis Watch, un juego de rol de acción isométrico con magia y ataques cuerpo a cuerpo. Infasia presenta una guerra entre clanes, mientras Echoes of Vatheria combina exploración automática, agricultura y mejoras permanentes.
También figuran Heavy Wake, que une combate por turnos y cartas en una isla maldita, y Kebechet Daughter of Anpu, inspirado en divinidades del antiguo Egipto. En estrategia aparecen Card Colony, con elementos de defensa de torres, y Holy Clash Cards, centrado en enfrentamientos entre castillos.
Radio Violence sigue en acceso anticipado. El juego plantea partidas competitivas para cuatro participantes, en las que cada jugador construye antenas de radio y trata de controlar territorios. Esa condición implica que puede recibir cambios relevantes durante su desarrollo.
Hay títulos para jugar en grupo y experiencias de realidad virtual
La selección incluye juegos multijugador como Beanu TAG, basado en persecuciones y movimientos acrobáticos; Kajipeet, de lucha local con katanas; Pandora Battle, con armas y poderes elementales; y Poly Peacocks, donde los participantes crean atuendos y desfilan en pasarelas.
En simulación aparecen Aerospace Engineering Sandbox, que permite construir aviones, helicópteros y cohetes, y Real Car Parking Simulator, enfocado en maniobras de estacionamiento. Entre los juegos de realidad virtual figuran Hockey Player VR, LOST CAVE, Sail y VR Houses: Glass Apartment.
Cómo añadir los juegos gratis a Steam
El procedimiento puede realizarse desde el programa de Steam o en el sitio web oficial:
- Iniciar sesión con la cuenta personal.
- Buscar el título por su nombre completo.
- Abrir la ficha oficial y comprobar que el precio sea cero.
- Pulsar “Añadir a la cuenta”, “Obtener” o la opción disponible.
- Confirmar la operación y revisar la biblioteca.
- Descargar el juego en ese momento o instalarlo más adelante.
La lista reúne títulos que antes costaban desde importes mínimos hasta propuestas con precios superiores a 15 euros. Steam ofrece así una alternativa para probar géneros distintos antes de que comiencen las rebajas del Black Friday, sin que la incorporación de estos juegos dependa de una promoción de fin de semana.

articles.title: FIFA Says It Has Been Victim of a Cyberattack Accessing ‘Personal and Business Information’
articles.text:
FIFA was the victim of a cyberattack that saw hackers gain access to what soccer’s world governing body describes as a “limited set of personal and business information,” it said Thursday.
“FIFA is working closely with the relevant authorities, including law enforcement,” the organization said in a statement sent to The Associated Press.
FIFA didn’t say when the cyberattack took place, or the precise nature of the hacked information.
Last week, a group calling itself the Handsome Boy Hacking Club posted a screenshot on X of what it claimed were FIFA files. Three days later, it appeared to take credit for the hack when responding to a post that said more than 12 gigabytes of internal documents had been leaked.
“FIFA condemns in the strongest possible terms the unlawful acquisition and publication of information, particularly personal data,” the governing body said in its statement. “Such actions constitute a serious and unacceptable violation of privacy and can have significant consequences for the individuals concerned.”
The breach comes at a time when FIFA and its president, Gianni Infantino, is under scrutiny after his foiled, secretive plan to sell stakes in the World Cup to private investors.
Infantino is also trying to extend his 11-year presidency of FIFA to 2031. He is the favorite when the election is held on March 18, with Kohzo Tashima of Japan and Philippe Diallo of France the other candidates.

iPhone 17 volta a receber desconto generoso em até 12x na Black Week 2026

articles.title: After mayor’s KD gaffe, Montréal developer creates Kraft-Dinner-themed city budget site
articles.text:
When Montréal mayor Soraya Martinez Ferrada made a remark about eating Kraft Dinner instead of filet mignon in the context of planning the city’s budget—which included a nearly 10-percent tax increase—many Montréalers expressed outrage.
The virtual KD box jokes the budget is “High in taxes. No filet mignon added.”
But local software developer Niko Draca spotted an opportunity to put his programming skills to work. Over a couple of days, Draca, a staff software developer at Shopify, built a free website that lets users visualize Montréal’s 2026-27 budget items on the back of a Kraft Dinner box (the solo project was not associated with his work at Shopify).
“High in taxes. No filet mignon added,” the virtual box jokes.
Martinez Ferrada has since walked back her comments, calling them “tactless.” Since sharing KDGate.ca on social media on Thursday, Draca told BetaKit he’s received an influx of positive responses from fellow Montréalers.
“I saw this outrage, and I was like, ‘Why don’t we try and make something positive come out of this?’” Draca said in an interview. “If I can get people to look at this data, try to interact with it, and reason with it, I think that’s a big win.
“Let’s take that outrage and use it to educate people, and present it in a digestible way.”
The main graphic on the website shows a three-dimensional representation of how many Kraft Dinner boxes (valued at $2.29 each) stack up to the city’s $8-billion budget. The answer: more than 3 billion boxes, which would form a 124-metre-wide cube that’s 71 times taller than a 5-foot-nine human.
“It’s obviously a ridiculous unit to measure things in,” Draca said. “I hope it gives people an interesting way to compare line items and be a little more informed.”
The site, available in English and French, lists the major items in the city’s operating budget and indicates how much certain envelopes have grown or shrunk compared to last year. Draca said he coded the website in TypeScript and JavaScript, with some help from Claude Code for the front-end design. He pulled his sources from publicly available datasets on Montréal’s financial allocations, and the site invites users to report any errors, which are noted in a changelog.
Draca is no stranger to making viral web apps that have received media attention. He previously created a ‘Dating Wrapped’ website (in the vein of Spotify Wrapped) featured in the Wall Street Journal, as well as the guessing game ‘Why Combinator’ that asked users to distinguish between AI-generated copy and real Y Combinator startup descriptions.
But would he create a budget-related site again next year? Draca said he hopes there’s no Kraft Dinner-related scandal next fall, but agreed it would be fun to do another visual exploration to boost civic engagement.
Feature image courtesy KDGate.ca.

articles.title: Federal judge blocks the FCC from reviewing ABC’s licenses early
articles.text:
US District Judge Loren AliKhan has blocked the Federal Communications Commission from conducting an early review of ABC’s broadcast licenses in a preliminary injunction, and rejected its efforts to dismiss ABC’s First Amendment lawsuit. ABC has accused the FCC of violating its free speech rights and claims the agency “waged a retaliatory campaign” against the network over content it broadcast. In her ruling the judge noted that the network was “likely to succeed on their retaliation claim.”
Federal judge blocks the FCC from reviewing ABC’s licenses early
The judge has preliminarily sided with ABC, rejecting the FCC’s efforts to dismiss the case.
Although Disney, ABC’s parent company, wasn’t set to renew its broadcast licenses until 2028, last April the FCC ordered the network to file for an early license renewal claiming it was part of an investigation into Disney’s policies on diversity, equity, and inclusivity. The FCC’s move came a day after President Donald Trump demanded ABC fire late-night talk show host Jimmy Kimmel following a skit about Melania Trump.
In response to the FCC’s order, Disney and ABC sued the agency in August and accused the FCC of “punishing ABC for its speech” by threatening its broadcast licenses. The preliminary injunction issued by the judge on Wednesday prohibits the FCC from taking any further action in the early review of ABC’s broadcast licenses and noted that the network had shown that the court’s intervention in the agency’s actions was in the public interest.
”No one doubts that the Commission may enforce the law in the manner it sees fit,” the judge wrote. “But in doing so, Defendants may not retaliate against or punish Plaintiffs and other broadcast license holders for disfavored speech.”

articles.title: The Witcher 4 sairá em todas as plataformas ao mesmo tempo, e Cyberpunk 2 chega a 199 devs
articles.text:
A CD Projekt Red divulgou o relatório do terceiro trimestre de 2026, com 513 desenvolvedores alocados em The Witcher 4, 199 em Cyberpunk 2 e novos acordos com a Sony. Foi o último item que gerou dúvida em questão de horas.
O acordo com a Sony e a dúvida sobre exclusividade
Os acordos cobrem a disponibilidade dos jogos da empresa no PlayStation, a presença no PlayStation Plus e a colaboração na campanha de marketing de The Witcher 4. O estúdio não divulgou valores nem quando a campanha começa. Foi o bastante para os fãs perguntarem se o jogo seria exclusivo do PS5, ou ao menos teria uma janela de exclusividade. A comparação com o acordo da Sony para o marketing de GTA 6 apareceu rápido.
A resposta veio na quarta-feira (25). O co-CEO Michał Nowakowski escreveu em uma publicação no X que “The Witcher 4 e nossos outros títulos futuros continuarão sendo multiplataforma”. Quando um usuário pediu que confirmasse que o jogo sairia em todas as plataformas ao mesmo tempo, ele respondeu em outra publicação:
“Todas as plataformas serão lançadas ao mesmo tempo: PS5, Xbox e PC. Ninguém ficará para trás.”
The Witcher 4 segue previsto para 2028, sem data definida. Quem esperava o Switch 2 continua sem resposta: Nowakowski citou apenas PS5, Xbox e PC, e a Nintendo nunca apareceu entre as plataformas anunciadas desde 2024.
A régua é GTA 6: o salto de The Witcher 3 para o 4
Na seção de perguntas e respostas da teleconferência de resultados, o analista Krzysztof Tkocz, do Erste, perguntou como Nowakowski avalia o salto de GTA 5 para GTA 6 e se algo parecido é possível entre The Witcher 3 e The Witcher 4. O co-CEO disse que a teleconferência era sobre a CD Projekt Red, não sobre a Rockstar, e que não faria uma análise aprofundada dos dois jogos, mas que a equipe olhou para GTA 6 e notou as diferenças. Depois respondeu:
“Se acreditamos que vai haver um salto comparável entre The Witcher 3 e The Witcher 4? Acho que sim. Já se passaram 11 anos, estamos trabalhando para deixar The Witcher 4 muito mais bonito e melhor em praticamente todos os aspectos do jogo, então sim, vocês devem esperar de nós um salto muito maior entre The Witcher 3 e The Witcher 4.”
A resposta foi além do “comparável”: ele falou em um salto “muito maior”. A régua é alta, já que entre GTA 5 e GTA 6 se passaram 13 anos.
Cyberpunk 2 chega a 199 desenvolvedores
Cyberpunk 2 chegou a 199 desenvolvedores em 31 de outubro, contra 184 no fim de julho, menos da metade do time de The Witcher 4. A meta é manter cerca de 200 até o fim de 2026 e chegar a cerca de 320 até o fim de 2027, uma alta de aproximadamente 61%. Os números mostram pessoas alocadas em cada projeto, não contratações novas.
O jogo segue em pré-produção. Na mesma teleconferência, a vice-presidente de Estratégia e Relações com Investidores, Karolina Gnaś, disse estar satisfeita com o andamento, mas evitou cravar quando a produção em larga escala começa:
“Estamos felizes com o ponto em que estamos, mas ainda é muito cedo para dar uma data específica e planejar quando iniciaremos a produção completa.”

articles.title: Brutal clip de ‘Avengers: Doomsday’ con el enfrentamiento de Magneto y el Doctor Doom: casi le arranca la máscara
articles.text:
Hace apenas unos días, Marvel estrenó el tráiler final de Avengers: Doomsday. Un avance muy esperado que se ha convertido en el segundo tráiler más visto de todos los tiempos en sus primeras 24 horas, solo por detrás del de Spider-Man: Brand New Day. Pero, horas después, La Casa de las Ideas sigue lanzando breves clips e imágenes adicionales para que los fans vean con aún mayor detalle lo que está por venir.
Y precisamente uno de esos teasers ha mostrado una impactante escena de la película. Por primera vez hemos podido ver el enfrentamiento entre el Doctor Doom y el mismísimo Magneto en Avengers: Doomsday. El mutante interpretado por Ian McKellen regresa ahora en el filme y será uno de los personajes más poderosos que le plante cara a Doom.
En este espectacular combate, Magneto llega incluso a arrancarle brevemente la máscara metálica al Doctor Doom, que necesita recurrir a toda su magia para evitarlo. A pesar de ello, puede observarse ligeramente el rostro del villano en el contorno de sus ojos. Parece que, como en los cómics, el personaje tendrá una cara totalmente masacrada y llena de cicatrices.
Robert Downey Jr. no se quitará la máscara del Doctor Doom
Este clip de Avengers: Doomsday con Magneto y el Doctor Doom llega, precisamente, cuando Chris Evans confirmó el mayor secreto que los fans esperaban. Y es que el actor de Steve Rogers aseguró que Robert Downey Jr. no dejará su rostro al descubierto en ningún momento de toda la película. Siempre tendrá la máscara puesta. Algo muy poco habitual en las cintas de Marvel, sobre todo con sus grandes estrellas.
"Lleva la máscara puesta todo el tiempo, y eso supone un gran reto interpretativo: hay que comunicarse con claridad sin dejar de mostrarse lo suficientemente abierto emocionalmente como para conectar con los espectadores. Esto no ha hecho más que confirmar lo que siempre he creído: Downey es capaz de todo", revela en una entrevista concedida a Empire.
Avengers: Doosmday se estrena en cines el 18 de diciembre.

Flipkart CEO Kalyan Krishnamurthy to step down; Lakshmi Venu moves court over family dispute
Under Krishnamurthy’s leadership, Flipkart grew more than fivefold and strengthened its position in India’s ecommerce market. The company is now preparing for a leadership transition.
Dear Reader,
Kalyan Krishnamurthy is stepping down as Flipkart CEO after more than 11 years with the company. More on who will lead Flipkart in the interim below.
India’s spacetech ambitions are getting a boost, with Karnataka approving Bengaluru-based Pixxel’s Rs 350 crore proposal to set up a satellite manufacturing facility in the state. The investment further strengthens Bengaluru’s position as a hub for aerospace and advanced manufacturing.
Meanwhile, AI infrastructure is attracting fresh capital, from data centres to startups that could test their products on live projects. Engineering consultancy Rodic Consultants has proposed a Rs 200 crore fund to back startups developing AI and other technologies for infrastructure, with selected companies getting access to live projects.
Nexent Capital has also launched a $1 billion fund to invest in AI data centres, quantum-ready infrastructure and advanced energy across India and North America, with a $20 million anchor commitment from the Tyagi family office.
Early-stage funding is broadening too. US-based VU Venture Partners has launched an accelerator and investment platform in India targeting cheques of $100,000 to $1 million, while Bengaluru-based Aeravti Ventures is targeting Rs 300 crore for its second fund to back 9 to 10 startups across food security, healthcare infrastructure and physical security.
Meanwhile, Goldman Sachs and Societe Generale have acquired a combined stake in eyewear retailer Lenskart for Rs 920.58 crore through block deals, signalling continued investor interest in the company.

articles.title: Ana (26 años) pasa seis horas al día en autobús para trabajar en Madrid: "Vivo en Aranda de Duero y me sale mucho más barato"
articles.text:
"Podía vivir en un estudio pero el alquiler se comía casi todo mi sueldo". Son palabras que resumen la decisión vital que un día tomó Ana, una vecina de la burgalesa Aranda de Duero. Entrevistada por ABC, esta joven de 26 años cuenta su experiencia viajando seis horas diarias para trabajar en la capital y que su dinero le rinda más.
Seis horas. Es lo que tiene, entre ida y vuelta, Ana para llegar a su casa en Aranda de Duero. Trabaja en Madrid, en Nuevos Ministerios, y cada día toma un autobús que luego combina con el Metro para ir desde casa hasta su lugar de trabajo. Tres horas de ida y tres horas de vuelta. La mayor parte del trayecto en autobús.
Explica que su día empieza a las 5:30 de la mañana. En ese momento sale de casa para tomar el autobús que conecta la localidad con Madrid y que sale cada mañana a las 6:00. Una vez lo toma, por delante tiene más de dos horas por delante. Dependiendo del día, el trayecto se puede ir por encima de las dos horas y media si hay mucho tráfico. Una vez en Madrid, toma el metro dos paradas para llegar a su destino.
Por las tardes, misma situación. Metro y autobús le obligan a hipotecar unas tres horas de su día para llegar a su casa.
Todo esto para qué. En el libro que lleva este nombre, Lionel Shriver cuenta la historia de un trabajador estadounidense que trabaja duro durante toda su vida con un solo objetivo, vender su empresa a una edad prudente e irse a un país exótico a disfrutar de su dinero lo que le quedara de vida.
Ana cuenta que su objetivo es más o menos similar. "Pagaba 420 euros por una habitación, ahora pago con mi pareja un piso por 450 euros, 225 euros cada uno". Y es que explica que sus gastos han caído en picado fuera de la ciudad. Tuvo que dejar un alquiler en el que estaba cómoda y al salir no había nada asequible a lo que poder agarrarse.
Expatriados madrileños. La experiencia de Ana es una canción que empieza a sonar más a menudo por las calles de la ciudad. La capital se ha convertido en un agujero negro laboral que todo lo absorbe. Si en el trabajo se exige presencialidad, lo tomas o lo dejas.
Cada vez son más los que buscan su vivienda en Valladolid, Segovia o Toledo. De hecho, los precios de estas ciudades han subido como consecuencia de quienes buscan refugio a un precio de la vivienda imposible. Las conexiones por tren son básicas para ello.
El problema de Ana es que "no tenemos tren". Y sin tren el transporte se vuelve todavía más pesado y dependiente de una ciudad cuyo tráfico empieza a colapsar con regularidad.
¿Y qué hacemos? La solución más sencilla lleva años inventada: un transporte público bueno, barato y fiable. Especialmente útil es el transporte intermodal que tiene al tren como núcleo vertebrador entre grandes ciudades. El problema en España es que el sistema ferroviario español ha colapsado, lastrado por inversiones que no se han hecho a tiempo. Ahora, no queda otra que revisar todo de nuevo al milímetro. Se ha acumulado el trabajo de décadas y hay que hacerlo ahora.
Tampoco hay que perder de vista que esta es la última tirita para una herida que ya no tiene solución. Cuando ponemos el sistema ferroviario japonés como ejemplo a seguir para nuestro día a día, nos olvidamos que esta es la solución que se ha encontrado para quienes no pueden permitirse los demenciales precios del alquiler de Tokyo y, al mismo tiempo, trabajar en la ciudad. La contrapartida, trenes llenos de personas que pasan tres, cuatro y cinco horas al día viajando.

articles.title: I’ve been testing these premium Xbox controllers against each other for weeks — this is the pro-level pad that’s become my go-to for playing GTA 6 and the one you should grab this Black Friday
articles.text:
I pitted my three favorite Xbox controllers against each other to decide which was best for playing GTA 6 — with lightning fast performance and innovative features, this pad would be my recommended buy this Black Friday
Mano a mano (a mano)
If you haven't yet started play Grand Theft Auto 6 on Xbox Series X yet, you'll be facing the same dilemma I did. No, not whether you should play as a disciplined, professional criminal or a stone-cold psychopath. If you're anything like me, you'll be wondering: which controller do I need to buy during the Black Friday sales to get the absolute best gameplay experience?
Fortunately, help is — quite literally — at hand. You see, I've spent the last few weeks testing out three premium examples of the best Xbox controllers side-by-side. I've been assessing them to see which offers the most comfortable design, the most game-changing features, the slickest performance and the most epic battery life. All to help you decide which will give you the best value when you're plunging the depths of Vice City's criminal underbelly.
The controllers I've picked for comparison are three of my favorites from the last year: the Asus ROG Raikiri II Xbox Wireless, the SteelSeries Aeon Pro, and the Scuf Valor Pro Wireless. Not only have I tested them for this article, but I've lived with them (some of them for months and months) and used them during my daily gaming. That means you can be sure I've given each of them a fair shake and tried them across a variety of titles.
So let me take you through what I thought of each pad, before I reveal which one I think is the best Black Friday buy for your adventures through Leonida.
Design
Okay, let’s start with the Asus ROG Raikiri II Xbox Wireless. While it’s arguably the least adventurous in terms of raw looks — only coming in black — I still really like what it’s throwing down, with its customizable RGB lightstrips and the gloss detail picking out the tiny lettering across its top half giving it a seriously premium look.
Ergonomically, it’s perfectly well-proportioned, resting comfortably in my hands even over long play sessions, and, unlike some pads I’ve tested, that textured grip isn’t too coarse, feeling comfortable even during epic crime sprees in GTA 6. Should you need slightly longer thumbsticks, it also comes with swappable high-profile sticks that will give you more reach and control.
All of its components are top quality too. Both its thumbsticks and shoulder triggers have TMR sensors — top of the line, drift-resistant sensors that should both activate faster than potentiometers and offer greater energy efficiency. The Raikiri II is the first pad I used with dual-mode triggers that allow you to switch between analog and clicky switches, something I now can’t live without. And its face buttons are wonderfully snappy micro-switches that pop off just like a mouse click.
Sign up for breaking news, reviews, opinion, top tech deals, and more.
Moving onto the SteelSeries Aeon Pro now, I’d say the controller again looks relatively modest and unassuming — but looks can be deceiving. It comes in just white or black but still gives off premium vibes to me. This is helped in a large part by its OLED screen, which sits front and center on the pad and, unlike some screens we’ve seen on pads in the past, actually serves a useful function: allowing gamers to swap platform, change profiles, check battery levels and remap buttons without leaving your game.
The Aeon Pro also feels pleasingly ergonomic to me. Its curves perfectly fit my hands, those rear paddles sit naturally right where my fingertips lie, while its micro-texture grips allowed me to cling onto it like Spider-Man onto a bathroom ceiling. And while the placement of its screen means its View and Menu buttons have been shifted down to the bottom of the pad, once I got used to it, I actually preferred this, as it allowed me to move my thumb laterally rather than having to stretch over the face buttons to pause the game.
Just like the Raikiri II, the Aeon Pro offers dual-mode triggers, making it easier to switch between granular control and super-fast digital actuation, and beautifully click micro-switch face buttons. It also rocks drift-resistant thumbsticks — although it uses Hall effect tech that falls just a jot below TMR in terms of sensitivity — and these can be hotswapped out in seconds, thanks to their smart magnetic design. Finally, its rear paddles are both super-responsive and perfectly positioned, sitting proud of the rest of the device and just underneath my fingertips.
Finally, the Scuf Valor Pro Wireless is the controller that I’d say takes the biggest swings when it comes to cosmetics. There’s a staggering array of hot-swappable faceplates available for it, whether you want the golden koi-bedecked Omen or the distinctly Vice-City-style Getaway, so you can match your look to your gaming experience.
I’d say it falls a little behind the other two pads when it comes to comfort, however. Don’t get me wrong: it’s still an eminently user-friendly controller with a satisfying shape that sat well in my hands. But compared to its rivals, I found the grips a little less comfortable than the others, with them tending to get sweatier. And its rear paddles — despite having a really satisfying action — are laid out horizontally, meaning they were a tiny bit more awkward to rest my fingers on when gripping shoulder trigger and buttons using two fingers.
On the plus side, the Valor Pro Wireless rocks some great inputs. Again, the thumbsticks and triggers are TMR, granting you incredibly sensitive control over the in-game action — you can also swap out the thumbstick caps, although this wasn’t as smooth as with the Aeon Pro. There’s no micro-switch face buttons here unfortunately but those dual-mode triggers are present again, which is definitely the biggest priority for me. Perhaps the pad’s most novel feature is the two volume knobs at its base, which allow you control game audio and chat sound levels separately: a huge asset for competitive gamers.
When it comes to design, this race is quite difficult to call. If it were just about sheer good looks, the Valor Pro Wireless would walk it. But ergonomically and in terms of controls, the other two come out just in front — albeit with very little light between them. I do prefer the Raikiri II’s TMR sensors but, honestly, the increase in sensitivity is so mild that you’re unlikely to notice in everyday use. In my book, the smart OLED screen, easier to reach buttons and easily swappable sticks of the SteelSeries just about allows it to nudge ahead in my opinion but, honestly, your feeling in terms of which comes out in front might just come down to your personal priorities.
Winner: SteelSeries Aeon Pro
Features
Like all of the controllers that I tested here, the ROG Raikiri II Xbox Wireless has lightning fast connectivity. It’s compatible with both PC and Xbox, allowing you to connect either via 2.4Ghz wireless, Bluetooth or a wired connection. And thanks to its 1,000Hz polling on PC, it offers super low-latency, with Asus ROG promising that it will respond in 3.2ms using a wireless connection.
Fire up ROG’s Gear Link software and there’s a whole host of functionality and tweaks available to you. Not only can you set deadzones for the thumbsticks but you can create custom response curves for both them and those TMR shoulder triggers. On top of this, you can also adapt the pad’s vibration level to suit your personal preference and tailor its RGB lighting by changing it to a block color, breathing or cycling colors or indicating battery level.
And while I criticized the Raikiri II in my original review because it was impossible to swap between saved profiles direct from the controller, that’s since been rectified in a firmware update. That means it’s packing a ton of functionality, while removing the principle complaint I had against it.
What's more, the battery life the Raikiri II wields is truly prodigious. Over a wireless connection — the way I used these pads a decent chunk of the time — Asus ROG says the Raikiri II will last at least 30 hours. This is a seriously long life compared to the average controller and definitely matches my experience — despite the fact that I rarely use the dock, I can often go weeks without reaching for my cable to charge it up, which is seriously good going.
Next up, let’s take a look at the feature set of the Scuf Valor Pro Wireless. In terms of connectivity, it can keep up blow for blow with the Raikiri II, providing the same lightning fast 1,000Hz polling rate on PC. Again, it can connect to either PC or Xbox using a 2.4GHz wireless dongle, Bluetooth or a wired connection, giving you plenty of options for controlling each platform.
On top of this, Scuf’s Valor Companion App allows you to create potentially unlimited custom profiles and assign three of them to the Valor Pro Wireless. You can tweak a wide variety of settings, such as remapping the controller’s back paddles, setting response curves and deadzones for its thumbsticks and triggers, dialling vibration intensity in the grips and triggers up and down and even set the vibration’s response curve.
Sadly, battery life is the feature where the Scuf falls shortest. Listed at 17 hours, its longevity isn’t the worst on the market by any means, but it is the weakest out of the three I’ve tested here. Additionally, as it doesn’t come packaged with a docking station, you’ll have to remember to stick it on charge occasionally or be willing to hook it up to a cable now and then.
So far then, I think the Raikiri II has taken the lead and will take some beating here. But, in a turnabout worthy of Whacky Races, SteelSeries Aeon Pro has some tricks up its sleeve.
First off, the Aeon Pro takes multiplatform play to a whole new level, thanks to its dual wireless connectivity. Essentially, plug its dock into both your PC and Xbox and you can switch your wireless connection between them simply by toggling a setting on the Aeon Pro’s screen. Every time I used this to switch platforms, it genuinely felt a little magical and meant I could use its 2.4GHz connectivity on both devices and keep using its 1,000Hz polling rate on PC without having to switch a dongle over.
SteelSeries’ GG software also possesses some special skills. My personal favorite is its profiles. Not only can you create a potentially infinite number of profiles and save up to eight on the Aeon Pro but its game profiles will detect when you’re playing that title on PC and switch to your assigned profile automatically, which is a really neat touch.
Sadly, GG is also missing some of the features of ROG Gear Link. While you can do things like adjusting the deadzones of triggers and thumbsticks, invert the stick, tweak the level of vibration for the grips and triggers and change up the settings of the Aeon Pro’s screen, you can’t set your own custom curves for the triggers, while the thumbsticks only offer three settings: default, dynamic and exponential. And the back paddles can only be mapped to existing buttons on the pad, not additional functions, slightly limiting their utility.
If I cut things off there, it’s likely the ROG would romp to victory. But the Aeon Pro has one last comedy anvil to drop on its opponents: its battery system. Its hot-swappable batteries mean that you always have a spare one charging up in the dock, allowing you to swap in a juice-up battery when your controller runs dry.
Even taking into account the fact that each battery offers much less juice than the Raikiri II at 12 hours a time, this system means you should never really be caught out without charge — I’ve genuinely not had to plug in a cable once while using this controller, which is fantastically freeing.
So while the SteelSeries misses a few functions here and there, it’s also the pro PC and Xbox controller I’ve tested that has most pushed the envelope with its features. Both the battery system and dual-platform connectivity are things that are hard to give up when you’ve got them, so I’m definitely granting the Aeon Pro the win here.
Winner: SteelSeries Aeon Pro
Performance
All three controllers felt responsive and snappy in use, especially on PC, thanks to that 1,000 Hz polling. No matter which I was using, their dual-mode triggers allowed me to better tailor their response to the game I was playing. In Clair Obscur: Expedition 33, the micro-switch triggers made firing off parry after parry much easier and gave me the speed I needed for taking down bosses like Creations. Meanwhile, their analog mode gave me much more granular control over my speed in Forza Horizon 6.
And while both the ROG Raikiri II Xbox Wireless and Scuf Valor Pro Wireless both utilize the slightly fancier TMR drift resistant tech, I honestly couldn’t distinguish much between them and the SteelSeries Aeon Pro. They both feel far more responsive than older potentiometer based inputs and unless you’re engaged in e-sports level play, I doubt you’ll notice a huge amount of difference in their respective sensitivities.
The only time any one of the pads felt anything less than lightning fast was when it came to face buttons. In contrast to the Raikiri II and Aeon Pro’s micro-switches, the Valor Pro has slightly spongier face buttons, meaning it doesn’t feel quite so quick off the mark. If you want that snappier activation though, you can easily remap these buttons to the rear paddles, which give you a much more rapid response and firmer feedback.
So all three controllers come very close in terms of in-game performance, with the Raikiri II perhaps inching a tiny bit in front, thanks to its TMR tech and micro-switch face buttons.
But before we start handing out ribbons, let’s take a look at customizability, as a big part of the draw for these kinds of premium controllers are how well you can adapt them to your play.
Using each controller’s software, I created a range of profiles for different genres of game, tweaking the settings to give the kind of response I desired for those titles. Creating profiles and loading them up mid-game was definitely easiest on the SteelSeries — with its eight locally saved profiles and the ability to switch between them using that OLED screen, it was always easy to find the right profile when I needed it. Conversely, the relatively restrictive number of profiles on the ROG and the Scuf meant I had to switch back to the software far more often to load up settings for new genres.
However, in use, I found the level of customizability offered by the Raikiri II and Valor Pro to have more impact in game. Thanks to the ability to dial in response curves, it was easy to set precise contours to my accelerator and brakes to improve my cornering in Forza Horizon 6 or meticulously refine the way my movement and aim reacted in games like Call of Duty: Modern Warfare 4. Conversely, the relatively limited responsiveness settings offered by the SteelSeries meant that sometimes my profiles didn’t feel that distinct in use, which is a shame given the number of options available.
All told, the ROG Raikiri II Xbox Wireless takes this one for me. Not only does it feel fast and responsive but it really is wonderfully flexible, allowing you to eke out absolutely the best performance you can for your playstyle.
Winner: ROG Raikiri II Xbox Wireless
Verdict
Picking a winner here isn’t easy. All three of these controllers offer great performance and I think you’re unlikely to be disappointed with any of them if you picked them up this Black Friday.
But there’s only one that I keep going back to as I explore the vast world of Vice City in GTA 6. That’s the SteelSeries Aeon Pro. In terms of speed and raw performance, it’s able to keep pace with the ROG Raikiri II at pretty much every turn, really only losing a few points for its reduced customizability.
And, in my opinion, it more than makes up for this in terms of innovative features. As a committed PC and Xbox gamer, its innovative dual-platform wireless connectivity means that I can count on it for every one of my games. Additionally, given I’m often wanting to settle in for lengthy play sessions, that swappable battery system means I can count on it to go the distance, even if I didn’t remember to plug it in the night before.

With over ten years of experience covering tech both in print and online, he’s served as editor of T3 and net magazines and written about everything from groundbreaking gadgets to innovative Silicon Valley startups. articles.title: What does it take to build a productive Canadian tech company?
articles.text:
Canada’s productivity challenges have put a renewed focus on how companies spend, hire, and invest in technology to support growth.
At BetaKit Talks: The Québec Productivity Engine, the spotlight was on a province showing signs of bucking the national trend.
“We plant the seed, we water the plant, we grow the plant, and someone else harvests it. That has to stop”
Presented by Float in Montréal’s Place Ville Marie, the event brought together Float Co-founder and CEO Rob Khazzam, Shakepay Co-founder and CEO Jean Amiouny, and Deck Co-founder and CEO Yves-Gabriel Leboeuf for a panel discussion moderated by BetaKit Editor-In-Chief Douglas Soltys.
The evening began with a French-language introduction to Float’s story, followed by a video address from Evan Solomon, Minister of AI and Digital Innovation, who highlighted new budget measures intended to improve access to investment capital and computing infrastructure.
“We plant the seed, we water the plant, we grow the plant, and someone else harvests it,” Solomon said to the audience of Québec founders. “That has to stop, and it is stopping now. Canadian companies must be able to grow here and stay here and compete with the world.”
Build where others see barriers
The three panellists have each helped build homegrown technology companies by identifying opportunities that established players had long overlooked. Amiouny launched Shakepay in 2015 when cryptocurrency was unfamiliar to investors, few banks were willing to work with FinTech startups, and Canadian consumers had limited access to Canadian-built financial products.
“Our view was there has to be something for Canadians, and I think this is the opportunity that most Canadian entrepreneurs see,” Amiouny said. “The barrier to entry can be high. I think FinTech generally is a little bit higher in Canada than in most countries, but beyond that, there’s not much competition.”
Shakepay, which allows Canadians to buy, sell, and hold Bitcoin, now serves just under two million Canadians. Its early years, however, were marked by difficult fundraising conditions. The company raised $20,000 in its first round, at a valuation below $1 million, when many investors were unwilling to back cryptocurrency companies.
Amiouny cautioned the next generation of founders against interpreting a difficult funding environment as a verdict on their ideas.
“VCs, the funding environment—these are all lagging indicators,” he said, adding that a founder’s conviction is a leading indicator. “The world may orient or adapt towards your idea in a year, two years, three years, or so on.” Amiouny added.
Make capital work harder
Khazzam also saw an opportunity to address inefficiencies in Canada’s business banking market. Float was founded to simplify corporate spending and expense management, and has since raised approximately $300 million CAD.
Float is now committing $5 million to expand its presence in Québec, where more than 1,000 businesses already use its platform. The investment includes plans to open the company’s first office outside Toronto in Montréal in 2027, recruit a General Manager, and build a local team dedicated to serving businesses in the province.
Khazzam pointed to Float’s customer data, which shows Québec businesses using the platform are more active in international transactions and AI adoption than their counterparts elsewhere in Canada.
“The productivity growth rate in Québec has been double that of Ontario and the rest of the country for the last 10 years,” Khazzam said. “I don’t know fully how it’s happening, but I want to learn, and I want to be a part of it, and I want to help amplify it because I think the rest of the country can learn a lot from Québec.”
Float’s growth has required a sustained focus on productivity. In the year or so after raising $30 million USD ($37 million CAD) at a $150-million USD ($215-million CAD) valuation in 2021, the broader tech funding market began to sour.
“We knew this valuation could kill the company if we didn’t grow into it,” Khazzam said. So, the company embarked on an 18-month push to improve revenue per employee ahead of its next funding round.
“We kept our headcount flat for 18 months,” he added. “We quadrupled our revenue. We didn’t spend another dollar.”
It was an exercise in capital efficiency born out of necessity, and one that Khazzam said made the company stronger.
Protect the freedom to make decisions
Leboeuf, who sold his first startup, Flinks, to National Bank of Canada in 2021, said having an exit behind him made raising capital for his next venture considerably easier.
“You raise more, faster, [on] better terms,” Leboeuf said.
“You can solve a revenue problem, you can solve a market problem, you can solve a product problem, all those things can be solved. What cannot be solved is you quitting.”
Leboeuf’s current venture, Deck, which develops infrastructure for accessing and interacting with websites, has raised approximately $25 million USD to date, and he acknowledged that investors tend to place greater confidence in founders who have completed a successful exit, even when their new ventures are still in their earliest stages.
When it comes to financing those ventures, Leboeuf strongly favours equity over debt. He argued that startups are inherently risky, and personally guaranteed loans can leave founders weighing their own financial security against the needs of their businesses.
“I would treat debt as almost poison when you’re early stage,” he added.
Turn AI into a productivity advantage
Advances in AI are also changing how much companies can accomplish with limited resources. Float encourages employees to experiment with AI, which has allowed them to create functional prototypes without weeks of back-and-forth between design and engineering teams.
“You can take an idea from a customer and have something ship within 24 hours,” Khazzam said. “I think right now we’re doing 70 percent more output per engineer at Float than six months ago. Over a one-year period, a three-year period, a five-year period, if we all have that mindset, how far are we going to get relative to the rest of the market? That’s what output and GDP per capita is all about.”
Deck has taken a more radical approach in the AI era. “We actually decided to scrap everything we had built and start a full replatforming earlier this year,” Leboeuf said.
The question of how to build—or rebuild—with limited resources was familiar to Leboeuf long before AI entered the picture. He recalled a period in 2017 when Flinks had just two weeks of cash remaining and no revenue, and what eventually got the company through.
“Just sign some deals and get revenues in your company,” he said to the audience. “That’s the only thing you have to do to survive.”
Amiouny argued that the need for perseverance doesn’t change as a company matures.
“Your idea dies when you quit,” Amiouny said. “I firmly believe this to be true. You can solve any problem: you can solve a revenue problem, you can solve a market problem, you can solve a product problem, all those things can be solved. What cannot be solved is you quitting.”
PRESENTED BY
Float helps Canadian businesses streamline spending, simplify financial operations, and do more with less. Learn more.

articles.title: Comment redonner vie aux vieux boîtiers : un Canon 5D de 2005 ou un Fuji X70 transformés en « argentiques » numériques
articles.text:
Open gate sur Sony, ProRes sur Nikon : nous venons de voir comment l’IA débloque les fonctions bridées des appareils photo récents. Mais en parallèle, un autre mouvement, beaucoup plus attachant, s’attaque aux vieux boîtiers que plus personne ne regardait. Ici, l’objectif n’est pas la course à la performance : il s’agit au contraire de ralentir la prise de vue pour retrouver le charme, le grain et même les contraintes de la pellicule.
    Pour aller plus loin
« Votre appareil sait déjà le faire » : grâce à l’IA, on peut débloquer les fonctions bridées des appareils photo Sony, Nikon et Panasonic
            
Le Canon 5D de 2005 se prend pour un argentique
L’étincelle est venue de Soup Engine. Dévoilé sur Reddit le 23 octobre, ce module greffé sur Magic Lantern tourne sur le tout premier Canon EOS 5D. Le principe est limpide : on choisit l’une des 13 « pellicules » intégrées, et chaque déclenchement génère un second JPEG avec le rendu appliqué, tout en laissant le fichier RAW intact.
Le détail le plus savoureux ? Le vieux processeur de 2005 met une vingtaine de secondes à traiter chaque cliché. Ce qui passerait pour un défaut rédhibitoire sur un boîtier moderne devient ici un atout : la cadence ralentit, on réfléchit avant de déclencher, et l’expérience devient selon son auteur plus « film like ».
Depuis, la communauté a porté le projet sur d’autres Canon, du 5D Mark II au 700D selon CineD, avec des rendus stockés dans de simples fichiers texte que chacun peut créer ou modifier depuis un éditeur web.
Film Roll, The Ritual, M-Film : la contrainte comme jeu
D’autres développeurs poussent l’idée encore plus loin en recréant volontairement les limites physiques de la pellicule :
- Film Roll (EOS 6D, 5D Mark III et 7D) : imaginé par Florin Kiritescu, il fait charger un « rouleau » de 12, 24 ou 36 vues à la sensibilité ISO du film choisi, et bloque carrément le déclencheur une fois le rouleau terminé.
- The Ritual (5D, 5D Mark II, 5D Mark III et 6D) : signé Latent Studios, il embarque directement dans le boîtier les rendus de leur logiciel de développement, proposé à prix libre.
- M-Film (dix boîtiers dont l’EOS M) : 68 pellicules au choix, un compteur de vues et aucune prévisualisation après la prise de vue.
Un esprit qui rappelle fortement le mode film du Fujifilm X Half, mais greffé ici sur des reflex qui ont plus de quinze ans.
Le Fuji X70 reçoit enfin la mise à jour que Fujifilm n’a jamais faite
Chez Fujifilm, la star du moment s’appelle FujiMod. Lancé fin octobre pour le X70, un compact APS-C de 2016 abandonné depuis longtemps par la marque , il lui ajoute pas moins de 23 fonctions : format panoramique 65:24, snap focus (une mise au point instantanée à distance fixe inspirée du Ricoh GR), mesure sur les hautes lumières, recettes nommées et simulations récentes comme Reala Ace. Le youtubeur bigheadtaco résume la frustration de nombreux fans : Fujifilm n’a jamais offert au X70 une mise à jour « Kaizen », ces gros firmwares qui enrichissent les boîtiers après leur sortie.
Sa version 0.2, publiée le 20 novembre, rassemble déjà 43 contributeurs et apporte le grain, l’halation (ce halo lumineux typique de la pellicule autour des sources de lumière) ou encore l’effet Color Chrome. D’autres anciens modèles comme le X100S ou le X-E2 sont déjà dans le viseur, avec un gros avantage : le mod démarre depuis la carte SD sans réécrire le firmware interne. La chaîne Micro Four Nerds l’a d’ailleurs mis à l’épreuve aux côtés de mods pour les Olympus PEN-F et E-P7.
| Projet | Boîtiers visés | Ce qu’il ajoute | Méthode | 
|---|---|---|---|
| Soup Engine | Canon EOS 5D à 700D | 13 pellicules (JPEG + RAW intact), fichiers personnalisables | Carte SD (Magic Lantern) | 
| Film Roll / M-Film | Canon 6D, 5D Mark III, 7D, EOS M… | Rouleaux de 12/24/36 vues, compteur, pas d’aperçu | Carte SD (Magic Lantern) | 
| FujiMod | Fujifilm X70 (X100S, X-E2 prévus) | 23 fonctions : Reala Ace, grain, halation, snap focus, 65:24 | Carte SD (sans flash) | 
Pas besoin d’être développeur : l’IA vous accompagne
Bidouiller un reflex Canon n’est pas nouveau : dans les années 2010, Magic Lantern avait déjà offert la vidéo RAW au 5D Mark III au prix d’années d’effort d’une poignée d’experts. Aujourd’hui, c’est exactement le même basculement que celui décrit dans notre dossier sur le débridage des appareils photo par IA : comme le résume la chaîne Pile et Face dans sa vidéo du 24 novembre, des passionnés qui ne savent pas coder entrent dans leurs boîtiers en discutant simplement avec un agent IA.
- Soup Engine : son auteur est développeur, mais assume pleinement que le projet est « vibe codé » tant ce type d’outil reste complexe à bâtir seul.
- FujiMod : Jake Teton-Landis a monté en deux week-ends un émulateur du X70 pour tester sans risquer de bricker son boîtier, pour 100 dollars d’abonnement IA selon Stringers. La page sécurité du projet précise même que les contributeurs ne sont pas censés lire le code qu’ils soumettent.
- Fujifilm X-H2S : le vidéaste Jacinto Salz raconte avoir modifié le firmware de son boîtier avec l’IA « en tant que non-ingénieur ».
- Sony A7 (2013) : le journaliste Chris Gampat (The Phoblographer) a réinstallé avec Claude les applis PlayMemories plus d’un an après la fermeture du store officiel par Sony, selon Camerahub.
- Nikon D2X : le youtubeur FUTC reprogramme son vieux reflex pro avec Claude dans une vidéo dédiée au « jailbreak » d’appareils par IA.
Sous le post de Soup Engine, un internaute demande même la marche à suivre pour confier le portage de son Lumix LX100 à Claude Code. C’est la même dynamique qui permet déjà de créer une application sans savoir coder, accélérée par la guerre que se livrent Claude Code et Codex.
Pourquoi justement les vieux boîtiers ?
La raison est d’abord très terre-à-terre : comme l’explique Digital Camera World, risquer de bloquer un vieux reflex qui ne coûte plus grand-chose et n’est plus sous garantie depuis longtemps fait nettement moins peur que de toucher à un boîtier neuf à 3 000 euros. C’est aussi le plaisir de ressortir un appareil qui « restait sur une étagère sans servir », d’autant que ces Canon, documentés depuis quinze ans par Magic Lantern, restent abordables en occasion et délivrent toujours d’excellents fichiers selon CineD.
Il y a enfin l’air du temps. L’argentique revient en force, au point que Pentax a lancé un nouveau boîtier à pellicule, le Pentax 17, et les simulations de film de Fujifilm sont devenues un argument commercial majeur. La lenteur naturelle de ces vieilles machines colle finalement à merveille à cette esthétique.
Et demain, des simulations Fuji sur n’importe quel boîtier ?
Les premiers signes sont déjà là. Le firmware custom Erlla pour Sony A7 IV, l’un des boîtiers stars de notre enquête sur les fonctions bridées, intègre déjà 12 filtres imitant des simulations Fujifilm, entraînés par un agent IA. Sur Ricoh GR IV, des youtubeurs chargent également des recettes Fujifilm via GRKit.
D’où une question qui donne déjà des sueurs froides aux équipes marketing : la même méthode pourrait-elle offrir un « Classic Chrome » maison à n’importe quel vieux Canon ou Nikon d’occasion ? Techniquement, la piste est ouverte. Juridiquement, c’est une autre histoire : Soup Engine précise d’ailleurs que ses noms de rendus sont des raccourcis, pas des copies exactes.
Comment ça marche concrètement (et les risques à connaître)
Contrairement à une idée reçue, la plupart de ces mods pour vieux boîtiers ne remplacent pas le système interne de l’appareil. Ils reposent sur une carte SD préparée sur ordinateur : au démarrage, le boîtier charge le programme en mémoire vive, et retirer la carte (ou la remplacer par une carte standard) suffit en principe à retrouver l’appareil d’origine.
Sur un boîtier de 2005, la garantie n’est certes plus un sujet, mais le risque de rendre l’appareil inutilisable demeure bien réel, même depuis la carte mémoire :
- Le piège du démarrage sur carte : Magic Lantern active un drapeau de démarrage sur la carte mémoire ; si la bonne carte est absente, le boîtier peut refuser de s’allumer, rappelle Camera Lookout.
- La version exacte du firmware : chaque mod est taillé pour un modèle et une version logicielle très précis.
- Les données de calibration : FujiMod lui-même juge le firmware custom « extrêmement risqué », le pire scénario étant de corrompre les données de calibration propres à chaque boîtier (restaurables uniquement depuis une sauvegarde ou en centre agréé).
- La garantie sur les boîtiers récents : Fujifilm considère que tout logiciel non licencié connecté au boîtier annule la garantie, selon Fuji X Weekly.
Bref, tentez l’expérience uniquement sur un appareil que vous êtes prêt à perdre, jamais sur le boîtier qui doit assurer un shooting payé ou vos photos de vacances.
Une seconde vie plutôt que le tiroir
Un appareil photo qui fonctionne parfaitement mais que sa marque a cessé de mettre à jour n’est pas cassé : il est abandonné. C’est exactement ce que nous soulignions dans notre analyse sur l’obsolescence programmée et le vrai problème de la durabilité : le véritable goulot d’étranglement, c’est le suivi logiciel, pas le matériel. Un vieux 5D qui reprend du service, c’est un boîtier de moins qui dort dans un tiroir et un achat neuf en moins, dans la même logique que le reconditionnement de nos smartphones.
Reste à voir comment les constructeurs réagiront. bigheadtaco espère que FujiMod poussera Fujifilm à proposer des mises à jour payantes pour ses anciens modèles. En attendant, ce sont des particuliers armés d’une IA qui s’en chargent — et qui prouvent que nos vieux appareils en ont encore largement sous le capot.

articles.title: Gemini Notebook veut vous faire réviser comme un pro et ses nouvelles fiches ont de quoi séduire
articles.text:
Les partiels approchent à grands pas ? Google a pensé à vous : les flashcards de Gemini Notebook viennent de recevoir une mise à jour conséquente.
Gemini Notebook poursuit son évolution à la vitesse grand V. L’ex-NotebookLM, qui a récemment dit adieu à ses plafonds journaliers au profit de limites basées sur la puissance de calcul, s’est récemment doté d’un catalogue de manuels gratuits, hélas réservés aux cursus américains et indiens. Depuis peu, il est même capable de générer des sites web interactifs à partir des documents des utilisateurs. Google va plus loin cette semaine en améliorant les flashcards du service.
Trois nouvelles fonctions pour des révisions plus efficaces
Les flashcards, ces fameuses cartes de révision particulièrement prisées outre-Atlantique, viennent de recevoir une mise à jour sur Gemini Notebook. Si elles étaient, jusqu’à récemment, uniquement textuelles, elles incluent désormais des illustrations. Grâce à la puissance de l’IA, les cartes peuvent en effet piocher des visuels dans les documents importés par l’utilisateur pour accompagner chaque question.
Autre nouveauté : un minuteur a été déployé pour permettre aux étudiants de se mettre en conditions d’examen. Cela pourrait considérablement aider ceux qui ont du mal à gérer leur temps en les incitant à se fixer un cadre. Côté mobile, l’application est devenue capable d’envoyer des notifications pour inciter l’utilisateur à réviser.
Des améliorations utiles à de nombreux types d’utilisateurs
Ces nouvelles options sont un coup de pouce bienvenu pour tous ceux qui veulent redoubler d’efficacité dans leurs révisions. Google ne vise toutefois pas uniquement ceux qui sont assis sur les bancs de la fac : « ces améliorations offrent aux étudiants, aux enseignants et aux équipes de formation un environnement plus flexible pour se préparer aux examens, aux certifications internes et au développement continu des compétences », peut-on notamment lire dans l’annonce.
- Réponses liées aux sources
- Nombreux formats de fichiers
- Génération audio et visuelle
Bien sûr, ces outils ont quelques limites. Le géant de Mountain View explique, par exemple, qu’il a voulu fournir « un contexte visuel en plus des indications textuelles pour faciliter la compréhension », ce qui est tout à son honneur. On aurait toutefois aimé savoir comment l'outil sélectionne les images et quels sont les risques que l’IA choisisse une illustration hors sujet : Google ne dit pas un mot sur le sujet. Quant au chronomètre et aux rappels, on espère que les utilisateurs ne finiront pas, à terme, par les ignorer.
Les nouvelles fonctionnalités sont disponibles dès aujourd’hui sur Gemini Notebook pour l’ensemble des clients Workspace, les abonnés Workspace Individual, mais aussi les détenteurs d’un compte Google Personnel.

articles.title: Vous trouvez la conduite de GTA 6 particulièrement pointue ? C’est normal
articles.text:
La conduite est l’un des éléments les plus impressionnants de GTA 6, tant elle est pointue, voire punitive si on ne fait pas attention. Elle est un mélange entre l’approche arcade de GTA 5 et l’orientation plus simulation de GTA 4. À l’arrivée, elle procure de bonnes sensations, avec un moteur physique qui encourage à bien conduire pour ne pas ruiner rapidement sa voiture.
Pour obtenir ce comportement, Rockstar Games n’est pas allé frapper à la porte de n’importe qui. Lewis Bentley, ancien compétiteur du championnat eSport Gran Turismo World Series, a passé trois ans et demi dans l’équipe chargée de la physique des véhicules, rapporte GTPlanet, site spécialisé dans Gran Turismo, ce mercredi 25 novembre. Il l’a annoncé lui-même le week-end du 21 novembre, dans une vidéo YouTube supprimée depuis, et le générique officiel de GTA 6 le confirme : il y figure comme développeur dans le pôle « Physics Development ».
Un finaliste mondial de Gran Turismo dans l’équipe physique de GTA 6
Lewis Bentley a officié sur la physique de la conduite, sans préciser ce qu’il a vraiment apporté à GTA 6 : il dit vouloir laisser les joueurs tout découvrir par eux-mêmes. En matière de gameplay automobile, il s’y connaît.
La carrière de Lewis Bentley dans le championnat officiel Gran Turismo ne lui a pas permis de remporter un titre majeur, mais il a quelques belles prestations à mettre en valeur. En 2018, lors du tout premier World Tour de GT Sport, organisé au Nürburgring en marge des 24 Heures, il termine deuxième de la course 1 puis quatrième de la finale des Manufacturer Series, avec l’équipe Renault Sport qu’il partage avec deux autres pilotes. La même année, aux finales mondiales de Monaco, il décroche la septième place de la finale des Manufacturer Series, cette fois sous les couleurs de Chevrolet. En 2019, il est encore sélectionné pour les étapes du World Tour à Paris et Salzbourg. En Autriche, au volant d’une Peugeot RCZ, il mène la première course sous la pluie.
Comme le rappelle The Drive ce lundi 23 novembre, Lewis Bentley n’est pas le seul spécialiste des sports mécaniques chez Rockstar Games. Trois employés de Rockstar North, Ben Lyons, Markus Low et Dale Lomas, ont piloté une BMW Série 3 aux 24 Heures du Nürburgring en 2022, et remporté leur catégorie. Ben Lyons est même l’un des deux directeurs techniques chargés de la physique, avec Eugene Foss.
Ben Lyons a détaillé la démarche dans des notes transmises à TechRadar ce mardi 24 novembre. Après GTA 5, une partie de l’équipe s’est mise à faire courir de vraies voitures, puis Rockstar a réécrit la simulation de chaque type de véhicule. Même les avions y passent : chaque aile, hélice et gouverne est simulée séparément, et réagit aux turbulences et à la météo.
