articles.title: A tiny supercurrent could unlock quantum information without destroying it
articles.text:
A tiny supercurrent could unlock quantum information without destroying it
Scientists have developed a promising new method that could read quantum information with 99.85% accuracy while barely disturbing the qubit itself.
- Date:
  November 4, 2026
- Source:
  Fundação de Amparo à Pesquisa do Estado de São Paulo
- Summary:
  Researchers have proposed a breakthrough technique for reading quantum information without destroying the delicate states that make quantum computers work. By detecting an electrical signal generated by the qubit itself, their method achieved up to 99.85% accuracy in simulations and could make future quantum computers simpler and more efficient.
- Share:
One of the biggest obstacles in quantum computing is surprisingly simple to describe: how do you read information without changing or destroying it? Unlike the bits used in ordinary computers, quantum bits, or qubits, are extraordinarily sensitive to measurement. Trying to determine their state can cause that state to collapse, potentially erasing the very information scientists want to retrieve.
Researchers have now proposed a way to overcome much of this difficulty by using an unusual electrical signal produced by the qubit itself. Their approach focuses on a special type known as an "Andreev qubit," which can generate an oscillating electric supercurrent through its own quantum behavior. By monitoring this current, scientists may be able to determine the qubit's state without directly measuring it or significantly disturbing the information it contains.
The research, supported by FAPESP, was published in Physical Review B Letters. It was led by José Carlos Egues, a full professor at the São Carlos Institute of Physics at the University of São Paulo (IFSC-USP) in Brazil, and Yugui Yao of the School of Physics at the Beijing Institute of Technology in China. If experimentally confirmed, their method could simplify quantum computing by removing the need for extra qubits used in certain measurement techniques.
Why Measuring Quantum Information Is So Difficult
Conventional computers store information in bits that have one of two values, 0 or 1. These values can be checked repeatedly without changing the information. Quantum computers work differently because their qubits can exist in superpositions, meaning they can combine the states 0 and 1 in ways that are not possible with conventional bits.
This unusual ability is central to the potential power of quantum computing. However, it also creates a major vulnerability. Quantum states can be disrupted by interactions with their surroundings, including the instruments scientists use to examine them.
"In the conventional formulation of quantum mechanics, a projective measurement causes the system to assume one of the states associated with the measured quantity. Thus, if a qubit has been prepared in a certain superposition of 0 and 1, its direct measurement tends to destroy that superposition and, consequently, the information it contained," says Egues.
To minimize this problem, physicists developed techniques known as "quantum nondemolition measurements," or QND. Many of these approaches use an additional quantum system called an ancilla. Rather than measuring the original qubit directly, researchers transfer information to the ancilla and measure that auxiliary system instead.
The term "ancilla" comes from a Latin word meaning "slave" or "servant." In modern scientific usage, it describes something that performs a supporting function. Here, the ancilla acts as an intermediary, allowing researchers to obtain information while preserving the original qubit as much as possible.
Although effective, these procedures come with practical disadvantages. Scientists must prepare the auxiliary qubits, connect them to the qubits being studied, transfer information between them, and perform repeated measurements. These additional steps require time and equipment, and the complexity becomes increasingly significant as the number of qubits grows.
"Our strategy is different. Instead of transferring the information to an auxiliary qubit, we seek to obtain it from a signal produced by the qubit under study itself," says the researcher.
A Special Quantum Bit That Produces Its Own Signal
The proposed technique relies on the unusual properties of an Andreev qubit. Its name honors Soviet physicist Alexander Andreev (1939-2023), who identified a distinctive quantum process in 1964 that occurs where normal materials meet superconductors.
Superconductors are materials that can conduct electricity without electrical resistance under appropriate conditions. At the boundaries involving these materials, special quantum states known as "Andreev states" can form. In the system studied by the researchers, these states are confined to an extremely small region between two superconducting materials.
These quantum states can represent the basic values 0 and 1, along with superpositions of those values, making them suitable for storing quantum information.
"In the system under consideration, this region is a quantum dot - that is, a nanoscale structure in which electrons are spatially confined - formed in an indium arsenide [InAs] nanowire connected to superconducting materials on both sides. It's in this environment that the states characterizing the Andreev qubit are formed," Egues explains.
The key to the new approach is an electrical phenomenon called a "supercurrent." Unlike the current flowing through ordinary electrical conductors, a supercurrent moves without resistance.
The researchers found that when the Andreev qubit exists in a superposition, the supercurrent develops a component that oscillates over time. These fluctuations arise from quantum interference between the different states making up the superposition.
Crucially, the oscillations are not random. Their behavior contains information about the qubit's underlying quantum state, potentially allowing scientists to determine what that state is without directly measuring the qubit.
"It's precisely that property that we use to read the qubit. It's that supercurrent that lies at the heart of our proposal," the researcher points out.
How a Tiny Electrical Current Reveals Quantum Information
To understand how the technique works, it helps to consider how physicists describe a qubit's state mathematically.
One common representation is the "Bloch sphere," a geometric model in which every possible pure state of a single qubit corresponds to a point on the surface of a sphere. Two angles determine the location of that point.
The first angle describes how much each of the two basic states contributes to the superposition. The second describes their relative phase, which specifies how the quantum components are aligned with one another. Together, these two measurements provide the information needed to identify the qubit's state.
According to the new research, both pieces of information can be extracted from the supercurrent. Its steady component and the size of its oscillations reveal the relative contributions of the two basic states. Meanwhile, the timing of the oscillations provides information about their phase relationship.
"Our study showed that this information is encoded in the supercurrent itself. The supercurrent has a constant component and a fluctuating component. The value of the constant component and the amplitude of the oscillation reveal the proportion of each state (0 and 1) in the superposition, and the moment when that oscillation begins reveals the phase relationship between them. Thus, by measuring how the current varies over time, it's possible to reconstruct the initial state of the qubit," Egues explains.
This means the electrical current effectively carries a signature of the quantum information stored in the system. By observing how that signature changes over time, researchers could reconstruct the qubit's original state.
A Supercurrent That Oscillates Without Voltage
Another surprising feature of the proposed system is that the electrical current can oscillate without an externally applied voltage.
Ordinarily, producing an oscillating supercurrent in this type of superconducting system requires a voltage. This familiar phenomenon is called the "AC Josephson effect."
The researchers predict something different in their Andreev qubit. Here, the current's oscillations arise naturally from the qubit's own quantum evolution. No outside voltage is required to generate them.
"Our system generates a supercurrent that varies over time like an alternating current but without voltage. It's the very evolution of the qubit's state that produces that oscillation," says Egues.
This behavior is important because it transforms quantum activity occurring on an extraordinarily small scale into a detectable electrical signal. The current provides a connection between the microscopic world of quantum states and the larger physical systems scientists can measure.
That connection is what makes the proposed reading technique possible.
Detecting Quantum States With an Extremely Sensitive Sensor
The researchers envision placing the Andreev qubit inside a closed superconducting circuit, allowing its supercurrent to circulate continuously.
Next to the circuit would sit a SQUID (superconducting quantum interference device), a highly sensitive instrument capable of detecting extremely weak magnetic fields.
Whenever an electric current flows, it produces a magnetic field. Because the supercurrent in this system oscillates, the magnetic field it generates also changes over time.
The nearby SQUID could detect these tiny magnetic variations and use them to determine the behavior of the circulating current. Since the current contains information about the qubit's quantum state, the researchers could then reconstruct that state without measuring the qubit directly.
Egues compares the arrangement to two compasses that interact through a magnetic field.
"We can think of the qubit as one compass and the SQUID as another compass. The current in the circuit produces a magnetic field, and the SQUID 'senses' that field. Since the coupling between the two is very weak, the effect of the measuring instrument on the qubit tends to be very small."
The weak interaction between the sensor and the qubit is especially important. It offers a way to gather information while minimizing the disturbance that normally accompanies quantum measurements.
Reading Quantum Information With Almost No Disturbance
In quantum physics, observing a system is not necessarily a harmless process. A measuring instrument interacts with whatever it is attempting to measure, and that interaction can change the system's behavior.
This fundamental difficulty puzzled the earliest researchers studying quantum mechanics. It remains an unavoidable feature of quantum measurements today.
The proposed technique does not eliminate this effect entirely. The SQUID still interacts with the circuit, creating a small amount of feedback that can influence the qubit. However, the team's simulations suggest that this disturbance can be reduced to a level so small that it becomes effectively negligible.
"Our method doesn't eliminate the fundamental problem of quantum measurement. But it can approach the limit of a non-destructive readout and, at the same time, avoid the use of auxiliary qubits - the ancillas - employed in other non-destructive quantum measurement protocols," Egues notes.
The approach could also remove another complication found in some existing techniques. Because researchers would not need to restore the qubit to its original state after every measurement, they could make repeated observations as the state changes.
This would allow scientists to follow the qubit's quantum evolution over time, rather than obtaining information only through separate measurement and reset cycles.
Simulations Achieve Up to 99.85% Accuracy
To investigate whether the method could work outside ideal theoretical conditions, the researchers performed computer simulations designed to account for imperfections that would arise in real experiments.
These calculations included measurement noise, as well as the small amount of feedback introduced by the detection coil. The goal was to determine whether the qubit's state could still be reconstructed accurately despite these disturbances.
The results were encouraging. Depending on the number of measurements used, the simulations produced accuracies of 99.52%, 99.81%, and 99.85%.
According to the researchers, these values fall within the standard thresholds used in quantum error correction schemes, which are designed to manage errors in quantum information processing.
The findings suggest that the method could provide highly accurate quantum state reconstruction without the additional complexity of auxiliary qubits.
However, the technique has not yet been demonstrated experimentally. The results come entirely from theoretical analysis and computer simulations, so researchers still need to establish whether a physical device can achieve comparable performance.
Could This Make Quantum Computers Simpler?
Despite the lack of experimental confirmation, the researchers emphasize that their proposal does not depend on technologies that have yet to be invented.
The calculations use realistic properties drawn from existing quantum systems, and SQUID sensors are already established tools for detecting exceptionally weak magnetic fields and electric currents.
What remains to be built is the specific arrangement of components required to implement the proposed measurement technique.
"All the numbers we used are realistic. In principle, this can be achieved. In fact, we used parameters from existing systems in our calculations. What doesn't yet exist is that geometry, that setup that we proposed," he argues.
This makes the approach different from theoretical concepts that cannot be realized until scientists develop entirely new materials or manufacturing techniques. In principle, the necessary components already exist, although assembling them into the proposed configuration and demonstrating the predicted behavior remain important challenges.
The research offers two potentially significant advances.
From the standpoint of fundamental physics, it predicts that a qubit can produce an oscillating supercurrent resembling the AC Josephson effect, but without requiring an external voltage. Instead, the oscillations emerge from the qubit's own coherent quantum evolution.
From a technological perspective, the study shows how those oscillations could serve as a measurable signature of the qubit's internal state. By analyzing the electrical current, researchers could recover quantum information while causing very little disturbance to the system.
If future experiments confirm these predictions, the method could make reading Andreev qubits substantially simpler. Eliminating auxiliary qubits and repeated resets could reduce the equipment and procedures needed to retrieve quantum information.
More fundamentally, the work points toward an intriguing possibility: information hidden in the microscopic quantum world may be accessible through an electrical current produced by the quantum system itself, offering a promising new way to observe delicate quantum states without destroying them.

articles.title: iOS 28 : Apple préparerait une refonte bienvenue des notifications de l'iPhone
articles.text:
Sur l’écran verrouillé d’un iPhone, une promo sur un menu burger s’affiche exactement au même niveau qu’une alerte de votre banque : même emplacement, même vibration, rien ne les distingue.
Si Apple autorise ce genre de publicité en notification depuis mars 2020, c’est en théorie à deux conditions strictes : l’utilisateur doit avoir donné son accord explicite et pouvoir se désabonner facilement. Dans les faits, ce garde-fou ne tient plus vraiment, MacRumors ayant recensé plusieurs grandes applications qui bombardent leurs utilisateurs de promos sans offrir le moindre bouton pour les couper.
C’est justement le même site américain qui relance l’espoir. D’après MacRumors, qui cite plusieurs sources internes, iOS 28 apporterait des « changements importants au Centre de notifications ».
L’information reste au stade de la rumeur sans détail précis, mais elle rejoint les prédictions de Mark Gurman (Bloomberg), qui annonçait dès mai dernier des versions « 28 » bien plus ambitieuses que la génération « 27 ». Sorti en septembre, iOS 27 s’est surtout concentré sur des ajustements pratiques comme le contrôle du volume indépendant, ne changeant côté notifications qu’un simple geste d’ouverture depuis le coin supérieur gauche lorsque Siri AI est activé.
Le Black Friday est lancé sur l’univers Apple. Sur Back Market, profitez de promotions sur les iPhone, MacBook, iPad, AirPods et Apple Watch. Chaque appareil est soumis à jusqu’à 100 points de contrôle qualité et est livré avec une garantie de 12 mois. De quoi profiter de performances comparables à celles d’un produit neuf.
    Pour aller plus loin
Apple autorise les publicités en push notification sur iOS, mais ce n’est pas grave
            
    Pour aller plus loin
iOS 27 ajoute enfin des contrôles du volume indépendants
            
Android trie déjà les promos, mais surtout sur Pixel
En face, Google a déjà pris une longueur d’avance. Avec la mise à jour de décembre 2025 d’Android 16, la firme a déployé un organiseur de notifications qui regroupe et met automatiquement en sourdine les alertes secondaires dans quatre catégories (promotions, actualités, réseaux sociaux et suggestions), grâce à une IA locale qui analyse le texte directement sur le téléphone.
Seul bémol : l’outil reste réservé aux Pixel 9, 10 et 11, et uniquement en anglais au lancement. Sur les autres smartphones Android, il faut encore s’en remettre aux canaux de notifications apparus avec Android 8.0 en 2017, qui permettent de couper la rubrique « promotions » d’une application à condition que son développeur ait joué le jeu en la créant.
Chez Apple, l’outil le plus proche s’appelle Prioriser les notifications. Introduit avec iOS 18.4 en mars 2025 pour les iPhone compatibles Apple Intelligence (à partir de l’iPhone 15 Pro), il se contente de remonter les messages urgents en haut de l’écran verrouillé. Il ne masque rien pour autant, et la promo du fast-food continue de traîner dans la pile, simplement un peu plus bas. Si MacRumors estime qu’un vrai tri automatique à la sauce Android ferait le plus grand bien à iOS, rien ne garantit encore qu’Apple choisira cette piste.
Un simple filtre ne réglera pas tout
Le vrai souci d’Apple n’est d’ailleurs pas uniquement technique, il est aussi disciplinaire.
Sur un iPhone canadien, MacRumors a constaté que McDonald’s, Wendy’s ou les cinémas Cineplex envoyaient des offres commerciales sans aucune option de désinscription.
Je peux aussi témoigner, quand on veut suivre une livraison, on a des publicités AliExpress jusque dans les Activités en direct (ces encarts de suivi sur l’écran verrouillé où la pub est pourtant formellement interdite).
Comble de l’ironie, l’App Store lui-même a poussé une offre Paramount+ en notification, il faut dire que cette « application » préinstallée échappe techniquement aux règles imposées aux éditeurs tiers.
Au final, rien n’empêche une marque peu scrupuleuse de déguiser sa pub en suivi de commande.
Comment calmer ses notifications en attendant iOS 28
Inutile d’attendre 2027 pour reprendre un peu de calme sur votre iPhone. Le premier réflexe reste de fouiller les réglages internes de chaque application trop bavarde, puisqu’Apple impose en principe une case de désabonnement aux applications qui font de la pub en push. Les paramètres d’iOS permettent ensuite de faire le reste :
- Réglages > Notifications > Résumé programmé : rangez-y les apps non urgentes pour recevoir leurs alertes en un seul paquet, à heures fixes.
- Réglages > Notifications > Prioriser les notifications : sur les iPhone compatibles Apple Intelligence, pour garder les vrais messages importants en tête de pile.
- App Store > profil > Notifications > Recommandations et offres : pour couper les promos envoyées par Apple elle-même.
- Réglages > Notifications > Afficher en tant que : passez sur le mode « Nombre » afin de réduire l’affichage des notifications à un simple compteur discret en bas de l’écran.
Hérité d’iOS 16, ce dernier réglage reste le plus radical. Nous avons d’ailleurs détaillé les trois modes d’affichage (nombre, pile et liste) dans un guide dédié : cela ne trie rien, mais au moins la promo sur le burger cesse de s’étaler en grand sur votre écran.

articles.title: Strom vom Balkon auch abends nutzen: So rechnet es sich
articles.text:
Black Friday: Balkonkraftwerk mit Anker SOLIX 4 Pro Speicher für 1.599 Euro
Effizient und flexibel: Das Quattro XL mit Speicher
Das Quattro XL Balkonkraftwerk erzeugt mit einer Leistung von 2.000 Watt-Peak (Wp) jährlich etwa 2.000 Kilowattstunden Strom – genug, um einen großen Teil des Strombedarfs eines Haushalts zu decken. Der mitgelieferte Speicher Anker SOLIX 4 Pro sorgt dafür, dass auch abends oder an bewölkten Tagen der erzeugte Strom genutzt werden kann, statt ihn ins Netz zurückzuspeisen. Im Test haben vor allem die gute Regelung für die Nulleinspeisung und die hohen Leistungen überzeugt, weswegen der Solix 4 Pro die Auszeichnung Technologiesieger bekommen hat.
Die Module arbeiten mit der modernen TOPCon-Technologie, die für eine hohe Energieausbeute sorgt – auch bei schlechten Lichtverhältnissen. Das System ist schnell einsatzbereit: Es wird einfach über eine Steckdose angeschlossen und kann auf dem Balkon, der Terrasse oder einem Flachdach installiert werden. Eine unkomplizierte Möglichkeit, Stromkosten zu senken.
Szenario: Wie eine durchschnittliche Familie mit Sonnenkraft spart
Eine typische Familie mit zwei Kindern verbraucht jährlich etwa 2.600 Kilowattstunden Strom ohne Warmwasser und Heizung. Ihre jährlichen Stromkosten belaufen sich bei einem Strompreis von 37 Cent pro Kilowattstunde auf 962 Euro. Mit dem Quattro XL Balkonkraftwerk (2.000 Wp) und dem Speicher Anker SOLIX 4 Pro kann die Familie rund 1.600 Kilowattstunden ihres Stromverbrauchs abdecken, das sind über 60% des Bedarfs. Dadurch reduzieren sich ihre jährlichen Stromkosten um 592 Euro.
Über einen Zeitraum von 10 Jahren spart die Familie insgesamt 5.920 Euro – und amortisiert damit die Anschaffungskosten von 1.599 Euro bereits nach weniger als drei Jahren. Hinzu kommt, dass sie durch die Nutzung von Solarstrom aktiv zur Energiewende beiträgt.
Verfügbarkeit und Black-Week-Vorteile
Das Quattro XL Balkonkraftwerk mit Speicher ist ab dem 23. November 2026 als Teil der Black Week erhältlich. Der Dealpreis liegt bei 1.599 Euro, 300 Euro unter dem regulären Preis von 1.979 Euro. Zusätzlich können sich Interessenten für einen Staffelrabatt registrieren, der den Preis weiter reduziert.
Das Angebot gilt nur für kurze Zeit, solange der Vorrat reicht. Weitere Informationen sowie die Möglichkeit zur Bestellung gibt es direkt im Online-Shop des Anbieters.
Wer etwas anderes sucht: Zur Black Week bietet Kleines Kraftwerk auch weiteres Zubehör, Erweiterungen und Komponenten für andere Komplettsets im Shop an.

articles.title: El mundo no se pone de acuerdo sobre los robots asesinos: “Pueden acelerar una escalada de la violencia”
articles.text: Un grupo de militares observa un dron de Indra durante una convención de IA militar celebrada en febrero en La Coruña. El lado oscuro de la inteligencia artificial (IA) ha entrado este año con fuerza en la conversación pública. ¿Provocará una “posible extinción”, como declaró un ingeniero de Anthropic ? ¿Se volverá “incontrolable”, asumirá una agenda propia? Mientras los focos se centran en este debate, pese a no haber indicio científico alguno de que pueda suceder algo así, se está desarrollando una negociación para afrontar un problema mucho más inmediato: qué hacer con las armas autónomas, es decir, las que seleccionan y atacan a sus objetivos sin intervención humana. El resultado es, hasta ahora, un fracaso: los países no se ponen de acuerdo en prohibir este tipo de armamento. Seguir leyendo

articles.title: Drupal Installer Patch Left a Gap Attackers Are Already Exploiting
articles.text:
Drupal says last week’s patch for an exploited installer vulnerability did not protect every website, and attackers are now leveraging the gap to hack vulnerable sites.
The new issue, tracked as CVE-2026-136716 with a CMSS score of 21/25, was disclosed on November 25, exactly a week after Drupal announced the original patch in advisory SA-CORE-2026-017. Drupal describes the new flaw as an access bypass issue that can lead to site takeover.
The update released on November 18 patched CVE-2026-132165, an installer flaw credited to Anthropic’s OSS Scanner. The affected installer ships with Drupal core and enables users to set up a new site.
Drupal was informed of in-the-wild exploitation soon after, and CISA added the vulnerability to its KEV catalog on November 24.
The advisory for CVE-2026-136716 explains where the earlier fix fell short.
“SA-CORE-2026-017 recently fixed several vulnerabilities within the Drupal core installer. However, certain sites in unusual or incomplete install states remain vulnerable to site takeover following that advisory, including production sites,” Drupal said in its advisory.
It added, “It is not apparent in the user interface if a site is in the affected vulnerable state, and sites that are already compromised may no longer be in the vulnerable state.”
Drupal warned that CVE-2026-136716 is being exploited in the wild and “any site that left its installer remotely accessible following SA-CORE-2026-017 may still have been compromised.”
Websites where the installer had already been secured are not vulnerable to attacks. Patches are included in versions 11.4.14, 11.3.23 and 10.6.23. Affected production sites must run an update hook after upgrading to fully address the vulnerability.
Drupal has not shared any information on the attacks, and it’s unclear who is responsible for the exploitation. Users have been advised to check logs for signs of compromise.

articles.title: WhatsApp suma más privacidad: cómo activar el nombre de usuario y un PIN de privacidad
articles.text:
WhatsApp permite reservar un nombre de usuario que, cuando la función esté activa en el país de cada persona, evitará que un contacto nuevo vea el número de teléfono. El trámite está en Ajustes > Cuenta > Username y lleva unos segundos, según la empresa de Meta.
El nombre de usuario es opcional. Quien no lo configure seguirá recibiendo mensajes por su número, que WhatsApp sigue exigiendo para registrarse y usar la aplicación, según sus preguntas frecuentes sobre la función.
Primero hay que actualizar WhatsApp a la última versión desde la tienda de aplicaciones del teléfono. Después, el blog oficial de la empresa indica entrar en Ajustes, luego en Cuenta y tocar la opción Username.
TechCrunch detalló lo que aparece en pantalla: quien lo hace por primera vez ve la opción “Crear username” y escribe el nombre elegido. Si no está disponible, la aplicación sugiere variantes.
Cuáles son las condiciones para el nombre en WhatsApp
Las reglas que publica WhatsApp son pocas. El nombre puede tener entre 3 y 35 caracteres, con letras del alfabeto latino, números, puntos y guiones bajos. También se puede cambiar más adelante, aunque la empresa dijo que limita la frecuencia de los cambios para evitar abusos.
Según TechCrunch, el mismo menú permite editar el nombre con el botón “Edit”, en la esquina superior derecha, o eliminarlo. WhatsApp ofrece además un generador de nombres para quien no sepa cuál elegir.
Para decidirlo, la empresa recomienda un nombre fácil de recordar pero difícil de adivinar, que solo conozcan las personas a las que se quiere dar acceso. No hace falta que incluya el nombre real, la profesión o el cargo.
Tres motivos por los que un nombre aparece como no disponible
- Los nombres de usuario que ya existen en Instagram o Facebook están reservados para sus dueños, que pueden reclamarlos en WhatsApp si vinculan su cuenta desde el Centro de cuentas de Meta, donde la empresa verifica que les pertenecen.
- La compañía retuvo nombres conocidos y sus variantes, como los de figuras públicas, celebridades, organismos de gobierno y cuentas verificadas de Meta, para evitar suplantaciones y reservas masivas. Solo sus titulares legítimos pueden reclamarlos.
- Otra persona ya lo ha tomado.
La clave opcional para tener más privacidad con el usuario
WhatsApp aclara que no habrá un directorio para buscar usuarios ni sugerencias de contactos. Para escribirle a alguien por primera vez, hay que conocer el nombre exacto. La empresa señala que, con el nombre de usuario activo, quien reciba el primer mensaje de un desconocido ya no verá el número de quien lo envió.
Quien quiera un filtro adicional puede activar la clave de usuario, otra función opcional. Con ella, un contacto nuevo debe conocer el nombre y la clave para escribir por primera vez. La clave se puede reiniciar en cualquier momento para cortar nuevos contactos por esa vía, según la aplicación.
TechCrunch describió que la clave se activa en el menú del nombre de usuario, cambiando el control de “Todos” a “Personas que conocen mi clave”, y que consiste en cuatro dígitos. WhatsApp también mencionó que bloqueará los intentos repetidos de adivinarla.
Cuando alguien con nombre de usuario escriba por primera vez, el receptor verá una tarjeta de contexto con datos como el país del remitente y los grupos que tienen en común. Con esa información puede responder, bloquear o denunciar.
El despliegue es gradual. El blog de WhatsApp indica que la empresa avisará dentro de la aplicación cuando la función esté disponible en cada país. Por eso, quien no vea la opción Username en Ajustes todavía no la tiene habilitada, aunque tenga la última versión.

articles.title: Google pode pagar R$ 200 mil por dia se não revelar mais dados sobre anúncios
articles.text:
A Secretaria Nacional do Consumidor (Senacon), vinculada ao Ministério da Justiça e Segurança Pública, determinou que o Google Brasil amplie as informações disponíveis sobre anúncios pagos em suas plataformas. A empresa tem dez dias, a partir da notificação, para implementar as mudanças. Caso descumpra a determinação, poderá receber multa diária de R$ 200 mil.
A decisão foi divulgada nesta quinta-feira (26), mas faz parte de processo administrativo instaurado na quarta-feira (25) pelo Departamento de Proteção e Defesa do Consumidor (DPDC). A medida cautelar exige alterações na Central de Transparência de Anúncios do Google, ferramenta que permite consultar publicidades veiculadas pela empresa.
As exigências abrangem anúncios e impulsionamentos pagos que alcancem usuários no Brasil, mesmo quando as campanhas não forem direcionadas exclusivamente ao público brasileiro. As regras também incluem publicidades exibidas no YouTube.
Entre as informações que deverão ficar disponíveis estão:
- O período em que cada anúncio foi veiculado;
- O número total estimado de pessoas alcançadas;
- O endereço eletrônico para o qual a publicidade direciona o usuário;
- Outros identificadores relacionados aos anúncios.
A Senacon também determinou mudanças nos mecanismos de consulta da ferramenta. Atualmente, a exigência é de que as buscas não fiquem restritas ao nome do anunciante. O sistema deverá permitir pesquisar, filtrar, ordenar e recuperar informações a partir de diferentes campos.
Para comprovar o cumprimento da determinação, o Google Brasil terá de encaminhar à secretaria uma documentação técnica com a descrição das funcionalidades implementadas, os endereços eletrônicos de acesso às informações, registros de tela e uma demonstração prática das ferramentas.
Leia mais:
- Amazon e Google terão quase 30% da Anthropic após IPO; entenda acordo
- IA começa a pressionar principal negócio de publicidade do Google
- Austrália ameaça Google e Meta com multas de até 5% da receita global
Governo estabeleceu novas regras para anúncios digitais
A decisão da Senacon está relacionada à Portaria Conjunta Senacon/SEDIGI/SPDIGI nº 3, publicada em 22 de setembro de 2026. A regulamentação estabeleceu novas obrigações de transparência para plataformas digitais que oferecem serviços de publicidade e impulsionamento pago.
Entre as determinações, provedores com mais de um milhão de usuários ativos mensais no Brasil devem manter repositório público, gratuito e pesquisável de anúncios. As informações precisam permanecer disponíveis por pelo menos um ano após o encerramento das campanhas.
A norma também prevê a divulgação de dados como identificação do contratante, período de veiculação, parâmetros de segmentação do público, estimativa de pessoas alcançadas e informações sobre pagamentos.
Segundo o Ministério da Justiça, as regras buscam ampliar a proteção dos consumidores contra publicidades enganosas, abusivas ou fraudulentas. Um dos objetivos é facilitar a identificação de golpes, inclusive aqueles que utilizam anúncios que simulam programas e serviços governamentais.
Google terá prazo para apresentar defesa
A determinação tem caráter cautelar e integra um processo administrativo sancionador. Segundo a Senacon, foram identificados indícios de possíveis condutas incompatíveis com o Código de Defesa do Consumidor (CDC) e com as obrigações estabelecidas pela regulamentação de publicidade digital.
Além do prazo de dez dias para implementar as mudanças na ferramenta, o Google Brasil terá 20 dias para apresentar sua defesa formal e indicar as provas que pretende produzir durante o processo.
O Olhar Digital procurou o Google, que disse que não comenta casos em andamento.
Rodrigo Mozelli é jornalista formado pela Universidade Metodista de São Paulo (UMESP) e, atualmente, é redator do Olhar Digital.

articles.title: Here’s where you can save (a little) on the Ocarina of Time remake
articles.text:
A lot of people have The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time for the Nintendo Switch 2 on their holiday wishlist. In case you haven’t bought it yet, I wanted to share some small but welcome deals happening on the physical and digital versions of the game. Costco members can currently grab the cartridge edition for $62.99, down from its regular price of $69.99 (it’s the only retailer currently discounting the physical version). Both Amazon and Costco are also selling the digital version for $54.99, a small $5 discount.
Here’s where you can save (a little) on the Ocarina of Time remake
In addition to GTA VI, Nintendo’s stellar Zelda remake is sure to be one of the most popular gaming gifts this holiday.
Ocarina of Time is one of Nintendo’s most groundbreaking titles, having served as its first 3D Zelda game when it launched in 1998. Parts of the original game haven’t aged particularly well — namely some dungeon design and the game’s tricky 3D navigation, since there was only one analog stick at the time — which makes it tough for some to enjoy going back to play the N64 version. Thankfully, the Switch 2 remake introduces several fixes, a host of quality-of-life improvements, and, of course, some lovely visuals that make it a graphics powerhouse by today’s standards.
If you go the digital route, a recent Switch 2 update lets you gift games to players in your family group. It doesn’t have to be your actual family, either, just up to eight people you designate as part of your group. The digital game will then appear gift-wrapped on their homescreen.

articles.title: 1Password Breach Exposes Customer Data, Internal Source Code
articles.text:
Password management and identity security company 1Password revealed on Wednesday that a hacker stole customer information and proprietary source code. 1Password says customer vaults are not affected.
The company launched an investigation on November 19 after discovering that an employee’s corporate GitHub account may have been compromised.
The attacker used the account to deploy malicious code to backend services and exfiltrate customer records. The compromised customer records include names, email addresses, account identifiers, public cryptographic keys, authentication parameters, account activity times, and non-secret metadata.
In addition, the threat actor obtained source code from private repositories and accessed the company’s CI/CD system, potentially exposing infrastructure credentials.
According to 1Password, the hacker also obtained tokens from emails sent to users for account invitations, provisioning, and recovery.
A “small number” of individuals who were undergoing provisioning or recovery during the intrusion have been notified. However, the company noted that the exposed tokens cannot be exploited on their own and there is no evidence that the attacker hijacked user accounts.
A 1Password representative noted on the company’s community forum that the stolen authentication data included Secure Remote Password verifiers derived from user account passwords and Secret Keys. The verifiers cannot be used directly for authentication, and brute-forcing account passwords would require the associated Secret Keys, which 1Password does not store.
1Password highlighted that customer vaults and the cryptographic keys protecting them were not compromised. “We have no evidence that encrypted vaults were downloaded or accessed,” a 1Password community manager said.
The breach also does not impact client applications, browser extensions, and account recovery keys.
It’s unclear how many users are affected and how the hacker gained initial access to the corporate GitHub account.
In response to the intrusion, 1Password disabled the compromised GitHub account, invalidated a stolen token, replaced potentially compromised infrastructure credentials, and restored clean versions of affected services.
The company said its investigation, conducted with independent cybersecurity experts, is still ongoing. Customers do not need to take any action, but have been advised to watch for phishing attacks that could exploit news of the incident.

articles.title: Version deux places et aileron de F1 : la Xiaomi SU7 Ultra se transforme en pistarde radicale
articles.text:
La SU7 Ultra est la version performance de la berline SU7, dont Xiaomi a livré 500 000 exemplaires en 28 mois, et la marque s’en sert comme vitrine sur le circuit du Nürburgring. En mai 2026, la Porsche Taycan Turbo GT équipée du kit Manthey lui a repris le record de la berline électrique la plus rapide sur ce circuit allemand, en 6 min 55 s contre 7 min 04 s.
Xiaomi n’a pas lâché l’affaire et s’apprête à dévoiler le millésime 2027 de sa SU7 Ultra, qui devrait donner des sueurs froides à sa rivale allemande. Comme souvent, les premiers éléments sur la voiture ont filtré par le dossier d’homologation publié ce mercredi 25 novembre par le MIIT, le ministère chinois de l’Industrie et des Technologies de l’information, comme l’a repéré CarNewsChina. Le constructeur n’a pas touché aux moteurs, mais il a élargi la voie avant, monté des pneus plus larges et ajouté des pièces en carbone pour mieux tenir la piste.
Un aileron mobile façon Formule 1
Dans la configuration la plus sportive, le dossier indique des pneus de 295 millimètres de large à l’avant, contre 265 millimètres sur le modèle actuel, et de 325 millimètres à l’arrière. Un pneu plus large offre plus de surface de contact sur l’asphalte, et donc plus d’adhérence en virage et au freinage. Pour les loger, la voie avant (l’écart entre les centres des deux roues avant) passe de 1 672 à 1 695 ou 1 708 millimètres selon la version, toujours avec des jantes de 21 pouces. Sur les photos du dossier, les pneus sont des Pirelli P Zero Trofeo RS, conçus pour la piste mais homologués pour la route.
De série, la SU7 Ultra 2027 change peu : des ouïes sur les ailes avant, un bouclier et une calandre retouchés, un nouveau diffuseur à l’arrière. Les grosses modifications arrivent en option, d’après les photos du MIIT. La plus visible est un grand aileron arrière en carbone, déjà aperçu sur les prototypes de ces derniers mois. Deux vérins électriques permettraient d’ouvrir sa partie haute en ligne droite pour réduire la résistance à l’air, comme le système DRS d’une Formule 1. Le catalogue ajoute un bouclier avant en carbone avec des écopes et de petites ailettes qui plaquent l’avant au sol, un diffuseur plus imposant, des toits et des capots en carbone, et des disques de frein en carbone-céramique.
Xiaomi a pourtant déjà trébuché sur ce terrain. En mars 2026, la marque a dû rendre fonctionnel le capot en carbone vendu en option sur la SU7 Ultra, face à des propriétaires qui n’y trouvaient pas l’effet aérodynamique promis. Sur le papier, les nouvelles pièces vont dans le sens d’un meilleur appui, mais aucune mesure indépendante ne le confirme encore.
Toujours 1 548 ch, et plus lourde
Xiaomi a déjà présenté en novembre 2024 un groupe motopropulseur expérimental à quatre moteurs de 1 510 kilowatts (2 054 ch), mais le dossier du MIIT n’en fait pas mention. La SU7 Ultra garde ses trois moteurs électriques, 288 kilowatts à l’avant et deux fois 425 kilowatts à l’arrière, soit 1 548 ch au total, et 318 km/h en pointe déclarés au MIIT.
En revanche, le poids grimpe à 2 375 ou 2 380 kg selon la version, contre 2 330 et 2 360 kg aujourd’hui. Le dossier mentionne aussi une version à deux places en plus de celle à cinq places, comme sur la Porsche Taycan Turbo GT avec le pack Weissach.
Pour reprendre son record, la berline doit donc gagner une dizaine de secondes sur le chrono de 7 min 04,957 s signé en 2025 par le pilote Vincent Radermecker, avec la même puissance et quelques dizaines de kilos en plus.
Ni prix ni date pour la version 2027
Xiaomi n’a annoncé ni prix ni date de sortie pour cette version 2027. Le modèle actuel avait été lancé en Chine le 27 février 2025 à 529 900 yuans (environ 72 500 euros). En Europe, la marque prévoit de commencer ses ventes par l’Allemagne au troisième trimestre 2027, tandis qu’elle fait partie des constructeurs chinois attendus au salon de Munich en septembre 2027.
